docket_metadata.case_name: Union Pacific / Norfolk Southern — Proposed Merger (FD-36873)

docket_entries.title: Union Pacific/Norfolk Southern Merger - Notice of Intent to File Application
docket_entries.entry_summary: Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern jointly notify the STB of their intent to file a merger application by January 29, 2026, seeking approval for UP's acquisition of NS through subsidiary Ruby Merger Sub 1 Corporation. The applicants argue the combination will create "America's first transcontinental railroad" that will "transform the U.S. supply chain, unleash the industrial strength of American manufacturing, and create new sources of economic growth." They emphasize that UP and NS have "highly complementary networks" and that current customers of both railroads "will benefit from a faster, more efficient, and more reliable network that provides single-line service from coast to coast, linking approximately 100 ports and nearly every corner of North America." The applicants also assert the combined entity "will compete more effectively with Canadian railroads to win back U.S. freight volume and American jobs" and will provide "new rail options for shippers in regions where railroad connections are less efficient, such as the Ohio Valley and on both sides of the Mississippi River." The filing commits applicants to providing 100% traffic tapes for 2023 (the impact analysis year) to requesting parties subject to a protective order and reciprocal access agreements. The transaction is structured as a merger of NSC into wholly owned subsidiaries of UPC, with anticipated filing on or before January 29, 2026.
key_arguments: The combination creates America's first true transcontinental railroad, providing single-line service from coast to coast linking approximately 100 ports and nearly every corner of North America
UP and NS networks are highly complementary, allowing combined entity to serve customers with faster, more efficient, and more reliable service than either railroad alone

The merger will provide new rail options in currently underserved regions such as the Ohio Valley and both sides of the Mississippi River, making the supply chain more accessible, sustainable, and lower-cost
The combined company will generate significant employment opportunities and economic growth in communities across the combined rail network
The merger will enable the combined railroad to compete more effectively with Canadian railroads (CN, CPKC) to win back U.S. freight volume and American jobs
key_excerpts: Applicants believe a combination of UP and NS represents an unprecedented opportunity to create America's first transcontinental railroad, which will transform the U.S. supply chain, unleash the industrial strength of American manufacturing, and create new sources of economic growth and workforce opportunity.

Current customers of both railroads will benefit from a faster, more efficient, and more reliable network that provides single-line service from coast to coast, linking approximately 100 ports and nearly every corner of North America.

A UP-NS combination will provide new rail options for shippers in regions where railroad connections are less efficient, such as the Ohio Valley and on both sides of the Mississippi River, creating a more accessible, sustainable, and lower-cost supply chain for manufacturers and consumers.

The combined UP-NS will produce rail volume growth that will drive additional employment opportunities in towns and cities across the combined rail network and generate economic growth in communities across the United States.
The combined company will also compete more effectively with Canadian railroads to win back U.S. freight volume and American jobs.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Authority under 49 U.S.C. §§ 11323-25 for the acquisition of control by Union Pacific Corporation, through subsidiary Ruby Merger Sub 1 Corporation, of Norfolk Southern Corporation and Norfolk Southern Railway Company.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This Notice of Intent formally initiates STB review of a Class I merger under 49 U.S.C. §§ 11323-25 and 49 C.F.R. § 1180.2(a) (major transaction standard). The filing establishes: (1) baseline year for impact analysis (2023); (2) procedural schedule framework (to be detailed in UP-2/NS-2); (3) data access commitments via 100% traffic tapes subject to protective order; (4) reciprocal waybill access obligations; and (5) protective order terms mirroring the CP/KCS precedent (Finance Docket 36500). The applicants have essentially framed the case narrative at entry: efficiency, transcontinental integration, regional benefits, and competitive positioning vs. Canadian carriers. The January 29, 2026 filing date gives applicants 6 months to prepare detailed application with competitive impact analysis, operational integration plans, and response to anticipated opposition.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Initiate Case
docket_entries.deadline_description: Applicants' anticipated filing date for full merger application

docket_entries.title: Union Pacific/Norfolk Southern Petition to Establish Procedural Schedule
docket_entries.entry_summary: Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern jointly petition the STB to establish a procedural schedule for the merger proceeding under 49 C.F.R. § 1180.4(b)(4)(i). The applicants propose a schedule modeled on prior major merger proceedings, running from filing (F) through final decision at F+420 days. Key milestones: notices of intent due F+45; comments/protests/condition requests due F+120; responses F+210; final briefs F+270; public hearing (if necessary) F+300; final decision F+390 (90 days after record close); effective date F+420. The applicants argue this schedule 'provides ample time for interested parties to comment and for the Board to complete its review within the statutory deadlines set by 49 U.S.C. § 11325(b).' The proposed schedule includes specific deadlines for Safety Integration Plan filing (F+60), responsive applications (F+75, F+120, F+150), environmental filings (F+115), and DOJ/DOT submissions (F+120). The petition requests the Board publish notice soliciting public comment on the proposed schedule before final adoption.
key_arguments: The proposed procedural schedule aligns with historical precedent in prior major merger proceedings, ensuring consistency with established STB practice

The schedule provides ample time for interested parties to submit comments, protests, and condition requests while ensuring the Board completes its review within the statutory 180-day deadline under 49 U.S.C. § 11325(b)
The schedule accommodates mandatory regulatory requirements including Safety Integration Plan filing (F+60), environmental analysis (F+115), and federal agency review (DOJ/DOT at F+120)
key_excerpts: The proposed procedural schedule is in line with those in prior major merger proceedings, and it provides ample time for interested parties to comment and for the Board to complete its review within the statutory deadlines set by 49 U.S.C. § 11325(b).

Applicants ask the Board to publish a Federal Register notice soliciting comments on the proposed procedural schedule and, after reviewing any comments and replies, to issue a procedural schedule governing the course of the proceeding.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Establish a procedural schedule governing the merger proceeding. Specifically: (1) Board publish Federal Register notice soliciting comments on the proposed procedural schedule; (2) after reviewing comments and replies, Board issue the procedural schedule; (3) adopt the attached proposed schedule (Appendix A).
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing establishes the procedural framework governing all subsequent filings, discovery, and hearings. The proposed F+420 timeline compresses the entire major merger review into approximately 14 months from filing to effective date, which will be contested by intervenors who may claim insufficient time for discovery and analysis. The schedule controls when intervenors can file notices of intent (F+45), when comments must be filed (F+120), and when responses are due (F+210, F+240). Any material deviation from this schedule will require subsequent motions and could extend the proceeding. The Safety Integration Plan requirement (F+60) and environmental analysis requirement (F+115) embed regulatory compliance deadlines into the schedule. The statute (49 U.S.C. § 11325(b)) allows 180 days from publication of notice to make a decision, so this F+390 target for service of final decision (with F+420 effective date) provides only a 210-day window from filing—meaning the Board must issue decision within 180 days of accepting the application (roughly F+210 based on typical notice publishing timelines).
docket_entries.deadline_description: No deadline for response to this petition; the STB will issue its own notice requesting public comment on the proposed procedural schedule.

docket_entries.title: Motion for Protective Order – Union Pacific/Norfolk Southern Control Application
docket_entries.entry_summary: Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern jointly request entry of a comprehensive Protective Order governing confidential information exchange during the merger proceeding. The applicants argue that 'unrestricted disclosure of confidential, proprietary, or commercially sensitive information and data could cause serious competitive injury to the parties' and that 'issuance of a protective order ensures that such information and data produced by any party in response to a discovery request or otherwise will be used solely for purposes of this proceeding and not for any other business or commercial purpose.' The proposed order establishes a two-tier confidentiality system: (1) 'CONFIDENTIAL' material (traffic data including waybills, shipper-specific data, contract terms, financial/cost data) accessible to in-house employees, outside counsel, and consultants who sign a confidentiality undertaking; and (2) 'HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL' material (the most competitively sensitive information) accessible only to outside counsel and outside consultants, with explicit prohibition on in-house employee access. The order further provides that if the control application is disapproved or not effected, all confidential documents must be destroyed or returned. Critically, paragraph 3 deems the exchange of confidential information 'essential for the conduct and disposition' of the proceeding and provides that such exchange 'will not be deemed a violation of 49 U.S.C. §§ 11323, 11904, or any other relevant provision of the ICC Termination Act,' thereby creating a safe harbor for competitor information-sharing that would otherwise violate antitrust strictures. The order references Finance Docket No. 36500 (Canadian Pacific/Kansas City Southern, April 2, 2021) as precedent for substantially similar terms. The applicants anticipate filing their merger application by January 29, 2026.
key_arguments: Unrestricted disclosure of confidential information would cause serious competitive injury; a protective order ensures information is used only for the proceeding and not for any other business or competitive purpose
The order is necessary to comply with 49 U.S.C. §§ 11323, 11904, and the ICC Termination Act of 1995, which restrict information-sharing between railroad competitors

Establishing a two-tier confidentiality system (CONFIDENTIAL and HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL) with tiered access restrictions allows parties to exchange necessary business intelligence while protecting the most competitively sensitive data from general in-house access

A protective order will facilitate prompt and efficient resolution of the proceeding by allowing parties to present confidential evidence at discovery, hearings, and in pleadings without fear of public exposure
The proposed terms are consistent with precedent in other railroad merger proceedings (CP/KCS, FD 36500) and reflect industry-standard protective order language

The order includes a safe harbor provision (paragraph 3) deeming information exchange essential to the proceeding and not a violation of ICC Termination Act antitrust provisions, allowing the parties to cooperate in case preparation despite their status as competitors
key_excerpts: Unrestricted disclosure of confidential, proprietary, or commercially sensitive information and data could cause serious competitive injury to the parties. Issuance of a protective order ensures that such information and data produced by any party in response to a discovery request or otherwise will be used solely for purposes of this proceeding and not for any other business or commercial purpose.

To the extent that any meetings, conferences, exchanges of data, or other cooperative efforts between representatives of Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern or their affiliates are held and carried out for purposes of these Proceedings, such meetings, conferences, exchanges of data and other cooperative efforts are deemed essential for the conduct and disposition of such proceedings and will not be deemed a violation of 49 U.S.C. §§ 11323, 11904, or any other relevant provision of the ICC Termination Act of 1995 (ICCTA).

Information and documents designated or stamped as 'HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL' may not be disclosed in any way, directly or indirectly, to any employee of a party to these proceedings, or to any other person or entity except to an outside counsel or outside consultant to a party to these proceedings, or to an employee of such outside counsel or outside consultant, who, before receiving access to such information or documents, has been given and has read a copy of this Protective Order and has agreed to be bound by its terms.

Applicants must exchange information that includes or is based on proprietary and commercially sensitive information, including shipper-specific data that are normally protected against public disclosure under 49 U.S.C. § 11904.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Entry of a Protective Order governing the production, exchange, and use of confidential and proprietary information during the proceeding, substantially in the form proposed in Appendix A. The order is necessary to: (1) protect shipper-specific data, contract terms, traffic data (waybills, abstracts, study movement sheets), cost workpapers, and other confidential financial and competitive information from public disclosure; (2) comply with 49 U.S.C. §§ 11323, 11904, and the ICC Termination Act of 1995; and (3) facilitate efficient discovery, evidence presentation, and litigation.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This protective order is legally and procedurally significant in multiple respects: (1) It creates an antitrust safe harbor under 49 U.S.C. §§ 11323 and 11904, explicitly stating that information exchange deemed 'essential for the conduct and disposition' of the proceeding will not violate ICC Termination Act restrictions on competitor information-sharing—effectively suspending antitrust/competitive injury concerns for discovery purposes. (2) It establishes tiered confidentiality tiers matching the sensitivity of information, with the most competitively sensitive data ('HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL') restricted to outside counsel/consultants only, preventing client access—a procedural mechanism to balance discovery needs against competitive harm. (3) It governs the scope and use of discovery throughout the proceeding, including deposition protocols (paragraph 16), hearing procedures (paragraph 15), and pleading submissions under seal (paragraphs 13-14), thereby affecting what evidence and arguments can be presented publicly vs. under seal. (4) It establishes post-proceeding destruction obligations (paragraph 12) and explicitly states that breach entitles the producing party to injunctive relief and specific performance, not merely damages—creating a strong enforcement mechanism. (5) It requires simultaneous filing of public, confidential, and highly confidential versions of submissions (paragraph 9), creating administrative burdens and potentially affecting pleading strategy. (6) The order references Finance Docket No. 36500 (CP/KCS) as precedent, suggesting the Board has developed a standardized approach to confidentiality in rail merger proceedings, which may affect how future intervenors approach discovery disputes.
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response deadline; this is a procedural motion requesting Board entry of the protective order prior to filing the merger application (anticipated by January 29, 2026). Intervenors may file objections or alternative proposals if they file interventions.

docket_entries.title: STB Response to Senators Baldwin and Marshall on UP-NS Merger Notice of Intent
docket_entries.entry_summary: On August 1, 2025, the STB responded to a letter from Senators Tammy Baldwin and Roger Marshall regarding the proposed UP-NS merger. The Board confirmed that UP and NS filed a Notice of Intent on July 30, 2025, indicating they intend to file their formal merger application on or before January 29, 2026. The Board stated that under its major merger regulations at 49 C.F.R. Part 1180, it must publish the notice of intent in the Federal Register within 30 days of filing. The Board declined to comment substantively on the pending matter but assured the senators that upon application filing, it would 'evaluate the evidence and argument and consider whether the transaction serves the public interest, consistent with applicable law.' The Board committed to a 'thorough examination of competitive effects, potential service impacts, environmental impacts, and other critical considerations' and confirmed that 'the Board's review process will include opportunities for public participation and comment.' This response establishes the formal procedural timeline and signals the Board's framework for evaluation.
key_arguments: The Board will evaluate competitive effects as a central element of its review
The Board will examine potential service impacts on the freight rail network
Environmental impacts will be considered as a critical consideration
Public participation and comment opportunities will be provided throughout the review process
The transaction will be evaluated under the public interest standard under applicable law
key_excerpts: UP and NS submitted to the Surface Transportation Board (STB) a notice of intent to file an application for Board approval of a proposed merger that would result in the combination of UP and NS, both Class I railroads... on July 28, 2025, they entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger under which UP, through a wholly owned subsidiary, would acquire all outstanding shares of NS for consideration consisting of shares of UP common stock and cash.

the Board will evaluate the evidence and argument and consider whether the transaction serves the public interest, consistent with applicable law. The Board's review will include a thorough examination of competitive effects, potential service impacts, environmental impacts, and other critical considerations.
The Board's review process will include opportunities for public participation and comment.
docket_entries.relief_requested: No relief requested. The Board states it cannot comment on the pending matter but affirms it will conduct a thorough review evaluating competitive effects, service impacts, environmental impacts, and other critical considerations, with public participation opportunities.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This establishes the formal regulatory timeline under 49 C.F.R. Part 1180. Key dates: (1) Notice of Intent filed July 30, 2025; (2) STB must publish notice in Federal Register within 30 days (by August 29, 2025); (3) Application to be filed on or before January 29, 2026. This confirms the merger is no longer speculative but in the formal pre-filing phase. The Board's stated framework—competitive effects, service impacts, environmental impacts, plus public interest standard—telegraphs the key issues that will drive the review and likely contested areas. The Board's emphasis on 'public participation and comment' indicates this will be a full notice-and-comment proceeding with likely extensive discovery and hearing phases.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Deadline for UP and NS to file formal merger application with STB (stated as 'on or before January 29, 2026')

docket_entries.title: Letter from Senators Baldwin and Marshall Urging STB to Scrutinize UP-NS Merger for Shipper Harms
docket_entries.entry_summary: Senators Baldwin (D-WI) and Marshall (R-KS) jointly urge the STB to rigorously scrutinize the UP-NS merger, stating it 'would be the most significant consolidation in freight rail in decades and would undoubtedly reshape the U.S. freight rail industry and supply chain.' They argue that further rail consolidation will 'diminish options for industry to transport goods, increase costs, create more unreliable service for U.S. shippers, and reduce overall competition.' The Senators emphasize that the rail industry has consolidated from 'over 100 Class I freight railroads to only six today,' with four carriers providing 'nearly 90 percent of the nation's freight rail transportation.' They cite specific harm: manufacturers, utilities, agricultural producers, and small businesses are 'experiencing service and reliability problems while paying excessive rates,' while UP and NS posted record profits (UP: $24.9B revenue in 2022, +14%; NS: $12.9B revenue, +14%). The Senators invoke the STB's 2001 merger rules requiring that 'Class I railroads prove that mergers would both enhance competition and are in the public interest,' urging the Board to 'keep this at the forefront of considerations.' The letter signals conditional opposition: they do not demand outright denial but demand rigorous application of competitive/public interest standards that would require demonstrable benefits to shippers and consumers.
key_arguments: Rail industry consolidation from 100+ Class I carriers (1950s) to only 6 today has 'dramatically increased the power of railroads over shippers,' leaving shippers with 'limited to no other options to move goods to market at a reasonable rate.'

The UP-NS merger would trigger further consolidation: 'A major rail merger has the potential to trigger additional industry consolidation,' which would amplify existing service and rate problems for shippers.

Shippers are experiencing demonstrable harms despite railroads' record profitability: UP and NS posted +14% operating revenue increases in 2022 ($24.9B and $12.9B respectively), yet 'shippers and consumers are paying the price' through 'excessive rates' and 'unreliable railroad service.'

The merger fails the STB's 2001 public interest standard: applicants must 'prove that mergers would both enhance competition and are in the public interest,' which the Senators imply this merger cannot meet.
Consumer inflation consequences: 'As a result, consumers continue to face higher costs for essential everyday goods,' linking rail consolidation to downstream cost-of-living impacts.
key_excerpts: If approved, this acquisition would be the most significant consolidation in freight rail in decades and would undoubtedly reshape the U.S. freight rail industry and supply chain.

Since the 1950s, the rail industry has consolidated from over 100 Class I freight railroads to only six today. A long trend of industry consolidation has dramatically increased the power of railroads over shippers in the last few decades — leaving four carriers to provide nearly 90 percent of the nation's freight rail transportation.

In recent years, we have heard from too many U.S. manufacturers, utility companies, agricultural producers and small businesses experiencing service and reliability problems while paying excessive rates.

The railroad industry has proven to be more concerned with increasing their rates and profits rather than improving their service. While Class I railroads continue to see record profits, shippers and consumers are paying the price.

We are encouraged that the STB shared this concern in the context of the 2001 rulemaking process, in which the STB set new rules governing major railroad mergers and started requiring Class I railroads to prove that mergers would both enhance competition and are in the public interest.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Urge the STB to 'keep the best interests of rail shippers and consumers in mind throughout your careful review of this matter' and to apply rigorous scrutiny under the 2001 merger rules requiring Class I railroads to 'prove that mergers would both enhance competition and are in the public interest.' If the merger proceeds, the letter signals conditions must address shipper service reliability, rate reasonableness, and competitive alternatives.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This letter reframes the merger review around the STB's 2001 merger approval standards (49 U.S.C. § 11324(d)), which require applicants to demonstrate that a merger 'is consistent with the public interest' and specifically authorize denial if the merger would 'reduce competition.' The Senators' invocation of these standards signals Congressional expectation that the STB will apply rigorous scrutiny and that perfunctory 'competitive analysis' will be insufficient. The bipartisan nature signals this is not partisan opposition and may influence how the STB frames its eventual decision—the Board must affirmatively address whether the merger enhances or diminishes competition, not simply defer to applicant assertions. The letter also establishes that Congressional actors representing shipper constituencies (Baldwin from Wisconsin grain/manufacturing; Marshall from Kansas agriculture) are monitoring the proceeding, which may increase political pressure on an approval decision.
docket_entries.deadline_description: This is an advocacy letter, not a formal pleading requiring response, but it signals that Congress is watching the proceeding and may hold hearings or request briefings if the STB approves the merger.

docket_entries.title: STB Grants Protective Order for Confidential Information in UP/NS Merger (Decision No. 1)
docket_entries.entry_summary: The STB granted Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern's motion for a protective order on August 5, 2025, establishing strict protocols for handling confidential information throughout the merger proceeding. The Board found 'good cause' exists because 'unrestricted disclosure of confidential, proprietary, or commercially sensitive information and data could cause serious competitive injury to the parties.' The protective order defines confidential information broadly to include 'traffic data (including but not limited to waybills, abstracts, study movement sheets, and any documents or computer tapes containing data derived from waybills), the identification of shippers and receivers in conjunction with shipper-specific or other traffic data, the confidential terms of contracts with shippers, confidential financial and cost data, and other confidential or proprietary business information.' The order creates two tiers: 'CONFIDENTIAL' material accessible to any party's in-house counsel and outside advisors upon execution of undertakings; and 'HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL' material restricted to outside counsel and consultants only, with strict prohibitions on access by company employees. Critically, paragraph 2 permits Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern 'to exchange Confidential Information for the purpose of participating in the proceedings, but not for any other business, commercial, or other competitive purpose, unless and until their control application in the Proceedings is approved,' effectively immunizing pre-merger information sharing from antitrust violations under 49 U.S.C. § 11904. The order applies to all discovery, depositions, hearing testimony, and filings, with violations subject to injunctive relief and specific performance. This procedural framework will constrain how much merger-sensitive competitive data becomes publicly visible and how freely intervenors can deploy confidential information in their testimony and briefs.
key_arguments: Good cause exists for the protective order because unrestricted disclosure of confidential, proprietary, or commercially sensitive information and data could cause serious competitive injury to the parties.
A protective order ensures that information and data produced in discovery will be used solely for purposes of the proceeding and not for any other business or commercial purpose.
A protective order will facilitate the prompt and efficient resolution of this proceeding.
The proposed protective order is similar to protective orders adopted in previous control cases, specifically Canadian Pacific-Kansas City Southern (FD 36500).

Information exchange between Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern personnel for purposes of the proceedings is deemed essential and will not constitute a violation of 49 U.S.C. §§ 11323, 11904, or other ICC Termination Act provisions.
key_excerpts: Unrestricted disclosure of confidential, proprietary, or commercially sensitive information and data could cause serious competitive injury to the parties. Issuance of a protective order ensures that such information and data produced by any party in response to a discovery request or otherwise will be used solely for purposes of this proceeding and not for any other business or commercial purpose.

To the extent that any meetings, conferences, exchanges of data, or other cooperative efforts between representatives of Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern or their affiliates are held and carried out for purposes of these Proceedings, such meetings, conferences, exchanges of data and other cooperative efforts are deemed essential for the conduct and disposition of such proceedings and will not be deemed a violation of 49 U.S.C. §§ 11323, 11904, or any other relevant provision of the ICC Termination Act of 1995.

Information and documents designated or stamped as 'HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL' may not be disclosed in any way, directly or indirectly, to any employee of a party to these proceedings, or to any other person or entity except to an outside counsel or outside consultant to a party to these proceedings.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Motion for protective order GRANTED. Applicants sought entry of a protective order to safeguard confidential information and facilitate compliance with 49 U.S.C. §§ 11323 and 11904.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This decision establishes the procedural and evidentiary framework governing all information disclosure for the remainder of the proceeding. Most significantly, it formally immunizes Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern from antitrust liability under 49 U.S.C. § 11904 for pre-merger competitive information sharing ('shall not be deemed a violation'), a critical antitrust shield during a merger between two major competitors. The two-tier confidentiality system (CONFIDENTIAL vs. HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL) creates asymmetric information access: intervenor-shippers may access standard confidential data through outside counsel, but shipper-specific rate and cost data remains restricted to outside counsel only, limiting competitor intelligence. The requirement that all parties file simultaneous public versions of submissions (paragraph 9) establishes that the public docket will contain redacted versions, narrowing the competitive intelligence available to non-parties and the public. The Board's reliance on precedent (CP-KCS) signals that this protective order framework is standard for major rail mergers and will likely apply throughout.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Board decision is effective on service date (August 5, 2025). Parties must comply with the protective order immediately.

docket_entries.title: STB Grant of Waybill Data Access (CCWS) to Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern for FD-36873 Analysis
docket_entries.entry_summary: On August 5, 2025, the STB Office of Economics granted Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern access to confidential Carload Waybill Sample (CCWS) data for 2019-2024 covering all traffic with unmasked revenues. The grant authorizes 33 named outside counsel and consultants (7 from Covington & Burling, 7 from Sidley Austin, 3 from Charles River Associates, 6 from Oliver Wyman, 8 from Econic Partners, and 3 from Analysis Group) to access the data solely for preparation of market and traffic impact analyses required under 49 C.F.R. §§ 1180.6(a)(2)(i) and 1180.7 in support of the planned FD-36873 application. The STB stated the CCWS is 'the only single source' of data needed for complete analysis of these issues. Access is effective upon execution of confidentiality agreements by all named individuals. The agreements impose strict limitations: data use limited to the proceeding and related judicial review; unaggregated CCWS data in pleadings must be filed under confidential procedures marked 'Highly Confidential Material: Contains Waybill Data'; data disclosable to other parties only if they have signed their own CCWS agreements; compelled disclosures require notice to STB within 3 days and no later than 5 days before release; annual renewal required by August 30, 2026, or all data must be destroyed/returned with certification; non-compliance may result in sanctions and permanent bar from future waybill data access. The STB noted important limitations of CCWS as a sample based on terminating shipments from carriers with more than 4,500 annual terminating carloads, which may substantially affect studies in areas served predominantly by smaller railroads. Payment of $2,546 ($200 processing plus $69 per individual for 34 individuals) was required.
key_arguments: CCWS waybill data with unmasked revenues for 2019-2024 is essential and the only complete single source available for the market and traffic impact analyses statutorily required by 49 C.F.R. §§ 1180.6(a)(2)(i) and 1180.7
Data access granted based on applicants' 'complete and sufficiently detailed explanations and justifications' of necessity
CCWS data is commercially sensitive and has potential to cause competitive harm to shippers and railroads if disclosed, necessitating strict confidentiality protocols
CCWS sample limitations (based on terminating shipments from carriers with >4,500 annual terminating carloads) may substantially affect studies in areas served predominantly by non-sampled railroads
key_excerpts: 'The STB Waybill Sample is the only single source of the data permitting a complete analysis of these issues' [and] 'The requested data are essential to the preparation, among other things, of the market and traffic impact analyses required by 49 C.F.R. §§ 1180.6(a)(2)(i) and 1180.7'
'Based on the complete and sufficiently detailed explanations and justifications contained in your request, I will grant access to 2019 through 2024 CCWS data for use in the FD 36873 proceeding'
'The CCWS is commercially sensitive and has the potential to cause competitive harm to shippers and railroads if disclosed'

'Only those railroads with more than 4,500 annual terminating carloads are included in the sample. The limited sampling of small railroads may have a substantial effect on studies covering areas served predominantly by non-sampled railroads'
docket_entries.relief_requested: Grant access to unmasked Carload Waybill Sample (CCWS) data for 2019-2024 to Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern outside counsel and consultants for preparation of market and traffic impact analyses required by 49 C.F.R. §§ 1180.6(a)(2)(i) and 1180.7
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This grant establishes the evidentiary foundation for applicants' mandatory statutory analyses under 49 U.S.C. § 11324 and 49 C.F.R. Part 1180. The STB's determination that CCWS data is 'the only single source' of complete market and traffic impact data likely forecloses challenges to applicants' analytical methodology on grounds of data insufficiency. The decision to grant 2024 data (when available) extends the contemporary data window beyond the initial request and provides more current competitive and traffic information. The detailed confidentiality regime established here will govern all merger analysis disclosure throughout the proceeding—any breach by applicants' counsel or consultants could result in sanctions and disclosure to competitors. The grant also implicitly confirms that applicants have satisfied preliminary threshold requirements for accessing confidential competitive data, suggesting STB has found the merger application warrants serious evidentiary development. The note about CCWS sampling limitations (underrepresenting small railroads) may become relevant in analyses of regional competitive impacts or short-line competition, potentially limiting the weight of CCWS-based conclusions in those areas.
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response required. This is a Commission grant. All named individuals must execute confidentiality agreements by unspecified date (before data delivery). Annual renewal request due by July 31, 2026 (30 days before August 31, 2026 expiration). Certification of destruction/return due by August 31, 2026 if no renewal requested.

docket_entries.title: BNSF Railway Company Notice of Intent to Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.entry_summary: BNSF Railway Company filed a notice of intent to participate in the UP-NS control proceeding without submitting substantive comments at this time. The filing reserves BNSF's right to participate 'as its interests may require,' indicating BNSF is monitoring the transaction and may submit detailed competitive concerns, testimony, or conditions later in the proceeding. BNSF retained Steptoe LLP counsel (Peter Denton, Anthony LaRocca, Timothy Strafford) to represent it, signaling this is a matter of serious consequence to the railroad. The notice-only filing is typical for major competitors at the initial intervention stage—BNSF is establishing standing and service list placement before potentially filing substantive opposition or conditions.
key_excerpts: BNSF Railway Company hereby provides notice of its intent to participate in this proceeding as its interests may require, and requests that the undersigned be placed on the service list for this proceeding as counsel for BNSF Railway Company.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Notice of intent to participate in the proceeding 'as its interests may require' and placement on the service list.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing establishes BNSF's right to participate in the proceeding and ensures all future substantive filings (comments, discovery motions, hearing testimony, briefs) will be served on BNSF. The 'as its interests may require' language is deliberately open-ended, preserving BNSF's ability to escalate involvement if competitive harms materialize. As a major competitor with extensive overlapping operations with both UP and NS, BNSF's participation is expected and will likely be material to the STB's competitive analysis.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response required. BNSF is now on service list for all future filings.

docket_entries.title: CSX Transportation Notice of Intent to Participate
docket_entries.entry_summary: CSX Transportation filed a notice of intent to participate in FD-36873 without expressing any substantive position on the merger. The filing is purely procedural: CSX's counsel (Crowell & Moring LLP) requests placement on the service list to allow CSX to receive filings and participate in the proceeding. No arguments are advanced, no conditions are proposed, and no opposition or support is stated. This is a hold-the-door filing typical of major competitors who want to monitor the proceeding before committing to a substantive position. CSX's status as a major Class I competitor suggests it will likely file substantive opposition or conditional support once discovery and applicant filings reveal merger impacts on competitive routes and service offerings.
key_excerpts: CSX Transportation, Inc. ('CSXT') hereby provides notice of its intent to participate in the above-referenced proceeding, and requests that the undersigned by placed on the service list for this proceeding as counsel for CSXT.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Requests placement on the service list for the proceeding to participate in the finance docket.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This is a procedural filing establishing intervention status. It does not change the scope or burden of review but secures CSX's right to receive all STB filings, participate in discovery exchanges, submit comments, cross-examine witnesses at hearing, and file briefs. In railroad merger proceedings, major competitor intervention is standard and often presages substantive opposition or negotiation of competitive access remedies.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.deadline_description: No responsive action required from applicants; establishes CSX's participation rights.

docket_entries.title: SMART-TD Notice of Intent to Participate - Labor Union of Train Service Employees
docket_entries.entry_summary: SMART-TD, representing train service employees including conductors at both Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern, filed a Notice of Intent to Participate to establish its right to participate in the merger proceedings. The filing contains no substantive arguments for or against the merger and requests no specific relief or conditions. SMART-TD's intervention notice is procedural in nature, signaling the labor union's status as an interested party and preserving its right to file substantive comments, present evidence at hearing, and advocate for labor-protective measures. The filing demonstrates that railroad labor has formally put the Board on notice of its interest in the outcome and the applicants' obligations to consider labor implications of the proposed control transaction.
key_excerpts: SMART-TD, the largest railroad labor organization in the United States, represents the craft and class of train service employees, including conductors, employed by Applicants Union Pacific Railroad Company and Norfolk Southern Railway Company. As a result, SMART-TD has a strong interest in this proceeding.

The Transportation Division of the International Association of the Sheet Metal, Air, Rail and Transportation Workers ('SMART-TD') respectfully submits its Notice of Intent to Participate in this proceeding.
docket_entries.relief_requested: No specific relief requested. SMART-TD filed a Notice of Intent to Participate to establish standing and monitor the proceeding due to its representation of craft and class train service employees at both Applicants.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing establishes SMART-TD's standing to participate fully in the merger proceeding under 49 U.S.C. § 11324 and STB procedural rules. The notice preserves SMART-TD's right to file substantive comments on labor impacts, participate in discovery, cross-examine witnesses at any hearing, and submit post-hearing briefs. It signals to the Board and applicants that labor-related issues (workforce reductions, job losses, seniority list integration, work rules changes) are within scope of the public interest review and that any approval conditions may need to address labor protection measures. This is particularly significant because railroad labor has statutory protification provisions under Section 4(f) of the Interstate Commerce Act (49 U.S.C. § 11347) that may apply to merger conditions.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.deadline_description: Notice of Intent to Participate does not trigger a response deadline; SMART-TD may now file substantive comments and participate in subsequent phases of the proceeding.

docket_entries.title: American Train Dispatchers Association Notice of Intent to Participate in Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern Control Proceeding

docket_entries.title: STB Approval of Waybill Data Access for Union Pacific's Advisors (Covington & Burling, Oliver Wyman)
docket_entries.entry_summary: On August 8, 2025, the STB Office of Economics approved Union Pacific's request to grant seven additional individuals access to confidential waybill data (CCWS) in FD 36873. The approvals cover: Matthew J. Glover (Covington & Burling LLP, outside counsel); and six Oliver Wyman consultants (Daniel Spiller, Haley Mathews, Simon Roberts, Dylan Cai, Harrison Wang, Jason Kuehn). Each signatory executed a Waybill Agreement WB25-42 binding them to CCWS confidentiality conditions, including requirements to return or destroy data within 30 days of agreement expiration and renewal notice requirements. Union Pacific prepaid processing and mailing costs of $483 ($69 per signature) via pay.gov. This administrative action indicates UP is expanding its economic and legal team for deeper analysis of competitive/service impacts—typical of the discovery phase where parties assemble detailed arguments on merger effects. The involvement of Oliver Wyman (major economic consulting firm) suggests preparation of economic modeling and competitive analysis to rebut any opposing economic submissions.
key_arguments: Administrative approval only—no substantive arguments on merger merits presented
Indicates Union Pacific is assembling sophisticated economic advisory team (Oliver Wyman) and outside counsel (Covington & Burling) for discovery-phase analysis
key_excerpts: I have approved the addition of the following individuals to the waybill access letter in WB25-42: Matthew J Glover – Covington and Burling LLP, Daniel Spiller – Oliver Wyman, Haley Mathews – Oliver Wyman, Simon Roberts – Oliver Wyman, Dylan Cai – Oliver Wyman, Harrison Wang – Oliver Wyman, Jason Kuehn – Oliver Wyman

I agree to comply fully with these conditions and the provisions of this confidentiality agreement. No later than thirty days before the agreement expires, I will request an extension of this agreement, if necessary. If no extension is requested, I will return or destroy all CCWS data and certify that I have done so.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This is procedural/administrative, not substantive to merger review. However, it signals that UP is moving into intensive economic analysis and competitive modeling phase of discovery. The addition of Oliver Wyman consultants typically precedes submission of economic exhibits, competitive impact analyses, and response briefs. The fact that Union Pacific is expanding its advisory team suggests preparation for either: (1) responding to shipper or competitor opposition with economic rebuttal; (2) proactive submission of economic evidence supporting competitive benefits; or (3) both. This is routine but indicative of case complexity and expected submission of detailed quantitative analysis.

The participation of a major competitor in such a concentrated industry suggests the STB can expect detailed competitive analysis regarding market concentration, pricing power, and service impacts from CN in subsequent filings.

docket_entries.title: STB Approval of BNSF Waybill Data Access (WB25-44) for FD 36873 Merger Analysis
docket_entries.entry_summary: The STB Office of Economics granted BNSF Railway Company's request for access to confidential Carload Waybill Sample (CCWS) data covering 2019-2024 (including unmasked revenues, all records, all fields) to 'accurately analyze the impacts of the transaction proposed in FD 36873, including traffic patterns, and to prepare verified statements in formal proceedings before the Board on behalf of BNSF.' BNSF requested and received the same data access as other parties in the proceeding. Access was approved for six attorneys at Steptoe LLP (outside counsel), three economists at Compass Lexecon, and eight consultants at FTI Consulting. The approval is conditional on strict confidentiality: data may only be used for the FD 36873 proceeding and judicial review; unaggregated waybill-derived evidence must be filed under seal; all work product is restricted to signatory parties; disclosure of data to third parties requires referral to the STB; and all data must be destroyed or returned by August 31, 2026 unless extension is sought. The filing demonstrates BNSF is mobilizing significant economic and legal resources to challenge or condition the merger, and has already begun detailed competitive impact analysis using granular traffic and revenue data that may form the basis of verified testimony.
key_arguments: BNSF is entitled to access the same confidential waybill data that has been granted to other parties in FD 36873 to conduct competitive impact analysis

Unmasked 2019-2024 CCWS data including all records, fields, and confidential revenues is necessary for BNSF's counsel and consultants to accurately analyze the merger's impacts on traffic patterns and competitive conditions
BNSF intends to prepare verified statements in formal proceedings before the Board based on this waybill analysis
Requested data access is standard and consistent with access granted to other FD 36873 parties under existing protective order protocols
key_excerpts: The purpose of this request is to allow BNSF's counsel and consultants to accurately analyze the impacts of the transaction proposed in FD 36873, including traffic patterns, and to prepare verified statements in formal proceedings before the Board on behalf of BNSF.
The access BNSF seeks is the same as the access granted to other parties in this proceeding.
Based on the complete and sufficiently detailed explanations and justifications contained in your request, I will grant access to 2019 through 2024 CCWS data for use in the FD 36873 proceeding.
docket_entries.relief_requested: STB approved BNSF's request for access to unmasked 2019-2024 Carload Waybill Sample (CCWS) data including all records, all fields, and confidential unmasked revenues for all traffic, under strict confidentiality protocols.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This procedural grant under 49 C.F.R. § 1244.9(b)(4) is significant because it: (1) confirms that unmasked waybill revenue data is available to major competitors in merger analysis, creating an evidentiary foundation for competitive impact arguments; (2) demonstrates that at least two tier-1 economic consulting firms (Compass Lexecon, FTI Consulting) are engaged by BNSF for merger impact analysis, indicating serious and well-resourced opposition preparation; (3) establishes the time period (2019-2024) and data granularity (all fields, unmasked revenues) that BNSF will use to construct competitive harm arguments; (4) constrains how BNSF can use and disclose this data in formal proceedings (confidential filing requirements, three-shipper aggregation rule at 49 C.F.R. § 1244.9(f)), which may limit the public evidence available in merger briefs. The August 31, 2026 expiration date suggests BNSF expects the merger proceeding to conclude by then or shortly thereafter.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Expiration of waybill data access agreement; BNSF must destroy or return all CCWS data by this date unless extension is requested at least 30 days prior.

docket_entries.title: STB Grant of Confidential Waybill Data Access to CSX Transportation for FD 36873 Analysis
docket_entries.entry_summary: The STB Office of Economics granted CSX Transportation's August 6, 2025 request for access to confidential Carload Waybill Sample (CCWS) data covering 2019-2024, including all records, all fields, and unmasked revenues for all traffic. CSX requested the data to 'accurately assess claims made in the above-captioned proceeding' regarding 'market and traffic impacts and effect on the public interest of the proposed transaction' and to 'prepare analyses and develop evidence and Verified Statements in support of any comments or other participation by CSXT in the Proceedings.' The STB approved the request on August 12, 2025 (letter dated August 8), finding CSX's justification 'complete and sufficiently detailed.' CSX's counsel (Crowell & Moring, Gentry Locke, NERA, and others) and designated consultants must execute confidentiality agreements before data delivery. Data is restricted to the named individuals and may only be disclosed to other parties if those parties have separately signed waybill agreements. CCWS data in CSX's filings must remain confidential unless aggregated to at least three shippers. Significantly, CSX noted 'the scope of its request is identical to that requested by and granted to the Applicants,' establishing parity in competitive discovery access. The approval becomes effective upon receipt of signed agreements from 20 named individuals (counsel, economic consultants from NERA and Monaco); expiration is August 31, 2026. Prior payment of $1,580 processing fee required.
key_arguments: CSX requires CCWS data as 'the only single source of the data permitting a complete analysis' of competitive impacts and must use it to 'verify propositions in and analyses supporting the Applicants' Application, participants' comments, any responsive applications' and to 'ensure full review of the potential competitive impacts of the transaction(s) proposed by Applicants.'

CSX's requested data scope is 'identical to that requested by and granted to the Applicants,' establishing that competing railroad intervenors should have parity access to the same traffic intelligence as the merger parties.

Waybill data is essential for outside counsel and consultants to develop 'analyses and develop evidence and Verified Statements' to support CSX's participation and to assess the validity of applicants' methodologies and assumptions.
key_excerpts: The purpose of this request is to allow CSXT's counsel and consultants to accurately assess claims made in the above-captioned proceeding and any sub-dockets and related proceedings (collectively, the 'Proceedings'), including (without limitation) with respect to the market and traffic impacts and effect on the public interest of the proposed transaction, and to prepare analyses and develop evidence and Verified Statements in support of any comments or other participation by CSXT in the Proceedings.
CSXT notes that the scope of its request is identical to that requested by and granted to the Applicants in the above-referenced proceeding.

As the only single source of the data permitting a complete analysis of these issues, the STB Waybill Sample is essential for CSXT, through its outside counsel and consultants, to verify propositions in and analyses supporting the Applicants' Application, participants' comments, any responsive applications, and the validity and methodology of and assumptions used in such analyses.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Grant CSX Transportation access to unmasked 2019-2024 Carload Waybill Sample data (all records, all fields, confidential unmasked revenues) for all traffic, subject to confidentiality agreement and Board restrictions on use and disclosure.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This approval implements 49 C.F.R. § 1244.9(b)(4), which permits conditional access to confidential waybill data for parties participating in STB proceedings. The decision establishes procedural framework for competitive discovery: (1) parity principle—CSX's access scope equals the applicants' access, supporting adversarial balance in merger review; (2) protective order structure—CCWS data remains confidential unless aggregated to three-shipper rule, enabling competitors to develop analyses without compromising shipper/carrier confidentiality; (3) substantive impact—CSX now possesses the granular traffic data required to develop detailed competitive impact testimony, directly affecting the evidentiary record the STB will review on competitive effects. The August 31, 2026 expiration and annual renewal requirement establish timeline constraints for CSX's analysis delivery. Notably, the Board notes CCWS limitations (sample-based, only includes carriers with 4,500+ annual terminating carloads), which may limit conclusions about small railroad impacts.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Signed confidentiality agreements from all 20 listed individuals must be returned to STB before data delivery; $1,580 payment also required. No specific STB deadline imposed, but CSX's participation timeline in the merger proceeding will drive urgency.

docket_entries.title: Rail Cents Enterprises: Merger Will Fail to Grow Revenue; Consolidation Opposite of What Rail Industry Needs
docket_entries.entry_summary: Rail Cents Enterprises argues that Union Pacific's and Norfolk Southern's proposed merger will fail to achieve stated benefits and instead represents misdirected strategy. The filer's core thesis: both railroads have fundamentally failed to grow revenue over 15 years (NS revenue declined 12% in constant 2024 dollars from $13.7B in 2010 to $12.1B in 2024; UP similarly stagnant), yet have distributed most free cash flow to shareholders rather than investing in revenue growth. The merger, Rail Cents argues, is not a solution to this problem but an acknowledgment of failure—and consolidation would worsen outcomes. Rail Cents contends that: (1) UP and NS lack the organizational structure and commercial resources needed to pursue the high-volume opportunity in short-to-medium-haul single-carload traffic (which comprises most freight tonnage), instead relying passively on bulk coal and intermodal traffic requiring minimal commercial effort; (2) both railroads have dramatically cut commercial/marketing expenses as a percentage of total expenses (declining from ~1.5% in the 1990s to ~0.3% by 2024), demonstrating organizational inability or unwillingness to compete for new traffic; (3) the merger would create an even larger, more monolithic entity incapable of developing local decision-makers and entrepreneurial commercial structures needed to capture growth—the opposite of the smaller geographic profit centers that short lines use successfully; (4) shippers will lose confidence in competition as a hedge against poor service and pricing; (5) the industry as a whole needs 'more degrees of freedom, not more monolithic structure.' Rail Cents explicitly states: 'The proposed combination would appear to be either empire-building or a ploy to deflect attention from the failure to grow revenue and profit.' No conditions would satisfy this opposition.
key_arguments: Norfolk Southern's operating revenues declined 12% in inflation-adjusted terms from $13.7 billion in 2010 to $12.1 billion in 2024, while overall U.S. freight transportation expenditures increased 72% during the same period, with rail's share dropping to 6%. The merger cannot solve a fundamental inability to capture market growth.

Union Pacific exhibits identical revenue stagnation: operating revenues in constant 2024 dollars were essentially flat from $24.4B (2010) to $24.3B (2024), despite claimed capital investments. This merger combines two companies with proven track records of operational failure.

Both UP and NS have dramatically reduced commercial, marketing, and sales expenses as a percentage of total expenses—from approximately 1.5% in the 1990s to 0.3% by 2024—demonstrating systematic disinvestment in revenue-generating commercial activity and proving organizational inability to pursue growth.

UP and NS lack the organizational structure and commercial resources to identify, solicit, and facilitate new single-carload traffic proactively; to price differentially; or to identify capital investments that grow revenue. The companies are 'grown accustomed to focusing on handling existing traffic efficiently and to relying for growth on traffic that does not require much internal commercial effort.'

90% of freight tonnage moves less than 750 miles, but Class I railroads focus on intermodal traffic (which requires 750+ miles to be competitive) and coal (in evolutionary decline). Short lines capture single-carload revenue through 'local decision-making by cross-functional managers,' but Class I policies hamper short lines by limiting customized revenue factors, car interchange frequency, and multi-carrier interchanges.

Further consolidation will create a larger monolithic entity incapable of developing the local decision-making and entrepreneurial organizational structure required to grow revenue. Smaller, decentralized geographic profit centers (not larger segregated departmental budgets focused on cost-cutting) are needed to attract new traffic.

Both railroads distribute most free cash flow to shareholders instead of investing in revenue growth. NS has reduced discretionary capital expenditures (excluding replacement capex) from $479M (2024 constant dollars) in 2019 to $172M in 2015; UP similarly reduced discretionary capex.
The merger is 'empire-building or a ploy to deflect attention from the failure to grow revenue and profit.' It is 'the opposite of what is required in order to grow rail revenue and profit.'

Shippers need 'assurances of competition—the best hedge against poor service and elevated pricing—before they invest in new sidetracks.' Other railroads benefit from multiple run-through and joint-rate partners and 'may not desire to be stampeded into their own mega-mergers.' General economic stimulus requires 'more degrees of freedom, not more monolithic structure.'
key_excerpts: 'NS's basic problem has been an inability to grow revenue. Revenue is the pertinent metric—not tons handled, not ton-miles moved—because of what revenue means for stockholder distributions, employment, and political clout.' (p. 2)

'NS's operating revenues for the last fifteen years, in constant 2024 dollars, declined twelve percent from $13.7 billion in 2010 to $12.1 billion in 2024. During the same fifteen-year time span the overall level of expenditures on freight in the U.S. increased seventy-two percent. Rail's share of expenditures dropped to six percent.' (p. 2)
'The same observations also apply to Union Pacific regarding an inability to grow revenue and a policy of paying out most of, sometimes more than, free cash flow to shareholders.' (p. 3)

'UP and NS do not have the commercial resources: to identify, solicit, and facilitate new single-carload traffic proactively, to influence non-commercial employees in order to customize single-carload service, to price either single-carload or intermodal traffic differentially, or to identify and champion capital investments that grow revenue and profit.' (p. 5)

'Most stockholders prefer growth engines to cash cows. Most shippers want the assurances of competition—the best hedge against poor service and elevated pricing—before they invest in new sidetracks.' (p. 6)
'The proposed combination would appear to be either empire-building or a ploy to deflect attention from the failure to grow revenue and profit.' (p. 6)
'Further consolidation of the American rail network is the opposite of what is required in order to grow rail revenue and profit.' (p. 6)

'The organizational structure needed to attract appreciable new traffic to an inherently safe and environmentally friendly mode of transportation would arguably have smaller geographic profit centers that can identify and support single-carload traffic, not bigger segregated departmental budgets that can focus only on cutting costs.' (p. 6)
docket_entries.relief_requested: Deny the proposed merger. Rail Cents argues the merger should be rejected outright because it represents 'empire-building or a ploy to deflect attention from the failure to grow revenue and profit' and that 'further consolidation of the American rail network is the opposite of what is required in order to grow rail revenue and profit.'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing raises a novel and substantive economic argument that challenges the merger's underlying premise: that consolidation will improve financial performance. Rather than disputing competitive harm per se, Rail Cents argues the merger is economically irrational because it addresses the wrong problem. The filing presents detailed financial analysis (15 years of constant-dollar revenue trends, discretionary vs. maintenance capex, commercial expense trends) that directly contradicts the applicants' claim that the combined company 'will produce rail volume growth.' If credited, this analysis could influence STB review of whether the applicants have adequately substantiated their growth and synergy claims—a key element of merger justification under 49 U.S.C. § 11324. The argument about organizational structure also potentially reframes the competitive question: not whether UP-NS will raise rates (traditional merger concern) but whether consolidation reduces the industry's capacity to innovate and capture new traffic, thereby harming consumers and economic efficiency by keeping rail market share flat. This could expand the factual record required to assess merger benefits.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Standard comment period responsive filing; no explicit deadline stated in filing itself

docket_entries.title: STB Grant of Waybill Data Access to Canadian National Railway for FD 36873 Analysis
docket_entries.entry_summary: The STB Office of Economics granted Canadian National Railway Company's request for access to confidential Carload Waybill Sample (CCWS) data covering 2019-2024, including unmasked revenues for all traffic. CN's outside counsel (Freshfields LLP) and economic consultants (Compass Lexecon) requested the data to 'prepare the various analyses and evidence needed to assess the effects of the proposed transaction,' with CN stating the CCWS is 'the only single source of the data permitting a complete analysis of these issues.' The grant is conditioned on strict confidentiality protocols: data use limited solely to the FD 36873 proceeding; disclosure only to other parties' counsel who have signed CCWS agreements; confidential filing of unaggregated data; destruction or return upon August 31, 2026 expiration unless extension obtained. The agreement covers 16 named individuals from Freshfields LLP (10), Compass Lexecon (5), and Fletcher & Sippel LLC (1). This approval indicates CN is preparing detailed competitive and market impact testimony and signals potential for aggressive, data-driven opposition based on actual carload revenue flows, pricing patterns, and traffic routing data across the six-year window.
key_arguments: CN stated unmasked CCWS data is 'the only single source of the data permitting a complete analysis' of the UP-NS combination's effects on competition and market dynamics
The specific request for confidential unmasked revenues across all traffic for 2019-2024 indicates CN intends to model pricing, volume, and competitive diversion impacts from the merger

CN engaged a sophisticated economic consulting team (Compass Lexecon experts Mary T. Coleman, Theresa Sullivan, Michael W. Matelis, Holly Chin, Arushi Ghosh) to conduct analyses, suggesting preparation for detailed economic testimony
key_excerpts: The purpose of this request is to allow CN's counsel and consultants to prepare the various analyses and evidence needed to assess the effects of the proposed transaction, with the STB's Waybill Sample being the only single source of the data permitting a complete analysis of these issues.

The CCWS is the only single source of the requested data. Your request further explained that these particular data are required to prepare the various analyses and evidence needed to assess the effects of the proposed transaction.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Grant CN access to unmasked Carload Waybill Sample (CCWS) data for 2019-2024 (2024 when available) including all records, all fields, and confidential unmasked revenues for all traffic, for purposes of preparing market and traffic impact analyses in FD 36873.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This is a discovery/evidentiary ruling under 49 C.F.R. § 1244.9(b)(4) that formally authorizes CN to access commercially sensitive railroad and shipper data in the merger record. The grant expands the evidentiary base available to oppose/challenge the merger by enabling a major competitor to conduct granular competitive impact analyses using actual STB waybill transaction data rather than relying on general economic principles. The conditioning on confidential filing procedures (aggregation thresholds, sealed submissions) reflects STB's balancing of competitive transparency against shipper/railroad data protection. The decision also signals that CN's showing of necessity—that CCWS is the 'only' data source for complete analysis—satisfied the regulatory standard for unmasked revenue access.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Agreement expiration date (data access terminates unless 30-day extension notice filed by August 31, 2026); initial processing and signature return by all 16 individuals required before data transmission via FTP

docket_entries.title: STB Directive Requiring Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern to Submit Complete 100% Traffic Tapes (2019-2024)
docket_entries.entry_summary: The STB Board issued Decision No. 2 on August 25, 2025, exercising its authority under 49 U.S.C. § 1321(b)(3) to require Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern to submit complete 100% traffic tapes for the six-year period January 1, 2019 through December 31, 2024 by September 8, 2025. The Board stated that 'having agency access to Applicants' 100% traffic tapes is likewise necessary to carry out its review of the proposed transaction and that Board access to this information prior to Applicants' filing of the anticipated application will facilitate that review.' The tapes must include: origin, destination, and interchange information; contract and tariff information; revenue information on a country-specific basis; shipper/consignee names; total freight revenues and surcharges; detailed commodity data (7-digit STCC codes, actual and tare weights); and comprehensive route data including physical origins/destinations, junction frequency, railroad-specific route information, and mileage (both loaded and empty). The Board requires concurrent submission of detailed metadata (data dictionary) specifying character encoding, delimiter characters, field definitions, data types, and compression formats for each traffic tape file. The Board emphasized balancing 'early access to this critical traffic data' to 'aid interested parties' while ensuring disclosure 'should not impede the prospective applicants in the preparation of their application.' All information will be treated as highly confidential given its sensitive commercial nature. Board staff will provide specific submission instructions given the expected large file sizes.
key_arguments: Board access to 100% traffic tapes prior to application filing is necessary to carry out its statutory review of the proposed transaction under 49 U.S.C. § 1321(b)(3)

Early disclosure of comprehensive traffic data (including origin, destination, revenue, commodity, and routing information) will facilitate the Board's competitive analysis while not impeding applicants' preparation
Six years of detailed data (2019-2024) is required to establish baseline competitive conditions and trends before the merger
Detailed metadata (data dictionaries specifying encoding, field definitions, data types, compression) is essential to enable proper interpretation and analysis of traffic tape files
key_excerpts: The Board finds that having agency access to Applicants' 100% traffic tapes is likewise necessary to carry out its review of the proposed transaction and that Board access to this information prior to Applicants' filing of the anticipated application will facilitate that review.
UP and NS are directed to submit to the Board their 100% traffic tapes kept in the normal course of business for the period January 1, 2019, through December 31, 2024, by September 8, 2025.

Specifically, the Board is seeking 100% traffic tapes kept in the normal course of business. This includes origin, destination, and interchange information; contract and tariff information; and revenue information on a country-specific basis.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Applicants (UP and NS) directed to submit their complete 100% traffic tapes for January 1, 2019 through December 31, 2024 by September 8, 2025, together with detailed metadata (data dictionary) to enable Board analysis of the proposed transaction.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This order establishes the evidentiary foundation for the entire merger review. The requirement for six years of complete traffic data (versus the customary single 'impact analysis year') signals the Board intends intensive competitive analysis. The requirement for detailed metadata ensures the data will be properly interpretable and usable in discovery and at hearing. The pre-application filing requirement for traffic tapes (rather than post-application) accelerates Board access and likely enables earlier identification of competitive issues, potentially affecting the procedural schedule. The detailed appendix specifying required data elements (shipper names, contract/tariff authority, surcharge details, commodity codes, route-specific mileage) indicates the Board will analyze not just volume but pricing, customer concentration, and competitive alternatives on specific routes—highly relevant to assessing whether the merger reduces viable competitive options for shippers.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern must submit their complete 100% traffic tapes for January 1, 2019 through December 31, 2024, and detailed metadata (data dictionary) by September 8, 2025

docket_entries.title: STB Approval of Waybill Data Access for Marc Meketon (Oliver Wyman) - UP/NS Merger Analysis
