The approval, dated August 13, 2025, was conditioned on Meketon's execution of a standard confidentiality agreement (WB25-42) and payment of $69 processing fee. Union Pacific counsel at Covington & Burling submitted the request on behalf of UP. This filing evidences that the merger parties are actively conducting detailed competitive and operational analysis using confidential railroad traffic data during the discovery phase.
key_excerpts: I have approved the addition of the following individual to the waybill access letter in WB25-42. Marc Meketon – Oliver Wyman

I agree to comply fully with these conditions and the provisions of this confidentiality agreement. No later than thirty days before the agreement expires, I will request an extension of this agreement, if necessary. If no extension is requested, I will return or destroy all CCWS data and certify that I have done so.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Approval of waybill data access authorization for additional analyst (Marc Meketon, Oliver Wyman) to review restricted railroad traffic data in connection with merger proceeding.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Administrative approval evidencing active discovery phase in merger proceeding. Use of Oliver Wyman consulting indicates sophisticated economic analysis being prepared for hearing or negotiation. Waybill data access is typically critical for analyzing competitive impacts on specific routes/commodities. No new legal standard or burden created, but indicates breadth of analysis planned.

docket_entries.title: CPKC Notice of Intent to Comment on Procedural Schedule
docket_entries.entry_summary: CPKC filed a notice letter on August 26, 2025, advising the STB and applicants of its intent to submit comments on the procedural schedule once the Board publishes notice in the Federal Register. The filing acknowledges the Board's Decision No. 2 (issued August 25, 2025), which indicated the Board would address the applicants' petition to establish a procedural schedule in a subsequent decision. CPKC commits to comply with whatever deadline the Board establishes for schedule comments. This is a protective filing to preserve intervention rights and signal participation; it does not express any position on the merger's merits.
key_excerpts: CPKC intends to submit comments on the procedural schedule proposed by Applicants in their Petition to Establish Procedural Schedule (UP-2/NS-2) once the Board issues notice of the proposal in the Federal Register.

CPKC anticipates that the referenced 'subsequent decision' will establish a date for interested parties to comment on Applicants' proposed schedule (and any modifications the Board may propose). CPKC will comply with that deadline.
docket_entries.relief_requested: CPKC advises the Board that it intends to submit comments on the procedural schedule proposed by Applicants once the Board issues notice in the Federal Register, and commits to comply with any deadline the Board establishes for such comments.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing establishes CPKC's participation in the proceeding and preserves its right to intervene. It signals that CPKC (a major competitor and Class I railroad with extensive U.S. network operations) intends to engage on procedural matters and potentially on the merits. As a competitor with operations overlapping UP and NS territory, CPKC's eventual substantive comments may be highly material to competition analysis. This notice preserves that possibility without committing to a specific position.
docket_entries.deadline_description: No deadline in this filing; CPKC commits to respond to future Board notice establishing schedule comment deadline

docket_entries.title: STB Decision No. 3: Notice of Receipt of Prefiling Notification, Assignment of ALJ Soulikias for Discovery, and Requirement for Additional Information by September 29, 2025
docket_entries.entry_summary: The STB issued Decision No. 3 formalizing receipt of the prefiling notification from Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern regarding UP's proposed acquisition of control of Norfolk Southern. The Board classified this as a 'major transaction' under 49 CFR 1180.2(a) because it involves control of two Class I railroads. The Board assigned Administrative Law Judge Jenifer Soulikias to handle all discovery matters and resolve discovery disputes. Most significantly, the Board required Applicants to submit extensive additional information by September 29, 2025—before the formal application filing anticipated by January 29, 2026—including: (1) Operating timetables, station lists, and track charts for both entire UP and NS systems in machine-readable format; (2) Geospatial Information System (GIS) maps for both systems with detailed specifications (track centerline points, operating divisions, subdivisions, mileposts, crossings, switches, permanent speed restrictions, joint facilities layers); (3) A comprehensive list of all joint facilities and joint use arrangements, including trackage rights, haulage agreements, yards, terminals, and common ownership agreements, with specification of facility type and involved carriers; (4) A list of all interchange commitments—agreements limiting or potentially limiting interchange with third-party connecting carriers. The Board emphasized that these documents must be in machine-readable format to the extent available, and provided a detailed 19-point Appendix establishing technical procedures for all evidentiary submissions, including requirements for data dictionaries, spreadsheet formatting, raw data submission, workpaper indexing, transparent citations, and use of open-source formats (Python, SQL preferred). This procedural framework signals the Board's intent to conduct a highly technical, data-intensive review with emphasis on transparency and reproducibility.
key_arguments: This is a 'major transaction' under 49 CFR 1180.2(a) because it involves control of two Class I railroads (UP and NS), triggering full merger review procedures

Applicants must provide complete operating infrastructure data (timetables, station lists, track charts, GIS maps) in machine-readable format for both entire railroad systems to enable Board analysis of operational integration and competitive impacts

Applicants must disclose all joint facilities, joint use arrangements, and interchange commitments between UP and NS, as well as arrangements with third parties, to identify potential operational dependencies and competitive constraints

Board will enforce strict evidentiary standards requiring detailed workpapers, data dictionaries, transparent calculations with formulas, consistent naming conventions, and open-source software to ensure reproducibility and prevent analytical disputes
key_excerpts: The Board finds that this is a major transaction under 49 CFR 1180.2(a), as it is a control transaction involving two or more Class I railroads. UPC presently controls UP, a Class I railroad, and proposes to acquire common control of NS, also a Class I railroad.

Operating timetables (including special instructions and/or operating rule books), station lists or station books, and track charts or 'track profiles' (including schematics that provide the number, length, and ownership status (i.e., whether railroad-owned or privately-owned)) of the entire UP system and the entire NS system... These documents must be in machine-readable format to the extent available.

GIS maps for the entire UP system and the entire NS system... The maps must include, at minimum: Track centerline points; Operating division; Operating subdivision; Integer mileposts; Crossings, including grade crossings; Switches (turnout leg, switch orientation); Permanent speed restrictions; And the joint facilities layer for all geolocated joint facilities.

A list of interchange commitments—agreements that limit or may limit interchange with a third-party connecting carrier, whether by outright prohibition, per-car penalty, adjustment in financial terms, positive economic inducement, or other means—involving UP or NS.
As a best practice, all empirical work should be submitted in enough detail so that Board staff can identify the methodology used to conduct the analysis and can review the results of the analysis.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Board hereby: (1) Ratifies appointment of Administrative Law Judge Jenifer Soulikias to handle all discovery matters and initial resolution of discovery disputes; (2) Requires Applicants to submit specified additional information by September 29, 2025; (3) Waives first-class mail service requirement; (4) Establishes detailed technical procedures for evidentiary submissions.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This decision establishes several critical procedural and evidentiary frameworks: (1) MAJOR TRANSACTION CLASSIFICATION triggers the full statutory review under 49 U.S.C. § 11324 and 49 CFR Part 1180, including public comment and hearing procedures; (2) PRE-FILING INFORMATION REQUIREMENTS under 49 CFR 1180.4(c)(2)(v) and 49 U.S.C. 1321(b) significantly expand the disclosure burden before the formal application is even filed, giving the Board and potential intervenors advance notice of operational and competitive facts; (3) ALJ ASSIGNMENT for discovery disputes shifts discovery authority from Board staff to an independent Administrative Law Judge, potentially making discovery disputes more formalized and appellable; (4) DETAILED TECHNICAL PROCEDURES (Appendix 1-19) impose unprecedented evidentiary standards that will govern all party submissions, including mandatory machine-readable formats, data dictionaries, workpaper indexing, transparent formulas, and open-source software preference—this creates a high bar for analytical work and will likely drive multiple rounds of discovery disputes over methodology and data integrity; (5) MACHINE-READABLE DATA MANDATE shifts burden away from narrative-heavy filings toward raw data submission, enabling independent Board analysis and comparative evaluation of competing parties' analyses. This framework signals Board's intent to conduct deep technical review with emphasis on competitive impact analysis rather than narrative legal arguments.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Applicants must submit all required additional information (timetables, station lists, track charts, GIS maps, joint facilities lists, and interchange commitments) by September 29, 2025

docket_entries.title: Union Pacific/Norfolk Southern Motion to Waive Fieldston Ban on Ex Parte Communications
docket_entries.entry_summary: Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern request waiver of the 1997 Fieldston decision that prohibits ex parte communications in railroad merger proceedings under § 11324. Applicants argue that Fieldston's justifications are outdated: (1) burden on agency resources has been remedied by relaxed rules in rulemaking contexts requiring written summaries posted to public docket; (2) ex parte communications would actually aid (not hinder) timely decision-making and allow "informal consultation to identify areas of concern at an early stage"; (3) transparency safeguards—public disclosure of ex parte substance and party response rights—now exist and are deployed by other agencies; and (4) Congress expressly authorized such communications in the ICC Termination Act of 1995 specifically to allow "procedural flexibility" lacking in former ICC process. Applicants propose ex parte period from Motion grant through Day 150 of procedural schedule, limited to parties of record, with mandatory written disclosure. Applicants frame this as enabling more "efficient and thorough decision-making" consistent with Congressional intent to allow "informal consultation." No opposition raised in filing; motion presents pure procedural request to expand applicants' ability to engage Board and staff substantively before formal hearing.
key_arguments: Congress provided express authorization in 49 U.S.C. § 11324(f)(2) and (f)(4) for ex parte communications in consolidation proceedings involving Class I carriers, yet STB imposed blanket Fieldston ban contradicting Congressional intent.

Fieldston's first concern—agency burden of reducing oral communications to writing—was remedied over seven years ago when the Board relaxed ex parte rules in informal rulemakings and required parties to submit written memoranda summarizing communications, which are posted to public docket, minimizing agency resources.

Fieldston's second concern—impeding timely decisions via strict timetable—is unfounded because "the Board has unnecessarily tied its own hands by prohibiting a congressionally authorized tool that actually could further the agency's ability to reach an efficient and timely decision."

Fieldston's third concern—public uncertainty whether record includes all facts and arguments—is addressed by existing safeguards: mandatory public disclosure of all ex parte communications and party opportunity to respond, consistent with FERC and other agencies' approaches.

Fieldston's fourth concern—complicating judicial review—cited no legal or factual support and would equally affect informal rulemaking context where Board already permits ex parte communications; other agencies conclude public disclosure is "consistent with creation of agency decision-making record capable of judicial review."

Congress enacted the express authorization for ex parte communications "in response to complaints that the former ICC process did not allow sufficient procedural flexibility to allow informal consultation to identify areas of concern at an early stage of the approval process."

Ex parte communications will facilitate more efficient and thorough Board decision-making by enabling early identification of areas of concern and allowing informal consultation consistent with Congressional direction in § 11324(f)(4).
key_excerpts: Congress provided 'express authorization' in the ICC Termination Act to allow the Board to entertain ex parte communications, subject to disclosure requirements. Yet despite this express authorization, the Board imposed a blanket prohibition on such communications in Fieldston.
The Board has unnecessarily tied its own hands by prohibiting a congressionally authorized tool that actually could further the agency's ability to reach an efficient and timely decision.

Congress enacted this 'express authorization' for communications between the decision makers and parties to the proceeding in response to 'complaints that the former ICC process did not allow sufficient procedural flexibility to allow informal consultation to identify areas of concern at an early stage of the approval process.'

Safeguards include the requirements that all ex parte communications be publicly disclosed and that parties have an opportunity to respond to the substance of those communications. These safeguards can be employed effectively in this proceeding to ensure a fair and orderly process.

A waiver of Fieldston will allow all interested parties to discuss substantive issues with Board Members and staff, and would allow such discussions after the Application and comments have been filed.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Grant waiver of the Fieldston ban on ex parte communications and permit Applicants and other interested parties to engage in ex parte meetings with Board Members and staff subject to written disclosure requirements per 49 C.F.R. § 1102.2(g).
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This motion directly challenges a 28-year-old STB decision (Fieldston, 1997) that has governed ex parte communication restrictions in railroad merger proceedings. Success would materially alter the procedural framework for this and potentially future consolidation proceedings by: (1) permitting ongoing substantive ex parte communications between applicants and Board decision-makers throughout the review period; (2) potentially creating asymmetric information advantages for applicants who can meet with Board staff repeatedly; (3) allowing applicants to identify and address Board concerns informally before formal written submissions; and (4) establishing precedent for future major consolidation filings. The motion relies on statutory construction (49 U.S.C. § 11324(f)(2) and (f)(4)) arguing Congressional authorization overrides STB regulatory choice, raising a fundamental question about agency discretion vs. statutory mandate. Success also invokes regulatory parity arguments (FERC, FCC permit ex parte communications) that may influence Board's willingness to modernize. Intervenors and competitors have strategic interest in whether this motion is granted, as it affects information flow and timing of substantive engagement with decision-makers.
docket_entries.deadline_description: No explicit deadline stated in motion. Board must rule on waiver request; typical motions practice in STB consolidation proceedings allows 10-14 days for oppositions/responses to procedural motions, though this timeline not specified in filing.

docket_entries.title: CPKC Request to Defer Response to Applicants' Ex Parte Communications Motion Pending Procedural Schedule Order
docket_entries.entry_summary: CPKC files a procedural request seeking Board confirmation that parties need not immediately respond to Applicants' Motion to Permit Stakeholder Communications, but instead may defer or coordinate responses with comments on the broader procedural schedule. CPKC states: 'Whatever path the Board chooses to take with respect to permissible ex parte communications...there is no doubt that the potential for ex parte communications should not be skewed in favor of Applicants and should not interfere with the orderly and fair development of an evidentiary record.' CPKC argues that addressing the ex parte motion piecemeal would 'create unnecessary burdens and interfere with the Board's timely adoption of appropriate procedures.' The filing signals CPKC's intent to participate substantively in this proceeding and its concern that applicants may gain procedural advantage through ex parte communications. CPKC indicates it will have views on how ex parte communications should be 'woven into an orderly and fair process' but that those views are interdependent with the overall procedural schedule. This is a baseline intervention filing establishing CPKC's status as an active, sophisticated competitor monitoring fairness in the proceeding.
key_arguments: Ex parte communication procedures should not be 'skewed in favor of Applicants' and must not 'interfere with the orderly and fair development of an evidentiary record'
Piecemeal responses to the ex parte motion would 'create unnecessary burdens and interfere with the Board's timely adoption of appropriate procedures'
Appropriate ex parte communication rules are interdependent with the Board's overall procedural schedule and should be addressed together
The Board should coordinate the timing of responses to avoid duplicative work and ensure comprehensive procedural clarity
key_excerpts: Whatever path the Board chooses to take with respect to permissible ex parte communications—e.g., whether to allow them at all, the timing of any such communications, allowable content, and other matters—there is no doubt that the potential for ex parte communications should not be skewed in favor of Applicants and should not interfere with the orderly and fair development of an evidentiary record supporting the Board's decision making in this important matter.
Addressing the issues piecemeal likely would create unnecessary burdens and interfere with the Board's timely adoption of appropriate procedures to govern this proceeding.
docket_entries.relief_requested: CPKC requests the Board confirm that parties may defer response to Applicants' Motion to Permit Stakeholder Communications (UP-4/NS-4) so responses can coincide with comments on the procedural schedule, rather than responding piecemeal. CPKC seeks clarification on the timing and structure of ex parte communications within the broader procedural framework.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing establishes that at least one major Class I competitor (CPKC) has intervened and is monitoring procedural fairness. CPKC's concern about ex parte communication skewing toward applicants may signal the Board's need to impose procedural restrictions on stakeholder communications to ensure competitive neutrality. The filing also indicates that procedural complexity—ex parte rules, discovery schedules, hearing structure—will be contested and likely to generate additional procedural motions. CPKC's sophisticated counsel (David L. Meyer, experienced STB practice) suggests litigation will be carefully structured and legally rigorous. The request to coordinate responses suggests CPKC may be coordinating with other competitors on procedural strategy.
docket_entries.deadline_description: This is a request for Board action on procedural scheduling; no response deadline imposed on other parties by this filing itself.

docket_entries.title: BLET Notice of Intent to Participate
docket_entries.entry_summary: BLET files notice of intent to participate in the UP-NS merger proceeding 'as its interests may require.' The filing provides no substantive position on the merger itself—no support, opposition, or conditions. It is purely procedural: requesting placement of two representatives (John Fink and attorney Joshua D. McInerney) on the service list and consenting to email service. This is a standard labor union filing at the threshold of major rail merger proceedings, indicating BLET will monitor the case and reserves the right to file substantive comments later. The phrasing 'as its interests may require' suggests BLET has not yet determined its position or conditions but recognizes the merger's potential impact on locomotive engineer employment, job security, seniority rights, and working conditions.
key_excerpts: The Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and Trainmen ... hereby provides its notice of its intent to participate in the above-captioned proceeding as its interests may require
request[s] that the following BLET Representative[s] be placed on the service list for this proceeding
docket_entries.relief_requested: Request to participate in the proceeding and place representatives on the service list. Service requests: John Fink (BLET Representative) and Joshua D. McInerney, Esq. (counsel). Consent to email service of all documents.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing establishes BLET's formal intervention status in the proceeding, preserving its right to file substantive comments, discovery requests, testimony, and briefs at later phases. Under 49 U.S.C. § 11324 and STB merger procedures, labor union intervention is permitted and common. The filing creates no new legal issues but signals that labor opposition or conditions are likely in subsequent filings. Mergers of this scale typically trigger labor objections regarding job preservation, seniority integration, and working conditions; BLET's participation is a baseline expectation and suggests substantive labor intervention should be anticipated.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)

docket_entries.title: Grand Trunk Corporation Substitution of Counsel – Freshfields Withdrawn Due to UP Financing Conflict
docket_entries.entry_summary: Grand Trunk Corporation (CN) substitutes counsel due to a conflict of interest discovered at Freshfields US LLP. Freshfields' financial institution clients, retained by Union Pacific for transaction financing, declined to waive the conflict, forcing withdrawal. CN has retained Simpson Thacher & Bartlett LLP as substitute lead counsel. The filing includes certification procedures for destruction of confidential Carload Waybill Sample data previously held by Freshfields personnel and requests Simpson Thacher's addition to the confidential waybill data access list. This is a routine procedural substitution but the underlying conflict highlights the extensive financial advisory involvement in the merger structure.
key_arguments: Freshfields US LLP withdrew due to conflict of interest: firm's financial institution clients retained by Union Pacific declined to waive the conflict, creating irreconcilable representation conflict
CN requires substitution of lead counsel as Freshfields' withdrawal prevents continued effective representation in the proceeding
key_excerpts: Freshfields US LLP has unexpectedly withdrawn from representing CN in the above-captioned matter due to a conflict of interest that the firm's clients, financial institutions retained by Applicant Union Pacific in connection with this proposed transaction, have declined to waive.

CN has since retained substitute lead counsel in this matter, a process that was complicated by conflicts given the numerous law firms that already represent various parties or related entities in the proposed transaction.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Substitution of counsel from Freshfields US LLP to Simpson Thacher & Bartlett LLP. Addition of Thomas J. Litwiler and Sara Razi to service list. Certification that confidential Carload Waybill Sample data held by Freshfields has been destroyed and access for Simpson Thacher to confidential waybill data.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Procedurally minor but substantively revealing. Demonstrates that multiple law firms represent both the applicant Union Pacific and various financial institutions advising on transaction financing, creating a dense web of potential conflicts. The waybill data access issues confirm CN's participation as a competitor requiring confidential data to assess competitive impacts. The certification of data destruction and re-access procedures under waybill agreement WB25-46 are standard protective measures for confidential discovery in merger proceedings.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Simpson Thacher to file notice of appearance separately; counsel substitution effective upon filing; certification of data destruction to follow to Office of Economics

docket_entries.title: CN (Grand Trunk Corporation) Substitution of Counsel - Simpson Thacher & Bartlett LLP
docket_entries.entry_summary: CN (Grand Trunk Corporation and its U.S. subsidiaries) substituted counsel from its prior representatives to Simpson Thacher & Bartlett LLP, effective September 5, 2025. Simpson Thacher is a specialized railroad/STB counsel firm, indicating CN is escalating its engagement in the merger proceeding. This is a routine administrative notice requesting placement of three attorneys on the service list (Sara Razi, Lindsey Bohl, Abram Ellis) and confirming CN's consent to electronic service. No substantive position on the merger is stated in this filing. The timing (September 5, 2025) falls in the discovery/substantive advocacy phase of the proceeding.
key_excerpts: Grand Trunk Corporation, on behalf of itself and its U.S. rail operating subsidiaries (Bessemer and Lake Erie Railroad Company, Cedar River Railroad Company, Chicago, Central & Pacific Railroad Company, Grand Trunk Western Railroad Company, Illinois Central Railroad Company, Iowa Northern Railway Company, The Pittsburgh & Conneaut Dock Company and Wisconsin Central Ltd.) (collectively 'CN') in the above-captioned action, hereby provides notice of the appearance of new counsel and requests that the following be placed on the service list for this proceeding.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Placement of new counsel (Sara Razi, Lindsey Bohl, Abram Ellis of Simpson Thacher & Bartlett LLP) on the service list for all documents in this proceeding. CN consents to email service.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Purely procedural. The substitution of counsel to Simpson Thacher & Bartlett LLP (major STB/railroad law specialist) suggests CN is preparing to actively contest or scrutinize specific aspects of the merger in upcoming discovery and hearing phases. The shift to specialized counsel is a signal CN intends substantive advocacy, not mere monitoring. No change to scope of review or evidentiary burden.

docket_entries.title: STB Approval of Waybill Data Access for Oliver Wyman Consultants (Union Pacific Request)
docket_entries.entry_summary: The STB Office of Economics approved Union Pacific's request to grant two Oliver Wyman consultants—Bhakti Vaidya and Sarojini Davis—access to confidential waybill data under Waybill Agreement WB25-42. Both individuals executed standard STB confidentiality agreements binding them to protect CCWS data and requiring return or destruction of materials upon agreement expiration. Union Pacific submitted the required $138 processing and mailing fee ($69 per signature) on September 5, 2025. This is a standard discovery-phase administrative action allowing merger applicants' economic consultants to analyze railroad operational and competitive data for merger impact assessment.
key_arguments: Waybill data access is necessary for Union Pacific to develop its economic case regarding competitive impacts and operational synergies
Oliver Wyman consultants are subject to binding confidentiality restrictions limiting use to authorized purposes and requiring data destruction upon agreement expiration
key_excerpts: I have approved the addition of the following individual to the waybill access letter in WB25-42. x Bhakti Vaidya – Oliver Wyman x Sarojini Davis – Oliver Wyman

I agree to comply fully with these conditions and the provisions of this confidentiality agreement. No later than thirty days before the agreement expires, I will request an extension of this agreement, if necessary. If no extension is requested, I will return or destroy all CCWS data and certify that I have done so.
docket_entries.relief_requested: None - Administrative approval of data access
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing does not change the scope of review or create new substantive issues. It is a routine administrative action confirming that Union Pacific's economic consultants have been granted the data access necessary to support merger analysis under 49 U.S.C. § 11307, which authorizes the STB to permit access to confidential carrier information when necessary for merger proceedings. The approval is consistent with standard discovery practice in major rail consolidation cases and imposes no conditions or limitations beyond standard confidentiality protections.
docket_entries.deadline_description: None - Administrative approval, no response required

docket_entries.title: Union Pacific Submits 100% Traffic Tapes (2019-2024) in Response to STB Discovery Order
docket_entries.entry_summary: Union Pacific complies with the STB's August 25, 2025 discovery order by submitting 100% traffic tapes covering January 1, 2019 through December 31, 2024, delivered via secure FTP (Kiteworks) due to file size constraints. The submission includes a data dictionary file as required by footnote 5 of the Board's decision. UP requests that these materials be treated as Highly Confidential per the Protective Order. This is a routine discovery compliance filing with no substantive positions on merger approval or conditions.
key_excerpts: Union Pacific writes in response to the Board's decision served August 25, 2025, in the referenced matter directing Union Pacific to make available its 100% traffic tapes for the period January 1, 2019, through December 31, 2024.
The traffic tapes should be treated as Highly Confidential, as that term is defined in the Protective Order served August 5, 2025.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Designation of submitted traffic tapes as Highly Confidential under the Protective Order served August 5, 2025
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Demonstrates compliance with STB discovery orders in merger proceedings. The traffic tape data represents core factual materials (6 years of systemwide transaction records) that will support competitive analysis, service impact assessments, and rate/efficiency projections. Confidentiality designation suggests UP is protecting commercially sensitive routing and customer-specific traffic patterns. No change to scope of review or evidentiary standards, but completion of this discovery component is essential for ALJ/Board analysis.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Compliance filing; no response deadline stated

docket_entries.title: Norfolk Southern Compliance Filing: Production of 100% Traffic Tapes (Jan 2019 - Dec 2024)
docket_entries.entry_summary: Norfolk Southern filed a compliance response to the Board's August 25, 2025 order directing production of 100% traffic tapes covering January 1, 2019 through December 31, 2024. NS submitted the materials via secure Box upload and included a data dictionary file per Board requirements. NS has designated the traffic tapes as 'Highly Confidential' under the Protective Order dated August 5, 2025. This filing indicates NS is cooperating with discovery obligations and the proceeding is in active discovery phase.
key_excerpts: Norfolk Southern Corporation and Norfolk Southern Railway Company (collectively, NS) write in response to the Board's decision served August 25, 2025, in the above-referenced matter directing NS to make available its 100% traffic tapes for the period January 1, 2019, through December 31, 2024.
The traffic tapes should be treated as Highly Confidential, as that term is defined in the Protective Order served August 5, 2025.
docket_entries.relief_requested: No affirmative relief requested. Filing is a compliance response to Board Order dated August 25, 2025 directing production of 100% traffic tapes.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Establishes that NS has timely complied with discovery obligations. Production of 100% traffic tapes is a core evidentiary foundation for competitive impact analysis in major rail merger review. The confidential designation protects proprietary business data while making it available for examination by authorized parties and the STB. No substantive legal or regulatory precedent is set by this compliance filing.
docket_entries.deadline_description: This is a response to a Board order; no further deadline created by this filing.

docket_entries.title: STB Grant of Waybill Data Access to CPKC for FD 36873 Analysis
docket_entries.entry_summary: The STB Office of Economics granted CPKC's August 26, 2025 request for access to confidential Carload Waybill Sample (CCWS) data for FD 36873 analysis. CPKC requested unmasked 1990-2023 data (including all records, fields, and revenues) plus 2024 when available. The STB found CPKC's justification 'complete and sufficiently detailed' and approved access to 21 outside counsel and consultants from the Law Office of David L. Meyer, The Brattle Group, and Cornerstone Research. CPKC explained the data 'is essential to analyzing and responding to, among other things, the market and traffic impact analyses that Applicants must prepare' and is needed to 'permit an analysis of the public interest impacts of prior major merger consolidations in which Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern, among others, have participated, particularly UP's acquisition of Southern Pacific in 1996 and NS's acquisition of much of Conrail in 1998.' Access is subject to Waybill Agreement WB25-53, a stringent confidentiality agreement expiring September 30, 2026. The agreement prohibits disclosure outside named individuals, requires confidential filing of disaggregated data, restricts use to the proceeding and judicial review only, and mandates destruction/return of data unless extended. Violation may trigger Board sanctions and future data access denial. This grant significantly arms CPKC with the quantitative historical data needed to construct competitive harm arguments based on post-merger consolidation effects.
key_arguments: Historical data from 1990-2023 is necessary to analyze competitive impacts of prior merger consolidations involving UP and NS (UP/Southern Pacific 1996, NS/Conrail 1998), establishing baseline for current merger analysis
Unmasked waybill data covering all records and fields is essential to match analytical access that Applicants have been granted, ensuring competitive parity in evidentiary development
Market and traffic impact analyses required by 49 C.F.R. §§ 1180.6(a)(2)(i) and 1180.7 cannot be properly analyzed or challenged without access to confidential CCWS revenue data
2019-present data access is necessary to align with Applicants' granted data access period, while historical data enables comparative analysis of consolidation effects
key_excerpts: The requested data are essential to analyzing and responding to, among other things, the market and traffic impact analyses that Applicants must prepare pursuant to 49 C.F.R. §§ 1180.6(a)(2)(i) and 1180.7.

Data for the period since 1990 is needed to permit an analysis of the public interest impacts of prior major merger consolidations in which Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern, among others, have participated, particularly UP's acquisition of Southern Pacific in 1996 and NS's acquisition of much of Conrail in 1998.
Based on the complete and sufficiently detailed explanations and justifications contained in your request, I will grant access to 1990 through 2024 CCWS data for use in the FD 36873 proceeding.
docket_entries.relief_requested: CPKC requested access to unmasked 1990-2023 Carload Waybill Sample (CCWS) data including all records, all fields, and confidential unmasked revenues for all traffic, plus 2024 data when available. STB GRANTED this request, authorizing 21 outside counsel and consultants (from Law Office of David L. Meyer, The Brattle Group, and Cornerstone Research) to access the data subject to confidentiality agreement WB25-53.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This order is procedurally significant because it: (1) grants a major competitor (CPKC) robust discovery access to 34 years of historical unmasked waybill revenue data, establishing CPKC's evidentiary foundation for competitive harm arguments; (2) confirms STB's willingness to grant deep historical data access when properly justified (not just 2019-forward data), enabling comparative analysis of prior consolidations' competitive effects; (3) imposes stringent confidentiality controls (WB25-53) that limit circulation but do not prevent incorporation into pleadings/evidence for the proceeding; (4) sets precedent for intervenor-level discovery parity with applicants in major merger cases; (5) validates CPKC's standing and analytical strategy to challenge the merger based on historical consolidation precedents. The grant materially enhances CPKC's ability to construct quantitative opposition arguments comparing UP and NS competitive positions pre- and post-prior acquisitions.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Waybill Agreement WB25-53 expires September 30, 2026. Unless CPKC seeks renewal at least 30 days prior (by August 31, 2026), all CCWS data must be destroyed or returned and certified as such.

The approval merely confirms that Union Pacific's consultant meets credentials and has executed the required confidentiality agreement. No party has standing to challenge this type of ministerial approval.

docket_entries.title: STB Decision No. 4: Extension of Reply Deadline for Ex Parte Communications Motion to September 22, 2025
docket_entries.entry_summary: The STB issued a procedural order extending the deadline for responses to Union Pacific's August 29 motion requesting a waiver of the ex parte communications ban established in Fieldston (1996). Union Pacific argued that the rationales underlying Fieldston are no longer valid and that ex parte communications would assist the Board's decision-making. Canadian Pacific Railway (CPKC), a competitor, requested an extension on September 2, arguing that its views on ex parte communications "will inevitably be somewhat interdependent with the structure of the Board's procedural schedule in this case" and that addressing the issues piecemeal would create unnecessary burdens. The Board declined CPKC's request to align the motion deadline with procedural schedule comments, but granted a modest extension from September 18 to September 22, 2025, to ensure adequate time for responses. The Board also signaled it will issue a separate decision this month on the procedural schedule, at which time interested parties may address how ex parte meetings should be incorporated. This procedural framework matters significantly: if ex parte communications are permitted, competitors and stakeholders will have direct access to Board members; if denied, all advocacy must proceed through formal written comments and hearings.
key_arguments: Union Pacific's core argument: The rationales underlying the 1996 Fieldston ex parte ban are no longer valid, and permitting ex parte communications would improve the Board's decision-making in this proceeding.

CPKC's strategic argument: Responses to the ex parte motion cannot be meaningfully developed in isolation from the procedural schedule; views on ex parte communications are 'interdependent with the structure of the Board's procedural schedule,' and piecemeal consideration would create unnecessary burdens and delay appropriate procedures.

STB's procedural resolution: The question of whether ex parte communications should be permitted can be considered separately from the procedural schedule structure; the Board will issue a separate procedural schedule decision allowing intervenors to address ex parte issues at that time.
key_excerpts: Applicants contend that the rationales underlying Fieldston are no longer valid and that ex parte communications would assist the Board's decision-making in this proceeding.

CPKC further argues that '[a]ddressing the issues piecemeal likely would create unnecessary burdens and interfere with the Board's timely adoption of appropriate procedures to govern this proceeding.'

However, to ensure that commenters have adequate time and because several days have passed since CPKC made its request, the Board will extend the period to reply to Applicants' motion to September 22, 2025.
docket_entries.relief_requested: The Board extended the deadline for responses to Applicants' August 29 motion on ex parte communications from September 18 to September 22, 2025, to allow adequate time for commenters and to align with the Board's separate issuance of a decision seeking comments on the procedural schedule.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This order establishes the procedural framework for communications in this major railroad merger proceeding. The decision on whether to permit ex parte communications will fundamentally affect how stakeholders interact with Board members: traditional merger review has strict ex parte prohibitions under Fieldston (1996), but Union Pacific's challenge—supported implicitly by the Board's willingness to consider it—may result in relaxed rules similar to those in other regulated industries. This has significant strategic implications: if ex parte meetings are permitted, competitors and major shippers gain direct Board access; if denied, advocacy is confined to formal comment periods and hearings. The STB's approach here—separating the ex parte question from procedural schedule details—keeps pressure on the substantive merits of the Fieldston waiver request while allowing the Board to develop comprehensive procedures.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Responses to Applicants' August 29 motion seeking waiver of ex parte communications ban are due by September 22, 2025. Parties may address ex parte issues in their responses without commenting on scheduling details, except to the extent scheduling impacts the substantive ex parte question.

docket_entries.title: Missouri Department of Transportation Notice of Intent to Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.entry_summary: Missouri Department of Transportation filed a notice of intent to participate in the UP/NS merger proceeding without submitting substantive comments or taking a position on the transaction. The filing designates three MoDOT officials (Chief Counsel Terri Parker, Assistant Chief Counsel Gary Holtmeyer, and Multimodal Operations Director Jerica Holtsclaw) as representatives. MoDOT states only that 'its interests may appear' in the proceeding, reserving the right to monitor the case and potentially submit substantive comments later. This is a watching brief with no relief requested, conditions proposed, or arguments advanced on the merger's competitive, operational, or public interest dimensions.
key_excerpts: The Missouri Department of Transportation ('MoDOT') respectfully submits its Notice of Intent to Participate in this proceeding before the Board, as its interests may appear.
docket_entries.relief_requested: None specified. MoDOT is filing notice of intent to participate without taking a position on the merger.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing preserves MoDOT's right to intervene and participate in discovery, hearing, and briefing phases without foreclosing future substantive involvement. As a state transportation authority, MoDOT's participation qualifies it as a government intervenor with potential standing to raise state-level public interest concerns (state transportation planning coordination, service adequacy, modal competition). The 'without comment' designation indicates MoDOT is still evaluating the merger's impact and may file substantive comments or discovery requests in later phases.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response deadline. This is a notice-only filing. MoDOT may file substantive comments or motions in subsequent proceeding phases.

docket_entries.title: BNSF Railway Notice of Appearance and Counsel Entry
docket_entries.entry_summary: BNSF Railway Company entered the proceeding by filing a Notice of Appearance and designating four attorneys from Kirkland & Ellis LLP to represent it on the service list. Future filings from BNSF will likely carry significant weight given its status as a major affected competitor.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response deadline; procedural filing

docket_entries.title: STB Approval of Waybill Data Access for Oliver Wyman Consultant (Union Pacific Request)
