docket_entries.title: Rail Customer Coalition Opposition to UP/NS Merger: Demand for Enhanced Competition Standard and Rejection of Consolidation
docket_entries.entry_summary: The Rail Customer Coalition, representing 30+ industry associations including major shippers in agriculture, chemicals, energy, and manufacturing, opposes the UP/NS merger as anticompetitive consolidation that would harm American manufacturing and supply chains. RCC argues: 'Past rail mergers have shown what happens when consolidation goes unchecked: service suffers, costs increase, and jobs disappear.' With four Class I railroads already controlling 90% of freight traffic, RCC contends a transcontinental merger would 'spark a new wave of consolidation, leaving captive shippers with even fewer Class I rail companies and competitive joint line options.' The coalition directly challenges the STB's competitive analysis framework, asserting: 'For any transaction that would so dramatically extend a single railroad's market power, we believe the threshold for enhanced competition should be broadly expanding access to competitive freight rail service, not solely claims that single line service could make certain lanes more competitive with other modes of transportation such as trucking.' This reframes the legal standard - RCC is arguing the Board should not accept rail-vs.-truck competition as satisfying the 'enhanced competition' requirement. RCC commits to 'actively engaging in the STB review process' but signals willingness to negotiate conditions if the Board moves toward approval, making this a conditional opposition with a fallback position emphasizing competitive safeguards rather than absolute denial.
key_arguments: Consolidation from 4 to 3 Class I railroads violates competitive principles: 'just four U.S. Class I railroads control over 90% of all freight traffic' and a transcontinental merger 'could spark a new wave of consolidation, leaving captive shippers with even fewer Class I rail companies and competitive joint line options'
Historical evidence demonstrates merger harms: 'Past rail mergers have shown what happens when consolidation goes unchecked: service suffers, costs increase, and jobs disappear'

The merger contradicts Administration economic policy: 'This is in direct contrast to the President's executive orders aimed at promoting American prosperity, curbing anti-competitive practices, and preventing monopolistic behavior'

The 'enhanced competition' standard must be elevated to require real rail-to-rail alternatives: 'For any transaction that would so dramatically extend a single railroad's market power...the threshold for enhanced competition should be broadly expanding access to competitive freight rail service, not solely claims that single line service could make certain lanes more competitive with other modes'

Rail competition is essential to inflation control and supply chain security: 'At a time when policy makers are working to strengthen American manufacturing, secure supply chains, and fight inflation, we must be careful not to allow further consolidation in a critical transportation sector to undo that progress'

Single-line service competing with trucking is insufficient competition: RCC rejects the notion that 'single line service could make certain lanes more competitive with other modes of transportation such as trucking' as meeting the enhanced competition threshold
key_excerpts: 'Past rail mergers have shown what happens when consolidation goes unchecked: service suffers, costs increase, and jobs disappear. Today, just four U.S. Class I railroads control over 90% of all freight traffic.'
'A transcontinental merger could spark a new wave of consolidation, leaving captive shippers with even fewer Class I rail companies and competitive joint line options to choose from.'

'For any transaction that would so dramatically extend a single railroad's market power, we believe the threshold for enhanced competition should be broadly expanding access to competitive freight rail service, not solely claims that single line service could make certain lanes more competitive with other modes of transportation such as trucking.'

'At a time when policy makers are working to strengthen American manufacturing, secure supply chains, and fight inflation, we must be careful not to allow further consolidation in a critical transportation sector to undo that progress.'
'Enhanced freight rail competition is essential for producing more goods in America, growing rail volumes and maintaining our leadership in global trade.'
docket_entries.relief_requested: The STB should rigorously evaluate potential merger impacts and take 'meaningful action to enhance and protect competition, service, and supply chain stability.' RCC argues that IF the Board considers approval, the threshold for 'enhanced competition' must be 'broadly expanding access to competitive freight rail service' - not merely claims that single-line service would make certain lanes more competitive with trucking. RCC demands that the Board reject the narrow competitive baseline.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: HIGH. RCC's opposition is legally significant on two dimensions: (1) COMPETITIVE STANDARD CHALLENGE - RCC directly contests how the STB should interpret '49 U.S.C. § 11324's requirement to enhance competition.' They argue the Board's framework for evaluating competitive effects is too narrow if it accepts rail-vs.-truck competition as sufficient. This frames a key interpretive issue: must the merger demonstrably increase rail-to-rail competition, or is it sufficient that single-line service improves modal competition? (2) CAPTIVE SHIPPER PROTECTION - RCC's coalition of captive freight customers (manufacturers, agricultural shippers, chemical companies with limited routing alternatives) may establish a record that the merger disproportionately harms the most vulnerable customer class. This could support argument that the merger fails the competitive 'public benefits' test under § 11324(b) if captive shippers face higher costs and fewer alternatives. The coalition's economic profile (7M+ jobs, $4.8T output) also establishes substantial national economic impact that elevates the proceeding's policy significance beyond individual railroad interests.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Initial comment period filing; RCC signals intent to participate throughout the proceeding, including discovery and hearing phases

docket_entries.title: Webb County Judge Supports UP-NS Merger for Port of Laredo Trade Benefits
docket_entries.filer_name: Webb County Judge Tano E. Tijerina
docket_entries.entry_summary: Webb County Judge Tano E. Tijerina supports the UP-NS merger based on Port of Laredo's critical role in U.S.-Mexico trade. He argues the merger will "strengthen the country's rail network to streamline the movement of goods across the country" and identifies four key benefits: (1) Improved Service Reliability through "more direct routes and greater operational flexibility" to prevent disruptions; (2) Reduced Transit Times by "eliminating certain interchanges" to speed delivery; (3) Increased Investment in "modern infrastructure, advanced technology and enhanced safety systems"; and (4) Expanded Reach to "open new markets for our state's products and strengthen supply chain resilience." Judge Tijerina emphasizes Port of Laredo's scale (241,727 rail cars in 2024, $339 billion in annual trade) and positions the merger as essential for American freight rail competitiveness globally. No conditions are requested; support is unconditional.
key_arguments: Merger will create more direct routes and greater operational flexibility, preventing service disruptions and improving schedule dependability for Port of Laredo traffic
Eliminating interchanges through unified UP-NS network will reduce transit times, allowing businesses to reach customers faster and more competitively
Combined entity will be better positioned to invest in modern infrastructure, advanced technology and enhanced safety systems critical to border trade
Broader geographic footprint will open new markets for Texas products and strengthen supply chain resilience for U.S.-Mexico trade corridor
American freight rail must remain globally competitive, and consolidation supports this objective
key_excerpts: Approximately 241,727 rail cars crossed through the Port of Laredo from Mexico last year and it is vital that we strengthen the country's rail network to streamline the movement of goods across the country.

The proposed merger offers a unique opportunity to strengthen this network and deliver tangible benefits for shippers, consumers and communities, including: Improved Service Reliability... Reduced Transit Times... Increased Investment... Expanded Reach.

This merger is about more than just railroads – it's about securing the future of our transportation network, supporting economic development and ensuring American freight rail remains globally competitive.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Give full and favorable consideration to the proposed merger, recognizing the benefits it will bring to Webb County and the national economy.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: As a government entity filing in support, this entry provides evidence of local/regional stakeholder support, which may be relevant to STB's broader public interest analysis under 49 U.S.C. § 11324(b). However, it does not introduce new legal issues, procedural challenges, or evidentiary burdens. It may be cited in applicant briefs as affirmative evidence of customer/community support, but does not change the scope of review or create competitive analysis requirements.
docket_entries.deadline_description: No deadline; filing is part of the public comment record

docket_entries.title: STB Office of Economics Approval - Waybill Data Access for Charles River Associates Economists (UP Request)
docket_entries.entry_summary: On September 17, 2025, the STB Office of Economics approved Union Pacific's request (filed September 16 by Covington & Burling) to authorize five Charles River Associates economists—Alex Arsenault, Colin Grimes, Pedro Degiovanni, Lang Xuan Luo, and Shuxin Wang—to access confidential waybill data (CCWS) in the FD 36873 docket. Each individual executed a Waybill Agreement WB25-42 agreeing to comply with STB confidentiality conditions and committing to return or destroy all data upon agreement expiration. UP paid the standard processing fee of $345 ($69 per authorized individual). This authorization signals that Union Pacific is preparing detailed economic analysis of competitive impacts and pricing effects for the merger proceeding, likely in response to anticipated shipper and competitor opposition arguments regarding service disruption, rate increases, and loss of competitive alternatives.
key_arguments: UP is deploying leading economic consulting firm (Charles River Associates) with multiple analysts to develop merger defense economic evidence
Access to confidential waybill data enables UP to construct detailed empirical arguments on traffic patterns, competitive flows, and pricing that are not publicly observable
key_excerpts: Union Pacific is requesting additional authorization for the following five individuals from Charles River Associates to access the Waybill Data in the Union Pacific – Norfolk Southern docket (FD 36873).
I have approved the addition of the following individual to the waybill access letter in WB25-42... Prior payment of processing and mailing cost of $345 ($69 per signature) is required and received.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Under 49 U.S.C. § 11307, the STB maintains the Carload Commodity Waybill Sample (CCWS), a confidential database of actual carload shipment data. Access is granted only to participants with legitimate need and under strict confidentiality agreements. This filing demonstrates that UP has cleared the procedural hurdle to access this restricted data, which is critical for developing empirical economic testimony on competitive effects, pricing, and modal competition. The waybill data will likely support UP's affirmative case on shipper benefits and refute allegations of rate increases or service degradation post-merger. This is standard in major merger proceedings but indicates the evidentiary phase is intensifying.
docket_entries.deadline_description: No deadline applicable—this is an STB approval order, not a request requiring party response.

docket_entries.title: CN Reply Supporting Full Waiver of Ex Parte Communications Prohibition
docket_entries.entry_summary: CN supports a complete waiver of the Fieldston prohibition on ex parte communications in this merger proceeding. CN argues that Congress expressly authorized ex parte communications in rail merger proceedings under 49 U.S.C. § 11324(f)(2), and the Board's 2018 procedures for informal rulemaking proceedings (EP 739) have already remedied the Fieldston Board's original concerns about burden on Board members and fairness. CN contends that 'ex parte meetings would enhance efficiency for the Board and parties in a proceeding that is likely to involve a complex and technical record' and 'would also contribute to more timely and informed decision-making.' CN emphasizes that modern safeguards—including placing responsibility on parties (not Board staff) to document oral communications and requiring public disclosure of meeting summaries and handouts—are 'sufficient to preserve fairness and transparency.' Notably, CN also signals disagreement with the Applicants' proposed procedural schedule, noting it will address scheduling issues in comments on the schedule.
key_arguments: Congress expressly authorized ex parte communications in STB rail merger proceedings under 49 U.S.C. § 11324(f)(2), making such communications lawful and appropriate.

The Board's concerns in Fieldston (1997) about burden on Board members and fairness have been remedied by 2018 procedures (EP 739) that place documentation responsibility on parties and require public disclosure of meeting summaries and handouts.
Ex parte meetings enhance efficiency and timely, informed decision-making in complex technical proceedings like this merger.
Modern safeguards under 49 C.F.R. § 1102.2(g)(4)—public disclosure of summaries and handouts—sufficiently preserve fairness and transparency in merger proceedings.
key_excerpts: Grand Trunk Corporation, on behalf of itself and its U.S. rail operating subsidiaries (collectively 'CN') supports a full waiver of the Fieldston prohibition as it relates to all parties in this proceeding in order to permit a fulsome discussion of the record.

Ex parte meetings would enhance efficiency for the Board and parties in a proceeding that is likely to involve a complex and technical record. Ex parte meetings would also contribute to more timely and informed decision-making.
Congress expressly authorized ex parte communications in STB proceedings relating to a transaction involving at least one rail carrier. 49 U.S.C. § 11324(f)(2).
docket_entries.relief_requested: Waive the Fieldston prohibition on ex parte communications to permit all parties to engage in full ex parte discussions with the STB Board and staff regarding the proposed merger.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing directly addresses the scope of procedural rules in the merger proceeding. A Board decision to grant the waiver would permit CN (and all intervenors) to conduct unlimited private meetings with Board members and staff, creating opportunities for direct lobbying without public record requirements beyond summary disclosure. This is significant for deal risk assessment because it removes a transparency constraint and signals the Board may be moving toward a more collaborative, settlement-oriented proceeding. Conversely, if the Board denies the waiver, it reinvigorates the 28-year-old Fieldston ban and limits CN's ability to lobby privately. The waiver decision will substantially affect how effectively competitors like CN can influence Board thinking without creating a public record of their arguments.
docket_entries.deadline_description: This is a reply to Applicants' motion; no response deadline applies to CN's filing itself.

docket_entries.title: YMCA of Northwest Louisiana Support Letter for UP-NS Merger
docket_entries.entry_summary: YMCA of Northwest Louisiana submits a brief support letter for the UP-NS merger, asserting that 'The merger promises faster, more dependable service, reduced congestion and expanded market reach for our businesses' and that it will deliver 'continued investment in rail infrastructure – enhancing safety, creating jobs.' The filer provides no evidence, data, or analysis to support these claims. The letter is a general expression of support based on anticipated economic benefits to the Shreveport/Caddo Parish region, without engagement with competitive, service, or regulatory issues central to merger review.
key_arguments: Merger will deliver faster and more dependable rail service to the local economy
Merger will reduce congestion and expand market reach for businesses
Merger will generate continued investment in rail infrastructure, enhance safety, and create jobs
key_excerpts: The proposed Union Pacific–Norfolk Southern merger offers an opportunity to strengthen these connections and deliver long-term benefits.

The merger promises faster, more dependable service, reduced congestion and expanded market reach for our businesses. It also means continued investment in rail infrastructure – enhancing safety, creating jobs and ensuring our community remains competitive in a growing economy.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Approve the proposed Union Pacific–Norfolk Southern merger
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Minimal. This is a form support letter with no legal or regulatory analysis. It does not address the statutory standards under 49 U.S.C. § 11324 (competitive impact, public interest, financial viability), nor does it raise any issues requiring Board response or condition imposition.

docket_entries.title: Illinois Department of Transportation Notice of Intent to Participate
docket_entries.entry_summary: Illinois Department of Transportation filed a bare notice of intent to participate in the UP-NS merger proceeding, signed by three officials: Jason Osborn (Intermodal Project Implementation Director), Mike Prater (Chief Counsel), and Tim McMahon (Federal Affairs Bureau Chief). The filing contains no substantive arguments, positions on the merger, conditions, or specific concerns. It is purely a procedural notice preserving IDOT's right to intervene and participate as the proceeding develops, likely in anticipation of potential impacts to Illinois' transportation infrastructure and intermodal connectivity.
key_excerpts: The Illinois Department of Transportation (IDOT) respectfully submits its Notice of Intent to Participate in this proceeding before the Board, as its interests may appear.
docket_entries.relief_requested: None specified. Filing is notice of intent to participate and monitor the proceeding.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: No legal or regulatory significance. This is a standard procedural notice of intervention. Under STB rules, the filing preserves IDOT's right to participate in discovery, submit comments, and potentially intervene formally at later proceeding phases.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response required. This is a notice of intent, not a motion or substantive filing requiring a responsive pleading.

docket_entries.title: Paso del Norte Community Foundation Support for UP-NS Merger
docket_entries.entry_summary: The Paso del Norte Community Foundation, based in El Paso, Texas, supports the merger as beneficial for regional and national economic growth. The foundation argues that Union Pacific 'has long been an essential transportation partner for our state, providing efficient, reliable and cost-effective service to businesses large and small.' It identifies four claimed benefits: (1) improved service reliability through 'more direct routes and greater operational flexibility,' (2) reduced transit times by 'eliminating certain interchanges,' (3) increased investment in 'modern infrastructure, advanced technology and enhanced safety systems,' and (4) expanded reach and supply chain resilience. The foundation emphasizes that freight rail is 'one of the most sustainable modes of transportation available, helping reduce highway congestion and emissions.' However, the filing contains no data on regional shipper needs, no analysis of service metrics, and no engagement with competitive concerns. It functions as a policy endorsement rather than an evidentiary submission.
key_arguments: The merger will improve service reliability by enabling 'more direct routes and greater operational flexibility' that 'will help prevent service disruptions and improve schedule dependability'
Eliminating interchanges will reduce transit times and help businesses 'reach customers faster and more competitively'
The combined railroad will increase investment in 'modern infrastructure, advanced technology and enhanced safety systems'
The merger will expand geographic reach and 'strengthen supply chain resilience' for regional products
Freight rail is 'one of the most sustainable modes of transportation available, helping reduce highway congestion and emissions'
key_excerpts: Freight rail is a cornerstone of our state's economy, safely moving the goods that power our industries, support our farmers and connect our communities to markets across the nation and the world.
Union Pacific has long been an essential transportation partner for our state, providing efficient, reliable and cost-effective service to businesses large and small.
The proposed merger offers a unique opportunity to strengthen this network and deliver tangible benefits for shippers, consumers and communities
docket_entries.relief_requested: The filer urges the Surface Transportation Board to 'give full and favorable consideration to this proposal, recognizing the benefits it will bring to our state and the national economy.'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Low. This filing adds no novel legal or regulatory argument and does not cite statutory standards or case law. It operates as general public comment endorsing applicants' narrative. It does not change the evidentiary burden or scope of review, nor does it identify specific service areas, routes, or competitive concerns that would require Board analysis.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Public comment filing; no response required unless Board requests clarification

docket_entries.title: Arkansas Travelers Youth Foundation support for UP-NS merger based on community investment and local economic benefits
docket_entries.entry_summary: The Arkansas Travelers Youth Foundation, led by Executive Director Lance Restum, supports the UP-NS merger primarily on community and heritage grounds rather than substantive transportation economics. The foundation emphasizes Union Pacific's historical role in North Little Rock: 'Union Pacific has played a direct and positive role in the North Little Rock and Central Arkansas community by providing grants that have greatly benefited hundreds of youth athletes and their families.' The filer frames the merger as an opportunity for regional economic development, stating: 'The merger is expected to result in faster, more reliable rail service, reduced congestion, and increased market access for local businesses. It also promises ongoing investment in rail infrastructure, which will enhance safety, generate new jobs, and help ensure America's competitiveness in an evolving global economy.' However, no specific evidence, data, or analysis supports these claims. The filing conflates Union Pacific's passenger heritage (Polar Express, Texas Eagle, 4014 Big Boy locomotive events) with the freight merger's competitive implications. As a grants recipient, the foundation has an apparent financial incentive to support Union Pacific. No conditions are proposed.
key_arguments: Union Pacific's community investment through grant funding to local youth programs demonstrates corporate commitment beyond transportation services
The merger will deliver 'faster, more reliable rail service, reduced congestion, and increased market access for local businesses'
Merger will enable 'ongoing investment in rail infrastructure, which will enhance safety, generate new jobs, and help ensure America's competitiveness'
Rail transportation is culturally significant to the region and the merger strengthens regional connectivity
key_excerpts: Union Pacific has played a direct and positive role in the North Little Rock and Central Arkansas community by providing grants that have greatly benefited hundreds of youth athletes and their families.

The merger is expected to result in faster, more reliable rail service, reduced congestion, and increased market access for local businesses. It also promises ongoing investment in rail infrastructure, which will enhance safety, generate new jobs, and help ensure America's competitiveness in an evolving global economy.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Approve the Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern merger
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Minimal. This is a form-letter style support statement with no legal or evidentiary contribution to the merger record. It does not raise new issues, propose evidence, or address statutory factors under 49 U.S.C. § 11324. The apparent financial relationship between the filer and Union Pacific (via grants) creates a credibility question but does not change the scope or burden of review.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Comment period filing; no response deadline

docket_entries.title: Mesilla Valley Economic Development Alliance - Support for UP/NS Merger
docket_entries.entry_summary: The Mesilla Valley Economic Development Alliance (representing New Mexico business interests) supports the merger on grounds that it strengthens national freight rail competitiveness and delivers local economic benefits. The filer argues that 'Freight rail is a cornerstone of our state's economy' and contends the merger will provide: (1) improved service reliability through 'more direct routes and greater operational flexibility'; (2) reduced transit times by 'eliminating certain interchanges' to speed goods movement; (3) increased investment in 'modern infrastructure, advanced technology, and enhanced safety systems'; and (4) expanded geographic reach 'to open new markets for our state's products and strengthen supply chain resilience.' The filer characterizes rail as 'one of the most sustainable modes of transportation available, helping reduce highway congestion and emissions.' No specific conditions or reservations are stated. This is a straightforward pro-merger advocacy filing without technical detail.
key_arguments: The merger will improve service reliability by enabling 'more direct routes and greater operational flexibility' that 'will help prevent service disruptions and improve schedule dependability'
Eliminating interchanges will reduce transit times, allowing 'our businesses reach customers faster and more competitively'
The combined transcontinental railroad 'will be better positioned to invest in modern infrastructure, advanced technology, and enhanced safety systems'
The broader geographic footprint will 'open new markets for our state's products and strengthen supply chain resilience'

Rail transportation is 'one of the most sustainable modes of transportation available, helping reduce highway congestion and emissions' and merger will help keep American freight rail 'globally competitive'
key_excerpts: Union Pacific has long been an essential transportation partner for our state, providing efficient, reliable, and cost-effective service to businesses large and small.
The proposed merger offers a unique opportunity to strengthen this network and deliver tangible benefits for shippers, consumers, and communities

This merger is about more than just railroads – it's about securing the future of our transportation network, supporting economic development and ensuring American freight rail remains globally competitive.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Respectfully urges the Surface Transportation Board to 'give full and favorable consideration to this proposal, recognizing the benefits it will bring to our state and the national economy.'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Minimal legal or regulatory significance. This filing is advocacy/support without raising novel legal arguments, procedural issues, or specific regulatory concerns under 49 U.S.C. § 11324. It does not challenge the Board's analytical framework, request specific conditions, or raise unaddressed competitive issues. The filing contributes to the record as a pro-merger voice from a regional economic constituency but does not change evidentiary burdens, scope of review, or substantive legal standards.
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response required; support statement for Board consideration

docket_entries.title: CPKC Reply to Applicants' Motion to Permit Stakeholder Communications in UP-NS Merger
docket_entries.filer_name: Canadian Pacific Railway Company (CPKC) and The Kansas City Southern Railway Company
docket_entries.entry_summary: CPKC opposes the Applicants' motion to allow stakeholder ex parte communications during the UP-NS merger proceeding, arguing that such communications violate fundamental due process principles and the longstanding precedent of Fieldston (1997). CPKC argues that merger proceedings are adjudicative in nature, not informal rulemakings, and therefore require a complete record with equal access for all parties. If the Board allows ex parte communications, CPKC proposes robust safeguards including equal access, full transcripts, and limited procedural windows.
key_arguments: Merger proceedings are adjudicative in fact requiring complete records, not informal rulemakings where ex parte communications are appropriate
Fieldston precedent (1997) correctly rejected ex parte communications in merger cases and remains valid despite being nearly 30 years old
Congress' authorization in Section 11324(f)(4) is discretionary, not mandatory, leaving the Board free to prohibit ex parte communications
The scale and significance of the UP-NS transaction (first Major Merger application under 2001 rules) counsel extreme caution with ex parte procedures
Equal access to Board and staff must be guaranteed to all parties, not just Applicants, to ensure fairness
Mere summaries of ex parte communications are inadequate; full transcripts are necessary for other parties to respond meaningfully
Statutory one-year timeline for evidentiary proceedings limits flexibility to accommodate ex parte communications without disruption
Applicants' AAR Petition contemplated ex parte communications only for routine, procedural matters, not major mergers
key_excerpts: Applicants are proposing—as a sharp break from longstanding Board and ICC practice in merger proceedings—an essentially unrestricted ability to meet privately (i.e., on an ex parte basis) with Board members and Board staff during key stages of this proceeding.
Fieldston was decided in the immediate aftermath of the Board's experience with the last mammoth consolidation proceeding in which UP participated—its acquisition of Southern Pacific in 1996.

railroad merger proceedings are not occasions when the agency is asked to broker a compromise solution to some set of challenges facing the industry... merger proceedings in particular are 'adjudications in fact.'
basic fairness requires that all parties—not just Applicants—be allowed equal access to the Board and Board Staff.
a mere 'summary' of the topics discussed in an ex parte session will not provide sufficiently specific information to enable a useful response.

docket_entries.title: CSX Transportation Response to UP/NS Motion on Ex Parte Communications - Procedural Safeguards Proposal
docket_entries.entry_summary: CSX Transportation does not oppose ex parte communications in principle, but proposes strict procedural safeguards to ensure fairness and due process. CSX argues that Applicants' proposed timing would give UP/NS unbalanced access to the Board: 'At the front end... Applicants want to begin ex parte communications even before they file their Application... there will be no 'schedule' within which communications could occur that (1) are efficient, (2) fair to all interested parties, and (3) can be of actual use to the Board in its decision-making.' CSX further contends that Applicants' proposed closing date unfairly allows them to conduct ex parte communications to 'determine what Applicants should focus on in their own rebuttal and responses to any responsive applications. But no similar period would be provided after the Applicants' responses, before the submission of rebuttals by other parties.' CSX advocates for strict disclosure requirements, arguing that 49 C.F.R. § 1102.2(g) requirements should be 'applied strictly, consistent with the importance of the issues the Board must decide here on their merits as set out in the record before the agency.' CSX signals intent to provide 'more specific comments on the appropriate temporal window(s) for, and numeric limits on, such communications once a proposed schedule is issued for comment,' indicating it will continue to engage constructively on this procedural issue.
key_arguments: Ex parte communications before the Application is filed would lack a procedural 'schedule' and could be perceived as pre-decisional solicitation: 'Until the Application is filed, there will be no 'schedule' within which communications could occur that (1) are efficient, (2) fair to all interested parties, and (3) can be of actual use to the Board in its decision-making.'

Applicants' proposed timing unfairly advantages them by permitting ex parte communications before their rebuttals while denying the same period to other parties: 'With no other limits, Applicants could communicate ex parte with the Board and staff in an effort to determine what Applicants should focus on in their own rebuttal and responses to any responsive applications. But no similar period would be provided after the Applicants' responses, before the submission of rebuttals by other parties supporting any responsive applications.'

Strict disclosure requirements are essential because this is 'a quasi-adjudicatory proceeding, subject to requirements for procedural due process,' unlike informal rulemakings where § 1102.2(g) was designed to apply

The Board must 'adhere to a strict timetable and impose and maintain a schedule' in consolidation proceedings; temporal windows and numeric limits on ex parte communications are necessary to prevent the process from becoming 'an inefficient free-for-all'

The statute 'demand[s] that the Board accord equal access to all members of the public' and this 'militat[ed] against a process under which the Board would decide issues based on any off-the-record considerations'

The Board should enforce strict compliance with disclosure requirements, including detailed substance summaries and timely filing (within two days) to ensure other parties can respond; 'In practice, however, disclosures under § 1102.2(g) in informal rule-making contexts have often lacked the detail that will be needed in a proceeding of this type.'
key_excerpts: If the Board permits ex parte communications, it should adopt safeguards that ensure they are conducted in a way that is efficient, fair to all interested parties, will assist the Board in its decision-making process, and does not undermine public confidence in that process.

Until the Application is filed, there will be no 'schedule' within which communications could occur that (1) are efficient, (2) fair to all interested parties, and (3) can be of actual use to the Board in its decision-making.

With no other limits, Applicants could communicate ex parte with the Board and staff in an effort to determine what Applicants should focus on in their own rebuttal and responses to any responsive applications. But no similar period would be provided after the Applicants' responses, before the submission of rebuttals by other parties supporting any responsive applications. This inconsistent approach could undermine public confidence in the Board's decision-making process.

This proceeding is a quasi-adjudicatory proceeding, 'subject to requirements for procedural due process.' The 'principles of fairness,' including actual fairness and the 'public's perception of, and confidence in' the Board's decision-making process, are 'critical to the Board's rail merger procedures.'

The Board should make clear that it expects parties engaging in those communications to provide substantial detail about their content, consistent with the on-the-record, evidentiary nature of this proceeding.
docket_entries.relief_requested: CSX requests the Board: (1) NOT permit ex parte communications before the Application is filed; (2) establish strict temporal windows and numeric limits on ex parte communications to ensure fairness and due process; (3) close the ex parte period on a balanced timeline that does not advantage Applicants; (4) enforce strict disclosure requirements under 49 C.F.R. § 1102.2(g) with Board admonition for 'robust and detailed disclosure' including attendee names/titles, detailed substance summaries, all written/electronic materials, and submission within two days.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing directly addresses the Board's authority to waive the Fieldston prohibition on ex parte communications in merger proceedings. CSX invokes the foundational Fieldston standards (1 S.T.B. 1083 (1996)) which require that any ex parte communications in rail consolidation proceedings must be (1) efficient, (2) fair to all parties, (3) helpful to Board decision-making, and (4) protect public confidence in the process. CSX's argument that this is a 'quasi-adjudicatory proceeding' subject to procedural due process requirements could influence the Board's characterization of the merger review scope and the applicable procedural standard. The filing also addresses interpretation and enforcement of 49 C.F.R. § 1102.2(g) in an adjudicatory context (rather than informal rulemaking), potentially establishing precedent for disclosure stringency. CSX's symmetry argument—that ex parte windows should not favor Applicants—may influence the Board's procedural schedule design itself, particularly the timing of the rebuttal period and any permitted ex parte communications window thereafter.
docket_entries.deadline_description: CSX indicates it will submit more detailed comments on appropriate temporal windows and numeric limits when the Board issues its proposed procedural schedule for comment, consistent with the Board's direction in Decision No. 4.

docket_entries.title: BNSF Response Supporting Ex Parte Communications with Procedural Safeguards
docket_entries.entry_summary: BNSF supports Applicants' motion to permit ex parte communications but demands strict procedural safeguards to prevent competitive advantage. While BNSF acknowledges that 'increasing the flow of information and technical expertise between the Board and its stakeholders facilitates decision-making that is grounded in the complex operational and market realities of the rail industry,' it insists that 'the Board should ensure that ex parte opportunities in this proceeding are available and open to all participants—not just the Applicants—and ensure that parties have a reasonable opportunity to respond to and address factual assertions, legal positions, and proposals advanced by Applicants during the proceeding.' BNSF specifically challenges the adequacy of Applicants' proposed Day 150 cutoff, stating that 'the Board should ensure that the procedural schedule set in this proceeding includes sufficient time for ex parte meetings at least until after the filing and Board consideration of comments and responsive applications.' This filing signals BNSF's intent to be an active, sophisticated competitor participant that will scrutinize procedural fairness and contest any structural advantages granted to the Applicants.
key_arguments: Ex parte communications should be permitted to facilitate rigorous, fact-based decision-making grounded in 'complex operational and market realities of the rail industry,' but ONLY if access is equal across all participants

Applicants' proposed Day 150 cutoff for ex parte communications is potentially unfair because it does not account for the full procedural schedule, particularly the filing and Board consideration of comments and responsive applications

The Board must ensure that all parties have 'a reasonable opportunity to respond to and address factual assertions, legal positions, and proposals advanced by Applicants during the proceeding' to prevent ex parte communications from creating informational asymmetries
Any procedural parameters governing ex parte communications 'should apply equally to all participants' to prevent differential treatment that would advantage the Applicants
key_excerpts: BNSF would support a Board decision to permit ex parte communications in this proceeding...increasing the flow of information and technical expertise between the Board and its stakeholders facilitates decision-making that is grounded in the complex operational and market realities of the rail industry.

The Board should ensure that ex parte opportunities in this proceeding are available and open to all participants—not just the Applicants—and ensure that parties have a reasonable opportunity to respond to and address factual assertions, legal positions, and proposals advanced by Applicants during the proceeding.
The parameters the Board sets for any ex parte communications should apply equally to all participants.

The Board should ensure that the procedural schedule set in this proceeding includes sufficient time for ex parte meetings at least until after the filing and Board consideration of comments and responsive applications.
docket_entries.relief_requested: BNSF requests that the STB: (1) permit ex parte communications in this merger proceeding as proposed by Applicants, BUT (2) ensure ex parte opportunities are available equally to ALL participants, not just Applicants; (3) ensure all parties have reasonable opportunity to respond to factual assertions and legal positions advanced during ex parte meetings; (4) apply procedural parameters equally to all participants; and (5) extend the ex parte period beyond Day 150 to include time after filing and STB consideration of comments and responsive applications.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing establishes the procedural ground rules for how evidence and arguments will be presented to the Board in a merger proceeding. BNSF's conditional support for ex parte communications—contingent on equal access and extended timelines—may influence the Board's Decision on Applicants' procedural motion. If the Board adopts BNSF's framework, it could materially affect the competitive dynamics of the proceeding by ensuring BNSF (and other intervenors) have equal opportunity to present technical and market evidence to the Board. Conversely, if the Board limits ex parte access or adopts Applicants' Day 150 cutoff over BNSF's objection, it creates a procedural record that BNSF can cite in post-Decision litigation challenging the fairness of the proceeding.
docket_entries.deadline_description: This is BNSF's response to Applicants' motion; no response deadline applies to BNSF itself. However, the Board's decision on Applicants' procedural motion will implicitly respond to BNSF's conditions.

docket_entries.title: Platte Institute Support for UP-NS Merger
docket_entries.entry_summary: The Platte Institute, an Omaha-based community organization, submits a brief support letter endorsing the UP-NS merger. The filer asserts that the merger 'promises faster, more dependable service, reduced congestion and expanded market reach for our businesses' and will result in 'continued investment in rail infrastructure—enhancing safety, creating jobs and ensuring our community remains competitive in a growing economy.' The filing provides no analysis of competitive effects, no data on Omaha's rail service needs, no modeling of how consolidation improves service (as opposed to reducing competition), and no engagement with counterarguments from shippers or competitors. The letter reads as template support rather than informed economic analysis. No conditions are requested; the filer simply urges approval.
key_arguments: The merger will deliver faster and more dependable rail service to Omaha-area businesses
The merger will reduce rail congestion and expand market reach for local businesses
The merger will generate continued infrastructure investment, safety improvements, and job creation in the Omaha region
The merger is necessary for Omaha to remain competitive in a growing economy
key_excerpts: The proposed Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern merger offers an opportunity to strengthen these connections and deliver long-term benefits.

The merger promises faster, more dependable service, reduced congestion and expanded market reach for our businesses. It also means continued investment in rail infrastructure—enhancing safety, creating jobs and ensuring our community remains competitive in a growing economy.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Approve the proposed Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern merger

docket_entries.title: Border Industrial Association Support Statement for UP/NS Merger
docket_entries.entry_summary: The Border Industrial Association, a New Mexico-based industrial development advocacy organization, files a support statement endorsing the UP/NS merger. The filer argues the merger will benefit border region industries by improving rail service to support 'economic growth' and 'international logistics hub' development. They claim the merger will deliver: 'Improved Service Reliability' through 'more direct routes and greater operational flexibility'; 'Reduced Transit Times' by 'eliminating certain interchanges'; 'Increased Investment' in 'modern infrastructure, advanced technology and enhanced safety systems'; and 'Expanded Reach' opening 'new markets for our state's products.' The statement characterizes freight rail as 'one of the most sustainable modes of transportation available, helping reduce highway congestion and emissions.' No specific service commitments, operational data, or conditions are requested. The filing is purely supportive without engaging operational or competitive details of the proposed transaction.
key_arguments: The merger will improve service reliability by enabling 'more direct routes and greater operational flexibility' that 'will help prevent service disruptions and improve schedule dependability'
Eliminating interchanges will reduce transit times, allowing 'our businesses reach customers faster and more competitively'
The combined railroad will be 'better positioned to invest in modern infrastructure, advanced technology and enhanced safety systems'
The broader geographic footprint will 'open new markets for our state's products and strengthen supply chain resilience'
Freight rail is a critical economic asset and 'one of the most sustainable modes of transportation available, helping reduce highway congestion and emissions'

The proposed merger offers a unique opportunity to strengthen this network and deliver tangible benefits for shippers, consumers and communities

This merger is about more than just railroads—it's about securing the future of our transportation network, supporting economic development and ensuring American freight rail remains globally competitive.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Give 'full and favorable consideration' to the merger proposal
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Minimal. This is a general support statement offering no new legal theories, evidentiary presentations, or substantive engagement with the merger's competitive effects or operational feasibility. It does not invoke specific regulatory standards or challenge any aspect of the STB's scope of review. The statement serves primarily as constituency support rather than substantive intervention.

docket_entries.title: Indiana Department of Transportation Notice of Intent to Participate
docket_entries.entry_summary: Indiana DOT filed a notice of intent to participate in the UP/NS merger proceeding without expressing any position on the merger itself. The filing requests only placement on the service list to monitor proceedings. No arguments, conditions, or specific concerns are articulated. This is a watching stance—INDOT is preserving the right to comment or intervene later if specific impacts emerge (e.g., rail service disruptions affecting highway commerce, freight routing changes, or state-level transportation planning). The vague language 'as its interests may appear' signals INDOT has not yet identified concrete issues but wants visibility into the record.
key_excerpts: INDOT respectfully submits its Notice of Intent to Participate in this proceeding and any related sub-dockets before the Board, as its interests may appear.
INDOT requests that the undersigned be placed on the service list as representative for INDOT.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Placement on service list to participate in proceeding and any related sub-dockets 'as its interests may appear'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Minimal direct significance. This is a procedural gatekeeping filing establishing INDOT's right to receive service of documents and potentially file subsequent comments or interventions. Does not alter the scope of review or evidentiary burden. However, state DOT participation can signal that state-level impacts (highway congestion relief, freight corridor efficiency, shipper access) may become issue areas during discovery or hearing.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response deadline; procedural participation notice only

docket_entries.title: Mayor of North Little Rock Supports UP-NS Merger, Cites Economic and Transportation Benefits
docket_entries.filer_name: Terry C. Hartwick, Mayor of North Little Rock
docket_entries.entry_summary: Mayor Hartwick of North Little Rock files in support of the UP-NS merger, framing it as beneficial to Arkansas's economy and the national freight rail network. He argues the merger will deliver: (1) improved service reliability through more direct routes and operational flexibility; (2) reduced transit times by eliminating interchanges; (3) increased investment in modern infrastructure and safety; and (4) expanded geographic reach to open new markets for state products. He characterizes freight rail as 'a cornerstone of our state's economy' and 'one of the most sustainable modes of transportation available,' and urges the STB to grant 'full and favorable consideration' to the proposal. No specific conditions, remedies, or operational concerns are raised. This is a pro forma governmental endorsement with no independent analysis of competitive, service, or regulatory impacts specific to North Little Rock.
key_arguments: Merger will improve service reliability by creating more direct routes and greater operational flexibility, preventing service disruptions and improving schedule dependability.
Elimination of certain interchanges will reduce transit times, enabling North Little Rock businesses to reach customers faster and more competitively.
Merged entity will be better positioned to invest in modern infrastructure, advanced technology, and enhanced safety systems.
Broader geographic footprint will open new markets for Arkansas products and strengthen supply chain resilience.
Freight rail is 'one of the most sustainable modes of transportation available,' helping reduce highway congestion and emissions.
key_excerpts: The proposed merger offers a unique opportunity to strengthen this network and deliver tangible benefits for shippers, consumers and communities, including: Improved Service Reliability... Reduced Transit Times... Increased Investment... Expanded Reach.
I respectfully urge the Surface Transportation Board to give full and favorable consideration to this proposal, recognizing the benefits it will bring to our state and the national economy.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Urges the Surface Transportation Board to 'give full and favorable consideration to this proposal, recognizing the benefits it will bring to our state and the national economy.'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Minimal. This is a form letter of governmental support offering no new factual record, no analysis of competitive impacts, service standards, rate regulation, or railroad operational specifics. It does not advance the merits case substantively or create evidentiary burdens on opposing intervenors.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Comment period filing; no response required

docket_entries.title: STB Notice of Proposed Procedural Schedule and Request for Comments (Decision No. 5)
docket_entries.entry_summary: The STB establishes a proposed 390-day procedural schedule (consistent with Applicants' petition) with extended comment periods beyond statutory minimums due to the 'high level of interest' and 'potential for numerous and highly complex issues.' Key timeline: (1) F+30: Board acceptance notice published in Federal Register; (2) F+45: Notices of intent to participate due; (3) F+60: Safety Integration Plan due; (4) F+120: Comments, protests, requests for conditions due (except DOJ/DOT, who have F+135); (5) F+210: Responses to comments and rebuttal due; (6) F+270: Final briefs due; (7) TBD: Public hearing if necessary and final decision. The Board modifies Applicants' proposal by conforming DOJ/DOT preliminary comment deadlines to statutory requirements under 49 U.S.C. 11325 and reserving final hearing and decision dates for later determination. The Board notes that 'substantive filings not contemplated by the procedural schedule are disfavored' and evidence attached to non-contemplated filings 'will not necessarily be considered.' Comments on this schedule are due October 16, 2025.
key_arguments: The proposed 390-day schedule from application filing to final decision aligns 'with those in prior major merger proceedings' and provides 'ample time for comments and the Board's review'
The extended comment period (to F+120) is justified by 'the high level of interest in this proceeding, and the potential for numerous and highly complex issues to arise'
A 90-day response period (F+120 to F+210) is necessary for Applicants to respond to comments, protests, requests for conditions, and opposition
DOJ and DOT preliminary comments are limited to F+135 per statutory requirements under 49 U.S.C. 11325, not aligned with general intervenor comment deadline
Public hearing will be held 'if necessary' as required by 49 U.S.C. 11324(a), with date and necessity to be determined later
The Board reserves discretion to modify all proposed dates based on comments received or other circumstances
key_excerpts: Given the high level of interest in this proceeding, and the potential for numerous and highly complex issues to arise, the Board proposes extending the period to file written comments and providing a corresponding 90-day period to file responses, as Applicants have proposed.

Substantive filings not contemplated by the procedural schedule are disfavored. Evidence attached to filings that are not contemplated by the procedural schedule will not necessarily be considered in any Board decision on the merits.
The dates proposed in this decision are subject to change depending on the comments received or other circumstances.
The Board shall hold a public hearing unless the Board determines that a public hearing is not necessary in the public interest.
docket_entries.relief_requested: The Board invites written comments by October 16, 2025 on the proposed procedural schedule. The Board states: 'The dates proposed in this decision are subject to change depending on the comments received or other circumstances.'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This decision establishes the binding procedural framework for all subsequent filings and participation in the merger review proceeding. It clarifies: (1) The extended comment period (F+120) goes beyond statutory minimum to accommodate complexity; (2) DOJ/DOT are on separate statutory timeline (F+135) per 49 U.S.C. 11325; (3) The Board reserves discretion to hold or waive public hearing depending on case development; (4) Non-conforming filings outside the procedural schedule may be disregarded; (5) Final decision must issue within 90 days of record closure per 49 U.S.C. 11325(b)(3); (6) The Board has authority to modify any timeline upon request and good cause per 49 CFR 1104.7(b). The ruling also addresses Applicants' pending August 29, 2025 motion on ex parte communications, allowing commenters to propose schedules both with and without ex parte periods.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Written comments on the Board's proposed procedural schedule due by October 16, 2025. Commenters may propose alternative schedules including or excluding ex parte communication periods but should not address the merits of the separate pending motion on ex parte communications.

docket_entries.title: BLET Second Notice of Intent to Participate - Service List Update
docket_entries.entry_summary: BLET files its second notice of intent to participate in the UP/NS merger proceeding and requests that John Fink be added to the service list. No position on the merger is stated, no conditions or relief are requested beyond the administrative update. This is a procedural entry indicating BLET's intent to remain engaged in the proceeding as its interests may require, but taking no substantive stance at this time.
key_excerpts: The Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and Trainmen, a Division of the Rail Conference of the International Brotherhood of Teamsters ('BLET'), hereby provides its second notice of its intent to participate in the above-captioned proceeding as its interests may require
docket_entries.relief_requested: Add John Fink (7061 East Pleasant Valley Rd., Independence, OH 44131; fink@ble-t.org) to the service list for the proceeding.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Minimal. This filing preserves BLET's right to participate and ensures its representative receives service of all future documents. It does not create new legal issues, change the scope of review, or create evidentiary burdens. It signals that labor unions representing operating employees will be monitoring the merger for potential employment/working condition impacts, but no specific concerns are articulated in this filing.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)

docket_entries.title: National Waste & Recycling Association - Support for UP/NS Merger
docket_entries.entry_summary: NWRA supports the UP/NS merger, arguing it will enhance competition and deliver three primary benefits to waste and recycling shippers: (1) improved service reliability through 'more direct routes and greater flexibility, minimizing the risk of service disruptions'; (2) reduced transit times by 'eliminating interchanges where rail cars are handed off' and 'remov[ing] several days from transit times, enabling faster delivery to the ultimate disposal site'; and (3) increased investment capacity, as 'the transcontinental railroad will be better positioned to invest in infrastructure, technology, and equipment, further improving service quality, capacity, and safety.' NWRA characterizes solid waste movement by rail as 'a critical part of the nation's environmental infrastructure' vital to public health and welfare. The Association encourages the STB to 'carefully consider the positive impact this merger will have on businesses like our members' but provides no quantified evidence, competitive analysis, or member testimony supporting these claims.
key_arguments: The combined network will offer more direct routes and greater operational flexibility, reducing service disruption risk for waste shippers dependent on reliable rail transport
Elimination of interchanges will remove multiple days from transit times, enabling faster delivery of solid waste to disposal sites and improving operational efficiency
A transcontinental combined railroad will have greater capital capacity to invest in infrastructure, technology, and equipment, improving overall service quality and safety for shippers
Solid waste movement by rail is a critical component of the nation's environmental infrastructure and merger benefits serve public health interests
key_excerpts: As the Association that represents the waste and recycling industry, I want to inform you that our members depend on efficient, reliable, and cost-effective rail service to meet the needs of the nation. The movement of solid waste by rail is a critical part of the nation's environmental infrastructure.

The combined network will offer more direct routes and greater flexibility, minimizing the risk of service disruptions. By eliminating interchanges where rail cars are handed off, the combination will remove several days from transit times, enabling faster delivery to the ultimate disposal site.
The transcontinental railroad will be better positioned to invest in infrastructure, technology, and equipment, further improving service quality, capacity, and safety.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Approval of the proposed merger between Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Low. This is a supportive filing from a shipper constituency that benefits from rail consolidation. It does not raise novel legal theories, challenge the STB's regulatory framework, or introduce material factual disputes requiring evidentiary development. The filing does not propose conditions or identify specific competitive harms that would expand the scope of regulatory review. It functions as a stakeholder endorsement supporting the applicants' case for merger benefits to rail-dependent industries.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Comment filing - no response deadline

docket_entries.title: STB Grants CN Waybill Data Access Agreement WB25-55 for FD 36873 Analysis
docket_entries.entry_summary: On September 23, 2025, the STB's Office of Economics granted CN (Grand Trunk Corporation and its U.S. rail operating subsidiaries) access to unmasked Carload Waybill Sample data for 2019-2024, including all records, all fields, and confidential unmasked revenues for all traffic. The STB found CN's request 'complete and sufficiently detailed' and authorized 33 outside counsel and consultants (from Simpson Thacher & Bartlett LLP, Berkeley Research Group LLC, Fletcher & Sippel LLC, and Compass Lexecon) to access the data. CN's initial request stated the CCWS is 'the only single source of the requested data' necessary to 'prepare the various analyses and evidence needed to assess the effects of the proposed transaction.' The waybill agreement expires September 30, 2026, and imposes strict confidentiality requirements: data must be filed under seal unless aggregated to three shippers; disclosed only to outside counsel from other parties with signed agreements; and destroyed/returned upon expiration unless extension is granted. The STB cautioned that the CCWS has inherent limitations—it is a sample based only on railroads with more than 4,500 annual terminating carloads, which 'may have a substantial effect on studies covering areas served predominately by non-sampled railroads.' This is CN's second waybill agreement request (amended from WB25-46 to reflect counsel changes after prior counsel withdrew on September 5, 2025).
key_arguments: The CCWS is the only single source providing the complete data necessary for CN to prepare market and traffic impact analyses required to assess effects of the proposed transaction
CN requires unmasked revenue data across all records and fields for 2019-2024, including 2024 data when available, to conduct adequate competitive analysis
The data access is necessary specifically to support CN's participation in the FD 36873 proceeding (CN is intervening competitor)
key_excerpts: Based on the complete and sufficiently detailed explanations and justifications contained in your request, I will grant access to 2019 through 2024 CCWS data for use in the FD 36873 proceeding.

Your request explained that the CCWS is the only single source of the requested data. Your request further explained that these particular data are required to prepare the various analyses and evidence needed to assess the effects of the proposed transaction.

Only those railroads with more than 4,500 annual terminating carloads are included in the sample. The limited sampling of small railroads may have a substantial effect on studies covering areas served predominately by non-sampled railroads.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Grant CN access to unmasked 2019-2024 Carload Waybill Sample data (all records, all fields, confidential unmasked revenues) for all traffic, subject to protective order and confidentiality conditions.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This ruling establishes that the STB is granting broad discovery access to confidential waybill data early in the proceeding, which will enable CN (and presumably other parties) to conduct detailed economic and competitive impact analyses. The decision confirms the STB's interpretation of 49 C.F.R. § 1244.9(b)(4) waybill release authority—the 'complete and sufficiently detailed explanations' standard is satisfied by showing data necessity for proceeding participation. The protective order framework (seal filing for unaggregated data, limited disclosure to counsel with agreements, ongoing confidentiality post-expiration for outside counsel workproduct) signals the STB's approach to balancing discovery needs against competitive sensitivity. The emphasis on CCWS sampling limitations may become relevant to evidentiary disputes about whether analyses based on CCWS data are sufficiently representative for merger analysis conclusions.
docket_entries.deadline_description: All named individuals must sign and return confidentiality agreements to STB before data can be released; processing fee ($2,477 noted as received) must be paid prior to data release.

docket_entries.title: Norfolk Southern Submission of Discovery Materials: Timetables, GIS Maps, Joint Facilities, and Interchange Commitments
docket_entries.entry_summary: Norfolk Southern submitted mandatory discovery materials in response to STB Decision No. 3. The filing provides: (1) current operating timetables, station lists, and track charts for NS's entire system organized by division, submitted as confidential; (2) GIS maps of active tracks with polyline representations of track centerlines and four separate speed restriction layers (for passenger trains, intermodal trains, freight trains, and tons-per-operative-brake restrictions), noting that non-PTC routes, yard track, and lines where common carrier obligation is discontinued are excluded; (3) a joint facility layer identifying trackage rights and haulage rights held by other railroads on NS tracks, with attributes identifying operating divisions and subdivisions, but excluding short line leases that are not geolocated in ordinary business practice; and (4) a comprehensive list of 39+ interchange commitments with short line operators across 20+ states (Buffalo & Pittsburgh, Yadkin Valley, B&H Rail, Western New York & Pennsylvania, West Tennessee, Central New York, Carolina Coastal, and others). NS represents that to its knowledge, none of these joint facility arrangements or interchange commitments become inoperative by their terms as a result of the proposed change in control. All materials are submitted as confidential under the Protective Order. This is primarily a compliance/procedural submission with no substantive arguments on deal merits.
key_arguments: NS has systematically catalogued its joint facility arrangements through its Real Property Management System (RPMS), relying on ordinary business classification methods to identify trackage rights, haulage rights, leases, and similar agreements, but excluded interchange agreements, passenger depot agreements, and track agreements with customers.

NS's GIS mapping includes specific speed restriction data organized by train type (passenger, intermodal, freight) and brake-ton limitations, indicating detailed operational constraints that may be material to network integration and competitive analysis.

NS maintains 39+ active interchange commitments with regional short line operators across geographically dispersed locations (Northeast, Southeast, Midwest), representing ongoing common-carrier access obligations that survive the proposed change in control.
key_excerpts: To respond to the Board's order, NS relied on its Real Property Management System (RPMS)—an electronic database that catalogs many thousands of agreements and other documents pertaining to NS and its predecessors. Due to the volume of potentially relevant documents, NS relied on how documents are classified in the ordinary course of business to identify digitized agreements with other carriers covering the use of track (e.g., trackage rights, haulage rights, leases, etc.).
To the best of NS's knowledge following a reasonable review, none of these arrangements by their terms become inoperative as a result of the proposed change in control.

NS is providing a joint facility layer for trackage rights and haulage rights of other railroads on NS tracks, which are the only joint facilities that are geolocated in the ordinary course of business. Short line leases are not geolocated in the ordinary course of business.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Compliance filing in response to Decision No. 3. NS is submitting required discovery materials: (1) Operating timetables, station lists, and track charts for entire system by division; (2) GIS maps with track centerline data and four layers of permanent speed restrictions; (3) List of joint facilities and joint use arrangements; (4) List of interchange commitments with short line operators.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing establishes the evidentiary record on NS's network topology, operational constraints, and common-carrier obligations to short lines. The GIS data with speed restriction layers and joint facilities information will be critical for: (1) competitive impact analysis by the Board regarding network integration and capacity; (2) factual foundation for any intervenor challenges regarding competitive access post-merger; (3) baseline for compliance monitoring if approval is conditional. The interchange commitments list demonstrates NS's existing obligation structure to regional carriers, relevant to determining whether merger approval requires preservation or enhancement of such access. The caveat that non-PTC routes and yard track may lack complete data is a potential gap in evidentiary completeness that could be challenged by intervenors or the Board.
docket_entries.document_type: Modify/Supplement Prior Filing Or The Record
docket_entries.deadline_description: Compliance submission to Decision No. 3; no further deadline indicated

docket_entries.title: Union Pacific Compliance Filing: Submission of Timetables, GIS Maps, Joint Facilities, and Interchange Commitments
docket_entries.entry_summary: Union Pacific submits compliance materials in response to STB Decision No. 3, providing: (1) Timetables, station lists, and track charts for its entire system (most in non-machine-readable format); (2) GIS maps in shapefile format showing operating divisions, subdivisions, mileposts, crossings, switches, speed restrictions, and layers for joint facility, passenger, and short line agreements; (3) A list of joint facilities and joint use agreements, with notation that UP is NOT including agreements for passenger depot use, interchange agreements, or agreements for crossing diamonds/interlockings/connecting/switching/side/industrial/customer track, which UP does not interpret as 'joint facility agreements' under the Board's order; and (4) A list of interchange commitments identifying locations and carriers. UP represents that to its knowledge, none of the joint use arrangements would become inoperative following the proposed change in control. Materials are submitted via secure FTP and are requested to be treated as Confidential except for lists of joint facilities and interchange commitments.
key_arguments: Union Pacific interprets 'joint facility agreements' narrowly to exclude passenger depot/station use agreements, interchange agreements, and crossing/interlocking/switching agreements—a potential dispute over discovery scope
Union Pacific represents that no joint use arrangements would be terminated by the proposed change of control, suggesting continuity of third-party access rights
key_excerpts: Union Pacific is not including agreements for use of passenger depots/stations, interchange agreements, or agreements for crossing diamonds, interlockings, or use of connecting, switching, side, industrial, or customer track, which it does not understand to be joint facility agreements as the term was used in Decision No. 3.
To the best of Union Pacific's knowledge, none of the joint use arrangements by their terms would no longer be operative following proposed change in control.
docket_entries.relief_requested: No affirmative relief requested. Filing is responsive compliance submission to STB Decision No. 3.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing is significant because it identifies potential discovery disputes: (1) UP's narrow interpretation of 'joint facility agreements' may conflict with the Board's intent in Decision No. 3—intervenors may challenge whether the excluded categories should have been included; (2) The representation that no arrangements would be terminated could be tested against contractual language during cross-examination; (3) The GIS and operational data will form the evidentiary foundation for competitive effects analysis, routing analysis, and service impact modeling by applicants and intervenors. The distinction between machine-readable and non-machine-readable formats may affect intervenor ability to conduct independent analysis.
docket_entries.document_type: Modify/Supplement Prior Filing Or The Record
docket_entries.deadline_description: Compliance response to Decision No. 3; no further deadline stated in this filing

docket_entries.title: BNSF Waybill Data Access Request (WB 25-44) - Confidential STB Data for Expert Analysis
docket_entries.entry_summary: BNSF seeks authorization for 35 outside counsel and consultants (from Steptoe LLP, Kirkland & Ellis LLP, Compass Lexecon, FTI Consulting, and North Dakota State University) to access confidential STB Waybill Sample data for 1990-2024. The request emphasizes that BNSF's outside counsel and consultants from Steptoe, Compass Lexecon, and FTI already have access to 2019-2024 data under WB25-44; the new request extends coverage back to 1990 and adds Kirkland & Ellis lawyers and three additional Compass Lexecon and five additional FTI consultants, plus Dr. William W. Wilson. BNSF states: 'The purpose of this request is to allow BNSF's counsel and consultants to accurately analyze the impacts of the transaction proposed in FD 36873, including traffic patterns, and to prepare verified statements in formal proceedings before the Board on behalf of BNSF.' The filing notes 'The access BNSF seeks is the same as the access granted to other parties in this proceeding,' suggesting Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern have already received comparable access. All data access will be governed by protective order restrictions; evidence will remain confidential unless aggregated to three-shipper level. BNSF paid required fees ($2,615 for new request plus $1,242 for WB25-44 extensions).
key_arguments: BNSF requires 34 years of historical carload waybill data (1990-2024) with unmasked revenues to accurately model traffic pattern impacts and competitive effects of the UP/NS transaction

Outside counsel (Kirkland & Ellis, Steptoe) and specialized economic consultants (Compass Lexecon, FTI Consulting, Dr. William Wilson from North Dakota State University) need access to prepare verified expert statements
BNSF is requesting the same data access already granted to other parties in the proceeding, establishing baseline competitive parity
key_excerpts: The purpose of this request is to allow BNSF's counsel and consultants to accurately analyze the impacts of the transaction proposed in FD 36873, including traffic patterns, and to prepare verified statements in formal proceedings before the Board on behalf of BNSF.
The access BNSF seeks is the same as the access granted to other parties in this proceeding.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Authorization for BNSF's outside counsel and consultants to access and use confidential Surface Transportation Board Waybill Sample data (carload waybill data covering 1990-2024, including all records, fields, and confidential unmasked revenues) for analysis of transaction impacts and preparation of verified statements in the proceeding.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This procedural filing reveals the regulatory framework for handling confidential waybill data in major merger proceedings (49 C.F.R. § 1244.9(b)(4)) and signals that the STB has already granted similar access to transaction applicants and other intervenors. The breadth of BNSF's consultant roster (Dennis Carlton at Compass Lexecon is a prominent industrial organization economist) and the extended historical period (1990-2024) suggest BNSF is building sophisticated econometric models to support competitive impact testimony. The three-shipper aggregation requirement (FSAC rule) under 49 C.F.R. § 1244.9(f) limits the granularity of public disclosure but allows detailed confidential analysis.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Procedural request for data access authorization; no responsive deadline specified in filing

docket_entries.title: Mayor of Springfield, Illinois Supports UP-NS Merger
docket_entries.entry_summary: Mayor Misty Buscher of Springfield, Illinois writes to express strong support for the proposed UP-NS merger. The City argues the merger will deliver 'more dependable rail service, reduce congestion, and expand market access for our local communities' and 'encourage continued investment in rail infrastructure by enhancing safety, supporting job creation.' The Mayor frames the merger as 'essential to the prosperity of our communities' and urges approval to build 'a resilient, innovative, and globally connected transportation system that serves the public interest.' No specific conditions or remedial measures are requested—the support is unconditional.
key_arguments: Merger will deliver more dependable rail service and reduce congestion in Springfield
Merger will expand market access for local communities
Merger will encourage investment in rail infrastructure and enhance safety
