Merger will support job creation and keep the community competitive in a growing economy
Merger will help build a resilient and globally connected transportation system serving the public interest
key_excerpts: This merger promises to deliver more dependable rail service, reduce congestion, and expand market access for our local communities. It will also encourage continued investment in rail infrastructure by enhancing safety, supporting job creation, and ensuring our community remains competitive in a growing economy.
Ultimately, it will help build a resilient, innovative, and globally connected transportation system that serves the public interest well into the future.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Approve the proposed merger between Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Minimal. This is a form-letter style support filing from a local government without technical, economic, or competitive analysis. It does not introduce new legal or regulatory issues, does not challenge the applicants' case, and adds only general public interest endorsement. Useful for demonstrating local support but not material to substantive merger review under 49 U.S.C. § 11324.

docket_entries.title: San Gabriel Valley Economic Partnership Support for UP-NS Merger
docket_entries.entry_summary: San Gabriel Valley Economic Partnership supports the UP-NS merger as beneficial for California's economy and freight rail network. The organization represents nearly 2 million residents and argues the merger will deliver four key benefits: (1) 'Improved Service Reliability: More direct routes and greater operational flexibility will help prevent service disruptions and improve schedule dependability'; (2) 'Reduced Transit Times: Eliminating certain interchanges will speed the movement of goods, helping our businesses reach customers faster and more competitively'; (3) 'Increased Investment: The transcontinental railroad will be better positioned to invest in modern infrastructure, advanced technology, and enhanced safety systems'; and (4) 'Expanded Reach: The broader geographic footprint will open new markets for our state's products and strengthen supply chain resilience.' The Partnership characterizes the merger as 'about securing the future of our transportation network, supporting economic development, and ensuring American freight rail remains globally competitive,' and emphasizes that 'freight rail is a cornerstone of our state's economy' and 'one of the most sustainable modes of transportation available, helping reduce highway congestion and emissions.' No specific conditions or performance metrics are proposed.
key_arguments: Merger will improve service reliability through more direct routes and greater operational flexibility, preventing service disruptions and improving schedule dependability
Merger will reduce transit times by eliminating certain interchanges, allowing businesses to reach customers faster and more competitively
Merged railroad will have greater capacity to invest in modern infrastructure, advanced technology, and enhanced safety systems
Expanded geographic footprint will open new markets for California products and strengthen supply chain resilience
Freight rail is critical to state economic growth and is a sustainable transportation mode that reduces highway congestion and emissions
key_excerpts: Union Pacific has long been an essential transportation partner for our state, providing efficient, reliable, and cost-effective service to large and small businesses.
The proposed merger offers a unique opportunity to strengthen this network and deliver tangible benefits for shippers, consumers, and communities

This merger is about more than just railroads – it is about securing the future of our transportation network, supporting economic development, and ensuring American freight rail remains globally competitive.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Grant full and favorable consideration to the proposed Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern merger
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Minimal. This is standard pro-merger advocacy from a regional stakeholder organization. Provides no novel legal arguments, no engagement with 49 U.S.C. § 11324 competitive analysis, and no specific operational or service data. Does not shift burden of proof, introduce new evidentiary issues, or challenge scope of STB review. Functions as generic record support for merger proponents.

docket_entries.title: Kerpatrick Lewis Opposition to UP-NS Merger – Market Concentration and Employment Concerns
docket_entries.entry_summary: Kerpatrick Lewis opposes the UP-NS merger on grounds of market concentration, reduced shipper optionality, employment risk, and historical merger performance. Lewis argues: 'This merger will grant UP unfair market dominance by controlling 45% of all rail freight and more than 50% for many individual commodities,' and that 'for many shippers this mega-merger will reduce options from multiple resources to now be only one option of UPNS.' Lewis expresses concern that prior mergers have failed to deliver promised benefits: 'UPNS claims they will grow volume, but prior mergers resulted in less volume,' and 'past examples show integration creates delays and cost.' Lewis also flags employment risk: 'I have concerns this mega-merger will reduce railroad employment across the USA and we saw in covid-19 having too few employees is a huge risk to industry.' Lewis requests outright denial with no conditions offered.
key_arguments: The merged entity will control 45% of all rail freight and more than 50% of many individual commodities, granting unfair market dominance.
For many shippers, the merger will reduce competitive options from multiple railroads to only one (UPNS), eliminating meaningful alternatives.
Historical railroad mergers have failed to deliver promised volume growth; past examples show the opposite result.
Integration of merged railroads historically creates operational delays and cost increases, contradicting UPNS efficiency claims.
The merger will likely reduce railroad employment across the USA, creating systemic supply chain risk similar to COVID-19 staffing shortages.
Merger will increase costs for shippers during a period of already elevated inflation in the U.S. economy.
key_excerpts: This merger will grant UP unfair market dominance by controlling 45% of all rail freight and more than 50% for many individual commodities. For many shippers this mega-merger will reduce options from multiple resources to now be only one option of UPNS.

UPNS claims they will grow volume, but prior mergers resulted in less volume. UPNS claims they will help the industry, but past examples show it increased costs and USA is already suffering from high inflation over the recent years.
I have concerns this mega-merger will reduce railroad employment across the USA and we saw in covid-19 having too few employees is a huge risk to industry.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Deny the UP-NS mega-merger
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing presents general competition and employment concerns within the framework of 49 U.S.C. § 11324 merger review standards (competitive impact, public interest) but does not cite specific regulatory precedent, econometric analysis, or commodity-specific data. The reference to historical merger outcomes is factual assertion without case citation or quantitative evidence. Low legal weight as a procedurally compliant but substantively underdeveloped opposition.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Filing is a comment; no response deadline triggered

docket_entries.title: Wisconsin Department of Transportation Notice of Intent to Participate
docket_entries.entry_summary: Wisconsin Department of Transportation files notice of intent to participate in the UP-NS merger proceeding. The filing contains no substantive arguments, conditions, or positions—it is purely procedural, establishing WisDOT's legal standing as an interested party. The involvement of the Railroads and Harbors division suggests WisDOT's concern about rail service, infrastructure, and economic impacts within Wisconsin, but the specific areas of concern are not identified in this filing. This is a watching brief that allows WisDOT to monitor proceedings and file substantive comments later if desired.
key_excerpts: The Wisconsin Department of Transportation ('WisDOT') respectfully submits its Notice of Intent to Participate in this proceeding before the Surface Transportation Board, as its interest may appear.
docket_entries.relief_requested: No specific relief requested. Filing is solely to establish legal standing to participate in the proceeding.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Establishes WisDOT as a party of record with standing to file comments, participate in discovery, and appear at hearing. No change to evidentiary burden or scope of review. Signals that state government entities view the merger as having material effects on state transportation policy/infrastructure, which may inform later substantive filings or conditions proposals.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response required for notice of intent to participate. WisDOT's substantive positions (if any) would come in later filings.

docket_entries.title: STB Grants BNSF Waybill Data Access (WB25-56) for FD 36873 Merger Analysis
docket_entries.entry_summary: The STB Office of Economics approved BNSF's request for full access to confidential Carload Waybill Sample (CCWS) data covering 1990-2024 (including all records, fields, and unmasked revenues) to support BNSF's competitive challenge to the Union Pacific/Norfolk Southern merger in FD 36873. The approval grants access to 39 personnel from Steptoe LLP, Kirkland & Ellis, Compass Lexecon (including Dennis Carlton), FTI Consulting, and North Dakota State University. The data access is contingent on strict confidentiality undertakings: use limited to the proceeding, disclosure only to counsel of other waybill-access parties, aggregation requirements for public filings (minimum three shippers to prevent individual railroad identification), and mandatory destruction or return upon agreement expiration (September 30, 2026). BNSF already had access to 2019-2024 data; this approval extends backward to 1990, allowing comprehensive historical traffic and revenue analysis. The scope of BNSF's consultant roster—particularly Compass Lexecon economists and FTI's large team—indicates preparation of detailed economic testimony on transaction-specific competitive impacts. Payment fee of $2,615 plus $1,242 has been satisfied.
key_arguments: BNSF requires historical carload waybill data (1990-2024) with unmasked revenues to accurately analyze transaction impacts on traffic patterns and competitive positioning
Data access is necessary for BNSF to prepare verified statements for formal proceeding testimony on merger competitive effects
BNSF's requested access level is identical to that granted to other parties in the proceeding (parity argument)
STB's justification: 'complete and sufficiently detailed explanations and justifications' in BNSF's request support approval
key_excerpts: The access BNSF seeks is the same as the access granted to other parties in this proceeding.

Your request will allow BNSF's counsel and consultants to accurately analyze the impacts of the transaction proposed in FD 36873, including traffic patterns, and to prepare verified statements in formal proceedings before the Board on behalf of BNSF.

The CCWS contains confidential shipper and railroad data...commercially sensitive and has the potential to cause competitive harm to shippers and railroads if disclosed. Therefore, the following agreement must be signed...
docket_entries.relief_requested: Grant BNSF access to Carload Waybill Sample (CCWS) data for 1990-2024 (unmasked, all records, all fields, including confidential revenues) under confidentiality agreement WB25-56.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This ruling operationalizes discovery in FD 36873 by granting a major competitor (BNSF) access to the most sensitive railroad financial data—unmasked carload revenues by shipper—covering 34 years of historical performance. Under 49 C.F.R. § 1244.9, such access is restricted and requires written confidentiality agreements. The STB's approval of BNSF's scope (1990-2024 unmasked, all fields) indicates the Board finds the merger's competitive impacts sufficiently material to justify disclosure of commercially sensitive data. The approval also confirms BNSF's intervention status as a serious party entitled to discovery parity with the applicants. The extensive consultant team (Compass Lexecon, FTI, academic experts) suggests the Board expects sophisticated economic analysis and testimony from BNSF challenging the merger's competitive effects. The ruling creates discovery discovery obligations on Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern to respond to BNSF's analyses with their own data.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Agreement expiration date; BNSF must request renewal 30 days prior (by 2026-08-31) or certify destruction/return of all CCWS data.

docket_entries.title: Allied Rail Unions Notice of Intent to Participate (BMWED, BRS, SMART-MD, NCFO, IBB, IAM #19, TCU)
docket_entries.filer_name: Allied Rail Unions (BMWED, BRS, SMART-MD, NCFO, IBB, IAM #19, TCU)
docket_entries.entry_summary: Seven railroad labor unions (BMWED, BRS, SMART-MD, NCFO, IBB, IAM #19, TCU) filed a joint notice of intent to participate in the UP-NS merger proceeding, adopting the collective designation 'Allied Rail Unions' (ARU) for convenience while maintaining separate participant status. The filing provides appearance of counsel (Richard S. Edelman and Aaron S. Edelman of Mooney, Green, Saindon, Murphy & Welch, P.C.) and indicates intent to participate in the docket and any related sub-dockets. No substantive position on the merger or specific conditions are stated in this procedural filing. The unions' participation signals labor will seek to influence the proceeding, likely on issues of employee protection, job preservation, wage standards, and working conditions—traditional STB labor docket concerns—though their specific arguments and relief requests will emerge in subsequent substantive filings.
key_excerpts: The Allied Rail Unions...hereby give notice of their intent to participate in this Finance Docket as well as any related Sub-dockets

Note that there is no formal organization known as the 'Allied Rail Unions', rather that name has been adopted by these organizations for convenient collective reference in this proceeding; each organization is a separate participant in this proceeding.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Notice of intent to participate in Finance Docket No. 36873 and any related sub-dockets
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Labor intervention in STB merger proceedings is statutorily significant. 49 U.S.C. § 11324(c) requires the STB to consider 'the effect of the proposed transaction on the adequacy of transportation to the public' and related public interest factors, which the STB has historically interpreted to include labor impacts (wages, job losses, working conditions). ARU's participation establishes labor standing to present evidence, cross-examine applicants, and seek conditions protecting union interests. This is particularly important in UP-NS given the railroads' massive combined workforce (~150,000 employees) and anticipated significant job elimination from consolidation. Labor parties typically propose conditions such as protective labor agreements, continuation of craft protections, wage standards, and limitations on workforce reductions.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.deadline_description: Procedural notice filing; no response deadline, but signals ARU will be active in subsequent comment rounds and discovery

docket_entries.title: State Senator Carol Alvarado - Support for UP/NS Merger with Community Engagement Conditions
docket_entries.entry_summary: Texas State Senator Carol Alvarado from Houston's District 6 files a letter of conditional support for the UP/NS merger, framing it as an economic opportunity for the Port of Houston and surrounding industries while requiring safeguards for the East End community. Alvarado states the merger "could foster the economic growth in Houston, especially through the Port of Houston and its surrounding industries" but conditions approval on applicants' commitment to community engagement: "I encourage both companies to continue working closely with residents in the community who could be directly affected to assure them that their concerns are heard and considered." She identifies three specific areas requiring STB priority oversight: rail operations, safety concerns, and quality of life for residents. The letter emphasizes that "through deliberate planning and constant communication the proposed merger can serve both our economy and community successfully" - signaling willingness to support approval if applicants demonstrate tangible community outreach and safety commitments. Alvarado does not raise competitive, service level, or operational efficiency arguments.
key_arguments: The merger presents an economic development opportunity for Houston: 'this merger will combine two of the largest freight carriers in the country which could foster the economic growth in Houston, especially through the Port of Houston and its surrounding industries'
Community engagement and safety oversight are necessary conditions: 'rail operations, safety concerns; and quality of life in the East End community remain safe and effective for its residents'

Deliberate planning and stakeholder communication can reconcile economic and community interests: 'through deliberate planning and constant communication the proposed merger can serve both our economy and community successfully'
key_excerpts: I encourage both companies to continue working closely with residents in the community who could be directly affected to assure them that their concerns are heard and considered.

I urge the Board to carefully evaluate these issues and have them remain top priorities. I am confident that through deliberate planning and constant communication the proposed merger can serve both our economy and community successfully.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Approve the merger contingent on: (1) Continued close collaboration between Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern with East End community residents; (2) Prioritization of rail operations safety concerns; (3) Maintenance of quality of life standards for affected residents; (4) Deliberate planning and constant communication between applicants and community.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Limited regulatory significance. The filing does not raise statutory merger review criteria under 49 U.S.C. § 11324 (competitive effects, service quality, financial viability) or substantive STB precedent. It functions as political advocacy requesting STB condition approval on community engagement commitments—a form of local stakeholder input rather than legal or regulatory argument. Could support settlement discussions if applicants offer community liaison commitments.
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response required; public comment filing

docket_entries.title: Rep. Kevin Kiley (CA-3) Letter Supporting UP-NS Merger - Roseville Economic Benefits
docket_entries.entry_summary: Rep. Kiley (CA-3) submits a letter of support for the UP-NS merger, arguing it presents 'a significant opportunity to strengthen' rail connections and deliver 'economic and community benefits' for his district and nation. He emphasizes Union Pacific's role as 'a cornerstone of Roseville's economic development—driving trade, supporting the growth of the agriculture industry and related businesses, spurring residential expansion, and serving as one of the city's major employers.' He asserts the merger 'promises to enhance rail service by improving speed, reliability, and network efficiency. It will help reduce congestion, expand market access for local businesses, and sustain critical investment in rail infrastructure.' No specific conditions are requested; this is straightforward political support based on local economic interests.
key_arguments: The merger will enhance rail service by improving speed, reliability, and network efficiency, benefiting the region's competitive position in an interconnected economy
Union Pacific's operations in Roseville are central to the district's economic development and the merger will sustain critical infrastructure investment and job creation
The merger will reduce congestion and expand market access for local businesses, particularly in agriculture
key_excerpts: The proposed Union Pacific–Norfolk Southern merger presents a significant opportunity to strengthen these connections and deliver lasting economic and community benefits for my district and the nation.

This merger promises to enhance rail service by improving speed, reliability, and network efficiency. It will help reduce congestion, expand market access for local businesses, and sustain critical investment in rail infrastructure.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Respectfully urge the Surface Transportation Board to approve the proposed merger
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing carries minimal legal significance but may carry rhetorical weight in STB deliberations regarding local/regional economic impacts and political support from affected Congressional district. No novel legal theories, evidentiary standards, or procedural changes proposed. Reflects political rather than technical intervention.

docket_entries.title: Missouri State Representative Riggs Supports UP-NS Merger for Economic Development Benefits
docket_entries.entry_summary: Rep. Riggs, representing Missouri's District 5 (Hannibal area), supports the UP-NS merger as a 'valuable opportunity to strengthen economic activity in Missouri and across the nation.' He argues that a 'streamlined railroad system would mean faster, more efficient movement of goods across ports and facilities nationwide' through 'reducing delays, eliminating unnecessary hand-offs, and lowering transportation costs.' He emphasizes local infrastructure benefits: 'Expanding rail capacity through this transcontinental merger would reduce the number of long-haul trucks on local roads – resulting in less wear and tear, safer streets for families, and cleaner air for our communities.' Riggs frames the merger as a 'generational investment in America's economic future' that would bring 'more jobs, improved infrastructure, and expanded opportunities for growth' to towns like Hannibal, which has historical reliance on rail transport. No conditions or concerns are raised; the filing is an unconditional endorsement based on regional economic development and infrastructure relief arguments.
key_arguments: A merged UP-NS system would create 'faster, more efficient movement of goods across ports and facilities nationwide' by reducing delays and hand-offs, lowering transportation costs and creating a 'more competitive and integrated system'

Merger would shift freight from trucking to rail, reducing long-haul truck traffic on local roads and providing infrastructure relief: 'less wear and tear, safer streets for families, and cleaner air for our communities'

Merger represents economic development opportunity for rural regions like Hannibal with historical railroad connections, promising 'more jobs, improved infrastructure, and expanded opportunities for growth'
key_excerpts: A streamlined railroad system would mean faster, more efficient movement of goods across ports and facilities nationwide. By reducing delays, eliminating unnecessary hand-offs, and lowering transportation costs, this merger would create a more competitive and integrated system that benefits businesses and consumers alike.

Expanding rail capacity through this transcontinental merger would reduce the number of long-haul trucks on local roads – resulting in less wear and tear, safer streets for families, and cleaner air for our communities, all while keeping commerce moving efficiently.
The UP-NS merger represents a generational investment in America's economic future. For towns like Hannibal, it means more jobs, improved infrastructure, and expanded opportunities for growth.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Urges the Surface Transportation Board to approve the proposed merger between Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Minimal regulatory significance. This is a political advocacy letter from a state legislator supporting merger approval based on local economic development and infrastructure benefits. It does not address STB statutory standards (49 U.S.C. § 11324), competitive effects on rail markets, shipper access, or rail service adequacy—the core regulatory metrics for merger review. The filing supports the applicants' narrative on system efficiency and supply chain benefits but introduces no new evidentiary claims or legal arguments that would alter the regulatory analytical framework.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Comment filing; no response deadline applies

docket_entries.title: CN (Grand Trunk) Challenges UP/NS Interchange Commitments Disclosures – Alleges Omissions in STB Decision No. 3 Filings
docket_entries.entry_summary: CN alleges that UP and NS have materially failed to disclose all interchange commitments ("paper barriers" – contractual provisions limiting third-party carrier access) as required by STB Decision No. 3. CN's counsel conducted a 'cursory review' of the applicants' submitted Interchange Commitments Lists and identified at least five specific omissions: three UP commitments (Waterloo Railroad connecting with CN at Waterloo, Iowa; Kansas City West Bottoms Railroad at Kansas City; Colorado Pacific Rio Grande at Walsenburg, Colorado) and two NS commitments (Jackson & Lansing Railroad connecting with CN at Lansing; Cleveland & Cuyahoga Railway connecting with CN's Illinois Central at Cleveland). CN states these are not speculative: each omitted carrier is identified by its STB docket number, confirming their regulatory existence. CN notes it is "not in a position to know whether UP and/or NS have overlooked any of their other arrangements" due to the recency of the 2008 STB disclosure requirement, signaling that the identified gaps may be the tip of a larger iceberg. CN requests formal reconfirmation of completeness and timely supplementation. This is not a procedural objection but a substantive competitive harm argument: if UP and NS are hiding interchange commitments (contractual arrangements that restrict competitors' access to their networks), the Board cannot properly assess whether the merger will foreclose competitive alternatives or whether required remedies are adequate. A merged UP-NS may use undisclosed paper barriers to further restrict CN's competitive position.
key_arguments: UP and NS have failed to fully disclose interchange commitments as required by STB Decision No. 3, specifically omitting known commitments with short-line railroads that directly connect with CN operations (WTRL at Waterloo, KCWB at Kansas City, CXRG at Walsenburg for UP; JAIL at Lansing, CCRL at Cleveland for NS).

The STB's 2008 interchange commitments disclosure requirement is recent and unfamiliar, creating substantial risk that additional undisclosed arrangements exist beyond those identified by CN's cursory review.

Incomplete disclosure of paper barriers prevents the Board from accurately assessing post-merger competitive foreclosure, anticompetitive effects on competitors like CN, and adequacy of proposed remedies to maintain competitive access.
Specific interchange commitments identified by STB docket number prove these are not hypothetical omissions but documented regulatory relationships that applicants should have disclosed.
key_excerpts: Our cursory review of the Interchange Commitments Lists indicates that UP and NS have omitted several of their interchange commitments with short-line railroads that Applicants were required to disclose in response to the Board's requests in Decision No. 3.

We are not in a position to know whether UP and/or NS have overlooked any of their other arrangements with connecting short-line carriers that involve an interchange commitment, at least in part because the STB's disclosure requirement for interchange commitments did not exist before 2008. In that regard, CN requests that UP and NS reconfirm the completeness of the information that they have provided to the STB, and identify any missing interchange commitments in existence. UP and NS should timely supplement their responses as appropriate.
These include: Union Pacific – Waterloo Railroad, LLC (WTRL). See STB Docket No. FD 36798. WTRL connects with CN at Waterloo, Iowa.
docket_entries.relief_requested: CN requests that UP and NS 'reconfirm the completeness of the information that they have provided to the STB, and identify any missing interchange commitments in existence. UP and NS should timely supplement their responses as appropriate.'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing challenges factual completeness of the record on a specific, Board-ordered disclosure requirement. Decision No. 3 directed applicants to file detailed interchange commitments lists. CN's identification of omissions creates a potential basis to: (1) reject the current record as incomplete and require supplementation before hearing/decision; (2) expand discovery into applicant document retention and disclosure practices; (3) shift burden to UP/NS to affirmatively prove no further omissions; (4) use omissions as evidence of applicant sophistication in structuring anticompetitive arrangements and unwillingness to disclose them. If CN's allegations are substantiated, it undermines applicant credibility and evidentiary submissions generally. This may also trigger issues under 49 U.S.C. § 11324(c) regarding adequacy of applicant proofs.
docket_entries.document_type: Modify/Supplement Prior Filing Or The Record
docket_entries.deadline_description: No explicit deadline stated, but CN's request for 'timely supplement' implies applicants should respond promptly. The filing date (October 6, 2025, filed November 13, 2025) and discovery phase context suggest response should be filed before record closure or hearing commencement.

docket_entries.title: Union Pacific Supplement to List of Interchange Commitments - Two Additional Carrier Agreements Disclosed
docket_entries.entry_summary: Union Pacific supplemented its September 29, 2025 response to Decision No. 3 by disclosing two additional agreements containing interchange commitments: (1) Waterloo Railroad (WTRL) at Waterloo, Iowa, and (2) Kansas City West Bottoms Railroad (KCWB) with no specified interchange point. The filing also responds to Canadian National's prior suggestion (CN-4) that Union Pacific's original list omitted Colorado Pacific Rio Grande Railroad, LLC. Union Pacific clarifies that Colorado Pacific does not have a formal interchange commitment with UP preventing BNSF connection; rather, Colorado Pacific's access to Walsenburg, Colorado via trackage rights is restricted to UP interchange only. The filing demonstrates UP's compliance with Board discovery orders regarding competitive constraints.
key_arguments: Union Pacific identifies two additional interchange commitment agreements beyond its original September 29, 2025 disclosure, indicating responsive compliance with Decision No. 3

Union Pacific distinguishes between formal interchange commitments (which prevent dual connections) and restricted trackage rights (which functionally channel traffic to one carrier), arguing Colorado Pacific lacks a true interchange commitment preventing BNSF access
key_excerpts: Union Pacific Corporation and Union Pacific Railroad Company (collectively, Union Pacific) hereby supplement their September 29, 2025, response to Decision No. 3. In that submission, Union Pacific provided a list of agreements that contain interchange commitments, as that term is understood in Board regulations. The two additional agreements disclosed below are in addition to that list.

Contrary to Canadian National's suggestion, Colorado Pacific does not have an interchange commitment with Union Pacific that prevents it from connecting to BNSF Railway at Walsenburg, Colorado. Colorado Pacific does not have a physical connection to BNSF Railway at Walsenburg. Rather, Colorado Pacific can reach Walsenburg only using trackage rights that are restricted to interchange with Union Pacific.
docket_entries.relief_requested: No affirmative relief requested; filing is responsive disclosure supplementing prior September 29, 2025 submission regarding interchange agreements
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing responds to an STB Decision No. 3 order (likely regarding remedial sufficiency of interchange commitments). The distinction UP draws between formal interchange commitments and restrictive trackage rights is legally significant to the Board's analysis of competitive remedy adequacy. If the Board views restricted trackage rights as functionally equivalent to formal commitments for competitive constraint purposes, UP's characterization may be dispositive of competitive concerns regarding Colorado Pacific's alternatives. Conversely, if the Board views trackage rights restrictions as weaker remedies than explicit interchange commitments, UP's attempt to narrow the definition of what constitutes a binding commitment may be challenged by intervenors.
docket_entries.document_type: Modify/Supplement Prior Filing Or The Record
docket_entries.deadline_description: Supplemental disclosure filing; no response deadline indicated, though parties of record may raise issues in subsequent filings

docket_entries.title: Norfolk Southern Supplement to Interchange Commitments List
docket_entries.entry_summary: Norfolk Southern supplements its September 29, 2025 response to STB Decision No. 3 by disclosing three additional lease agreements containing interchange commitments with regional carriers: Jackson & Lansing Railroad (Jackson, MI interchange), Cleveland Commercial Railroad/Cleveland & Cuyahoga Railway (Von Willer Yard and Falls Junction in Ohio), and Aiken Railway Company (Warrenville, SC). NS notes that the Jackson & Lansing agreement predates the STB's current interchange commitment requirement, and that Aiken Railway initially did not view its lease credit as an interchange commitment. This supplemental filing indicates NS is complying with discovery obligations regarding its network of short-line relationships, which may be relevant to intervenor arguments about post-merger service access and competitive bottlenecks at key interchange points.
key_arguments: NS discloses additional short-line lease agreements with interchange commitments at three geographic points: Jackson (Michigan), Cleveland (Ohio), and Warrenville (South Carolina)
NS clarifies that some agreements predate or were not initially understood to contain formal interchange commitments under current STB standards
key_excerpts: NS hereby supplement their September 29, 2025 response to Decision No. 3. In that submission, NS provided a list of agreements that contain interchange commitments, as that term is understood in Board regulations. The agreements disclosed below are in addition to that list.
NS notes that the STB case caption for authorizing JAIL's operations does not reflect the existence of an interchange commitment, as that requirement was not in place at the time.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Supplementation of prior disclosure of interchange commitments with three additional agreements involving Jackson & Lansing Railroad, Cleveland Commercial Railroad/Cleveland & Cuyahoga Railway, and Aiken Railway Company.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This supplemental disclosure responds to STB's discovery order (Decision No. 3) regarding interchange commitments. The filings reveals potential gaps in NS's initial disclosures and establishes the geographic scope of NS's short-line relationships. These interchange points may become material to hearing testimony regarding post-merger competitive access and service guarantee conditions, as intervenors may argue that consolidated UP/NS control of key interchange facilities creates bottleneck vulnerabilities. The disclosure also clarifies that certain historic agreements do not formally trigger current interchange commitment rules, which could limit remedial leverage.
docket_entries.document_type: Modify/Supplement Prior Filing Or The Record
docket_entries.deadline_description: Supplemental filing - no response deadline stated

docket_entries.title: Terminal Railroad Association of St. Louis Notice of Intent to Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.filer_name: Terminal Railroad Association of St. Louis
docket_entries.entry_summary: TRRA filed a Notice of Intent to Participate on November 13, 2025, establishing itself as a party of record in FD-36873. The filing contains no substantive position on the merger, no conditions, and no opposition or support statement. TRRA is watching the proceedings but has not commented on the transaction's substance. This is a procedural notice only, indicating TRRA reserves the right to participate further if and when issues affecting terminal operations, interchange rates, or service connectivity emerge. The organization's involvement signals that rail terminal operators in key geographic markets view this merger as material to their future relationships with the combined company.
key_arguments: No substantive arguments presented in this filing.
key_excerpts: The Terminal Railroad Association of St. Louis ('TRRA') hereby gives notice of its intent to participate in the above-captioned proceeding as a party of record. Service of all filings and decisions may be made on counsel for TRRA at david.hirsh@dentons.com.
docket_entries.relief_requested: No specific relief requested. TRRA filed notice of intent to participate and be a party of record to monitor proceedings.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This is a procedural intervention with no immediate impact on the scope or evidentiary burden of the proceeding. However, TRRA's status as a party of record preserves its right to submit substantive comments, interrogatories, testimony, or motions at later phases. If TRRA later files on the merits (in discovery or hearing phases), it would signal concerns specific to terminal operations, interchange, or connectivity that the applicants may need to address through settlements or conditions.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.deadline_description: Notice of Intent filings do not require applicant responses, but preserve the filer's procedural rights.

docket_entries.title: Individual Consumer Intervention: Baton Rouge Resident Opposes UP-NS Merger on Grounds of Consumer Price Impact
docket_entries.entry_summary: Justin Green, a 10-year Baton Rouge resident, opposes the UP-NS merger on consumer protection grounds. His core argument: "Mergers result in reduced competition in freight rail that drives higher costs, and history shows these expenses don't stop at the rail yard. Instead, they trickle down to hardworking families in the form of higher prices on groceries and everyday goods." Green emphasizes Louisiana's economic dependence on freight rail for stocking stores, creating jobs, and ensuring affordable goods for families. He does not request outright denial but rather conditional approval: he wants the STB to ensure any approval includes conditions that "enhance competition and safety" and prevent "rail industry consolidation from leading to higher costs and weaker service." Green frames his concern as protecting small-town Louisiana residents and everyday families, positioning this as a downstream consumer impact issue rather than a competitive carrier or shipper complaint.
key_arguments: Rail merger consolidation reduces freight competition, which raises railroad costs that 'trickle down to hardworking families in the form of higher prices on groceries and everyday goods'
Louisiana's economy depends critically on freight rail infrastructure for consumer goods availability, job creation, and affordability
Without appropriate merger conditions protecting competition, consumer prices and service levels will deteriorate
The STB should condition any approval on standards that 'enhance competition and safety' and prevent consolidation-driven cost increases
key_excerpts: Often, mergers result in reduced competition in freight rail that drives higher costs, and history shows these expenses don't stop at the rail yard. Instead, they trickle down to hardworking families in the form of higher prices on groceries and everyday goods.

As you evaluate this merger, please keep the interests of everyday Louisiana residents in mind, especially those in small towns. A competitive freight rail system is critical not just for businesses, but for the families and communities that depend on it.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Deny the merger unless approval is conditioned on: (1) enhanced competition protections; (2) service quality guarantees; (3) consumer price safeguards. Specifically requests that 'the Surface Transportation Board ensures the tenets of the merger and conditions imposed on the transaction meet the standards for enhancing competition and safety.'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing represents the public interest/consumer advocacy perspective in the STB's decisional record. While it does not raise novel legal issues or challenge merger justifications with industry-specific evidence, it documents consumer concern about downstream effects of rail consolidation. Under 49 U.S.C. § 11324, the STB must consider impacts on the 'public interest,' which includes consumer welfare. This filing, combined with similar consumer comments, may be cited by the STB as evidence of public concern regarding competitive effects of the merger, though it lacks the factual specificity to independently support legal conclusions about anticompetitive harm.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Comment period filing; no direct response deadline

docket_entries.title: Kelly Reese (Inside Medicine) - Small Business Opposition to UP-NS Merger
docket_entries.entry_summary: Kelly Reese, founder of Inside Medicine in Alabama, opposes the UP-NS merger as a threat to small business competitiveness and supply chain reliability. She argues that merger-driven consolidation eliminates competition, drives up costs, delays shipments, and reduces service reliability—impacts that disproportionately harm small, minority-, and women-owned businesses that lack the resources of large corporations to absorb price increases. She contends the merged entity would create a rail market duopoly, stating: 'When large corporations merge and competition disappear, it's small, independent businesses — especially those that are minority- or women-owned — that end up paying the price. Shipping delays, higher costs, and less reliable service hit us directly.' She frames the issue as one of fairness and opportunity: 'It's about making sure every business, no matter its size, has a fair shot to grow and thrive.' She requests the Board deny the merger to protect competition, reliability, and fairness for Alabama's small business economy. No specific conditions or fallback positions are offered; her opposition is unqualified.
key_arguments: Merger eliminates competitive rail options, creating a duopoly that reduces service reliability and increases shipping costs for small businesses
Small, minority-, and women-owned businesses lack financial cushion to absorb price increases and service disruptions that larger corporations can withstand
Consolidated rail market reduces opportunity for small business growth and fair competition in Alabama's economy
Higher rail costs flow through to everyday consumers and working families, creating broader economic harms beyond business
key_excerpts: When large corporations merge and competition disappear, it's small, independent businesses — especially those that are minority- or women-owned — that end up paying the price. Shipping delays, higher costs, and less reliable service hit us directly, while big companies can usually absorb the impact.

If this merger goes through, Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern would control most of the rail market, basically creating a duopoly. And when competition fades, costs go up — not just for businesses, but for everyday consumers and working families too.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Deny the merger to preserve competition, protect small business access to reliable and affordable rail service, and prevent duopolistic control of the rail market by Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Low legal/regulatory significance. Filing does not cite specific statutory provisions, prior STB precedent, or economic evidence. Does not challenge the merger on grounds of specific competitive harm to identifiable routes or services. However, the filing may be indicative of broader stakeholder opposition from small business constituencies and could factor into the Board's consideration of public interest factors under 49 U.S.C. § 11324(d), which requires assessment of the merger's effect on adequate service to the public and communities.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Comment filed; no response deadline applicable to applicants

docket_entries.title: Trey Vasquez - New Orleans Resident Consumer Impact Letter
docket_entries.entry_summary: New Orleans resident Trey Vasquez opposes the proposed UP-NS merger without specific protective conditions, framing the deal as a threat to local consumers through anticipated price increases for goods distributed via rail from the port. He argues: 'Mergers are known to result in reduced competition in freight rail that drives higher costs, and these expenses don't stop at the rail yard. They trickle down to hardworking families in the form of higher prices on groceries and everyday goods.' He conditions support on STB certification that 'the tenets of the merger and conditions imposed on the transaction meet the standards for enhancing competition in the market which is essential to a capitalist society.' He specifically requests the Board keep interests of 'everyday Louisiana residents' and 'southern economic hubs like mine' in mind. This is conditional opposition—he would support approval if appropriate competition-enhancing conditions are imposed, but provides no specific condition proposals (e.g., service guarantees, pricing commitments, or competitive access requirements).
key_arguments: Rail industry consolidation historically results in reduced competition and higher freight costs that are passed through to consumer prices for groceries and everyday goods
New Orleans depends on freight rail for international port distribution, job creation, and economic viability—merger threatens that without protections
Merger approval must be conditioned on affirmative enhancement of market competition to align with capitalist market principles
Consumer protection and service preservation are necessary to prevent merger-driven consolidation harms
key_excerpts: Mergers are known to result in reduced competition in freight rail that drives higher costs, and these expenses don't stop at the rail yard. They trickle down to hardworking families in the form of higher prices on groceries and everyday goods.

I hope that the Surface Transportation Board certifies that the tenets of the merger and conditions imposed on the transaction meet the standards for enhancing competition in the market which is essential to a capitalist society.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Condition approval on STB certification that 'the tenets of the merger and conditions imposed on the transaction meet the standards for enhancing competition in the market.' Require 'appropriate protections for competition' and conditions to 'prevent rail industry consolidation from leading to higher costs and weaker service.'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Low legal significance. This is advocacy-based consumer comment that does not cite specific regulatory standards, competitive analysis, or measurable impacts. It does not advance novel legal theory or create evidentiary burdens, but does reflect potential public interest framing that could appear in STB's public interest analysis. The reference to enhancing competition as a certification standard may reinforce applicants' burden under 49 U.S.C. § 11324(b) to affirmatively demonstrate competitive benefits, though the filing provides no technical support for that analysis.

docket_entries.title: Sweet Brew owner opposes UP/NS merger, citing service degradation and competitive harm to small businesses
docket_entries.entry_summary: Adam Stewart, co-owner of Sweet Brew, an Alabama-based food service manufacturer, opposes the UP/NS merger on grounds that railroad consolidation will harm small businesses like his own. Stewart argues that merged railroads will reduce competition, leading to higher shipping costs and less reliable service. He states: 'When rail service slows down or becomes unreliable it has a real impact on our operations—and on our bottom line.' Stewart characterizes the merger as concentrating 'control into the hands of just a couple of rail companies' and predicts 'Less competition usually means higher prices and fewer choices, especially for small businesses that don't have the leverage of a large corporation.' He does not propose specific conditions for approval and instead requests that the STB deny the transaction. Stewart has copied the Small Business Administration and Department of Justice, suggesting he seeks broader regulatory attention to small business concerns.
key_arguments: Railroad consolidation reduces competition, which leads to higher shipping costs and lower service reliability for small businesses without bargaining power
Slower rail service and delays directly impact Sweet Brew's operations and bottom line by disrupting supply chain and product distribution
Mergers concentrate control among a few rail companies, limiting choices and enabling price increases that ultimately harm consumers
Small and mid-sized businesses lack leverage to negotiate favorable rates and service terms with consolidated carriers
key_excerpts: When rail service slows down or becomes unreliable it has a real impact on our operations—and on our bottom line.

If this merger goes through it will put even more control into the hands of just a couple of rail companies. Less competition usually means higher prices and fewer choices, especially for small businesses that don't have the leverage of a large corporation.
Over the years I've seen how big mergers like this can create problems for small and mid-sized businesses. They often lead to slower service, more delays, and higher shipping costs.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Deny the proposed merger between Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing represents retail customer opposition based on general competitive harm theory. Under 49 U.S.C. § 11324, the STB must consider public interest, including effects on competition and small businesses. However, this filing lacks the specificity (route-level impacts, quantified volume/revenue data, comparative rate analysis) that would materially burden applicants' burden of proof or establish record evidence of deal-specific harms. It illustrates the type of diffuse competitive concern that STB precedent typically addresses through general competitive analysis rather than individual shipper testimony, absent detailed demonstration of market foreclosure or service degradation in specific lanes.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Comment filing; no response deadline applicable to applicants

docket_entries.title: Union Pacific Errata - Updated GIS Files Correcting Joint Facility Shapefiles
docket_entries.entry_summary: Union Pacific filed a brief errata notice supplementing its September 29, 2025 response to Decision No. 3 by providing corrected GIS (Geographic Information System) files. The updated files address three technical issues: (1) correction of an issue with Joint Facility shapefiles, (2) addition of new data 'layers' to distinguish different categories of rail lines, and (3) exclusion of track lines marked with 'N' in the 'UP_OPER_AL' field to clarify which track Union Pacific does not own. The filing is administrative in nature and represents UP's effort to ensure accuracy and clarity of geospatial data provided to the Board during discovery.
key_arguments: Updated GIS files correct technical issue with Joint Facility shapefiles previously submitted
New data layers distinguish between various categories of lines contained in the geospatial data
Exclusion of non-owned track lines (marked 'N' in UP_OPER_AL field) clarifies ownership and operational control
key_excerpts: The updated GIS files (i) correct an issue with the Joint Facility shapefiles, (ii) provide additional 'layers' to distinguish between various categories of lines contained in the data, and (iii) to avoid confusion, exclude lines with an 'N' value in the 'UP_OPER_AL' field (which indicates track Union Pacific does not own).
docket_entries.relief_requested: Accept updated GIS files via Kiteworks (Covington's FTP site) as supplement to September 29, 2025 response to Decision No. 3
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: No change to scope of review or evidentiary burden. Procedural correction ensuring accurate technical record. No substantive legal or regulatory implications.

docket_entries.title: Steve Hurst (Alabama State Representative) - Regional Economic Impact Concern on UP-NS Merger
docket_entries.entry_summary: Steve Hurst, Alabama State Representative from Talladega County, opposes the UP-NS merger on grounds of regional economic harm from reduced competition. He argues that consolidation of two major railroads into one company will reduce competitive alternatives for Alabama businesses, leading to higher costs and service disruptions that 'ripple through the whole supply chain—hurting manufacturers, small business owners, and even the folks just trying to keep food on the table.' Hurst characterizes freight rail as 'a lifeline' for East Alabama communities and invokes Alabama's reputation for 'reliability and opportunity,' asserting that strong competition is necessary for communities to 'thrive.' He does not propose specific conditions or remedies, instead urging the Board to 'take a close look' during formal review. This is ideological opposition rooted in general competitive principles rather than deal-specific operational concerns or settlement-negotiable demands.
key_arguments: Consolidation of two major railroads into one company reduces competitive options available to regional businesses and communities, putting 'that much control in the hands of one company'

Reduced competition inherently leads to cost increases that burden local businesses and families: 'When competition goes down, costs tend to go up, and that eventually lands on the shoulders of our local businesses and families'

Service disruptions and bottlenecks from merger integration will 'ripple through the whole supply chain—hurting manufacturers, small business owners, and even the folks just trying to keep food on the table'
Alabama's economic competitiveness and regional development depend on 'strong, fair competition in the freight rail system,' which merger will undermine
key_excerpts: These are two of the biggest railroads in the country, and putting that much control in the hands of one company could make it harder for small communities like ours to compete. When competition goes down, costs tend to go up, and that eventually lands on the shoulders of our local businesses and families.

We've seen before how bottlenecks and service slowdowns can ripple through the whole supply chain—hurting manufacturers, small business owners, and even the folks just trying to keep food on the table.
After nearly twenty years representing East Alabama, I've seen firsthand how strong, fair competition in the freight rail system helps our communities thrive.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Urges the Board to 'take a close look and make sure any changes promote safety and competition—without putting our regional economies at risk.' Implicitly requests merger denial or rejection based on competitive and regional economic harm.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Low. This filing presents no novel legal theory or evidentiary framework. It does not cite specific statutory criteria (49 U.S.C. § 11324), precedent, or merger-specific data. It is a general statement of competitive concern from an elected official that may be cited as evidence of public opposition to consolidation but carries minimal probative weight regarding actual competitive harm, service impacts, or remedy feasibility. Does not advance intervenor's capacity to challenge applicants' showing or propose alternative findings.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Public comment filing; no formal response deadline for applicants

docket_entries.title: Marvin Harrell (Harrell Custom Clothes) - Small Business Opposition to UP-NS Merger
docket_entries.entry_summary: Marvin Harrell, founder of a custom clothing business in Alabama, opposes the UP-NS merger on grounds that consolidation will harm small and minority-owned businesses through reduced competition, higher shipping costs, service delays, and unreliability. His core argument is structural: 'If this merger goes through, Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern would control most of the rail market, creating what's a near duopoly. Less competition always leads to higher costs, and those costs eventually make their way down to consumers and working families.' Harrell frames the issue as one of economic opportunity and fairness: 'Healthy competition isn't about economics—it's about opportunity. It's about making sure every business, large or small, has a fair shot to grow and serve its customers.' He does not propose specific remedial conditions, instead urging the STB to ensure the decision 'strengthens competition, reliability, and fairness'—indicating outright opposition rather than conditional acceptance. His opposition is rooted in ideological concerns about market consolidation's disproportionate impact on under-resourced entrepreneurs rather than quantified operational data.
key_arguments: UP-NS merger would create a near-duopoly in rail service, eliminating competitive alternatives for small shippers: 'If this merger goes through, Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern would control most of the rail market, creating what's a near duopoly.'

Consolidation leads to inevitable price increases that disproportionately harm small and minority-owned businesses: 'Less competition always leads to higher costs, and those costs eventually make their way down to consumers and working families. That's not good for business, and it's not good for our communities.'

Small businesses lack the negotiating power and resources to absorb the service degradation and cost increases that follow railroad consolidation: 'When large corporations merge and competition fades, it's the small, independent businesses—many of them minority-owned—that get squeezed the hardest. Delays, higher shipping costs, and unreliable service can hit us in ways big companies barely feel.'

Competition is essential for economic opportunity and fair access for all business sizes: 'Healthy competition isn't about economics—it's about opportunity. It's about making sure every business, large or small, has a fair shot to grow and serve its customers.'
key_excerpts: If this merger goes through, Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern would control most of the rail market, creating what's a near duopoly. Less competition always leads to higher costs, and those costs eventually make their way down to consumers and working families.

When large corporations merge and competition fades, it's the small, independent businesses—many of them minority-owned—that get squeezed the hardest. Delays, higher shipping costs, and unreliable service can hit us in ways big companies barely feel.
Healthy competition isn't about economics—it's about opportunity. It's about making sure every business, large or small, has a fair shot to grow and serve its customers.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Urge the Surface Transportation Board to 'carefully weigh the impact this merger could have on small and minority-owned businesses like mine and ensure any decision strengthens competition, reliability, and fairness.' Implicitly requests denial to preserve competitive rail market.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Filing establishes a record argument that the merger's competitive harm falls disproportionately on small and minority-owned businesses (MOBs), potentially creating issues under competitive analysis and public interest review under 49 U.S.C. § 11324(d). While not a formal disparate impact claim, Harrell's testimony could support arguments that the STB must affirmatively address effects on under-capitalized market participants who cannot absorb service degradation or cost increases. May also influence how STB frames 'public interest' findings post-approval.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Comment submission; no response deadline (this is public comment, not interrogatory or discovery demand)

docket_entries.title: Blair Blacker (Setatech, Inc.) - Small Business Owner Opposition to UP-NS Merger
docket_entries.entry_summary: Blair Blacker, owner of Setatech, Inc. (small manufacturer in Huntsville, Alabama), opposes the UP-NS merger on broad anti-consolidation grounds. His argument: 'If this merger is approved, Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern would form a near duopoly, greatly reducing competition across the rail network. A reduction in competition inevitably leads to higher shipping costs and diminished service reliability.' He does not allege specific harms to Setatech's operations, rates, or service levels, nor does he request measurable conditions that would satisfy him. Instead, he frames opposition around general principle that consolidation harms small businesses and consumers: 'When businesses cannot absorb these rising costs, they are passed down to consumers, driving up prices for essential goods and materials.' He calls for the Board to deny approval unless it can demonstrate 'measurable benefits to competition, safety, and service performance—not just to shareholders,' but provides no roadmap for what such conditions would look like. This is ideological opposition (against consolidation as a matter of policy) rather than conditional opposition (specific remedies would fix it).
key_arguments: UP-NS merger would create a near-duopoly that greatly reduces competition across the rail network, inevitably leading to higher shipping costs and diminished service reliability for shippers
Large rail consolidations, when poorly executed, cause service slowdowns and increased congestion that disproportionately harm small manufacturers and businesses lacking alternative shipping options
Higher shipping costs imposed by consolidated railroads are passed through the supply chain to consumers, driving up prices for essential goods
Merger approval should require demonstrable benefits to competition, safety, and service performance, not just shareholder value
key_excerpts: If this merger is approved, Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern would form a near duopoly, greatly reducing competition across the rail network. A reduction in competition inevitably leads to higher shipping costs and diminished service reliability.
When major rail mergers are poorly executed, service slows, congestion increases, and small businesses like mine bear the brunt of the disruption.
Any merger approval should clearly demonstrate measurable benefits to competition, safety, and service performance—not just to shareholders.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Deny the merger unless the Board can clearly demonstrate measurable benefits to competition, safety, and service performance. The filer urges the STB to 'carefully consider the potential impacts of this proposed merger on small businesses, local economies, and the broader supply chain.'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Low significance. This filing is a form comment from a retail customer/small shipper expressing general anti-consolidation sentiment. It does not raise novel legal theories, challenge the STB's regulatory framework, or present evidence-based arguments that would change the scope of review or evidentiary burden. It is exemplary of public opposition sentiment but lacks the specificity (route-specific impacts, rate data, service metrics) that would trigger serious analytical response from applicants or substantive engagement with statutory factors under 49 U.S.C. § 11324.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Comment period; no response deadline for intervenor

docket_entries.title: National Grain and Feed Association Notice of Intent to Participate
docket_entries.entry_summary: The National Grain and Feed Association filed a procedural notice of intent to participate in the merger proceeding and requested placement on the service list. NGFA provided no substantive position on the merger's merits in this filing. The filing identifies Thomas W. Wilcox as counsel and Max D. Fisher as NGFA's representative for service purposes. This is a standard notice-of-intent filing typical of major shippers preparing to monitor and potentially comment on merger impacts to transportation costs and service availability for grain and feed shipments.
key_excerpts: The National Grain and Feed Association ('NGFA'), hereby provides notice of its intent to participate in this proceeding as a Party of Record and requests that the undersigned and Mr. Max D. Fisher of NGFA ( mfisher@ngfa.org ) be placed on the service list for this proceeding.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Request to be added as Party of Record on service list for the proceeding
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing establishes NGFA as an official party of record entitled to receive all service documents and potentially participate in discovery, hearing, and briefing phases. It does not establish substantive legal positions but preserves NGFA's right to file comments, testimony, and briefs in subsequent proceeding phases. NGFA's intervention signals that shipper interests will be represented in the evidentiary record.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.deadline_description: Procedural notice only; no response deadline

docket_entries.title: Aaron Cooper - Texas Rancher Opposition to UP-NS Merger on Competition Grounds
docket_entries.entry_summary: Aaron Cooper, a multi-generational Texas rancher, opposes the UP-NS merger on competition grounds, characterizing it as creating a 'near duopoly' that will leave farmers with 'fewer options and higher costs at a time when margins are already razor thin.' Cooper frames the competitive harm through agricultural economic vulnerability: 'When rail service falters—whether through higher rates, reduced options, or poorly executed mergers—it creates ripple effects across the entire supply chain. These changes can be the difference between a profitable season or closing the doors on a farm that has sustained the community for generations.' He explicitly requests the Board deny the merger to preserve rail competition for agriculture, stating 'Agriculture needs a competitive rail system to survive, and we cannot afford changes that would weaken that system further.' This is not a conditional opposition—Cooper does not propose remedies or conditions that would make the merger acceptable, but rather advocates for outright denial based on the fundamental competitive threat to agricultural viability.
key_arguments: The merger would create a near duopoly in the freight rail industry, further reducing competition in an already highly concentrated market where a small number of players dominate
Higher rail rates and reduced service options resulting from the merger would be catastrophic for agriculture, where 'margins are already razor thin' and shipper options are limited
Rail service disruptions—rate increases, reduced competition, poorly executed mergers—create cascading supply chain damage that directly threaten farm viability and generational operations
Farmers cannot afford to lose rail competition when they are competing globally and operating on narrow profit margins
key_excerpts: If this merger is approved, the two companies would create a near duopoly, further reducing competition and leaving farmers with fewer options and higher costs at a time when margins are already razor thin.

When rail service falters—whether through higher rates, reduced options, or poorly executed mergers—it creates ripple effects across the entire supply chain. These changes can be the difference between a profitable season or closing the doors on a farm that has sustained the community for generations.
Agriculture needs a competitive rail system to survive, and we cannot afford changes that would weaken that system further.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Merger should be denied to preserve competitive rail options for agricultural shippers. Cooper requests that the Board 'keep farmers and ranchers in mind' and reject changes that would 'weaken' the competitive rail system further.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing demonstrates early mobilization of agricultural shipper opposition and provides factual predicate for competitive harm arguments in the agricultural sector. Under 49 U.S.C. § 11324(b), the STB must consider whether the merger will 'result in substantially increased market concentration or competitive harm' and impacts on shippers. Cooper's testimony establishes that agricultural shippers—a significant and vulnerable customer class—view the merger as reducing their bargaining power and increasing input costs. This framing will likely be echoed in formal comments and could support STB findings that the merger poses unmitigated competitive harm to agricultural transportation users.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Pre-filing comment submitted to Chief Counsel in advance of formal merger application filing

docket_entries.title: Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern Joint Comments on Proposed Procedural Schedule—Request for Accelerated 345-Day Timeline
docket_entries.entry_summary: Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern jointly request the STB adopt a 345-day maximum timeline from application filing to final Board decision (reduced from their original 390-day proposal). The applicants argue: 'Because of the merger's end-to-end nature, the transaction does not present any complex competitive or operating issues,' justifying compressed timelines for their responses and intervenor comment periods. They specifically propose reducing their own response-to-comments period from 90 to 75 days, their final brief period from 30 to 15 days, and the intervenor comment period by 15 days. Applicants cite the Administration's Executive Order 14219 favoring elimination of regulations that 'unjustifiably impeding economic development' as policy support. They emphasize they have spent 'more than two months to prepare the application' and argue the early ALJ appointment and already-commencing discovery support further compression. Critically, applicants request binding timing certainty: hearing within 30 days of final briefs, decision within 90 days of record close, and decision effective date within 30 days of service. The filing strategically frames acceleration as benefiting 'the public and all stakeholders' while advancing applicant business interests.
key_arguments: Transaction presents no complex competitive or operating issues due to its end-to-end nature, justifying accelerated review: 'because of the merger's end-to-end nature, the transaction does not present any complex competitive or operating issues'

Applicants have already invested substantial preparation time over two months, supporting timeline compression: 'Applicants have been working for more than two months to prepare the application. Their work has confirmed that...the transaction does not present any complex competitive or operating issues'

Early ALJ appointment and pre-acceptance discovery already underway create factual basis for reducing intervenor comment period: 'the Board has already appointed an Administrative Law Judge, and Applicants have already begun responding to discovery requests from interested parties. In that context, it would be appropriate for the Board to reduce the period allowed for other parties to file comments'
Binding timing certainty serves public interest and all stakeholders: 'Providing that timing certainty and transparency would benefit the public and all stakeholders'

Accelerated timelines align with Administration policy on eliminating regulations that harm economic development: 'The Board's commitment and Applicant's comments are consistent with the Administration's initiative to eliminate or reduce regulations that harm the national interest by unjustifiably impeding economic development and infrastructure development'
key_excerpts: Applicants have been working for more than two months to prepare the application. Their work has confirmed that, because of the merger's end-to-end nature, the transaction does not present any complex competitive or operating issues.

the Board has already appointed an Administrative Law Judge, and Applicants have already begun responding to discovery requests from interested parties. In that context, it would be appropriate for the Board to reduce the period allowed for other parties to file comments, protests, requests for conditions, and responsive applications by 15 days.
Providing that timing certainty and transparency would benefit the public and all stakeholders.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Adopt an accelerated procedural schedule reducing the total review period from the Board's proposed timeline to a maximum 345 days from application filing to final Board decision. Specifically: (1) reduce applicant response time from 90 days to 75 days; (2) reduce applicant final brief period from 30 days to 15 days (45 days from response due date); (3) reduce intervenor comment period by 15 days; (4) require hearing and record close within 30 days of final briefs; (5) require final decision within 90 days of record close; and (6) require decision effective date within 30 days of service.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing attempts to establish binding procedural constraints that would compress discovery, intervenor participation, and Board deliberation windows. The 345-day target (versus typical multi-year railroad merger reviews) and the specific requests for 30-day hearing/close windows and 90-day post-record decision timelines would materially limit the evidentiary record development and deliberative process available to the STB and intervenors. The applicants' assertion that the merger presents 'no complex competitive or operating issues' is outcome-determinative framing that, if accepted, could justify abbreviated procedures. Conversely, if the STB or intervenors dispute this characterization, the filing becomes exhibit A in demonstrating applicant pressure for expedited review over thorough analysis. The citation to Executive Order 14219 introduces political/policy considerations into what is ostensibly a technical transportation regulatory proceeding, potentially signaling administration priority. The filing's strategic value lies in anchoring expectations and constraining countervailing pressure for extended discovery and hearing periods.
docket_entries.deadline_description: No explicit response deadline stated; filing is procedural recommendation to Board. Board response expected in formal procedural order.

docket_entries.title: Travis DeCock (DeCock Services, LLC) - Small Business Opposition to UP-NS Merger
docket_entries.entry_summary: Travis DeCock, owner of a Texas-based residential handyman service, opposes the UP-NS merger based on concerns that consolidation will reduce competition and harm small businesses. He argues: 'If the merger is approved, Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern would form a near duopoly. This would be detrimental to competition.' He contends that 'less competition in rail service leads to higher costs across the board' and that small businesses like his 'are impacted the most' when 'poorly executed rail mergers slow service and cause congestion, disrupting the supply chain.' He further warns that when businesses cannot absorb cost increases, they 'eventually get passed down to consumers who are forced to pay more for the essential goods and products they need.' His position is NOT outright denial but conditional: he requests that if approved, the merger must 'meet the standards for enhancing competition and safety' and that the STB 'consider the impact on local businesses.' This conditional framing suggests he would accept approval if competitive safeguards and service protections are built in, though he does not specify what those safeguards should be. No evidence of settlement discussions or organized representation.
key_arguments: UP-NS merger creates 'near duopoly' that 'would be detrimental to competition'
Poorly executed rail mergers 'slow service and cause congestion, disrupting the supply chain' affecting small business ability to source supplies and deliver products
Less competition in rail service leads to higher costs, which get passed to consumers when small businesses cannot absorb them
Small mom-and-pop businesses are 'impacted the most' by consolidation effects
Merger must be evaluated against statutory standard of 'enhancing competition and safety' per STB authority
key_excerpts: If the merger is approved, Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern would form a near duopoly. This would be detrimental to competition.
Poorly executed rail mergers slow service and cause congestion, disrupting the supply chain and our ability to get products to customers – and it's the mom-and-pop stores who are impacted the most.

I've consistently seen how less competition in rail service leads to higher costs across the board. Unfortunately, when businesses can't absorb these costs, they eventually get passed down to consumers who are forced to pay more for the essential goods and products they need.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Deny the merger OR, if approved, ensure the merger 'meets the standards for enhancing competition and safety' and that the STB 'considers the impact on local businesses.'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Low. Filing does not raise novel legal issues or establish new evidentiary standards.
