The county frames the merger as advancing the 'national rail system' into a 'new era of efficiency and connectivity' and supporting Nevada's workforce development and economic growth. No specific conditions are requested, and no settlement negotiations or reservations are indicated.
key_arguments: The merger will create a 'more seamless, coast-to-coast rail network that improves coordination, reduces shipping delays, and enhances performance,' with benefits for Northern Nevada shippers through reduced transit times and improved logistics
Shared resources and technology investments from the combined entity will improve safety and efficiency across the system
Increased rail freight will reduce truck traffic on local highways, lowering congestion, emissions, and wear on local infrastructure

docket_entries.entry_summary: West Virginia House of Delegates Energy Chair Gary Howell writes in support of the UP-NS merger, framing it as a critical opportunity for West Virginia's coal and export economy. Howell argues the merger will deliver three specific benefits to West Virginia: (1) 'improved service, capacity, and network reach will give our businesses dependable access to national and international markets' with 'faster and more reliable service, less congestion, and greater market access'; (2) infrastructure investment 'which means new jobs in construction and maintenance and stronger transportation corridors'; and (3) most significantly, creation of a unified coast-to-coast network enabling west coast port access. Howell emphasizes coal competitiveness: 'For our coal industry this merger could be especially important. West Virginia leads the nation in coal exports and improved logistics directly reduce cost per ton. International buyers are very sensitive to transportation costs and the ability to move coal efficiently and affordably helps our miners stay competitive.' He specifically cites West Virginia's recent Taiwan trade office and $175 million in Taiwan trade, arguing the merger will 'provide a direct rail route from the West Coast ports for both imports and exports' and 'open new opportunities in the Pacific Rim. Lower transportation costs make West Virginia coal more competitive in Asia and help sustain our export base.' Howell predicts merger approval will 'support jobs in mining, rail logistics, and port operations while increasing severance tax revenues that benefit our schools, roads, and communities.'

Consolidation will better connect local East Texas businesses to national and international markets
The merger will support job growth and economic development in Senate District 3 and surrounding communities
East Texas industries (timber, agriculture, manufacturing, energy) depend on efficient rail transportation and will benefit from improved service
key_excerpts: The consolidation of these two major carriers will improve service reliability, expand capacity, and better connect local businesses to national and international markets. This, in turn, will support job growth and economic development throughout Senate District 3 and the surrounding communities.

East Texas, including my hometown of Jacksonville, which is directly served by Union Pacific rail lines, relies heavily on efficient rail transportation for industries ranging from timber and agriculture to manufacturing and energy.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Approval of the proposed merger between Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern railways
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Minimal. This is a political support letter from a regional government official but contains no substantive regulatory analysis, competitive impact assessment, or legal arguments relevant to STB merger review standards. It does not address the statutory criteria under 49 U.S.C. § 11324 (effect on competition, adequacy of service, financial condition). The filing may be used by applicants as evidence of regional political support but carries limited evidentiary weight in the formal proceeding.

docket_entries.title: City of Rawlins Mayor Supports UP-NS Merger, Cites Economic and Infrastructure Benefits
docket_entries.entry_summary: City of Rawlins Mayor Jacquelin Wells, representing the City and Carbon County, Wyoming, submitted a letter of support for the UP-NS merger. The City characterizes the merger as an opportunity to 'strengthen connections and deliver long-term benefits' for the local economy and businesses. Mayor Wells specifically cites: 'faster, more dependable service, reduced congestion and expanded market reach for our businesses.' She further emphasizes that the merger 'means continued investment in rail infrastructure—enhancing safety, creating jobs and ensuring our community remains competitive.' The letter does not raise concerns, conditions, or caveats—it is an unqualified endorsement urging STB approval so the community can 'take advantage of the efficiencies, investments and opportunities it will bring.'
key_arguments: The merger will deliver faster and more dependable rail service to Rawlins businesses and community
The merger will reduce rail congestion and expand market reach for local businesses
The merger promises continued infrastructure investment that will enhance safety and create jobs
The merger will keep Rawlins competitive in a growing economy through regional, national, and global connectivity
key_excerpts: The proposed Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern merger offers an opportunity to strengthen these connections and deliver long-term benefits.

The merger promises faster, more dependable service, reduced congestion and expanded market reach for our businesses. It also means continued investment in rail infrastructure—enhancing safety, creating jobs and ensuring our community remains competitive in a growing economy.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Approval of the Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern merger
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: None. This is a non-expert local government statement of support. It does not raise novel legal questions, propose regulatory conditions, cite statutory standards (49 U.S.C. § 11324), or provide competitive analysis. It is ministerial support correspondence with no impact on the scope or burden of STB review.

docket_entries.title: Pennsylvania State Senator Greg Rothman - Support for UP/NS Merger
docket_entries.entry_summary: Pennsylvania State Senator Greg Rothman (34th District) files in support of the UP/NS merger, characterizing it as 'a generational opportunity to strengthen our national economy.' He argues the merger will 'unlock more than $5 billion in annual investment in safer, more resilient infrastructure, creating jobs and driving long-term economic growth' and will modernize the rail system while enhancing safety and reliability. For Pennsylvania constituencies—agriculture, energy, manufacturing, logistics—he contends the merger means 'more efficient transportation, lower shipping costs, and greater access to national and global markets.' He argues 'A more unified and technologically advanced rail network will reduce supply chain bottlenecks, helping to lower prices and improve competitiveness for American-made goods.' No conditions, qualifications, or specific operational details provided. Filing reflects broad economic support rather than detailed regulatory analysis.
key_arguments: Merger represents 'a generational opportunity to strengthen our national economy' and will 'unlock more than $5 billion in annual investment in safer, more resilient infrastructure'
Transaction will modernize the rail system while enhancing safety and reliability across the board
For Pennsylvania industries and working families, merger means 'more efficient transportation, lower shipping costs, and greater access to national and global markets'
Unified and technologically advanced rail network will 'reduce supply chain bottlenecks, helping to lower prices and improve competitiveness for American-made goods'
Transportation is the 'backbone of economic opportunity' and this merger ensures it is 'strong, safe, and built for the future'
key_excerpts: This merger represents a generational opportunity to strengthen our national economy. It will unlock more than $5 billion in annual investment in safer, more resilient infrastructure, creating jobs and driving long-term economic growth.
A more unified and technologically advanced rail network will reduce supply chain bottlenecks, helping to lower prices and improve competitiveness for American-made goods.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Give 'full and favorable consideration' to the merger proposal
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Minimal regulatory significance. Filing is standard political support with no engagement with STB merger review standards (49 U.S.C. § 11324), competitive effects analysis, operational integration concerns, or service guarantee proposals. Does not address antitrust concerns or provide expert testimony. Adds political backing from state legislator but no evidentiary or legal support for approval decision.
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response deadline; comment filing

docket_entries.title: Mayor of Sedalia Supports UP/NS Merger - Economic Development and Service Benefits
docket_entries.entry_summary: Mayor Andrew Dawson of Sedalia, Missouri, files a letter in strong support of the UP/NS merger. He argues that freight rail is 'a cornerstone of our state's economy, safely moving the goods that power our industries, support our farmers and connect our communities to markets.' The Mayor identifies four purported benefits: (1) 'Improved Service Reliability' through 'more direct routes and greater operational flexibility' to 'prevent service disruptions and improve schedule dependability'; (2) 'Reduced Transit Times' by 'eliminating certain interchanges' to help 'businesses reach customers faster and more competitively'; (3) 'Increased Investment' in 'modern infrastructure, advanced technology and enhanced safety systems'; and (4) 'Expanded Reach' through a 'broader geographic footprint' that will 'open new markets for our state's products and strengthen supply chain resilience.' The Mayor characterizes the merger as essential to 'securing the future of our transportation network, supporting economic development and ensuring American freight rail remains globally competitive.' No specific conditions, remedies, or operational requirements are requested. The letter does not engage with competitive concerns, service disruption risks, rate impacts, or employment effects.
key_arguments: Merger will deliver 'Improved Service Reliability' through 'more direct routes and greater operational flexibility' that will 'prevent service disruptions and improve schedule dependability'
Merger will enable 'Reduced Transit Times' by 'eliminating certain interchanges' allowing 'businesses reach customers faster and more competitively'
Combined railroad will have 'better positioned' capacity 'to invest in modern infrastructure, advanced technology and enhanced safety systems'
Merger will expand geographic reach and 'open new markets for our state's products and strengthen supply chain resilience'
Freight rail is 'one of the most sustainable modes of transportation available, helping reduce highway congestion and emissions'
key_excerpts: Freight rail is a cornerstone of our state's economy, safely moving the goods that power our industries, support our farmers and connect our communities to markets across the nation and the world.
The proposed merger offers a unique opportunity to strengthen this network and deliver tangible benefits for shippers, consumers and communities

This merger is about more than just railroads—it's about securing the future of our transportation network, supporting economic development and ensuring American freight rail remains globally competitive.
docket_entries.relief_requested: The Mayor 'respectfully urge[s] the Surface Transportation Board to give full and favorable consideration to this proposal, recognizing the benefits it will bring to our state and the national economy.'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing demonstrates local government support for the merger on economic development grounds. It does not establish legal precedent or change the scope of STB review. However, it may be cited by applicants to argue local community benefit and could be used to counter allegations of local economic harm. It does not raise new legal theories, challenge the evidentiary record, or propose remedial conditions that would require applicant response under procedural rules. Its significance is political/advocacy rather than legal.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Comment filing - no response deadline applies

docket_entries.title: Virginia House Delegate Oates Supports UP-NS Merger, Emphasizes Economic and Transportation Benefits
docket_entries.entry_summary: Virginia House Delegate Delores Oates, representing Clarke County and portions of Frederick and Warren County, submitted a letter of support for the UP-NS merger dated November 7, 2025. She frames the merger as beneficial to Virginia's economy and the national transportation system, emphasizing that 'Freight rail is a cornerstone of our state's economy, safely moving the goods that power our industries, support our farmers and connect our communities to markets across the nation and the world.' She identifies four claimed benefits: (1) improved service reliability through 'more direct routes and greater operational flexibility'; (2) reduced transit times by 'eliminating certain interchanges'; (3) increased investment in 'modern infrastructure, advanced technology and enhanced safety systems'; and (4) expanded geographic reach to 'open new markets for our state's products and strengthen supply chain resilience.' She also emphasizes the environmental advantage of rail as 'one of the most sustainable modes of transportation available, helping reduce highway congestion and emissions.' The letter contains no analysis of competitive impacts, service standards, or specific operational concerns, and requests no conditions on approval.
key_arguments: The merger will improve service reliability by providing more direct routes and greater operational flexibility to prevent service disruptions and improve schedule dependability.
The merger will reduce transit times by eliminating certain interchange requirements, enabling Virginia businesses to reach customers faster and more competitively.
The merged transcontinental railroad will be positioned to invest in modern infrastructure, advanced technology, and enhanced safety systems.
The broader geographic footprint will open new markets for Virginia products and strengthen supply chain resilience.
Rail transportation is one of the most sustainable modes available and will help reduce highway congestion and emissions.
key_excerpts: Freight rail is a cornerstone of our state's economy, safely moving the goods that power our industries, support our farmers and connect our communities to markets across the nation and the world.
The proposed merger offers a unique opportunity to strengthen this network and deliver tangible benefits for shippers, consumers and communities.

This merger is about more than just railroads-it's about securing the future of our transportation network, supporting economic development and ensuring American freight rail remains globally competitive.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Urges the Surface Transportation Board to 'give full and favorable consideration to this proposal, recognizing the benefits it will bring to our state and the national economy.'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Minimal. This is standard legislative support correspondence with no legal or evidentiary significance. It does not raise new issues under 49 U.S.C. § 11324, does not propose conditions that would require STB action, and does not contest STB jurisdiction or methodology. It may be cited by applicants as evidence of state-level support for economic benefits, but does not shift regulatory burdens or change the scope of the competitive analysis.

docket_entries.title: Senator Owen Henry (NJ) Support for UP/NS Merger - Economic Benefits Letter
docket_entries.entry_summary: Senator Henry expresses support for the UP/NS merger on behalf of New Jersey economic interests. He argues that Norfolk Southern 'has long been an essential transportation partner for our state, providing efficient, reliable and cost-effective service to businesses large and small.' The merger, he contends, will deliver four specific benefits: (1) 'More direct routes and greater operational flexibility will help prevent service disruptions and improve schedule dependability'; (2) 'Eliminating certain interchanges will speed the movement of goods, helping our businesses reach customers faster and more competitively'; (3) 'The transcontinental railroad will be better positioned to invest in modern infrastructure, advanced technology and enhanced safety systems'; and (4) 'The broader geographic footprint will open new markets for our state's products and strengthen supply chain resilience.' Henry frames the merger as a competitive necessity, stating 'This merger is about securing the future of our transportation network, supporting economic development and ensuring American freight rail remains globally competitive.' He requests STB approval without conditions or caveats.
key_arguments: Merged entity will provide 'more direct routes and greater operational flexibility' reducing service disruptions and improving schedule dependability for New Jersey shippers
Elimination of interchanges through the merger will reduce transit times, allowing 'our businesses reach customers faster and more competitively'
Transcontinental railroad resulting from merger will have greater capacity to 'invest in modern infrastructure, advanced technology and enhanced safety systems'
Expanded geographic footprint post-merger will 'open new markets for our state's products and strengthen supply chain resilience'
Merger is necessary to ensure 'American freight rail remains globally competitive' against international transportation modes
key_excerpts: Norfolk Southern has long been an essential transportation partner for our state, providing efficient, reliable and cost-effective service to businesses large and small.
The proposed merger offers a unique opportunity to strengthen this network and deliver tangible benefits for shippers, consumers and communities

This merger is about more than just railroads—it's about securing the future of our transportation network, supporting economic development and ensuring American freight rail remains globally competitive.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Urges the Surface Transportation Board to 'give full and favorable consideration to this proposal, recognizing the benefits it will bring to our state and the national economy.'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Minimal. This is a legislative endorsement for STB consideration in the public interest analysis but does not raise novel legal issues, challenge STB jurisdiction, or introduce new evidentiary standards. It is a pro-forma statement of state-level support typical in major transportation merger proceedings.

docket_entries.title: Arkansas State Representative Tracy Steele Letter Supporting UP-NS Merger for Economic Development
docket_entries.entry_summary: Arkansas State Representative Tracy Steele submitted a letter supporting the UP-NS merger on behalf of Arkansas economic interests. Steele argues the merger will 'modernize rail operations, alleviate congestion, and reduce costs for shippers' while generating 'nearly $3 billion in efficiencies.' For Arkansas specifically, Steele contends the merger will provide: (1) improved market access for 'energy producers, manufacturers, and farmers' in the state; (2) reduced shipping costs that 'can be poured right back into our businesses with the necessary tools for growth and expansion'; and (3) enhanced rail network connections 'from coast to coast' that strengthen 'economic competitiveness.' Steele does not raise competitive concerns, seek conditions, or address potential merger risks. The letter is purely supportive, framed as advancing regional economic development and job creation.
key_arguments: The merger will 'modernize rail operations, alleviate congestion, and reduce costs for shippers' by unlocking 'nearly $3 billion in efficiencies'
For Arkansas specifically, the merger will improve 'access to both national and international markets for energy producers, manufacturers, and farmers—the bread and butter of the Arkansas economy'

Reduced shipping costs from the merger will enable 'Arkansans to reap benefits through reduced costs that can be poured right back into our businesses with the necessary tools for growth and expansion'
An 'enhanced rail network' is 'fundamentally linked to economic competitiveness' and will offer 'more stability for job creators' and encourage 'long-term growth in our communities'
key_excerpts: By combining resources, this deal will modernize rail operations, alleviate congestion, and reduce costs for shippers, unlocking nearly $3 billion in efficiencies. For Arkansas, this translates to improved access to both national and international markets for energy producers, manufacturers, and farmers—the bread and butter of the Arkansas economy.
an enhanced rail network not only transcends mere transportation, but it is fundamentally linked to economic competitiveness
docket_entries.relief_requested: Respectfully urge the STB to approve the merger and 'support for this merger and the economic promise it holds for the people of Arkansas'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Minimal. This is a legislative advocacy letter expressing political support for merger approval. It does not raise novel legal interpretations, challenge the scope of STB review, propose new evidentiary standards, or address specific merger-related harms that would change the regulatory framework. It is generic support from a state official, comparable to other political endorsements.
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response deadline; this is a comment filing during the public comment phase

docket_entries.title: CPKC Comments on Proposed Procedural Schedule for UP/NS Merger
docket_entries.filer_name: Canadian Pacific Railway Company d/b/a Canadian Pacific Kansas City (CPKC)
docket_entries.entry_summary: CPKC opposes the proposed Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern merger and submits detailed comments on the procedural schedule, arguing that the Board should allocate more time to evidence development. CPKC contends this transaction represents an unprecedented 'end game' creating a transcontinental duopoly and warrants use of the full statutory 395-day evidentiary period rather than the accelerated 270-day schedule proposed.
key_arguments: The proposed evidentiary schedule is 125 days (four months) shorter than the statutory maximum of 395 days allowed by Congress, which is inappropriate for this unprecedented transaction
This is the first application of the Board's 2001 Major Merger Rules and raises novel issues about whether a transcontinental duopoly structure serves the public interest

Past expedited merger schedules (UP/SP, CSX/NS/Conrail, BN/Santa Fe) involved unique exigencies (competitor financial distress, Conrail split plan) not present here, making them non-germane precedents
Norfolk Southern is financially healthy and nearly revenue adequate, unlike Southern Pacific or Conrail, eliminating justification for expedited review
The transaction's transformation of the entire U.S. rail map and downstream effects require thorough evidentiary development impossible in an accelerated timeline
A sur-reply round is essential to allow commenters to respond to new evidence and arguments Applicants will offer in their responses to initial comments
Post-hearing briefing is necessary because recent merger hearings have evolved into quasi-evidentiary proceedings with new factual content, not merely appellate-style oral arguments
Ex parte communications should be limited to discrete windows following each evidentiary round to promote fairness and prevent interference with record development
key_excerpts: This proceeding will consider a transaction that is not just another rail merger in a long line of rail mergers approved by the agency since the 1940 Transportation Act was passed.

This proceeding also will be the Board's one, only, and final chance to determine whether the public interest is served by a rail merger 'End Game' that leads the U.S. rail network down the path towards just two transcontinental duopolies. If this transaction is approved, there will be no turning back.

The Board's Proposed Schedule, on the other hand, calls for the close of the evidentiary record as early as Day 270 (upon filing of Final Briefs), in which case a decision would be required by Day 360. In other words, the Board's Proposed Schedule is potentially 125 days (more than four months) shorter than the statutory maximum period.

Up's proposed takeover of NS entails no similar exigency. NS is financially healthy and nearly revenue adequate. As NS's CEO Mark George proclaimed in NS's Annual Report for 2024, filed in early 2025 before UP's offer to acquire NS: 'We are well positioned to build on our success and consistently deliver competitive results for our stakeholders.'

Unless the parties filing comments at F+120 have an opportunity to submit a response to Applicants' 'Responses' filed at F+210, Applicants' new evidence will be effectively unchallengeable (except to the limited extent of potential cross examination via depositions of Applicants' witnesses).

docket_entries.title: BNSF Railway Company Comments on Proposed Procedural Schedule for UP/NS Merger
docket_entries.entry_summary: BNSF Railway Company opposes the proposed Union Pacific/Norfolk Southern merger as unprecedented in scale and risk, controlling 43% of U.S. rail market. BNSF requests the STB use the full statutory time period (F+395) for review, permit supplemental evidence rounds, allow both pre- and post-hearing briefs, and deny applicants' request to shorten the procedural schedule. BNSF also filed contemporaneous discovery dispute letters challenging insufficient document productions from UP and NS.
key_arguments: The proposed merger is unprecedented in scale and would create an industry dominant player controlling 43% of U.S. rail market and 52,000 track miles across 43 states
The Board should utilize all 395 days allowed by statute rather than leaving 100 days unused
Applicants have failed to adequately explain how the merger would create 'new or enhanced rail-to-rail competition' as required by Board merger rules
UP's past merger integration failures (1996 UP/SP merger causing 'the mess in the West') raise serious concerns about achievability of claimed efficiencies
Applicants' request to shorten the procedural schedule contradicts UP's prior position from 2001 merger rules negotiations advocating for 15-month schedules
Executive Order 14219 citations are inapt and irrelevant to STB merger procedures
The CP-KCS merger precedent demonstrates that end-to-end nature does not eliminate complexity requiring extended timeframes
Applicants have slow-walked discovery, producing only 331-367 documents with minimal substantive content regarding merger impacts
Supplemental evidence rounds are necessary to pressure-test applicants' claims about efficiencies, competition, customer impacts, labor effects, and gateway impacts
Combined UP/NS would leave many customers crossing the Mississippi with fewer rail options
key_excerpts: No railroad merger of this scale has ever been proposed. It would create an industry goliath far larger than other railroads and allow UP/NS to exert leverage on industry stakeholders.
UP/NS would control 43% of the U.S. rail market and 52,000 track miles in 43 states. It dwarfs prior mergers—in both scale and risk.

The Board has been planning for this day for 25 years. When the Board imposed a temporary moratorium on major mergers in 2000 and then adopted its 2001 merger rules, the Board recognized that the next Class I merger—such as UP/NS—would likely be its last opportunity to determine whether further consolidation would enhance competition and serve the public interest.
With so much at stake, there is no reason to leave nearly a quarter of statutorily available time unused.
Applicants have not identified a single element of the UP/NS merger that would enhance rail-to-rail competition.

UP claims these efficiencies stem from 'new single-line service.' However, UP's past merger integrations raise concerns about the achievability of these purported merger efficiencies and how this one could go wrong.
To date, UP has produced only 367 documents in discovery; most documents in that modest production were lease agreements and waiver conditions.
the parties—both Applicants and non-Applicants—can use the additional time productively by preparing a supplemental round of evidence for the Board's review.

docket_entries.title: Super Neighborhoods 64 & 88 Comments on UP-NS Merger: Request for Houston Public Hearing, Enhanced Environmental Analysis, and Community Mitigation
docket_entries.filer_name: Super Neighborhood 64 & 88, Greater Eastwood, Lawndale, and Wayside (Lindsay Williams, President)
docket_entries.entry_summary: Community organization representing ~23,000 Houston East End residents opposes the UP-NS merger due to severe existing rail congestion impacts and requests rejection or comprehensive mitigation. The filer presents documented data showing 148-206 trains monthly at key crossings with 25-27% stopping for extended periods, causing emergency response delays and quality-of-life degradation.
key_arguments: Houston serves as critical hub in national freight network; merger would intensify already overwhelming rail operations
East End neighborhoods trapped in 'Rail Triangle' with only one grade-separated crossing, creating severe mobility constraints
Current EIS methodologies inadequate for Houston's complex interlinked rail system; they fail to account for stopped trains causing extended blockages
Cascade effects from secondary line interactions not captured in previous merger reviews (CP-KCS)
Houston Fire Department documents hundreds of annual incidents where stopped trains delay emergency vehicles
27% of trains stop for average of 48 minutes, but standard EIS calculations only use average train length and speed
Cumulative impacts of post-pandemic freight increases plus CP-KCS merger already untenable; further consolidation unacceptable
Community data from Eastwood Civic Association tracks 206 trains/month in 2025 vs. 148/month in 2024, showing accelerating impacts
key_excerpts: Our East End neighborhoods—including Greater Fifth Ward, OST/South Union, and Northside communities—are among the most rail-impacted urban areas in the nation. We are effectively trapped in a 'Rail Triangle,' surrounded by the Houston East Belt Subdivision, the Houston West Belt Subdivision, and the Galveston Subdivision.
In 2024, the Eastwood & Rusk crossing experienced an average of 148 trains per month, with 27% stopping for more than 10 minutes and blocking the crossing for an average of 48 minutes
Train lengths of 9,000 to 9,300 feet mean that a single train can simultaneously block 14 of our 15 at-grade crossings
The Houston Fire Department documents hundreds of incidents each year where stopped trains delay emergency vehicles or force reroutes, creating unacceptable risks to life and safety.
Current methodologies calculate blocked crossing time as a function of average train length and speed, failing to account for trains that stop completely for extended periods.

We implore the Surface Transportation Board to consider rejecting the current proposal and requiring Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern to seek an alternative routing that avoids further burdening the already overwhelmed Houston Complex.

docket_entries.title: STB Decision No. 6: Procedural Schedule Reset Following Federal Government Shutdown
docket_entries.entry_summary: The STB issued Decision No. 6 resetting procedural deadlines following the federal government shutdown that ran from October 1-November 13, 2025. The Board previously (in Decision No. 5, September 26, 2025) invited comments on a proposed procedural schedule due October 16, 2025, but that deadline was tolled under STB Docket EP 751 when the shutdown began. The Board now establishes a new deadline of November 20, 2025 for comments on the proposed procedural schedule. The decision clarifies that all materials submitted during the shutdown are deemed filed on November 13, 2025 (provided filing requirements were met) and should not be resubmitted. This procedural reset affects all stakeholders in the proceeding, including merger applicants, intervenors, and the Board's own hearing preparation.
key_arguments: Federal government shutdown from October 1-November 13, 2025 tolled all submission deadlines under STB Docket EP 751
New deadline established for comments on proposed procedural schedule: November 20, 2025
All filings submitted during shutdown period are deemed filed on November 13, 2025 (no resubmission required)
key_excerpts: However, by decision served in Docket No. EP 751 on October 1, 2025, all deadlines for the submission of pleadings, filings, comments (including environmental comments) and other material due to be submitted during the pendency of the Federal government shutdown that began that day were tolled.
Comments on the proposed procedural schedule will be due November 20, 2025.

Materials submitted during the shutdown should not be resubmitted. All filings submitted during the shutdown will be considered filed on November 13, 2025, provided all filing requirements have been met.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Comments on the Board's proposed procedural schedule due by November 20, 2025. All filings submitted during the federal government shutdown (October 1 - November 13, 2025) are deemed filed on November 13, 2025 and should not be resubmitted.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This order resets the procedural clock for the entire merger proceeding. It establishes November 20, 2025 as a hard deadline for all parties and intervenors to comment on the Board's proposed procedural schedule (which was originally due October 16, 2025 but was tolled). The Board's procedural schedule will govern discovery deadlines, hearing preparation, testimony deadlines, and all subsequent phases of this major railroad merger review. The clarification that shutdown filings are deemed filed on November 13, 2025 prevents duplicative submissions and ensures the Board has a clean record of submissions. This decision is critical for all participants in the proceeding to understand their compliance obligations going forward.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Comments on the Board's proposed procedural schedule due to STB

docket_entries.title: STB Leadership Response to Senate Letter on UP-NS Merger
docket_entries.entry_summary: STB Chairman Fuchs, Vice Chairman Schultz, and Board Member Hedlund respond to a bipartisan Senate letter (signed by 19 senators including Klobuchar, Duckworth, Ernst, Durbin, Wicker, and others) expressing concern about merger impacts on agricultural supply chain, long-term competition, and efficient rail service. The Board assures senators that "should a merger application be filed, the Surface Transportation Board (STB or Board) will conduct a rigorous and comprehensive review of the transaction as required by law." The Board confirms it has already issued an information request requiring UP and NS to submit "100% traffic tapes for six previous years, timetables, track charts, geospatial information system maps, joint facility information, and summary information concerning interchange commitments." Applicants indicated intent to file by January 29, 2026. The Board commits to examining "potential competitive effects, economic efficiencies, service effects, environmental impacts, and other critical considerations, including safety integration planning," with opportunities for public participation. The response signals the Board will apply rigorous scrutiny to competitive impacts and service effects, directly addressing the senators' core concerns about supply chain disruption and competition preservation.
key_arguments: STB will conduct 'rigorous and comprehensive review' of merger 'as required by law' - establishing heightened review standard from Board leadership

Board will examine 'potential competitive effects, economic efficiencies, service effects, environmental impacts, and other critical considerations, including safety integration planning' - specifying analytical scope beyond traditional merger analysis

Applicants must submit detailed competitive data including '100% traffic tapes for six previous years' and 'interchange commitments—agreements that limit or may limit interchange with connecting carriers' - signaling Board focus on competitive constraint analysis
Board commits to 'opportunities for public participation and comment' in review process - establishing intervenor access and evidentiary record development
key_excerpts: the Surface Transportation Board (STB or Board) will conduct a rigorous and comprehensive review of the transaction as required by law

The Board's review will include a rigorous examination of potential competitive effects, economic efficiencies, service effects, environmental impacts, and other critical considerations, including safety integration planning

Among other things, the Board ordered applicants to submit 100% traffic tapes for six previous years, timetables, track charts, geospatial information system maps, joint facility information, and summary information concerning interchange commitments—agreements that limit or may limit interchange with connecting carriers
docket_entries.relief_requested: No relief requested. STB confirms it will conduct rigorous review consistent with statutory requirements if application is filed.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This is an official STB statement of review scope and methodology that will frame the evidentiary record and burden allocation in the merger proceeding. The Board's explicit commitment to examining 'competitive effects' and 'service effects' combined with the detailed information requests for traffic data and interchange agreements suggests the Board is preparing to conduct detailed competitive analysis. The reference to 'safety integration planning' as a 'critical consideration' may establish a new or elevated evidentiary burden on applicants to address operational integration risks. The statement does not prejudge the application but establishes that congressional concerns about agricultural supply chain disruption and competition preservation will receive explicit Board attention.
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response required; this is a Board statement of procedural and analytical intent. Applicants have indicated intent to file application by January 29, 2026.

docket_entries.title: STB Chairman Fuchs Response to Rep. Kiley Letter on UP/NS Merger - Procedural Acknowledgment
docket_entries.entry_summary: STB Chairman Patrick J. Fuchs responds to Representative Kevin Kiley's letter regarding the UP/NS merger. The Chairman confirms that UP and NS submitted a notice of intent on July 30, 2025, with an application deadline of January 29, 2026. He states that 'because this is a pending matter, I cannot comment further' but assures Rep. Kiley that 'the Board will conduct a thorough and fair review of the evidence and argument and consider whether the transaction serves the public interest, consistent with applicable law.' The letter places Rep. Kiley's original correspondence in the public docket and provides contact information for the Board's Office of Public Assistance.
key_arguments: The Board will conduct a thorough and fair review of the merger application when filed, evaluating evidence and argument to determine whether the transaction serves the public interest under applicable law
key_excerpts: I cannot comment further; however, please be assured that, should an application to merge be filed, the Board will conduct a thorough and fair review of the evidence and argument and consider whether the transaction serves the public interest, consistent with applicable law.
docket_entries.relief_requested: No substantive relief requested. Chairman acknowledges Rep. Kiley's letter and commits Board to 'thorough and fair review' of merger application consistent with applicable law.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Minimal. This is a standard administrative response establishing that the Board's merger review process under 49 U.S.C. § 11324 and 49 C.F.R. part 1180 will proceed. No new legal standards, burden allocations, or procedural requirements are introduced. The Chairman's statement that the Board will apply the 'public interest' standard reflects existing statutory language but provides no guidance on its application to this specific merger.
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response deadline. UP/NS application deadline remains January 29, 2026.

docket_entries.title: Coalition of Nine State Attorneys General Opposes UP/NS Merger as Threatening Competition, Prices, and National Security
docket_entries.filer_name: State Attorneys General Coalition (TN, KS, FL, MS, IA, MT, ND, SD, OH)
docket_entries.entry_summary: Nine state attorneys general jointly oppose the UP/NS merger as creating 'undue market concentration that stifles competition' resulting in 'higher prices, lower reliability, and less innovation' for manufacturers and consumers. They argue the merger 'could compromise our national security' by increasing shipping costs that 'kneecap American companies' ability to compete with foreign manufacturers' and create 'inflationary pressure on household budgets.' They invoke the statutory standard that mergers must be 'consistent with the public interest' and STB regulations requiring that 'mergers serve the public interest only when substantial and demonstrable gains...outweigh any anticompetitive effects.' Their core framing is that consolidation in an already-consolidated rail industry (states note 'as the railroads have consolidated, many shippers have seen rail service suffer while costs have increased dramatically') will worsen existing problems. They condition their opposition on the STB's ability to satisfy four specific requirements: the merger must 'clearly enhance competition, improve service for rail customers, preserve accountability, and advance safety.' They frame opposition through a Trump Administration lens, arguing approval would 'undermine the President's policies to unleash American energy, curb anti-competitive regulations, and prevent monopolistic behavior.' This is a sophisticated opposition framing that: (1) focuses on economic harm to domestic industry and consumers rather than state parochial interests; (2) cites the actual statutory/regulatory standards; (3) provides conditional relief pathways; (4) attempts to align with stated executive branch priorities; and (5) identifies specific stakeholder classes (farmers, workers, manufacturers, consumers) likely to generate consumer/constituency pressure.
key_arguments: The proposed merger will result in 'undue market concentration that stifles competition and therefore creates higher prices, lower reliability, and less innovation at the expense of America's manufacturers and, ultimately, America's consumers.'

Historical railroad consolidation has already harmed shippers: 'as the railroads have consolidated, many shippers have seen rail service suffer while costs have increased dramatically. Further freight rail consolidation could make these problems worse.'

The merger threatens national security and economic competitiveness: 'high internal shipping costs kneecap American companies' ability to compete with foreign manufacturers. The downstream impact of the merger poses significant risk not just for our industrial base but also our agricultural producers. Ultimately, then, this merger could compromise our national security.'

The merger will create inflationary pressure on consumers: 'increased monopolistic power does not stifle innovation and productivity in industry, put inflationary pressure on household budgets, or otherwise throttle the economy as a whole.'

Approval would contradict President Trump's executive orders: 'A merger that fails to meet these standards would be inconsistent with President Trump's Executive Orders aimed at promoting American prosperity...A merger against the public interest would undermine the President's policies to unleash American energy, curb anti-competitive regulations, and prevent monopolistic behavior.'
key_excerpts: An America First economy will not work if high internal shipping costs kneecap American companies' ability to compete with foreign manufacturers.
As the railroads have consolidated, many shippers have seen rail service suffer while costs have increased dramatically. Further freight rail consolidation could make these problems worse.

Mergers serve the public interest only when substantial and demonstrable gains in important public benefits—such as improved service and safety, enhanced competition, and greater economic efficiency—outweigh any anticompetitive effects, potential service disruptions, or other merger-related harms.
No approval should be granted unless the merger clearly enhances competition, improves service for rail customers, preserves accountability, and advances safety.
docket_entries.relief_requested: The STB should conduct 'a thorough and exacting review' and deny approval unless the merger 'clearly enhances competition, improves service for rail customers, preserves accountability, and advances safety.' Approval should only be granted if 'substantial and demonstrable gains in important public benefits...outweigh any anticompetitive effects, potential service disruptions, or other merger-related harms.'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing invokes the statutory merger standard (49 U.S.C. § 11324 'consistent with the public interest') and explicitly cites STB merger regulations (49 C.F.R § 1180.1(c)) requiring 'substantial and demonstrable gains in important public benefits' to outweigh anticompetitive effects. It attempts to frame the merger review within the Trump Administration's stated competition and deregulation agenda, which could influence STB board members' weighing of policy considerations. The national security framing (rare in merger comments) could trigger interagency coordination requirements or shift the evidentiary burden to require UP to affirmatively demonstrate offsetting public benefits. The coordination by nine state AGs signals potential state-level antitrust or regulatory intervention if the merger is approved.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Comment period deadline (date depends on STB's established comment window; this filing is dated November 14, 2025, suggesting it was filed during an open comment period)

docket_entries.title: NGFA Procedural Comments: Challenge to Accelerated Schedule & Request for 15-Day Extensions
docket_entries.entry_summary: NGFA objects to the Board's proposed procedural schedule, arguing it violates the statutory mandate of 49 U.S.C. §11325(b)(3) requiring the Board to 'conclude the evidentiary phase of a major merger proceeding within 12 months.' NGFA contends the proposed schedule 'cuts the time for stakeholder input by approximately three months' and is 'a full four months shy of the 12-month statutory period.' NGFA characterizes this as the 'most consequential railroad merger the STB has ever considered' and emphasizes 'The Board's consideration of the Applicants' proposal pursuant to regulations that have never before been applied will have huge ramifications for the railroad industry, the agricultural industry, and the United States' and global economies.' NGFA requests 15-day extensions to both the evidence submission deadline and the response/rebuttal deadline, arguing this adds '30 days to the schedule for building the evidentiary record, while still leaving room for any additional extensions.' NGFA additionally opposes the Applicants' counter-proposal to further compress the schedule by 45 days, asserting that doing so would 'unfairly shorten the time for all parties of record to file submissions' and that early discovery requests by some parties should not justify across-the-board schedule compression. NGFA's position signals it intends to participate actively in the proceeding and expects substantial discovery and written advocacy.
key_arguments: The proposed procedural schedule violates statutory requirements: 'The Board is required to conclude the evidentiary phase of a major merger proceeding within 12 months of the date it provides notice of acceptance of a merger application. 49 U.S.C. §11325(b)(3). The Board then has 90 days to issue a final decision.' The Board's schedule 'is a full four months shy of the 12-month statutory period.'

The magnitude of the merger demands maximum statutory time: 'In many respects, the proposed merger of UP and NS will be the most consequential railroad merger the STB has ever considered. The Board's consideration of the Applicants' proposal pursuant to regulations that have never before been applied will have huge ramifications for the railroad industry, the agricultural industry, and the United States' and global economies.'

The proposed schedule is compounded by holiday interference: 'should Applicants file their Application in late November or early December, stakeholder review of the Application and any related activity such as discovery will be further shortened and otherwise affected by the 2025 Holiday Season.'

Applicants' further compression proposal is unjustified and inequitable: 'shortening these time periods would unfairly shorten the time for all parties of record to file such submissions' and 'the fact that a few parties may have commenced seeking discovery from Applicants at this very early stage of the process is not grounds for reducing the time allowed to all other parties of record.'

The Board must 'use the maximum time allotted to it by statute for consideration of the proposed merger' and 'summarily reject the Applicants' proposal to substantially reduce the evidentiary phase of the proceeding.'
key_excerpts: In many respects, the proposed merger of UP and NS will be the most consequential railroad merger the STB has ever considered. The Board's consideration of the Applicants' proposal pursuant to regulations that have never before been applied will have huge ramifications for the railroad industry, the agricultural industry, and the United States' and global economies.

The Board is required to conclude the evidentiary phase of a major merger proceeding within 12 months of the date it provides notice of acceptance of a merger application. 49 U.S.C. §11325(b)(3)... the NGFA objects to the Board's proposal to establish a deadline for the submission of written evidence and argument that is a full four months shy of the 12-month statutory period.
Even generously allowing 30 days for the Board to announce and hold a public hearing, the proposed schedule would cut the time for stakeholder input by approximately three months.

should Applicants file their Application in late November or early December, stakeholder review of the Application and any related activity such as discovery will be further shortened and otherwise affected by the 2025 Holiday Season.

shortening these time periods would unfairly shorten the time for all parties of record to file such submissions... the fact that a few parties may have commenced seeking discovery from Applicants at this very early stage of the process is not grounds for reducing the time allowed to all other parties.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Extend the proposed deadline for submission of written evidence and argument by 15 days; extend the deadline for responses to comments and rebuttal by an additional 15 days (30 days total); reject Applicants' proposal to shorten the procedural schedule by 45 days.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: NGFA raises a substantive statutory interpretation issue regarding Board compliance with 49 U.S.C. §11325(b)(3). The filing potentially constrains the Board's procedural discretion by invoking a mandatory statutory floor (12-month evidentiary phase). If NGFA's statutory reading is correct, the Board's proposed schedule may be vulnerable to challenge or may need reformation. The filing also signals that major shipper constituencies will contest accelerated procedures, which may influence the Board's final schedule adoption. Additionally, NGFA's objection to Applicants' compression proposal flags early procedural maneuvering by the parties that could become a recurring point of contention. The statutory argument (if endorsed by Board or other intervenors) could establish precedent for future major merger proceedings under the new RETE Act framework.
docket_entries.deadline_description: This is a comment on a Notice of Proposed Procedural Schedule (Decision No. 5). No specific response deadline stated, but Board will likely issue final procedural schedule in near term.
