docket_entries.title: FRCA Comments on Proposed Procedural Schedule - Demand for Maximum Timeline, Opposition to UP-NS Expedited Review
docket_entries.entry_summary: FRCA opposes Union Pacific's request to accelerate the procedural schedule and truncate the comment period by 15 days. FRCA argues: (1) The UP-NS merger is 'the largest, by far, in terms of affected traffic volumes, geographic scope, revenue dollars, and market share' and 'the first under the Board's new merger rules,' requiring maximum procedural time, not acceleration; (2) UP's characterization of the merger as 'purely end-to-end' with 'only a small number of 2:1 locations' and 'not present[ing] any complex competitive or operating issues' grossly misreads the new merger rules and ignores core competitive harms: 'market foreclosure, coordinated effects, downstream effects, market concentration, competition reduction, rate increases, and service impairment and disruption'; (3) The critical unanswered question is whether cost savings 'will be passed through or pocketed by the carrier' and whether the merger will 'continue and exacerbate the trend of the past twenty years for railroads to increase their rates in excess of cost increases and reduce their operating ratios and capital investment as a percentage of revenues with the concomitant loss of volume and deterioration of service'; (4) UP's record on common carrier obligations, capacity investment, service reliability, and regulatory compliance is poor (citing multiple STB and enforcement proceedings); (5) UP cannot simultaneously claim credit for merger benefits in an application not yet filed while criticizing others for raising concerns; (6) UP's suggestion that 'shippers...will or can benefit from the merger' is premature and unsubstantiated. FRCA signals willingness to accept merger IF conditions address rate discipline, cost passthrough, investment mandates, and competitive mitigation—making opposition conditional rather than absolute.
key_arguments: UP-NS merger is 'the most significant ever brought before the Board' with 'the largest, by far, in terms of affected traffic volumes, geographic scope, revenue dollars, and market share' and as the first proceeding under new merger rules, it requires maximum procedural timeline, not acceleration

UP's depiction of merger as 'purely end-to-end' with only 'a small number of 2:1 locations' and 'not present[ing] any complex competitive or operating issues' misreads the new merger rules; the transaction carries 'most potential harm in terms of market foreclosure, coordinated effects, downstream effects, market concentration, competition reduction, rate increases, and service impairment and disruption'
The fundamental unknown is whether cost savings and efficiencies 'will be passed through or pocketed by the carrier'—central to whether shippers will actually benefit

20-year industry trend shows railroads 'increase their rates in excess of cost increases and reduce their operating ratios and capital investment as a percentage of revenues with the concomitant loss of volume and deterioration of service'; no reason to believe UP-NS merger reverses this trend
UP has poor compliance record on common carrier obligations, capacity investment, service provision, and regulatory candor, including embargoes, emergency service failures, and shipper disputes
UP cannot claim credit for merger benefits in an application not yet filed while simultaneously criticizing others for raising concerns about that same unfiled application

UP's claim of 'broad support' for merger is based on review of an application 'yet to be submitted' and may reflect undisclosed representations, considerations, or 'suggestions or threats of retaliation' to obtain support

Reduced competition among Class I railroads—the core problem in the industry—will be exacerbated, not remedied, by this merger; UP's suggestion that 'regional counterpart should find its own merger partner' demonstrates disregard for shipper interests and ignores whether shippers 'will or can benefit from the merger'
key_excerpts: 'The UP-NS merger application will be the first under the Board's "new" merger rules and, not coincidentally, the most significant ever brought before the Board. It will be the largest, by far, in terms of affected traffic volumes, geographic scope, revenue dollars, and market share, among other measures. It necessarily carries the most potential harm in terms of market foreclosure, coordinated effects, downstream effects, market concentration, competition reduction, rate increases, and service impairment and disruption.'

'UP's efforts in its filing and elsewhere to depict the merger as purely end-to-end, requiring regulatory treatment of only a small number of 2:1 locations, and "not present[ing] any complex competitive or operating issues," represent a gross misreading of the new merger rules and the concerns that led to their adoption.'

'UP's not unrelated suggestion on its recent earnings call that its regional counterpart should find its own merger partner completely ignores key considerations whether shippers, including the carload shippers that are FRCA members, will or can benefit from the merger, whether the cost savings and efficiencies, if any, will be passed through or pocketed by the carrier, and whether the merger will continue and exacerbate the trend of the past twenty years for railroads to increase their rates in excess of cost increases and reduce their operating ratios and capital investment as a percentage of revenues with the concomitant loss of volume and deterioration of service.'

'Much of the current trouble in the industry flows from a lack of competition that in turn results from excess concentration. There is no good reason to think, especially based on what UP has said to date, that the UP-NS merger will stem, much less reverse, the established trend, and every reason to think that the merger will instead result in more of the same, particularly reduced competition among the few remaining Class I railroads.'

'UP improperly claims credit for work on and/or the substance of an application it has not yet filed, even as it criticizes others for taking positions or raising concerns regarding the merger because that same application has not been filed. UP cannot have it both ways.'
'FRCA/NCTA understand UP to have indicated that it is not in shippers' best interests to oppose the merger.' [Signals potential intimidation/retaliation threats]
docket_entries.relief_requested: FRCA requests: (1) Rejection of Union Pacific's proposal to shorten the procedural schedule and reduce comment period by 15 days; (2) Adoption of the longest procedural schedule permitted by statute; (3) If Board approves merger, conditions addressing: (a) passthrough of cost savings to shippers, (b) rate discipline and limits on increases exceeding cost growth, (c) capital investment commitments as percentage of revenues, (d) service level guarantees, (e) mitigation of market foreclosure and competitive concentration effects
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing challenges the procedural framework itself under the Board's newly adopted merger rules (49 U.S.C. § 11324). FRCA's argument that the new rules require substantive competitive review of coordinated effects, market foreclosure, and downstream harms—not just 2:1 overlap locations—could establish interpretive precedent for how the Board applies its updated merger standards. The retaliation/intimidation allegation ('UP indicated it is not in shippers' best interests to oppose') raises potential procedural safeguard issues and may trigger Board inquiry into ex parte communications. FRCA's explicit conditions (cost passthrough, rate discipline, investment mandates) foreshadow the types of behavioral remedies that may be required if merger is approved. The filing also creates record evidence of pre-application activity by UP that may be used in later discovery disputes.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Union Pacific likely to respond to procedural schedule challenge; Board will issue procedural order establishing final schedule before discovery commences

docket_entries.title: Multi-State Legislative Leaders' Letter Opposing UP-NS Merger on Competition and Economic Grounds
docket_entries.filer_name: State Legislative Leaders Coalition (46 legislators from 23 states)
docket_entries.entry_summary: A coalition of 46 Republican state legislative leaders from 23 states opposes the UP-NS merger, arguing it would create an impermissible concentration of rail market power with severe consequences for consumers, manufacturers, farmers, and workers. The signatories contend that a combined UP-NS system would control 'nearly 45 percent of all U.S. rail tonnage' and hold 'dominant market share in critical commodity sectors including chemicals, metals, lumber, motor vehicles and equipment, crushed stone, sand and gravel, food and kindred products, and iron and steel scrap.' They argue: 'Reduced competition in these areas will inevitably lead to higher prices and fewer choices,' and warn that 'many shippers would face limited or no viable rail alternatives at origin or destination, creating a new generation of captive customers.' The letter further contends that 'past mergers have shown that integration challenges can lead to widespread service disruptions, with ripple effects across the entire rail network,' and that 'the risks of operational breakdowns and supply chain instability are real and significant' given the merger spans 50,000 route miles across 43 states. The signatories frame this as having implications for America's competitiveness with China and the viability of state economies. While the closing language urges the Board to 'ensure that any approved transaction clearly enhances freight rail competition,' the overall framing is one of fundamental opposition rather than conditional support.
key_arguments: The combined UP-NS system would control nearly 45 percent of all U.S. rail tonnage and hold dominant market share in chemicals, metals, lumber, motor vehicles, crushed stone, sand and gravel, food and kindred products, and iron and steel scrap—commodities that directly affect consumer prices, housing costs, energy costs, and food costs for American families.

Reduced competition from the merger will 'inevitably lead to higher prices and fewer choices' for consumers and businesses, creating 'a new generation of captive customers' with 'limited or no viable rail alternatives at origin or destination,' which would be 'especially harmful to smaller communities and businesses that depend on reliable rail access.'

The merger could 'negatively affect America's ability to compete with China' and 'pose significant risks for the industrial and agricultural production that powers state economies and the broader American manufacturing base.'

Integration challenges in past mergers have caused 'widespread service disruptions with ripple effects across the entire rail network,' and the proposed merger's span of 50,000 route miles across 43 states creates 'real and significant' risks of 'operational breakdowns and supply chain instability.'

The merger threatens innovation and productivity across American industry, creates 'inflationary pressure on household budgets,' and imposes broader 'costs of this merger' on the economy as a whole through monopolistic power.
key_excerpts: If approved, the combined UP-NS system would control nearly 45 percent of all U.S. rail tonnage and hold dominant market share in critical commodity sectors including chemicals, metals, lumber, motor vehicles and equipment, crushed stone, sand and gravel, food and kindred products, and iron and steel scrap. These commodities directly affect the cost of consumer goods, housing, energy, and food—core expenses for American families and small businesses. Reduced competition in these areas will inevitably lead to higher prices and fewer choices.

Many shippers would face limited or no viable rail alternatives at origin or destination, creating a new generation of captive customers. This loss of routing flexibility and competitive pressure would be especially harmful to smaller communities and businesses that depend on reliable rail access to stay competitive in national and global markets.

Past mergers have shown that integration challenges can lead to widespread service disruptions, with ripple effects across the entire rail network. The proposed UP-NS merger spans 50,000 route miles across 43 states, and the risks of operational breakdowns and supply chain instability are real and significant.

It is vital that the STB use its process to fully consider how this merger will affect all stakeholders, including workers, manufacturers, farmers, and consumers, so that increased monopolistic power does not stifle innovation and productivity in industry, put inflationary pressure on household budgets, or otherwise burden the economy as a whole with the costs of this merger.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Deny approval of the merger. The letter states: 'We urge the Board to carefully evaluate this merger and ensure that any approved transaction clearly enhances freight rail competition, protects service quality, strengthens supply chains, improves safety, and supports a resilient freight rail system that works for all Americans.' The phrasing frames these as preconditions that cannot be met by the merger as proposed, not as conditions for conditional approval.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing introduces significant political economy considerations into the merger review. While the STB's primary mandate is competitive analysis under 49 U.S.C. § 11324, the coordinated intervention by 46 state legislative leaders across 23 states signals substantial political opposition and may influence the Board's framing of competitive effects, consumer impact, and the breadth of stakeholder harm. The filing emphasizes macroeconomic effects (inflation, consumer prices, competitiveness with China) rather than purely transportation market effects, potentially broadening the scope of 'public interest' considerations the Board must weigh. The letter does not propose specific conditions or remedies, suggesting the signatories view the merger as fundamentally problematic rather than remediable through conditions.
docket_entries.deadline_description: No specific response deadline indicated; this is an ex parte letter in the comment phase. Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern may respond through subsequent filings.

docket_entries.title: CXRG Petition to Compel Union Pacific to Include Walsenburg Interchange Commitment in Decision No. 3 Response
docket_entries.entry_summary: CXRG, a short-line railroad operating inherited restrictions on its interchange options, filed a petition challenging Union Pacific's refusal to disclose an interchange commitment at Walsenburg, Colorado as required by the Board's Decision No. 3. CXRG argues that Union Pacific imposed both a 'steel barrier' (physical control of the last 5 miles of track between CXRG's line and BNSF connection) and a 'paper barrier' (contractual ban on CXRG interchanging with BNSF) when it sold the Alamosa Subdivision to San Luis & Rio Grande in 2003. CXRG inherited these restrictions through bankruptcy acquisition in 2022. Union Pacific twice refused to include this in its interchange commitments list, first claiming CXRG has no physical connection to BNSF (only restricted trackage rights to UP), then arguing that granting limited trackage rights to track UP retained does not constitute an 'interchange commitment.' CXRG contends this clearly falls within the Board's definition of interchange commitment—'agreements that limit or may limit interchange with a third-party connecting carrier, whether by outright prohibition, per-car penalty, adjustment in financial terms, positive economic inducement or other means'—specifically the 'outright prohibition' and 'other means' categories. CXRG argues that 'conditioning the sale of a Class 1 railroad line to a short line on (1) physically preventing it from interchanging with a third-party connecting carrier; and then also on (2) contractually preventing it from interchanging with a third-party railroad by granting limited overhead trackage rights that may only be used to interchange with the selling railroad, falls within the "outright prohibition" category.' CXRG emphasizes that the Board's interchange commitment disclosure rules (49 C.F.R. §1150.33(h)) exist to identify anticompetitive restrictions, and that 'elimination of anti-competitive interchange commitments, particularly ones that have been in existence for many years, could provide one means to enhance competition post-merger.' This dispute has significant implications for the merger analysis because it challenges whether UP and NS have made complete disclosures, and because it identifies specific arrangements the Board should consider when evaluating anticompetitive effects and potential remedies.
key_arguments: The restrictions on CXRG—both physical (UP's retained track blocking BNSF connection) and contractual (prohibition on BNSF interchange)—constitute an 'interchange commitment' under 49 C.F.R. §1180.4(g)(3)(i) and Decision No. 3's definition, specifically falling within 'outright prohibition' and 'other means' categories

Union Pacific's argument that restrictions on trackage rights are not 'interchange commitments' is a semantic evasion: conditioning a line sale on preventing future BNSF interchange is precisely the kind of restriction the Board's disclosure rules target

The existence of anticompetitive interchange commitments is material to the merger analysis because 'elimination of anti-competitive interchange commitments, particularly ones that have been in existence for many years, could provide one means to enhance competition post-merger'

UP's refusal to disclose appears inconsistent with prior Board precedent recognizing that 'parties should expect a higher level of scrutiny on agreements that contain a total ban on interchange with other carriers'
CXRG's disclosure of the restriction in its own exemption filing (showing transparency) contrasts with UP's refusal, suggesting UP is attempting to conceal material information from the merger review
CN (a competing railroad) had already flagged this omission in its October 6, 2025 letter identifying missing interchange commitments, lending credibility to CXRG's complaint of incomplete disclosure
key_excerpts: Union Pacific twice refusing to include on its list of interchange commitments certain restrictions imposed on CXRG on tracks owned and operated by CXRG in Walsenburg, Colorado. The interchange commitment at issue is comprised of both a 'steel' barrier (where Union Pacific sold its line but retained physical possession of the last few miles of track between the conveyed tracks and an interchange with a third-party railroad – BNSF Railway Company ('BNSF')) and a 'paper' barrier (where Union Pacific has imposed a contractual ban on CXRG from interchanging with BNSF).

Conditioning the sale of a Class 1 railroad line to a short line on (1) physically preventing it from interchanging with a third-party connecting carrier; and then also on (2) contractually preventing it from interchanging with a third-party railroad by granting limited overhead trackage rights that may only be used to interchange with the selling railroad, falls within the 'outright prohibition' category of §1180.4(g)(3)(i).

Union Pacific's confirmation to CN that it had contractually prohibited SLRG's—and now CXRG's—ability to interchange with any carrier other than Union Pacific at Walsenburg is an admission that it created an interchange commitment recognized by the Board in the form of 'a total ban on interchange with any carrier other than the seller or lessor.'

[UP stated] 'we do not believe that these transactions – in which Union Pacific gave SLRG additional limited rights to access track retained by Union Pacific – involve an interchange commitment as defined in Decision No. 3.' [But CXRG counters:] Union Pacific's strained efforts to claim otherwise fail.

A complete list of each railroad's interchange commitments is a valuable category of information, particularly when the regulations that will be applied to analyze the proposed merger are geared toward finding ways to enhance competition between railroads and for railroad shippers going forward. The elimination of anti-competitive interchange commitments, particularly ones that have been in existence for many years, could provide one means to enhance competition post-merger.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Direct Union Pacific to supplement its response to Decision No. 3 by adding the Walsenburg, Colorado interchange commitment involving CXRG to Union Pacific's list of interchange commitments. In the alternative, the Board should itself add the Walsenburg interchange commitment to the list of Union Pacific interchange commitments in response to this Petition.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This petition directly implicates the Board's information-gathering authority under Decision No. 3 and raises questions about the adequacy and accuracy of mandatory merger disclosures. It clarifies the scope of 'interchange commitment' as defined in 49 C.F.R. §1150.33(h) and §1180.4(g)(3)(i)—specifically whether agreements restricting access to third-party carriers through a combination of physical control and contractual limitations fall within the definition. The dispute may establish precedent on whether UP and NS can use semantic arguments ('trackage rights' vs. 'interchange commitment') to avoid disclosure of economically restrictive arrangements. Additionally, CXRG's arguments suggest the Board should consider elimination of existing interchange commitments as a potential competitive remedy in the merger approval. The filing raises the broader issue of whether the applicants have made complete disclosures—CN also identified missing interchange commitments for both UP and NS in its October 6, 2025 letter. If CXRG prevails, it may trigger further supplemental disclosure obligations and could inform the Board's competitive effects analysis.
docket_entries.deadline_description: No explicit deadline stated in the petition; however, as a motion to compel supplementation, the Board will likely establish a response deadline in any ruling.

docket_entries.title: US Army Transportation Command Notice of Intent to Participate
docket_entries.entry_summary: ARTRANS filed a notice of intent to participate in the UP/NS merger proceeding on behalf of the Department of War and U.S. Transportation Command. The Army states it has 'an interest in ensuring continued, adequate rail service to meet the needs of national defense' and is participating through its Railroads for National Defense program. The filing cites statutory authority under 49 C.F.R. § 1180.1(l). ARTRANS requests placement on the service list but does not indicate support or opposition to the merger at this stage. The filing suggests the Army will monitor the proceeding and may raise national defense-related issues in future submissions, potentially concerning military transportation capacity, continuity of service, or strategic rail corridor access.
key_arguments: ARTRANS has a federal interest in ensuring the merger does not impair 'continued, adequate rail service to meet the needs of national defense'
Military transportation requirements represent a distinct statutory consideration in rail merger review under 49 C.F.R. § 1180.1(l)
key_excerpts: ARTRANS, through the Railroads for National Defense program, has an interest in ensuring continued, adequate rail service to meet the needs of national defense in accordance with 49 C.F.R. § 1180.1(l) and other applicable laws and regulations.
On behalf of the Department of War and U.S. Transportation Command, ARTRANS...requests the undersigned be placed on the service list for filings in this proceeding.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Service on the service list for all filings in this proceeding
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing invokes 49 C.F.R. § 1180.1(l), which requires the STB to consider defense transportation needs in merger review. ARTRANS's participation may expand the evidentiary scope beyond typical economic competition factors to include military logistics, strategic corridor protection, and defense industrial base rail access. If ARTRANS later files substantive comments, it could introduce novel legal arguments about national security that the Board must address under its statutory obligations.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response deadline; procedural notice of intent to participate

docket_entries.title: SMART-TD Statement in Support for UP-NS Merger with Historic Job Protection Agreement
docket_entries.entry_summary: SMART-TD, representing the nation's largest railroad union, filed a statement of support for the UP-NS merger on November 19, 2025, based on a historic September 2025 agreement with Union Pacific. The union emphasizes: 'While a unified, transcontinental railroad has the potential to support sustained investment in infrastructure, expand network capacity, and improve service reliability, past mergers have not always delivered greater job security or long-term stability for railroad workers.' SMART-TD and Union Pacific negotiated an unprecedented job protection commitment: 'Union Pacific guaranteed these employees job protection for the length of their careers following the transaction, committing that these employees of both Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern will not face involuntary furloughs.' This agreement applies to train and yardmaster service employees. SMART-TD frames the settlement as a model for future transactions: 'It demonstrates that genuine engagement between labor and management can produce solutions that support operational goals while safeguarding the livelihoods of the employees who make rail service possible.' The union acknowledges regulatory review is essential and 'respectfully encourage[s] the Board to consider the significance of these job-protection commitments and the stability they provide to thousands of working railroaders and their families.' SMART-TD explicitly requests the Board weigh these commitments in its public interest analysis and has indicated commitment to safe, lawful execution of the merger.
key_arguments: The merged UP-NS will have potential to support sustained investment in infrastructure, expand network capacity, and improve service reliability - benefits that depend on labor stability

This agreement provides unprecedented job protection in modern rail consolidations: guaranteed career-length employment with no involuntary furloughs for train and yardmaster service employees from both railroads
Past mergers have failed to deliver job security; this agreement specifically addresses that historical failure pattern and provides stability for thousands of workers and their families
The settlement demonstrates a model where major transactions can proceed with genuine labor-management engagement that safeguards workforce livelihoods while supporting operational goals
Board should weigh job-protection commitments as part of public interest analysis under merger review standards
key_excerpts: 'Union Pacific guaranteed these employees job protection for the length of their careers following the transaction, committing that these employees of both Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern will not face involuntary furloughs. This commitment is unprecedented in modern rail consolidations.'

'It demonstrates that genuine engagement between labor and management can produce solutions that support operational goals while safeguarding the livelihoods of the employees who make rail service possible.'
'SMART-TD respectfully encourage[s] the Board to consider the significance of these job-protection commitments and the stability they provide to thousands of working railroaders and their families.'
docket_entries.relief_requested: Approval of the proposed merger between Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern; encourage the Board to consider the significance of job-protection commitments and the stability they provide to railroad workers and their families
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Under 49 U.S.C. § 11324(b), the STB must consider the public interest in evaluating merger applications, including impacts on rail service and labor. SMART-TD's settlement demonstrates a negotiated resolution to labor opposition that historically has complicated merger reviews. The filing creates an explicit record that the nation's largest railroad union has evaluated this specific merger on labor criteria and found it acceptable conditional on the job protection agreement already executed. This removes a major category of public interest opposition and may influence the Board's discretionary balancing of merger benefits against harms. The union's characterization of the agreement as 'unprecedented' and 'a model for future transactions' signals industry recognition that this merger sets precedent for labor protections in consolidation.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Statement filed in comment phase; no response deadline indicated

docket_entries.title: ASLRRA Notice of Intent to Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.entry_summary: ASLRRA filed a notice of intent to participate without substantive comment. The association represents short line and regional railroad members nationally and advocates for policies promoting "a strong regional and short line rail component for the national transportation infrastructure." The filing seeks placement on the service list to enable participation as "its interests may appear." No position on the merger is stated, no conditions are requested, and no arguments are presented. This is a procedural notice preserving ASLRRA's right to intervene substantively in later phases of the proceeding.
key_excerpts: ASLRRA is a national trade association representing the interests of short line and regional railroad members in legislative and regulatory matters.
ASLRRA advocates for enlightened public policies which promote a strong regional and short line rail component for the national transportation infrastructure.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Placement on service list to participate in the proceeding
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing preserves ASLRRA's right to participate in discovery, hearing phases, and settlement discussions. Short lines often rely on interchange relationships with Class I railroads; a UP/NS merger could affect intermodal flows, switching requirements, or competitive access. ASLRRA's participation creates an additional stakeholder voice on supply-side competitive impacts.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.deadline_description: Procedural notice only; no response deadline. ASLRRA is now on the service list.

Attorney Kent A. Gardiner from Crowell & Moring enters his appearance on behalf of CSXT to receive all future pleadings and orders in the proceeding.
key_excerpts: Kent A. Gardiner notices his appearance in the above-captioned proceeding on behalf of CSX Transportation, Inc. ("CSXT"). He is authorized to represent CSXT and asks to receive all future pleadings and orders in this proceeding via the email address appearing below.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)

docket_entries.title: CSX Transportation Notice of Appearance
docket_entries.entry_summary: CSX Transportation filed a Notice of Appearance through counsel Luke van Houwel ingen at Crowell & Moring to formally participate in the proceeding. The appearance notification indicates CSX intends to monitor the proceeding and preserve its right to participate in later phases (comments, hearing, etc.), consistent with the competitive interest of a major railroad that would be directly affected by a UP-NS combination. docket_entries.title: Public Comment on UP-NS Merger - Houston East End Community Opposition
docket_entries.entry_summary: Community leader from Houston's East End opposes the Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern merger due to severe impacts from train blockages on emergency response, school access, and quality of life. While not seeking outright denial, Williams demands comprehensive conditions including full public hearings, traffic projections, operational accountability measures, and mandatory grade separations before merger approval.
key_arguments: Current train blockages already exceed 6 hours per day, with first responder arrival times over 11 minutes (double national average)
Children and mothers documented crawling under stopped trains to access schools due to prolonged blockages
Houston Fire Department reported 905 delayed emergency responses in 2019, increasing to nearly 1,400 by 2021
Merger will add 10% volume growth by 2030 to already inadequate infrastructure unchanged in 100 years
East End submits more blocked-crossing reports to FRA than any other region nationally
Union Pacific has been disingenuous about merger impacts while claiming safety initiatives
key_excerpts: These children are crawling under trains because: It is often the only way they will eat that day—they cannot miss their free breakfast at school.
What I see are trains stopped—constantly—blocking the same crossings for hours at a time while children risk their lives to access food and education.
Your decision will determine whether a baby's death in 2023 will be followed by more preventable tragedies.
Union Pacific cannot claim these costs are prohibitive when they can donate $200 million to a White House ballroom and report billions in profit each quarter.

docket_entries.title: CSX Transportation Comments on Proposed Procedural Schedule for UP-NS Merger
docket_entries.entry_summary: CSX Transportation, a competing Class I railroad, filed comments opposing the abbreviated procedural schedule proposed by UP and NS for their merger review before the Surface Transportation Board. CSXT argues the schedule should be extended to the full statutory 12-month evidentiary period, should include post-hearing briefs, should not impose premature responsive application filing requirements, and should include discovery protocols and limitations on ex parte communications.
key_arguments: The proposed schedule is unprecedented and would be the first application of the Board's 2001 New Rules for major rail mergers in 25 years, warranting full statutory review period
UP itself previously argued in 2000 that the 12-month period was necessary to apply new merger rules, consider downstream effects, and review detailed service and market evidence

The abbreviated schedule fails to provide adequate time for non-applicants to meaningfully review and respond to a massive Application addressing complex issues like enhanced competition and downstream effects for the first time
UP and NS's pre-Application discovery responses consisted primarily of objections with minimal document production, demonstrating this period should not justify shortening post-filing timeframes
Using 2023 as the baseline year when 2024 data is available fails to capture significant market shifts, volume growth, operational improvements, and industry disruptions
The schedule should include clear limitations on ex parte communications (one hour-long meeting per party with each Board member within 30-60 days of principal submissions) to ensure fairness
A discovery protocol is essential to promptly resolve disputes in a proceeding of this scope and complexity
key_excerpts: This will be the first transaction reviewed under the New Rules since their adoption twenty-five years ago. The New Rules reflect a significant change in the way the Board will apply its statutory public interest test and place a high burden on applicants.

A massive transcontinental merger like this was precisely what the Board had in mind when it issued its New Rules, including its default schedule. No transaction like this has ever been proposed, nor have the New Rules yet been applied.
It remains as premature today to adopt an expedited schedule as it was in 2001.
Ensuring an adequate schedule will be vital to the Board's execution of its duty to determine whether the proposed UP/NS merger is in the public interest.

Applicants now propose, however, to cut 15 critical days from the already scant time non-applicants will have to digest, and then prepare comments, requests for conditions, and any responsive applications

docket_entries.title: DOJ Antitrust Division Notice of Intent to Participate
docket_entries.filer_name: U.S. Department of Justice, Antitrust Division
docket_entries.entry_summary: The U.S. Department of Justice, Antitrust Division, filed a Notice of Intent to Participate in the UP/NS merger proceeding on November 20, 2025. This is a procedural notice formally establishing DOJ's participation rights and adding two senior antitrust attorneys to the service list. The filing contains no substantive position on the merger itself—DOJ makes no argument for approval, denial, or conditions at this stage. However, the notice is highly significant because it signals that DOJ's antitrust experts are actively monitoring the proceeding and maintaining the option to file substantive comments, evidence, or recommendations as the proceeding develops. The assignment of Don Amlin and Russell Pittman (both from DOJ Antitrust Division headquarters at 450 Fifth Street) indicates this is not a routine review but active engagement by senior antitrust lawyers. DOJ has explicit statutory authority under 49 U.S.C. § 11326 to institute proceedings challenging railroad mergers if DOJ believes they would substantially lessen competition or tend to create a monopoly. This notice preserves that authority and signals DOJ's intent to exercise close oversight.
key_excerpts: The United States Department of Justice (DOJ) respectfully submits its Notice of Intent to Participate in the above-captioned proceeding as its interests may require
requests that the following additional DOJ representatives be placed on the service list for this proceeding
docket_entries.relief_requested: Notice of Intent to Participate in the proceeding and placement of DOJ Antitrust Division representatives (Don Amlin and Russell Pittman) on the service list for receipt of all documents.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing activates DOJ's substantive participation rights in the STB proceeding. Under 49 U.S.C. § 11326, DOJ has independent authority to challenge the merger if it determines the transaction would substantially lessen competition. DOJ's formal notice of intent to participate signals it is conducting parallel antitrust review and may file substantive evidence, testimony, or briefs opposing approval or proposing conditions. The presence of senior Antitrust Division attorneys on the service list indicates DOJ is preparing for substantive engagement, not merely monitoring. This is distinct from routine AG service-list notice; Antitrust Division involvement suggests DOJ may be evaluating whether to oppose the merger independently or coordinate with the STB on competitive analysis.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response deadline; this is a notice filing. DOJ participation rights are now formal, and DOJ may file substantive comments, evidence, or briefs on its own schedule.

docket_entries.title: National Industrial Transportation League Files Notice of Intent to Participate

The filing contains no position on the merger's merits, no substantive arguments, and no requested conditions. NITL is represented by counsel at Thompson Hine LLP. This is a standard procedural intervention notice and signals NITL's intent to monitor the proceeding and potentially file substantive comments or testimony later. As a shipper advocacy organization, NITL's eventual position will likely focus on impacts to transportation costs, service reliability, and competitive access for their members.
key_excerpts: The National Industrial Transportation League intends to participate in this proceeding as a party of record.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Intervention and participation in the proceeding as a party of record
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing establishes NITL's standing to participate in all subsequent phases of the proceeding, including discovery, hearing, and briefing. It places them on the service list and entitles them to receive all Board orders and filings. No substantive legal or regulatory questions are raised.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.deadline_description: None—this is a procedural notice requiring no response

docket_entries.title: Alliance for Chemical Distribution - Notice of Intent to Participate
docket_entries.entry_summary: The Alliance for Chemical Distribution filed a bare notice of intent to participate in the proceeding as a party of record on November 20, 2025. This is a procedural filing with no substantive argument, condition, or position statement. ACD represents chemical distribution companies that are customers of Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern. The filing is a limited entry into the record, typically followed by substantive comment or testimony. No indication of support, opposition, or specific concerns is provided in this document.
key_excerpts: The Alliance for Chemical Distribution intends to participate in this proceeding as a party of record.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Notice of intent to participate in proceeding as a party of record
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing formally establishes ACD as an intervenor in the proceeding, entitling it to receive service of documents, file comments and briefs, and potentially participate in discovery and hearing. As a shipper trade association, ACD's participation broadens the record to include customer/shipper perspectives. Its full substantive position will be determined in subsequent filings (comments, testimony, briefs).
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)

docket_entries.entry_summary: The Fertilizer Institute filed a notice of intent to participate as a party of record in the UP-NS merger proceeding. The filing contains no substantive arguments, positions, conditions, or relief requests—it is purely procedural notice that TFI intends to participate going forward. The filing is represented by Thompson Hine LLP counsel (Jason D. Tutrone and Richard M. Couch). As a major industrial shipper of fertilizer inputs via rail, TFI has potential interest in service, pricing, and network access impacts from consolidated UP-NS operations, but this filing does not yet reveal what positions TFI will take or what specific concerns may motivate its participation.
key_excerpts: The Fertilizer Institute intends to participate in this proceeding as a party of record.
docket_entries.relief_requested: None. Filing only states intent to participate as party of record.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing establishes TFI as a party of record in the proceeding, entitling it to receive service of documents, submit comments and testimony, and potentially participate in settlement discussions. However, it does not yet establish TFI's substantive position or evidentiary interests. Subsequent filings from TFI will be more substantively significant.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)

docket_entries.title: RBMN Procedural Schedule Comments: Request for 30-Day Extension of Discovery/Comment Deadlines
docket_entries.entry_summary: RBMN supports intervention based on substantial historical injury: severe operational disruption lasting 15+ years following the 1999 Conrail split (which created NS as RBMN's primary interchange partner). RBMN states: 'Given its past experience with a control proceeding involving its primary interchange partner, RBMN has concerns about the proposed Union Pacific Corporation and Union Pacific Railroad Company control of NS and intends to vigorously participate in the proceeding to ensure that history does not repeat itself and to ensure that any potential adverse effects are ameliorated or conditioned.' On the schedule, RBMN argues the Board's F+270 final brief deadline is inadequate: 'Parties participating in the proceeding will no doubt have to wade through and digest massive amounts of material presented in the application, the proposed safety integration plan as well as the environmental information provided by the applicants to determine what if any discovery is necessary and to formulate what relief may be necessary.' RBMN requests 30-day extension of comment (F+75→F+105) and response (F+120→F+150) deadlines, preserving Board's statutory 90-day post-hearing decision window. RBMN explicitly signals it will participate substantively to seek 'protection through responsive applications, comments or request for conditions'—flagging future conditional opposition.
key_arguments: RBMN and its customers experienced severe operational disruption lasting 15+ years following 1999 Conrail split to NS/CSX; identical control proceeding now threatens repeat injury because NS is now RBMN's primary interchange partner.

Transcontinental merger under new STB merger guidelines requires maximum discovery time permitted by statute (49 U.S.C. §11325(b)(3)): parties must digest 'massive amounts of material' in application, safety integration plan, and environmental filings to determine discovery needs and formulate relief requests.

Board's proposed F+270 final brief deadline compresses evidentiary phase unnecessarily; extending comment/response deadlines to F+105/F+150 and final briefs to F+300 still leaves Board full 60-day window for hearings and evidentiary closure, within statutory one-year limit.
key_excerpts: Given its past experience with a control proceeding involving its primary interchange partner, RBMN has concerns about the proposed Union Pacific Corporation and Union Pacific Railroad Company control of NS and intends to vigorously participate in the proceeding to ensure that history does not repeat itself and to ensure that any potential adverse effects are ameliorated or conditioned.

Parties participating in the proceeding will no doubt have to wade through and digest massive amounts of material presented in the application, the proposed safety integration plan as well as the environmental information provided by the applicants to determine what if any discovery is necessary and to formulate what relief may be necessary.
RBMN respectfully requests that the Board extend the evidentiary phase of the procedural schedule to the maximum time permitted by statute.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Extend initial comment and response deadlines by 30 days (from F+75/F+120 to F+105/F+150), shift final rebuttal to F+270 and final briefs to F+300, allowing maximum evidentiary period permitted under 49 U.S.C. §11325(b)(3) while preserving Board's 90-day post-hearing decision window.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This is a statutory interpretation argument under 49 U.S.C. §11325(b)(3). RBMN correctly identifies that the Board has discretion to set schedules within the one-year evidentiary/90-day decision windows and argues the Board should utilize maximum time rather than compress it. The filing creates precedent pressure on the Board to justify any schedule that does not maximize discovery time. RBMN's invocation of 'new merger guidelines' signals that evolved competitive analysis may require extended discovery—relevant to burden-of-proof issues if RBMN later files substantive opposition.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Filing is responsive to Board's September 26, 2025 Notice of Proposed Procedural Schedule (Decision No. 5); comment period was extended to November 20, 2025 by Decision No. 6. This deadline has passed. RBMN's proposed schedule adjustments would affect future deadlines if Board adopts them.

docket_entries.title: Three State Attorneys General (Nebraska, West Virginia, Georgia) Support UP-NS Merger, Citing Economic and Environmental Benefits
docket_entries.entry_summary: Three state attorneys general (Nebraska, West Virginia, Georgia) jointly file a support letter urging the STB to approve the UP-NS merger in a timely fashion. Their argument centers on three pillars: (1) the merged entity will create 'the first unified transcontinental railroad' with 50,000+ miles of track, directly connecting 100 North American ports and expanding operational access to 43 states; (2) efficiency gains from eliminating 'car touches and interchange delays' will lower supply chain costs for shippers and ultimately consumer prices, while also enabling new routes and expanded intermodal services; (3) the merger aligns with broader environmental and economic policy objectives—freight rail already accounts for 40% of long-distance U.S. shipping while generating less than 2% of transportation-related emissions, and 'all this will increase freight rail demand and thus increase the number of jobs at the newly-formed company.' The filers note that 'the nation's largest railroad union has announced its support for the merger' and cite President Trump's recent statement that the merger 'sounds good to me.' The filing frames the merged railroad as consistent with Trump administration infrastructure priorities. No conditions or concerns are raised; this is unqualified support.
key_arguments: The merger will create the first unified transcontinental railroad under one company in the United States, bringing more than 50,000 miles of track under one umbrella and directly connecting 100 North American ports, expanding operational access to 43 States.

By eliminating car touches and interchange delays, the merger will move freight faster and at lower cost, enabling the opening of new routes and expansion of intermodal services that will lower supply chain costs for shippers and ultimately consumer prices.

The merged railroad will increase freight rail demand, thereby increasing the number of jobs at the newly-formed company, with the nation's largest railroad union having announced support for the merger.

Freight rail is already three to four times more fuel efficient than trucks and accounts for only 2% of transportation-related emissions despite moving 40% of long-distance U.S. freight; the merger will further enable mode shift from truck to rail, reducing highway congestion and emissions.
The merger is consistent with President Trump's infrastructure vision and commitment to revitalizing America's infrastructure.
key_excerpts: This merger will create the first unified transcontinental railroad, bringing more than 50,000 miles of track under one umbrella, directly connecting 100 North American ports, and expanding operational access to 43 States. By eliminating car touches and interchange delays, even more freight will be moved faster than ever and at a lower cost.

These improvements are likely to lower supply chain costs for shippers, which ultimately means lower prices for consumers. And it is projected that all this will increase freight rail demand and thus increase the number of jobs at the newly-formed company, which is one reason why the nation's largest railroad union has announced its support for the merger.

It only takes a single gallon of fuel to move one ton of freight nearly 500 miles; thus, on average, freight rail is between three to four times more fuel efficient than trucks... And as demand for freight rail increases, more trucks can be taken off our highways and other roadways, reducing congestion and further lowering emissions.
On behalf of our States, we urge you to give regulatory approval to the proposed merger of Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Give regulatory approval to the proposed merger of Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern in a timely fashion
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: State attorney general support signals political acceptance of the merger at the state government level, which may carry weight in the STB's discretionary approval analysis. This filing does not introduce novel legal theories or challenge STB jurisdiction, but the absence of state-level opposition (particularly from three geographically diverse states) may reduce the likelihood of state-coordinated intervention against the merger. The letter references economic and environmental policy benefits that align with federal transportation policy, potentially influencing the STB's public interest analysis under 49 U.S.C. § 11324.

docket_entries.title: AFPM Notice of Intent to Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.entry_summary: AFPM filed a notice of intent to participate as a party of record in Docket FD 36873 regarding the proposed Union Pacific control of Norfolk Southern. The filing does not state any position on the merger, does not oppose or support approval, and does not propose conditions or remedies. AFPM reserved its rights to participate and present evidence at subsequent phases (comments, discovery, hearing) without committing to a substantive stance at this preliminary stage. This is a protective intervention filing typical of major customer groups that may have competing interests (e.g., some members may benefit from consolidation, others may fear anticompetitive effects) and elect to preserve intervention rights while monitoring case development.
key_excerpts: American Fuel & Petrochemical Manufacturers intends to participate in this proceeding as a party of record.

As a party of record, AFPM will be entitled to notice of orders, may participate in discovery, may file substantive comments at the comment stage, and may request hearing participation. The filing establishes AFPM's organizational standing without conceding or adopting any substantive position, allowing for strategic flexibility as case facts develop.

docket_entries.title: Harris County Attorney requests comprehensive merger review, public hearing in Houston, and robust comment process
docket_entries.entry_summary: Harris County Attorney Christian D. Menefee requests that the STB conduct a 'comprehensive, rigorous, and transparent review' of the UP-NS merger and specifically demands procedural accommodations for Harris County stakeholders. The County emphasizes that Harris County's 5+ million residents 'live and work alongside some of the busiest rail corridors in the nation' and identifies concrete harms from current rail operations: 'blocked crossings that delay emergency services, disrupted traffic patterns that affect commutes and commerce, and businesses and consumers that bear the burden of service breakdowns and increased costs due to a merger.' The County requests at least one public hearing in Houston to allow residents, local officials, emergency-response agencies, labor organizations, and businesses to provide direct testimony. The County also urges establishment of a 'robust public comment process that allows sufficient time for all stakeholders to thoroughly analyze the merger's impacts and submit meaningful feedback.' The filing frames this as necessary to evaluate 'environmental protection, safety and accessibility, community investment, economic impacts, and operational improvements.' Notably, the County does not take a position on approval or denial, but demands that 'the STB must ensure that the merger preserves long-term competition and efficient, economically viable rail service while also minimizing the burden our community will face. We should not be forced to tolerate service breakdowns, safety lapses, or higher prices because of this deal.' This is primarily a procedural/transparency filing but with implicit conditions regarding service preservation and community protection.
key_arguments: Harris County residents live alongside some of the nation's busiest rail corridors and directly experience rail operation harms: 'blocked crossings that delay emergency services, disrupted traffic patterns that affect commutes and commerce, and businesses and consumers that bear the burden of service breakdowns and increased costs due to a merger'

Local public hearing in Harris County is necessary because merger impacts directly affect the county's 5+ million residents and its role as 'a critical hub for freight movement' and 'one of the nation's vital economic engines'
STB review must evaluate not only competition but also 'environmental protection, safety and accessibility, community investment, economic impacts, and operational improvements'

Merger approval must be conditioned on preservation of 'long-term competition and efficient, economically viable rail service while also minimizing the burden our community will face' - specifically avoiding 'service breakdowns, safety lapses, or higher prices'
key_excerpts: Harris County residents live and work alongside some of the busiest rail corridors in the nation. With over five million residents, Harris County is the third-largest County in the US and a critical hub for freight movement. It is also one of the nation's vital economic engines. While I understand the crucial economic benefits of freight rail to our community, the County's residents also bear the consequences of rail operations: blocked crossings that delay emergency services, disrupted traffic patterns that affect commutes and commerce, and businesses and consumers that bear the burden of service breakdowns and increased costs due to a merger.

The STB must ensure that the merger preserves long-term competition and efficient, economically viable rail service while also minimizing the burden our community will face. We should not be forced to tolerate service breakdowns, safety lapses, or higher prices because of this deal.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Harris County requests: (1) At least one public hearing held in Harris County, Texas to allow residents, local officials, emergency-response agencies, labor, community organizations, and businesses to provide direct testimony to the STB; (2) Establishment of a robust public comment process with sufficient time for all stakeholders to analyze merger impacts and submit meaningful feedback; (3) STB evaluation of merger's impacts on environmental protection, safety, accessibility, community investment, economic impacts, and operational improvements; (4) Preservation of long-term competition and efficient, economically viable rail service while minimizing community burden from service breakdowns, safety lapses, or higher prices.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing represents a geographic and functional stakeholder group asserting that STB's statutory obligation to ensure 'public interest' review (49 U.S.C. § 11324) requires consideration of local community impacts beyond traditional antitrust analysis. The request for a Harris County hearing and extended comment period, if granted, could expand the evidentiary record to include local safety, environmental, and operational testimony. The County's framing of 'service breakdowns, safety lapses, or higher prices' as conditions of approval suggests STB may face pressure to address operational service-level guarantees and community-benefit commitments as merger conditions, not just rate/access remedies.
docket_entries.deadline_description: No specific deadline stated; procedural request to be addressed in STB's procedural schedule ruling.

docket_entries.title: Joint Comments of Shipper Associations on Proposed Procedural Schedule for UP-NS Merger
docket_entries.filer_name: American Chemistry Council, American Fuel & Petrochemical Manufacturers, Alliance for Chemical Distribution, National Industrial Transportation League, and The Fertilizer Institute
docket_entries.entry_summary: Five shipper associations oppose the STB's proposed compressed procedural schedule for the UP-NS merger, arguing the largest rail merger in U.S. history requires full use of the 365-day statutory evidentiary period and extended comment deadlines. The filers seek a more thorough process including a public hearing, post-hearing briefing, and adequate time for discovery and expert analysis under the Board's heightened 2001 Merger Rules.
key_arguments: The proposed transaction is unprecedented in scale ($250+ billion, 50,000 route miles, 43 states), controlling over 50% of traffic in chemicals, metals, and lumber, and represents first application of 2001 Merger Rules requiring enhanced competition scrutiny

Compressed procedural timelines impair full participation and create incomplete record development, preventing thorough evaluation of cumulative impacts, crossover effects, and service integration plans
Discovery is incomplete; Applicants have failed to produce substantial material in response to discovery requests, including critical traffic tape data elements
Extended comment periods necessary to allow sufficient time for expert analysis, network modeling, and evaluation of efficiency claims under heightened scrutiny
Public hearing and post-hearing briefing precedent established in CPKC and CSX/Pan Am mergers, which were less impactful and subject to less rigorous pre-2001 rules
Approval would invite 'end game' consolidation creating transcontinental railroad duopoly with profound implications for captive shippers facing higher rates and reduced service options
Sur-reply opportunities essential given complexity and novel legal issues of first impression under 2001 Merger Rules
key_excerpts: The proposed transaction constitutes the largest rail merger in U.S. history and the first major transaction the Board will decide under its 2001 merger rules that impose a heightened, competition-enhancing public interest test.
Approval would invite 'end game' consolidation and risks a transcontinental railroad duopoly, with profound implications for captive shippers on Applicants' and other carriers' lines.
The Board's proposed procedural schedule is too short to permit careful, thorough review commensurate with the transaction's importance.

This merger presents greater discovery needs than past mergers since it is the first merger under the 2001 Merger Rules, which call for closer examination of claims of improved carrier efficiency and of the potential for transitional service disruptions.
Extended comment periods provide important benefits for this proceeding. First, they allow sufficient time to conduct discovery and ensure data transparency.

docket_entries.title: STB Procedural Notice: Environmental Information Submission Deadline
docket_entries.entry_summary: The STB's Office of Environmental Analysis issued a procedural notice on November 24, 2025, establishing that Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern must submit environmental information requested in OEA's September 16, 2025 letter no later than the filing of their merger application with the Board. The notice cites 49 C.F.R. § 1105.7(f) and § 1180.6(a), which require applicants to submit environmental materials with their application. OEA had requested this information 'as soon as possible' in its September letter, and the notice formalizes that deadline: the materials must be completed by the time the merger application is filed, though applicants may submit them earlier. This is a procedural requirement tied to the Board's environmental review authority, not a substantive challenge to the merger.
key_arguments: Environmental materials must be submitted pursuant to 49 C.F.R. § 1105.7(f) as part of the environmental review process in this merger proceeding
49 C.F.R. § 1180.6(a) requires applicants to submit information and data on environmental matters with their merger application to the Board
The September 16, 2025 OEA letter established specific information requests that must be fulfilled by application filing
key_excerpts: Applicants shall submit the information requested in the September 16, 2025 letter no later than the filing of their application with the Board and may do so earlier, if practicable.
Under 49 C.F.R. § 1180.6(a), Applicants are required to submit information and data with respect to environmental matters prepared under 49 C.F.R. part 1105 with their application to the Board.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Applicants shall submit the information requested in the September 16, 2025 OEA letter no later than the filing of their application with the Board and may do so earlier, if practicable.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This notice operationalizes the STB's mandatory environmental review authority under 49 C.F.R. Part 1105 for major rail mergers. It establishes a hard deadline (application filing) for compliance with environmental information requests, which means incomplete or deficient environmental documentation could delay application acceptance or trigger board requests for supplemental information post-filing. The reference to EO-4064 suggests additional executive order compliance requirements may apply. This is a gating procedural requirement—the application cannot be complete without these materials.
docket_entries.deadline_description: No later than the filing of Applicants' merger application with the Board (exact date not specified in this notice; applicants may submit earlier if practicable)

docket_entries.title: New Mexico House Representative Ferreray Letter Supporting UP-NS Merger
docket_entries.entry_summary: New Mexico House Consumer Affairs Committee Chair Ferreray files letter expressing strong support for the UP-NS merger. She argues the merger will 'protect union jobs and ensure job security for rank and file members who work in train and yardmaster service' and will deliver four tangible benefits: (1) 'Improved Service Reliability' through 'more direct routes and greater operational flexibility' to 'prevent service disruptions and improve schedule dependability'; (2) 'Reduced Transit Times' by 'eliminating certain interchanges' to 'speed the movement of goods'; (3) 'Increased Investment' positioning the combined railroad to 'invest in modern infrastructure, advanced technology and enhanced safety systems'; and (4) 'Expanded Reach' opening 'new markets for our state's products and strengthen supply chain resilience.' She frames the merger as critical to New Mexico's economy because 'freight rail is a cornerstone of our state's economy, safely moving the goods that power our industries, support our farmers and connect our communities to markets.' She also invokes environmental benefits, noting freight rail is 'one of the most sustainable modes of transportation available, helping reduce highway congestion and emissions.' No specific conditions requested; unconditional support for approval.
key_arguments: The merger will 'protect union jobs and ensure job security for rank and file members who work in train and yardmaster service'
Combined railroad will achieve 'Improved Service Reliability' through 'more direct routes and greater operational flexibility' to 'prevent service disruptions'
Merger will enable 'Reduced Transit Times' by 'eliminating certain interchanges' and allowing 'goods' to move 'faster and more competitively'
Transcontinental railroad will be 'better positioned to invest in modern infrastructure, advanced technology and enhanced safety systems'
Merger's 'broader geographic footprint will open new markets for our state's products and strengthen supply chain resilience'
Freight rail is 'one of the most sustainable modes of transportation available, helping reduce highway congestion and emissions'
key_excerpts: The merger will protect union jobs and ensure job security for rank and file members who work in train and yardmaster service.
Freight rail is a cornerstone of our state's economy, safely moving the goods that power our industries, support our farmers and connect our communities to markets across the nation and the world.
The proposed merger offers a unique opportunity to strengthen this network and deliver tangible benefits for shippers, consumers and communities
docket_entries.relief_requested: Urges the Surface Transportation Board to 'give full and favorable consideration to this proposal, recognizing the benefits it will bring to our state and the national economy.'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Limited. This filing represents state legislative support but does not raise novel legal issues under 49 U.S.C. § 11324 or advance specific factual evidence of competitive or service impacts. The letter reiterates pro-merger arguments already advanced by applicants (service reliability, reduced transit times, investment capacity) without independent economic or operational analysis. However, it provides political/constituent support evidence that STB may consider under its authority to assess public interest factors. No discovery obligations or hearing preparation implications flow from this filing.

docket_entries.title: Agricultural Retailers Association et al. Comment: Broad Coalition Opposes UP/NS Merger as Anticompetitive and Harmful to Supply Chain
docket_entries.entry_summary: A coalition of 51+ major trade associations and business groups—including the Freight Rail Customer Alliance, National Industrial Transportation League, American Chemistry Council, Agricultural Retailers Association, and regional chambers spanning agriculture, chemicals, automotive, manufacturing, and energy sectors—opposes the proposed UP/NS merger on fundamental competitive and economic grounds. The coalition argues: (1) The transaction would create unprecedented rail consolidation, placing over 40% of U.S. freight rail traffic under a single railroad, reducing competition from four dominant Class I carriers to effectively three; (2) "History has shown that increased rail consolidation leads to fewer choices, higher transportation costs, service disruptions, and reduced economic competitiveness"; (3) Past rail mergers have "triggered major breakdowns in the supply chain and increased costs for businesses and consumers alike"; (4) The combined entity would threaten U.S. manufacturing strength, energy security, and supply chain reliability by eliminating competitive pressure on rates and service. The coalition requests no specific conditions—they argue the merger is fundamentally anticompetitive and call for the Board to "thoroughly scrutinize" and implicitly deny the proposal. No settlement signals or willingness to negotiate conditions is expressed.
key_arguments: The proposed UP/NS merger would create unprecedented consolidation: 'The proposed UP/NS transaction would be the largest rail merger in history and would put control of more than 40% of rail traffic in the hands of a single railroad.' This reduces meaningful competition from four Class I carriers controlling 90% of traffic to effectively three.

Historical precedent demonstrates consolidation harms: 'History has shown that increased rail consolidation leads to fewer choices, higher transportation costs, service disruptions, and reduced economic competitiveness. Past rail mergers have triggered major breakdowns in the supply chain and increased costs for businesses and consumers alike.'

The merger threatens supply chain integrity and economic competitiveness: 'Reliable and affordable freight rail service is essential to maintaining U.S. manufacturing strength, supporting energy security, and ensuring reliable supply chains.' The transaction would eliminate competitive discipline on rates and service.
The merger would 'further weaken the small amount of competition that currently exists in the railroad industry,' leaving shippers with severely limited alternatives for routing and pricing.
key_excerpts: The proposed UP/NS transaction would be the largest rail merger in history and would put control of more than 40% of rail traffic in the hands of a single railroad. It would further weaken the small amount of competition that currently exists in the railroad industry.

History has shown that increased rail consolidation leads to fewer choices, higher transportation costs, service disruptions, and reduced economic competitiveness. Past rail mergers have triggered major breakdowns in the supply chain and increased costs for businesses and consumers alike.

Reliable and affordable freight rail service is essential to maintaining U.S. manufacturing strength, supporting energy security, and ensuring reliable supply chains. The creation of a transcontinental railroad must not come at the expense of competition, service reliability, or the broader health of the U.S. supply chain.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Urge the Board to 'thoroughly scrutinize this merger proposal to ensure it does not undermine the integrity of our nation's transportation network or disrupt the supply chain.' No specific conditions listed; the filing constitutes a request to deny based on fundamental market concentration and competitive concerns.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing establishes a major customer opposition constituency that the STB must address in its competitive analysis under 49 U.S.C. § 11324(c). The coalition's evidence that 'past rail mergers have triggered major breakdowns in the supply chain' creates factual contentions the applicants must rebut. The coalition's claim that the merger threatens 'energy security' and 'U.S. manufacturing strength' broadens the competitive analysis beyond bilateral shipping costs to systemic economic consequences. The participation of the Freight Rail Customer Alliance—a sophisticated shipper advocacy group—and NITL suggests coordinated customer opposition will be sustained throughout the proceeding. The filing does not propose settlement conditions, signaling this is ideological/structural opposition unlikely to be resolved by behavioral remedies.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Comment period deadline; this filing has been submitted. Applicants will need to address in reply comments and at hearing.

docket_entries.title: NCFO Support for UP/NS Merger Based on Job Protection Agreement
docket_entries.entry_summary: NCFO, representing mechanical service workers, expresses strong support for the UP/NS merger based on a binding job protection agreement negotiated with Union Pacific. NCFO states: 'Union Pacific has made a commitment that employees of both Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern will not face involuntary furloughs as a result of the merger. This is an unprecedented guarantee in the history of American railroading.' The union characterizes the agreement as 'a model of collaboration' and urges the STB to 'recognize Union Pacific's commitment to its workforce and carefully consider the positive impact this merger will have on labor and the broader economy.' NCFO frames the merger as a 'transformative opportunity' that 'strengthens long-term stability, expand[s] opportunities for our members, and protect[s] quality jobs for the future.' The filing provides no conditions or reservations—it is unqualified support predicated on the completed labor agreement.
key_arguments: Union Pacific has provided an unprecedented guarantee: 'employees of both Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern will not face involuntary furloughs as a result of the merger,' covering the length of NCFO members' careers in mechanical service

The merger represents a 'transformative opportunity for the railroad industry and its workforce' that will 'strengthen long-term stability, expand opportunities for our members, and protect quality jobs for the future'
The labor agreement 'demonstrates that even in times of great change, industry leaders and unions can come together to secure both economic progress and the livelihoods of working people'
NCFO urges the STB to consider 'the positive impact this merger will have on labor and the broader economy' as part of regulatory review
key_excerpts: 'Union Pacific has made a commitment that employees of both Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern will not face involuntary furloughs as a result of the merger. This is an unprecedented guarantee in the history of American railroading.'

'Recently, NCFO and Union Pacific entered into a historic agreement that guarantees NCFO members working in mechanical service will have job protection for the length of their careers following the transaction.'
docket_entries.relief_requested: NCFO requests that the STB approve the proposed merger, noting that Union Pacific has committed to job protections for NCFO members and urging the Board to 'recognize Union Pacific's commitment to its workforce and carefully consider the positive impact this merger will have on labor and the broader economy.'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing demonstrates successful pre-filing labor settlement and removes a significant category of potential opposition. Under 49 U.S.C. § 11324(b), the STB must consider 'the effect of the proposed transaction on the public interest,' which includes labor impacts. NCFO's support converts labor from a potential litigation risk into affirmative evidence of public benefit. The filing establishes that the applicants have negotiated binding labor protections, which may be cited as evidence of responsible merger planning and reduce the likelihood of labor-based intervention from other unions. This also creates pressure on other rail unions (BLET, SMART-TD, BRS, TCU) to negotiate similar agreements or explain why their members should receive less protection.
