docket_entries.title: Allied Rail Unions (BMWED, BRS, SMART-MD, IAM #19, TCU) – Amended Notice of Intent to Participate
docket_entries.filer_name: Allied Rail Unions (BMWED, BRS, SMART-MD, IAM #19, TCU)
docket_entries.entry_summary: Five allied labor unions (BMWED, BRS, SMART-MD, IAM #19, TCU) filed amended notice of intent to participate in the UP/NS merger proceeding on December 1, 2025. The filing establishes their formal intervention status and designates counsel (Richard S. Edelman and Aaron S. Edelman of Mooney, Green, Saindon, Murphy & Welch, P.C.). Critically, the unions explicitly state they 'take no position at this time with respect to merits of the proposed transaction(s), as to whether the proposed transaction could be approved...as to what conditions...should be attached to any approved transaction.' This language indicates the unions are reserving their position and have not yet disclosed their substantive stance on the merger. The filing notes that three additional unions (National Conference of Firemen and Oilers, 32BJ/SEIU, and International Brotherhood of Boilermakers) are no longer participating through the ARU as of this amendment. The unions' decision to retain experienced merger counsel and to intervene early suggests they are preparing to file substantive comments, likely focusing on labor protections, employment guarantees, working conditions, job preservation, and implementation of 49 U.S.C. § 11326 labor protective conditions that are standard in major railroad mergers.
key_arguments: No substantive arguments presented in this filing. Filing is procedural notice of intervention only.
Unions reserving position on merits, conditions, and labor-specific demands for future filings.
key_excerpts: The ARU take no position at this time with respect to merits of the proposed transaction(s), as to whether the proposed transaction could be approved under the requirements of the statute and the regulations governing 'major mergers', as to what conditions (other than those required under 49 U.S.C. §11326) should be attached to any approved transaction, or as to any conditions that may be sought by any other party.
The Allied Rail Unions' [notice of] intent to participate in this Finance Docket as well as any related Sub-dockets...
docket_entries.relief_requested: No substantive relief requested at this time. Filing constitutes notice of intent to participate in proceeding and related sub-dockets.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This is a formal intervention notice establishing labor union standing in the proceeding. Under 49 U.S.C. § 11326, major railroad mergers trigger mandatory consideration of labor protective conditions ('labor protective orders' or LPOs). The unions' intervention activates their statutory right to propose and negotiate labor conditions. The reference to § 11326 conditions in their neutrality statement signals they will seek statutory labor protections. This is procedurally significant because: (1) unions become parties of record entitled to discovery, hearing participation, and briefing opportunities; (2) their counsel designation enables formal communication; (3) the STB must address labor issues in any approval order; (4) unions' future filings will likely propose specific labor conditions regarding seniority, job preservation, wage protections, and implementation processes.
docket_entries.document_type: Modify/Supplement Prior Filing Or The Record
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response deadline. This is a notice of intervention filing. Unions will likely file substantive comments/conditions during subsequent comment periods.

docket_entries.title: CMAP Notice of Intent to Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.entry_summary: Chicago Metropolitan Agency for Planning (CMAP) filed a Notice of Intent to Participate in the UP/NS merger proceeding. The filing contains no substantive arguments, no position on the merger, no conditions, and no statement of specific interests affected. CMAP is the regional metropolitan planning organization for the Chicago area responsible for transportation planning coordination. By filing this notice, CMAP preserves its right to intervene and comment at later stages of the proceeding, but has not yet articulated what specific issues or harms warrant its participation. The filing is silent on whether CMAP supports, opposes, or is neutral on the merger.
key_excerpts: The Chicago Metropolitan Agency for Planning (CMAP) respectfully submits its Notice of Intent to Participate in this proceeding before the Board, as its interests may appear.
docket_entries.relief_requested: None specified - filing is limited to notice of intent to participate without substantive position or conditions
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Procedurally establishes CMAP's standing to intervene and participate in the record. Indicates a governmental entity with regional planning authority intends to monitor the proceeding, potentially to assess transportation network impacts. Does not change burden of proof or scope of review, but signals potential future comments on regional rail connectivity, service coordination, or land use implications.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.deadline_description: Notice of Intent to Participate requires no response; CMAP may file substantive comments in subsequent filings if it chooses to do so.

docket_entries.title: City of Bay City Support for Union Pacific/Norfolk Southern Merger
docket_entries.entry_summary: City of Bay City Mayor Jim Folse filed a letter of support for the Union Pacific/Norfolk Southern merger, characterizing the transaction as beneficial to Texas economy and freight rail competitiveness. The Mayor argues the merger will deliver 'Improved Service Reliability' through 'more direct routes and greater operational flexibility,' 'Reduced Transit Times' by 'eliminating certain interchanges,' 'Increased Investment' in 'modern infrastructure, advanced technology and enhanced safety systems,' and 'Expanded Reach' opening 'new markets for our state's products.' The filing frames freight rail as 'a cornerstone of our state's economy' and 'one of the most sustainable modes of transportation,' asserting the merger will 'strengthen this network' and 'ensure American freight rail remains globally competitive.' No specific conditions requested; filing is generic supportive advocacy.
key_arguments: Merged entity will provide 'more direct routes and greater operational flexibility' preventing 'service disruptions and improve[ing] schedule dependability'
Elimination of interchanges through merger will 'speed the movement of goods, helping our businesses reach customers faster and more competitively'
Transcontinental railroad post-merger will be 'better positioned to invest in modern infrastructure, advanced technology and enhanced safety systems'
Broader geographic footprint will 'open new markets for our state's products and strengthen supply chain resilience'
Merger is necessary to 'ensure American freight rail remains globally competitive'
key_excerpts: The proposed merger offers a unique opportunity to strengthen this network and deliver tangible benefits for shippers, consumers and communities, including: Improved Service Reliability... Reduced Transit Times... Increased Investment... Expanded Reach.
Freight rail is a cornerstone of our state's economy, safely moving the goods that power our industries, support our farmers and connect our communities to markets across the nation and the world.

This merger is about more than just railroads—it's about securing the future of our transportation network, supporting economic development and ensuring American freight rail remains globally competitive.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Full and favorable consideration of the merger application, recognizing benefits to state and national economy
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: No legal or regulatory significance. Filing does not raise novel statutory interpretation issues, procedural objections, or evidence that would alter burden of proof or scope of STB review. Generic municipal support carries minimal evidentiary weight in competitive analysis.

docket_entries.title: CPKC Notice of Intent to Participate - Counsel Appearance and Data Access Request
docket_entries.entry_summary: CPKC files a notice of intent to participate, adding Sullivan & Cromwell LLP as additional counsel representing the railroad in this proceeding. The filing requests addition of two Sullivan & Cromwell partners to the service list and seeks access to Confidential Waybill Sample Data for counsel and consultants. This is a purely procedural filing that signals CPKC's intent to actively participate in the merger review but contains no substantive position on the proposed UP-NS transaction. The engagement of a major outside law firm with M&A expertise suggests CPKC is preparing for substantive involvement, but the content and scope of CPKC's opposition or conditions remain unstated.
key_excerpts: I am writing on behalf of Canadian Pacific Railway Company, d/b/a Canadian Pacific Kansas City and CPKC, and its U.S. rail carrier subsidiaries (collectively 'CPKC') to notice the appearance of Sullivan & Cromwell as additional counsel representing CPKC in this proceeding.
Relevant personnel at Sullivan & Cromwell will in due course be seeking access to the Confidential Waybill Sample Data previously provided to outside counsel and consultants acting on behalf of CPKC.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Add Sullivan & Cromwell counsel (Joseph J. Matelis and Dylan M. Aluise) to service list; grant access to Confidential Waybill Sample Data for counsel and consultants.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing establishes CPKC's formal intervention status and signals engagement of sophisticated outside counsel. The request for access to Confidential Waybill Sample Data is procedurally significant—it indicates CPKC will conduct detailed competitive analysis using operational data to assess merger impacts on its business. This is a standard but important step for a competitor intervenor and suggests substantive filings will follow. No change to scope of review, but confirms CPKC will be an active participant.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response deadline; procedural notice only

docket_entries.title: South Dakota Corn Growers Association Letter Opposing UP-NS Merger as Threat to Agricultural Competition and Rural Elevator Access
docket_entries.entry_summary: The South Dakota Corn Growers Association opposes the UP-NS merger as a threat to already-concentrated freight rail competition and agricultural shipper access. SDCGA argues: 'Four large freight railroads control over 90% of rail traffic already. We are concerned that fewer firms in an already concentrated environment may impact reliability, access and rates for rail transportation of grain.' The organization documents structural decline in rural grain elevator infrastructure over 20 years—attributable to prior consolidation—and warns: 'past declines in rail competition likely impacted the closures of rural elevators as many of those small and mid-sized elevators did not have shuttle-train loading capacity. Thus, we fear that UP-NS focus on high-density lanes will have similar effect leading ultimately to lower margins for farmers.' SDCGA's opposition appears conditional rather than absolute: it requests the STB use merger review as 'an opportunity to enhance and prioritize rail competition' and expresses willingness to 'work with the STB' on solutions. This framing suggests SDCGA would accept merger approval if coupled with conditions protecting elevator access and competitive routing for non-high-density agricultural corridors.
key_arguments: Merger increases consolidation in already-concentrated market: 'Four large freight railroads control over 90% of rail traffic already. We are concerned that fewer firms in an already concentrated environment may impact reliability, access and rates for rail transportation of grain.'

Prior rail consolidation has demonstrably harmed rural agricultural infrastructure: 'past declines in rail competition likely impacted the closures of rural elevators as many of those small and mid-sized elevators did not have shuttle-train loading capacity.'

Merger threatens to replicate consolidation harms by prioritizing high-density routes: 'we fear that UP-NS focus on high-density lanes will have similar effect leading ultimately to lower margins for farmers.'

Agricultural sector has experienced cascading structural harm from transportation consolidation: 'an increase in consolidation have not improved profitability at the farmgate. Costs increase, either through rate changes or the required use of at least partial alternative transportation, and margins tighten.'

Merger threatens existing supply chain viability for smaller rural shippers: 'Reliable access to affordable rail transportation, especially during the latter months of the year, is a key component to that mission' and transportation costs/changes 'negatively affect farmers' bottom lines.'
key_excerpts: 'Four large freight railroads control over 90% of rail traffic already. We are concerned that fewer firms in an already concentrated environment may impact reliability, access and rates for rail transportation of grain.'

'past declines in rail competition likely impacted the closures of rural elevators as many of those small and mid-sized elevators did not have shuttle-train loading capacity. Thus, we fear that UP-NS focus on high-density lanes will have similar effect leading ultimately to lower margins for farmers.'

'It has been our experience in the grain subsector that structural issues such as an increase in consolidation have not improved profitability at the farmgate. Costs increase, either through rate changes or the required use of at least partial alternative transportation, and margins tighten.'

'We appreciate that the Surface Transportation Board's upcoming review is an opportunity to enhance and prioritize rail competition and respectfully request careful consideration of the merger application.'
docket_entries.relief_requested: SDCGA requests 'careful consideration of the merger application' and looks forward to 'working with the STB to further a freight rail network that supports and serves South Dakota corn farmers.' The letter does not explicitly demand denial but frames opposition conditional on whether merger can be structured to 'enhance and prioritize rail competition.'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: SDCGA's filing introduces direct evidence of consolidation-related customer harm in agricultural markets—a major shipper constituency. The letter establishes causal linkage between prior railroad consolidation and rural infrastructure decline (elevator closures), creating record evidence that merger-induced consolidation can produce durable structural harms to non-high-density shippers. This supports STB scrutiny of merger impacts on captive customers lacking modal alternatives. The conditional framing ('opportunity to enhance rail competition') signals SDCGA may be responsive to service commitments or competitive access remedies, potentially limiting scope of customer opposition if applicants offer targeted protections for agricultural shippers. The filing also elevates regional agricultural interests as distinct from national shipper trade associations, potentially influencing STB's assessment of geographic service quality impacts.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Comment filing; no response deadline imposed on applicants, though applicants may choose to address agricultural shipper concerns in reply comments or hearing testimony.

docket_entries.title: Saint Paul Commodities Letter: Opposition to UP/NS Merger Based on Loss of Competition and Captive Shipper Risks
docket_entries.entry_summary: Saint Paul Commodities, a commodity shipper, submitted a letter of opposition arguing that the UP/NS merger would substantially reduce competition and create captive shipper risks. The filer contends that the merged railroad would control 'nearly half of existing U.S. freight, with some commodity groups exceeding 50%,' and that 'for many origins and destinations, customers would lose any competitive routing options.' Saint Paul specifically identifies UP's existing 'bundling' of captive plants in the southeast chemical corridor as a strategy that would become 'even more effective' with NS traffic. The filer argues that UP would gain 'operational dominance' over critical gateways including majority interests in joint facilities like the Belt Railway in Chicago, and would extend its influence over pooled equipment assets like TTX. Critically, Saint Paul rejects the possibility of conditional approval, stating that 'traditional remedies such as trackage rights depend on the merged carrier's willingness to comply' and citing UP's history of failing to meet regulatory obligations, including issuing 'over 1,000 embargoes recently that triggered an STB investigation.' The filer asserts that 'UP does not honor competitive conditions or regulatory commitments from past consolidations' and therefore conditions cannot protect shippers. This is a categorical, outright opposition with no fallback conditions requested.
key_arguments: The merged railroad would control nearly half of U.S. freight, with some commodity groups exceeding 50%, creating unprecedented market concentration.
For many origins and destinations, shippers would lose all competitive routing options and become captive to a single railroad with no incentive for UP to allow alternative access.
UP already engages in anticompetitive bundling of captive plants in regions like the southeast chemical corridor, and adding NS captive traffic would make this strategy even more effective.
UP would gain operational dominance over key terminals and gateways across the central U.S., including majority control of joint facilities such as the Belt Railway in Chicago.
UP would extend its influence over pooled assets like TTX, further extending its ability to disadvantage competitors.
Past rail mergers have shown that integration failures ripple across the entire freight system, causing congestion and poor service at facilities not directly served by the merging carriers.
UP's claim it will fund the merger through 10% volume growth is not credible because in its last mega-merger, UP's volumes actually declined while revenues and profits rose at customers' expense.
UP has repeatedly violated regulatory obligations, including issuing over 1,000 embargoes recently that triggered an STB investigation.
UP has a documented history of ignoring competitive conditions and regulatory commitments from past consolidations, making traditional remedies like trackage rights unenforceable.

Traditional remedies such as trackage rights cannot fix this merger because they depend on the merged carrier's willingness to comply, and shippers cannot rely on protracted legal processes given UP's compliance record.
key_excerpts: The merged railroad would control nearly half of existing U.S. freight, with some commodity groups exceeding 50%.

For many origins and destinations, customers would lose any competitive routing option. Facilities currently served by only UP or NS would become captive to a single railroad, with no incentive for UP to allow access to alternatives.
UP already engages in 'bundling' of captive plants in regions like the southeast chemical corridor. Adding NS captive traffic would make this anticompetitive strategy even more effective.
UP would effectively control key terminals and gateways across the central U.S., including majority interests in joint facilities such as the Belt Railway in Chicago.
UP has repeatedly failed to meet its obligations, including issuing over 1,000 embargoes recently that triggered an STB investigation.
History shows UP does not honor competitive conditions or regulatory commitments from past consolidations.

Traditional remedies such as trackage rights depend on the merged carrier's willingness to comply. Given UP's record of ignoring obligations, shippers cannot rely on protracted legal processes to protect competition.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Reject the UP/NS merger. The filer states: 'For these reasons, I urge the Surface Transportation Board to reject the UP/NS merger. At a minimum, the Board must carefully weigh the risks of unprecedented market concentration, service disruption, and the irreversible loss of competitive options that would harm shippers and the broader economy.'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing raises the captive shipper issue as a central antitrust concern, challenging the sufficiency of proposed remedies on grounds of enforceability and UP's compliance history. Saint Paul's explicit rejection of trackage rights as an adequate remedy based on UP's documented regulatory violations may shift the burden on applicants to address enforcement mechanisms and shipper protection beyond standard competitive access remedies. The argument that conditions are unenforceable due to UP's past non-compliance could influence the Board's threshold determination of whether the merger can be conditioned to competitive standards.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Comment filing; no specific response deadline noted in the letter itself.

docket_entries.title: STB Approval of Additional Waybill Data Access for BNSF Consultants (Lexecon, FTI Consulting)
docket_entries.entry_summary: STB Office of Economics approved BNSF's request to grant five additional consultants access to confidential Carload Waybill Sample (CCWS) data with unmasked revenues for 1990-2024. BNSF retained two major economic consulting firms: Compass Lexecon (four consultants: Kataria, Heyler, Li, Carless) and FTI Consulting (Brown). The approval was conditioned on compliance with STB confidentiality agreements requiring return or destruction of data within 30 days of agreement expiration, with renewal requests required in advance. BNSF had previously obtained waybill access on August 12, 2025 (WB25-44 for 2019-2024) and September 30, 2025 (WB25-56 for 1990-2018). This filing demonstrates BNSF is conducting detailed economic analysis of historical carload patterns and pricing to build competitive opposition arguments.
key_arguments: BNSF's need for historical waybill data (1990-2024) demonstrates preparation of detailed competitive analysis of traffic flows and revenue patterns that would be affected by UP/NS control merger

Engagement of two major economic consulting firms (Compass Lexecon and FTI Consulting) indicates BNSF is building quantitative evidence on competitive impacts, likely focusing on shipper diversion, pricing power, and market concentration changes
key_excerpts: On August 7, 2025, we submitted a request, on behalf of BNSF Railway Company ('BNSF'), that BNSF's outside counsel and consultants in the above-referenced proceeding be granted permission to access the confidential Carload Waybill Sample (CCWS) with unmasked revenues for 2019 through 2024 (Waybill Request WB25-44).

Pursuant to 49 C.F.R. § 1244.9(b)(4), we hereby request that the following additional consultants of BNSF in the above-referenced proceeding, none of whom is a regular employee of BNSF, be granted permission to access the confidential CCWS with unmasked revenues in this proceeding for 1990 through 2024: Compass Lexecon and its employees ... FTI Consulting and its employees
docket_entries.relief_requested: Approval to add five additional consultants (Aarushi Kataria, Madeline Heyler, Yueru Li, Samuel Carless from Compass Lexecon; Richard Brown from FTI Consulting) to waybill access letter WB25-44 for access to confidential CCWS data with unmasked revenues for 1990-2024.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This is a procedural disclosure under 49 C.F.R. § 1244.9(b)(4) governing access to confidential waybill data in railroad merger proceedings. The approval establishes that BNSF has legitimate access to detailed competitive data (including historical 35-year carload patterns and unmasked revenue figures) necessary to support expert economic testimony. The consultant roster (major economic consulting firms) signals that BNSF will likely submit detailed quantitative analysis of competitive impacts. The timeline of requests (August, September, November 2025) indicates ongoing refinement of BNSF's expert analysis as the proceeding advances.
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response required; procedural approval issued

docket_entries.title: STB Approval of Waybill Data Access for BNSF Consultants (Lexecon, FTI Consulting)
docket_entries.entry_summary: STB Acting Director Francis X. O'Connor approved BNSF Railway's request to grant five additional outside consultants access to confidential Carload Waybill Sample (CCWS) data with unmasked revenues covering 1990-2024. The approved individuals are: Aarushi Kataria, Madeline Heyler, Yueru (Josh) Li, and Samuel Carless from Compass Lexecon, and Richard Brown from FTI Consulting. This is the second expansion of BNSF's consultant access (initial WB25-44 granted August 12, 2025 for 2019-2024 data; WB25-56 expansion granted September 30, 2025 for historical 1990-2018 data). BNSF has paid $720 in processing fees. All signatories executed confidentiality agreements requiring return/destruction of data upon expiration. This approval indicates BNSF is conducting granular economic analysis of railroad traffic patterns to construct competitive harm arguments in discovery phase.
key_arguments: BNSF required historical waybill access (1990-2024) with unmasked revenue data to conduct economic analysis of competitive impacts from UP/NS control merger
BNSF engaged top-tier economic consulting firms (Compass Lexecon, FTI Consulting) with multiple analysts, indicating substantial analytical effort to quantify harm allegations
key_excerpts: On September 24, 2025, we requested additional access to CCWS data for 1990 through 2018 (Waybill Request WB25-56). The request was granted on September 30, 2025. Pursuant to 49 C.F.R. § 1244.9(b)(4), we hereby request that the following additional consultants of BNSF in the above-referenced proceeding... be granted permission to access the confidential CCWS with unmasked revenues in this proceeding for 1990 through 2024

docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This is routine discovery administration under 49 C.F.R. § 1244.9(b)(4) governing confidential waybill data access in STB proceedings. The approval is ministerial upon fee payment and confidentiality agreement execution. No legal significance to burden of proof or scope of review. Procedurally notable only in confirming BNSF's active discovery preparation during the discovery phase, consistent with sophisticated opposition.

docket_entries.title: Congressional Letter on Passenger Rail Impacts of UP/NS Merger
docket_entries.entry_summary: Rep. Larsen (D-WA), Ranking Member of House Transportation & Infrastructure Committee, urges the STB to consider passenger rail impacts when reviewing the UP/NS merger. He identifies three specific passenger rail concerns: (1) On-time performance impacts, noting that 'more than half of state-supported and long-distance Amtrak routes operate on either UP or NS track,' with particular concern about UP's historical struggles on the Washington state-supported Cascades service; (2) Threat to new intercity passenger rail corridors funded under the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law—'69 corridors were selected for intercity passenger rail planning and development. More than half of these corridors will require coordination with UP and NS'; and (3) Operational conflicts from long freight trains, stating 'long freight trains negatively impact passenger trains. When long trains block crossings on passenger rail routes, they contribute to Amtrak delays on state-supported and long-distance routes.' No specific conditions or denial requested; filing is procedurally requesting that STB factor passenger rail into merger review.
key_arguments: More than half of state-supported and long-distance Amtrak routes operate on either UP or NS track, creating vulnerability to merger-related service disruptions
UP has historically struggled to provide on-time performance on the Washington state-supported Cascades service, demonstrating track record of passenger rail service deficiency

Over half of 69 Bipartisan Infrastructure Law corridors selected for intercity passenger rail development will require coordination with UP and NS, making merger compatibility critical to federal infrastructure investment goals
Long freight trains block passenger rail crossings and cause Amtrak delays on state-supported and long-distance routes, and merger-enabled longer trains will exacerbate this operational conflict
key_excerpts: More than half of state-supported and long-distance Amtrak routes operate on either UP or NS track, including the Washington state-supported Cascades service where UP has struggled to provide on-time performance.
More than half of these corridors will require coordination with UP and NS.
long freight trains negatively impact passenger trains. When long trains block crossings on passenger rail routes, they contribute to Amtrak delays on state-supported and long-distance routes.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Urges STB to 'consider the passenger rail implications of a potential merger between Union Pacific (UP) and Norfolk Southern (NS) when reviewing their application.'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing signals that passenger rail impacts may enter the merger review record as a public policy consideration. While not creating new statutory obligations (49 U.S.C. § 11324 does not explicitly require passenger rail consideration), it establishes congressional awareness and concern. The reference to Bipartisan Infrastructure Law corridors may create a nexus argument for considering federal policy objectives in merger conditions. Likely to prompt responses from Amtrak, state transportation authorities, and potentially the applicants regarding passenger rail accommodation.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Letter to STB; no reply deadline. May trigger procedural responses from parties or other intervenors regarding passenger rail issues.

docket_entries.title: Virginia Passenger Rail Authority Notice of Intent to Participate
docket_entries.entry_summary: The Virginia Passenger Rail Authority filed a minimal notice of intent to participate without submitting substantive comments. The filing provides no arguments, positions, or relief requested beyond seeking status as a party to monitor the proceeding. This is a placeholder intervention indicating VPRA reserves the right to engage substantively later. The agency's decision to intervene (rather than remain silent) suggests it has identified potential impacts to Virginia passenger rail service or infrastructure that warrant monitoring, though VPRA has not yet articulated specific concerns.
key_excerpts: The Virginia Passenger Rail Authority (VPRA) respectfully submits its Notice of Intent to Participate in this proceeding before the Board, as its interests may appear.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Permission to participate in the proceeding without submitting comments at this time
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Establishes VPRA's right to receive service of documents and participate in discovery and hearing phases if VPRA subsequently identifies specific issues. As a state agency, VPRA may have standing to raise issues under 49 U.S.C. § 11324(d) regarding impact on public interest, including passenger rail service preservation. The filing does not change the scope of review but preserves VPRA's option to file substantive comments or testimony later.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.deadline_description: Notice of intent requires no response; VPRA must file substantive position if it elects to do so in subsequent comment periods

docket_entries.title: Amendment to Notice of Intent - Filing Date Change to December 19, 2025
docket_entries.entry_summary: Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern jointly amend their Notice of Intent to File Application, notifying the STB that they will file their merger application on or about December 19, 2025 (rather than an earlier anticipated date). The amendment is filed pursuant to 49 C.F.R. § 1180.4(b)(3) and the Board's Decision No. 3. The application will seek authority under 49 U.S.C. §§ 11323-25 for UPC, through wholly owned subsidiary Ruby Merger Sub 1 Corporation, to acquire control of NSC and NS, resulting in common control of UP and NS. This is a pure procedural notice of scheduling change with no substantive arguments or conditions proposed by the applicants.
key_arguments: Filing date is now December 19, 2025 (amendment to prior Notice of Intent)
key_excerpts: Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern (collectively, 'Applicants') now anticipate filing their application on or about December 19, 2025.

This amendment to their Notice of Intent to File Application (UP-1/NS-1) to notify the Surface Transportation Board of a change in the anticipated filing date for their application seeking authority under 49 U.S.C. §§ 11323-25
docket_entries.relief_requested: Amendment to Notice of Intent to File Application to change anticipated application filing date from original date to December 19, 2025.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing establishes the formal application date, which triggers the statutory review timeline under 49 U.S.C. § 11324. The December 19, 2025 filing date will launch the clock on: (1) intervenor comment periods, (2) discovery deadlines, (3) hearing schedule, and (4) the Board's statutory decision deadline (typically 24 months from application filing). This date is material to all parties' strategic planning and compliance obligations.
docket_entries.document_type: Modify/Supplement Prior Filing Or The Record
docket_entries.deadline_description: Applicants' anticipated filing date for the formal merger application.

docket_entries.title: Amtrak Notice of Intent to Participate (No Comment)
docket_entries.entry_summary: Amtrak filed a procedural notice of intent to participate in the UP/NS merger proceeding without submitting substantive comments on the merger's merits. The filing designates two attorneys (Byl Herrmann, EVP/Chief Legal Officer, and Christopher Perry, Associate General Counsel) for the service list and consents to electronic service. No position on approval, denial, or conditions is expressed. This is a monitoring/placeholder filing typical of parties with potential but uncertain interests. Amtrak's intervention signals concern about passenger rail access to freight infrastructure, but the company defers substantive engagement pending further development of the record.
key_excerpts: The National Railroad Passenger Corporation (Amtrak) respectfully submits its Notice of Intent to Participate in the above-captioned proceeding as its interests may require
docket_entries.relief_requested: Amtrak requests placement on the service list and notification of all documents in the proceeding. No substantive position on the merger is stated.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing establishes Amtrak's intervention status and right to receive all docket materials, allowing later substantive filings without requiring new intervention motions. It signals to the Board and parties that a passenger rail operator views the transaction as potentially affecting its interests, which may influence the Board's consideration of passenger service impacts and trackage rights preservation. Amtrak's formal notice may also prompt the applicants to proactively address passenger rail access in their applications or negotiated remedies.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.deadline_description: No deadline; this is a notice of intent filing that requires no response

docket_entries.title: Norfolk Southern Supplemental Filing: Updated Traffic Tapes, GIS Data Dictionary, and Interchange Commitments
docket_entries.entry_summary: Norfolk Southern submitted supplemental materials at STB staff request, including updated traffic tapes spanning 2019-2024 with a revised data dictionary, a data dictionary for previously submitted GIS shape files, and an updated list of agreements containing interchange commitments. All materials except the GIS data dictionary were designated Highly Confidential under the Board's Protective Order. Norfolk Southern notes that some information described in prior Board decision filings is not provided because it is 'not kept in the normal course of business.' Materials were submitted via Box due to file size constraints. This filing is purely procedural compliance with no advocacy component.
key_arguments: Norfolk Southern is providing the materials in the format and with the designations required by the Board's Protective Order
Some historically requested information cannot be provided because Norfolk Southern does not maintain it in its ordinary business records
key_excerpts: At the request of Surface Transportation Board staff, Norfolk Southern Corporation and Norfolk Southern Railway Company (collectively, 'Norfolk Southern') provide the following additional information
Where information described in the appendix to Decision No. 2 is not provided, it is because it is not kept in the normal course of business.

The designation of traffic tapes as Highly Confidential protects proprietary routing and customer data while providing the Board with the information needed to model competitive effects. The interchange commitments list is relevant to the Board's evaluation of potential service remedies or commitments. The filing does not change the scope of review but demonstrates compliance with the discovery regime established under the Protective Order.
docket_entries.document_type: Modify/Supplement Prior Filing Or The Record

Implicit acknowledgment that certain historical data (noted where appendix to Decision No. 2 describes) is not maintained in normal business course

The traffic tapes are being submitted as Highly Confidential, as that term is defined in the Protective Order served in this docket on August 5, 2025.
