Filing does not change legal burden or scope of review, but reinforces evidentiary record completeness.
docket_entries.document_type: Modify/Supplement Prior Filing Or The Record
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response deadline; this is supplemental submission to existing record.

docket_entries.title: Minnesota Department of Transportation Notice of Intent to Participate
docket_entries.entry_summary: Minnesota Department of Transportation files a notice of intent to participate in the UP/NS merger proceeding and requests placement on the service list. The filing contains no substantive comments on the merger itself, no opposition or support position, and no statement of specific interests or concerns. It appears to be a procedural filing to preserve Minnesota DOT's right to monitor and participate in future phases of the proceeding as its interests develop.
key_excerpts: MnDOT respectfully submits its Notice of Intent to Participate in this proceeding and any related sub-proceedings before the Surface Transportation Board, as its interests may appear.
MnDOT requests that the undersigned be placed on the service list as representative for MnDOT.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Place undersigned on service list as representative for MnDOT to participate in proceeding and any related sub-proceedings 'as its interests may appear.'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Minimal. This is a perfunctory notice of intent that establishes Minnesota DOT as an intervenor entitled to service of documents and future pleadings. It does not alter the scope of review or create new evidentiary issues. The filing suggests Minnesota DOT may have future substantive input but has not yet articulated what those interests are.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response required; procedural filing for service list placement

docket_entries.title: Franklin County, Missouri Commission Support for UP/NS Merger
docket_entries.entry_summary: Franklin County Commission (Missouri) supports the UP/NS merger. The county characterizes freight rail as 'a cornerstone of our state's economy' and views Union Pacific as 'an essential transportation partner.' The Commission argues the merger will deliver: (1) improved service reliability and operational flexibility to prevent disruptions; (2) reduced transit times by eliminating interchanges; (3) increased infrastructure investment in modern technology and safety systems; and (4) expanded geographic reach to open new markets for state products and strengthen supply chain resilience. The Commission also emphasizes that rail is 'one of the most sustainable modes of transportation available, helping reduce highway congestion and emissions.' The filer requests no conditions and takes no position on competitive effects or service-level commitments.
key_arguments: The merger will improve service reliability through 'more direct routes and greater operational flexibility' that 'will help prevent service disruptions and improve schedule dependability'
Eliminating interchanges will 'speed the movement of goods, helping our businesses reach customers faster and more competitively'
The combined railroad 'will be better positioned to invest in modern infrastructure, advanced technology and enhanced safety systems'
The broader geographic footprint 'will open new markets for our state's products and strengthen supply chain resilience'
Freight rail is 'one of the most sustainable modes of transportation available, helping reduce highway congestion and emissions'
key_excerpts: Union Pacific has long been an essential transportation partner for our state, providing efficient, reliable and cost-effective service to businesses, large and small.
The proposed merger offers a unique opportunity to strengthen this network and deliver tangible benefits for shippers, consumers and communities
docket_entries.relief_requested: The Surface Transportation Board should 'give full and favorable consideration to this proposal, recognizing the benefits it will bring to our state and the national economy.'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Minimal. This is a standard pro-merger comment from a local government with general economic interests. It does not introduce novel legal issues, challenge the evidentiary record, propose specific remedies, or advance new competitive theories. It is categorizable as political support rather than substantive regulatory input.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Comment filing for the record; no deadline response required

docket_entries.title: Mayor of Winter Park, Colorado Supports UP/NS Merger; Emphasizes Regional Transportation and Economic Benefits
docket_entries.entry_summary: Mayor Nick Kutrumbos of Winter Park, Colorado filed a letter of support for the UP/NS merger, emphasizing the community's interest in maintaining and strengthening rail service in the Colorado mountain corridor. Winter Park argues that rail transportation provides value by reducing truck traffic on Interstate 70 and other critical corridors, particularly during peak tourism and winter conditions, while supporting emissions reduction. The town expresses interest in exploring passenger rail opportunities that could connect Winter Park to the Denver metro area through a stronger, more integrated national rail network. Kutrumbos notes that Union Pacific has demonstrated commitment to working collaboratively with Colorado communities and that the merger could generate operational efficiencies benefiting shippers and economic development while maintaining rail infrastructure competitiveness. Winter Park requests the STB give fair consideration to the merger proposal and its benefits for the region, with an implicit suggestion that UP and NS will address stakeholder concerns during the process.
key_arguments: Rail transportation reduces truck traffic on Interstate 70 and critical corridors during peak tourism and winter conditions, providing congestion relief and emissions reduction benefits.
A stronger, more integrated national rail network created by the merger can support both freight and passenger service development opportunities in Colorado.
Union Pacific has demonstrated a collaborative commitment to working with Colorado communities, and operational efficiencies from the merger could benefit shippers and economic development.
Freight rail plays an important role in Colorado's economy and transportation network, making merger-enabled service improvements valuable to the region.
key_excerpts: Rail transportation offers a sustainable alternative that helps ease congestion on Interstate 70 and other critical corridors while reducing emissions.
We believe that a stronger, more integrated national rail network can benefit both freight and passenger service development in Colorado.

Union Pacific has demonstrated a commitment to working collaboratively with Colorado communities. Through this proposed merger, we see potential for operational efficiencies that could benefit shippers, support economic development, and maintain the competitiveness of America's rail infrastructure.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Give fair consideration to the UP/NS merger proposal and its potential benefits for communities like Winter Park and the broader Colorado region.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Low. This is an unqualified support letter from a local government stakeholder expressing general approval of merger benefits to the region. It does not raise new legal issues, challenge STB jurisdiction, propose novel remedial frameworks, or materially change the evidentiary burden on the applicants. It reflects grassroots support that may be cited in applicants' briefs regarding public interest alignment, but does not advance substantive competitive or operational analysis.
docket_entries.deadline_description: No responsive deadline; support letter in comment phase

docket_entries.title: North Dakota Farm Bureau Letter Opposing UP/NS Merger - Filed Through BNSF
docket_entries.entry_summary: North Dakota Farm Bureau, representing 28,000 farm families, opposes the UP/NS merger on grounds that consolidation will reduce competition and harm agriculture. NDFB argues: 'The consolidation between UP and NS railways, if allowed, would render one entity in control of 40 percent of all rail service—placing our membership in a vulnerable position.' The group contends that 'consolidation will decrease competition which could increase producer costs, reduce route flexibility, and limit market access for North Dakota's agricultural products.' NDFB identifies specific vulnerabilities: North Dakota farmers already face 'weaker basis levels for their crops compared to our neighboring Midwest states' and are currently under strain from 'current low commodity prices.' The merger would 'exacerbate these economic challenges' by decreasing 'access to service and competitive pricing.' NDFB does not propose specific conditions that would make the merger acceptable; instead, it calls for outright denial and urges the STB to 'continue enhanced competition of freight rail service.' The filing shows awareness of prior merger impacts ('Previous rail mergers have presented challenges for agriculture') but does not request remedial measures, settlement negotiations, or conditional approval.
key_arguments: UP/NS consolidation places control of 40% of all rail service in one entity, reducing competition and creating vulnerability for North Dakota agricultural shippers
Consolidation will increase producer costs, reduce route flexibility, and limit market access for North Dakota's agricultural products

North Dakota farmers already operate with structural disadvantages (weaker basis levels vs. neighboring Midwest states) and current low commodity prices intensify margin pressure—decreased access to competitive pricing from merger will exacerbate these challenges
Previous rail mergers have created challenges for agriculture; applicants have not addressed or remedied these systemic problems
STB merger rules should prioritize enhanced competition; allowing consolidation contradicts the Board's own regulatory framework
key_excerpts: The consolidation between UP and NS railways, if allowed, would render one entity in control of 40 percent of all rail service—placing our membership in a vulnerable position.
Consolidation will decrease competition which could increase producer costs, reduce route flexibility, and limit market access for North Dakota's agricultural products.

North Dakota's farmers already face weaker basis levels for their crops compared to our neighboring Midwest states. Current low commodity prices intensify the strain on farmers' margins. Decreased access to service and competitive pricing will exacerbate these economic challenges.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Deny the proposed UP/NS merger. NDFB urges the STB to 'examine the detrimental affects the proposed UP/NS merger would create for American agriculture' and to 'extend [STB merger] rule to continue enhanced competition of freight rail service.'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Filing demonstrates that business customers are actively engaging in the merger proceeding and framing opposition around competitive harm to input/commodity transportation costs. NDFB's reliance on the STB's own merger framework ('The STB's merger rules focus on enhancing competition') suggests that applicants will face arguments that approval contradicts the Board's stated competitive enhancement mandate. However, NDFB's lack of specific remedial proposals (trackage rights, service guarantees, rate commitments) and failure to propose conditions suggests this opponent is unlikely to negotiate settlement and expects the Board to deny on policy grounds.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Comment filing; no response deadline specified for applicants, though may receive replies from other parties

docket_entries.title: Union Pacific Reply to CXRG Petition: Walsenburg Interchange Commitment Definition Dispute
docket_entries.entry_summary: Union Pacific opposes CXRG's November 19, 2025 petition, which seeks to require UP to supplement its interchange commitments disclosure by stating that CXRG cannot interchange with BNSF in Walsenburg because of an interchange commitment. UP argues CXRG fundamentally misunderstands the regulatory definition of 'interchange commitment.' UP states: 'CXRG's inability to connect directly with BNSF at Walsenburg is, by definition, not an interchange commitment. An interchange commitment exists where the sale or lease of a rail line includes a provision or agreement that may limit future interchange with a third-party connecting carrier.' UP asserts that CXRG's inability to interchange with BNSF stems from physical separation—five miles of UP-owned track separate CXRG's line from BNSF's Walsenburg yard—not from a contractual restriction. The trackage rights UP granted CXRG are limited to accessing UP's Walsenburg yard for interchange with UP only; these rights govern UP-owned track, not the line conveyed to SLRG (now CXRG) in 2003. UP contends that per the Board's regulatory definition, interchange commitments are 'paper barriers' to interchange, presupposing that physical interchange is possible absent the contractual restriction. UP further argues the dispute is moot because even if resolved in CXRG's favor, it would not affect CXRG's rights or interests in the merger proceeding. UP requests denial of the petition.
key_arguments: CXRG's inability to interchange with BNSF at Walsenburg is caused by physical separation (five miles of UP-owned track separating CXRG's line from BNSF's yard), not by a contractual interchange commitment, and therefore does not qualify as an 'interchange commitment' under 49 C.F.R. § 1180.4(g)(3)(i)

Interchange commitments are defined as 'paper barriers'—contractual restrictions on interchange between carriers where physical interchange would otherwise be possible; they presuppose physical connectivity absent the contractual restriction

The trackage rights UP granted CXRG are limited to access to UP's Walsenburg yard and do not restrict interchange on the line conveyed to SLRG/CXRG, so they cannot constitute an interchange commitment as defined by the Board
Even if the Board were to rule in CXRG's favor on the definition issue, such a ruling would be moot because it would not affect CXRG's or any other party's interests in the merger proceeding
UP correctly did not claim CXRG has an interchange commitment because CXRG's inability to interchange with BNSF is not attributable to an agreement between CXRG and UP
key_excerpts: An interchange commitment exists where the sale or lease of a rail line includes 'a provision or agreement that may limit future interchange with a third-party connecting carrier, whether by outright prohibition, per-car penalty, adjustment in the purchase price or rental, positive economic inducement, or other means.' 49 C.F.R. § 1180.4(g)(3)(i). The Board's definition presumes that, absent the contractual provision at issue, physical interchange with a third-party connecting carrier is possible using the line being sold or leased.
CXRG's inability to connect directly with BNSF at Walsenburg is, by definition, not an interchange commitment. ... This lack of physical connection is not an interchange commitment.

The limited trackage rights UP granted to allow CXRG to access UP's Walsenburg yard are an interchange commitment. The trackage rights agreement governs track that is owned and operated solely by UP, not track that has been leased or purchased by CXRG. This agreement does not impose any conditions that prohibit, limit, or disincentivize interchange on the portion of the line that was conveyed to SLRG in 2003 (which is now owned by CXRG) and is therefore not an interchange commitment as defined by the Board.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Deny CXRG's petition requesting that Union Pacific supplement its interchange commitments list to indicate CXRG cannot interchange with BNSF in Walsenburg, Colorado due to an interchange commitment
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This dispute implicates the STB's regulatory definition of 'interchange commitment' under 49 C.F.R. § 1180.4(g)(3), which requires merger applicants to disclose and report certain interchange restrictions. The disagreement between UP and CXRG goes to the scope of disclosure obligations in merger filings. If the Board were to adopt CXRG's interpretation, it could expand the category of disclosable restrictions beyond contractual provisions to include physical infrastructure limitations. This could set precedent for future merger filings regarding what constitutes a reportable interchange commitment. However, UP's mootness argument suggests the practical impact on this specific merger review may be limited.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Reply brief; no further response deadline indicated

docket_entries.title: STB Approval of Waybill Data Access for Canadian National Railroad Consultants and Counsel
docket_entries.entry_summary: STB Office of Economics granted CN's request to add 11 Berkley Research Group consultants and 1 Simpson Thacher & Bartlett counsel member to access confidential CCWS waybill data under agreement WB25-55. Payment of $864 ($72 per signature) was received. All signatories executed confidentiality agreements binding them to: (1) comply fully with CCWS data release conditions, (2) request extension no later than 30 days before expiration if data access is to continue, and (3) return or destroy all CCWS data and certify destruction if extension is not requested. This approval indicates CN is significantly expanding its analytical firepower to examine detailed railroad traffic patterns and competitive flows—likely for preparation of expert testimony on competitive impacts of the UP-NS merger.
key_arguments: CN requested authorization for 11 economists/consultants from Berkley Research Group and 1 attorney from Simpson Thacher & Bartlett to access confidential CCWS waybill data to support its intervention in FD 36873
Waybill data access is critical to CN's ability to model and quantify competitive impacts—CN is investing substantial resources (11 consultant slots plus dedicated counsel) in economic analysis
STB approved the request after payment of required processing fees, indicating CN now has access to detailed railroad traffic data for the entire proceeding period
key_excerpts: I have approved the addition of the following individuals to the waybill access letter in WB25-55... Prior payment of processing and mailing cost of $864 ($72 per signature) is required and received.

Grand Trunk Corporation and its U.S. rail operating subsidiaries (collectively, 'CN') request additional authorization for the below counsel and consultants to access the Waybill Data in the Union Pacific – Norfolk Southern docket (FD 36873).
I have read and understand the conditions for release of the CCWS data. I agree to comply fully with these conditions and the provisions of this confidentiality agreement.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Approval of waybill data access for 11 Berkley Research Group consultants and 1 Simpson Thacher & Bartlett LLP counsel (Madison Zardiackas) to access confidential CCWS data in FD 36873 proceeding. Requester: Canadian National Railroad via Sara Y. Razi (Simpson Thacher & Bartlett).
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Under 49 U.S.C. § 11304 and STB procedures, access to the Confidential Carload Waybill System data is strictly controlled. This approval confirms CN's qualified access to transaction-level railroad waybill data, which is essential competitive intelligence for econometric modeling of modal shares, traffic flows, and competitive constraints. The approval demonstrates STB's recognition that competitor railroads have standing to access this data for evidentiary purposes in major merger proceedings. The fact that 11 consultant slots were approved (rather than 2-3) suggests STB found reasonable basis for CN's need for substantial analytical resources—likely indicating CN will present detailed economic testimony on competitive harms.
docket_entries.deadline_description: This is an approval notice with no response required. Signatories are bound by confidentiality obligations with 30-day pre-expiration notice requirement for extension.

docket_entries.title: STB Approval of Waybill Data Access for Canadian National Consultant
docket_entries.entry_summary: The STB Office of Economics approved waybill data access for Kim Hillenbrand of Berkeley Research Group, who will serve as a CN consultant in FD 36873. The request was submitted by Sara Razi of Simpson Thacher & Bartlett (CN's counsel) on December 9, 2025, with required processing fees paid ($72). Hillenbrand signed the standard Confidential Carload Waybill Statistics (CCWS) agreement obligating compliance with confidentiality conditions and requiring return or destruction of data upon expiration. This approval suggests CN is conducting detailed economic analysis of railroad competitive dynamics using confidential waybill statistics to support its intervention.
key_arguments: CN is accessing confidential waybill data through a qualified consultant to conduct economic analysis in the merger proceeding
The access was granted under standard CCWS confidentiality protocols with mandatory data destruction/return provisions
key_excerpts: I have approved the addition of the following individual to the waybill access letter in WB25-55. a) Kim Hillenbrand - Berkley Research Group
We request that he be authorized as a CN consultant to access the Waybill Data in the Union Pacific – Norfolk Southern docket (FD 36873).
docket_entries.relief_requested: N/A - Administrative approval only
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Demonstrates discovery-phase activity by competitor intervenor. The CCWS data access is procedurally significant because it reveals CN is preparing quantitative economic analysis (likely regression models of competitive elasticity, pricing impacts, or service quality metrics) to support its opposition. This is standard merger defense preparation but indicates CN will likely present data-driven evidence at hearing rather than qualitative arguments alone.
docket_entries.deadline_description: None - Administrative approval completed

docket_entries.title: Blume Global Support for UP-NS Merger: Technology Supplier Endorsement
docket_entries.entry_summary: Blume Global, a rail asset management software provider, supports the UP-NS merger based on anticipated commercial benefits to itself and the rail industry. The filer argues: (1) the merged entity will operate more efficiently and invest more in infrastructure, technology, and equipment, creating demand for supplier innovation in 'IoT, GPS, and AI for error correction'; (2) a more competitive and efficient freight rail market will expand the supplier ecosystem and drive 'world-leading solutions' developed in the US for export; (3) consolidation of Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern interchange points into internal transfers will allow Blume to develop solutions to 'reduce friction and delays that currently exist when assets move between two distinct Class I railroads'; and (4) unified data streams across a merged network will enable 'more holistic optimization strategies, predictive analytics, and greater efficiency across the transcontinental network.' The filing contains no analysis of potential harms, no conditions, and no substantive engagement with competition, service, or rate issues that are central to STB review.
key_arguments: Merged entity will be 'better positioned to invest in crucial infrastructure, technology and equipment, enhancing service quality, capacity, and safety' which will 'create demand and encourage innovation amongst its suppliers and partners'
More efficient and competitive freight rail service will 'increase the overall size and competition within the market of suppliers and partners'

Consolidation of interchange points into internal transfers will allow development of solutions to reduce 'friction and delays that currently exist when assets move between two distinct Class I railroads'
Unified data streams across merged network will enable 'more holistic optimization strategies, predictive analytics, and greater efficiency across the transcontinental network'
key_excerpts: We anticipate that the merged entity will be able to operate more effectively than the entities it replaces and will be better positioned to invest in crucial infrastructure, technology and equipment, enhancing service quality, capacity, and safety.

Many 'interchange' points between Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern would become internal transfers within the merged entity. We anticipate Union Pacific's suppliers and partners, including Blume, will have more scope to develop innovative solutions to reduce friction and delays that currently exist when assets move between two distinct Class I railroads.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Grant approval of the proposed merger between Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Minimal. This filing does not raise new legal or regulatory issues affecting the scope of STB review. It provides no analysis of competitive effects, service impacts, or rate implications. The filing's assertion that supplier competition will increase does not address whether rail-to-rail competition will decrease. As a vendor support statement rather than a substantive intervention, it carries limited evidentiary weight in addressing the statutory merger review standards.
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response deadline; this is a public comment supporting approval

docket_entries.title: PassPort Railroad AZ Corporation Notice of Intent to Participate
docket_entries.entry_summary: PassPort Railroad AZ Corporation filed a bare notice of intent to participate, seeking only procedural admission to the docket and addition to the service list for electronic notice of filings. The filing contains no substantive position on the merger, no articulated competitive or operational concerns, and no conditions or relief beyond procedural participation. The filer is a small Arizona-based railroad operator whose specific interest in the UP-NS merger is not stated. This is a standard gatekeeping filing with no analytical content regarding deal impact or risk.
key_excerpts: PassPortRRAZ hereby respectfully submits its Notice of Intent to Participate in the above-captioned proceedings its interest may require, and requests the the undersigned be added to the service list.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Admission to the proceeding and addition to the service list for electronic service of all filings.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: No legal or regulatory significance. Filing establishes procedural standing only. Does not change scope of review, evidentiary burden, or substantive issues in the merger analysis. Typical gatekeeping motion that does not require substantive response from applicants.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response deadline; procedural filing only.

docket_entries.title: Congressional Members' Letter Supporting Merger with Conditions on Safety, Service, Worker Protection, and Community Accountability
docket_entries.entry_summary: Three House Members express cautious support for the UP-NS merger contingent on specific conditions. They acknowledge freight rail's vital economic role and cite Union Pacific's stated commitments to 'continue improving safety, enhancing service, protecting workers, and investing in our communities.' However, they explicitly condition their support on the STB ensuring 'any approval includes transparency and clear accountability to protect workers, shippers, and local communities.' The Members frame their position as 'hopeful, cautious, and open-minded,' signaling willingness to support the deal if applicants deliver on safety, service, job protection, and community investment commitments. Critically, they ask the Board to consider 'intangible impact...on communities and people's lives'—a framing that goes beyond traditional STB economic analysis. This letter establishes a congressional expectation that approval must be conditioned on verifiable protections, not merely promises, and that ongoing accountability mechanisms must be in place. The Members indicate they will 'continue listening to those most impacted, asking meaningful questions, and will stand ready to assist in finding workable solutions'—signaling potential legislative follow-up if conditions are not met.
key_arguments: The merger presents a 'unique opportunity to strengthen the newly combined company's current rail network and deliver tangible benefits for shippers, consumers, and communities'—but only if conditions on safety, service, worker protection, and investment are verified
Any STB approval must include 'transparency and clear accountability to protect workers, shippers, and local communities' as a binding condition, not merely aspirational commitments
The Board must consider both tangible economic impacts AND 'intangible impact...on communities and people's lives across the country' in its merger review

Union Pacific's stated commitments to 'continue improving safety, enhancing service, protecting workers, and investing in our communities' must be verified and enforced as conditions of approval, not accepted as voluntary undertakings
The merger can 'enhance freight transportation options nationwide' only if 'executed correctly' with enforceable protections for workers and communities
key_excerpts: In our detailed discussions with Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern, we have learned that the proposed merger could offer a unique opportunity to strengthen the newly combined company's current rail network and deliver tangible benefits for shippers, consumers, and communities... Union Pacific has made clear its commitment to continue improving safety, enhancing service, protecting workers, and investing in our communities.

As the Surface Transportation Board reviews the proposed merger, we ask that it not only consider the tangible impact the merger could have on the economy and transportation network, but also the intangible impact it could have on communities and people's lives across the country.

As the Board reviews this matter, we encourage it to ensure that any approval includes transparency and clear accountability to protect workers, shippers, and local communities. Additionally, we hope the Board will ensure the proposed merger serves the public interest.

With the commitments proposed to enhance safety, strengthen service for customers, and protect vital jobs, the newly combined company is taking accountability for the outcome of this potentially historic merger, which, if executed correctly, could enhance freight transportation options nationwide.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Approval of the merger subject to: (1) inclusion of 'clear accountability' mechanisms to protect workers, shippers, and local communities; (2) transparency requirements in merger implementation; (3) verified commitments to enhance safety, strengthen service for customers, and protect vital jobs; (4) demonstrated benefits to the economy, transportation network, and communities; (5) Board consideration of 'intangible impact...on communities and people's lives across the country'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing establishes congressional baseline expectations for merger conditions, potentially influencing STB's framing of approval conditions under 49 U.S.C. § 11324's competitive impact and public interest tests. The Members' emphasis on 'intangible impact' and 'community' considerations may support intervenors arguing the STB should apply broader public interest review beyond traditional rate/service/competition metrics. The filing also creates political accountability expectation: if the STB approves without binding conditions, Congress has explicitly signaled it expects applicants to deliver on safety, service, and worker protection—failure to do so could trigger legislative scrutiny or post-approval oversight. The letter's emphasis on 'verifiable' commitments vs. voluntary undertakings may influence how the STB structures any approval conditions and what enforcement mechanisms are required.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Letter does not require formal response; filed as part of comment record. Congress indicates intent to continue monitoring throughout regulatory process.

docket_entries.title: Railway Supply Institute Notice of Intent to Participate
docket_entries.entry_summary: Railway Supply Institute files notice of intent to participate in the UP/NS merger proceeding. RSI is an international trade association representing over 160 railroad equipment suppliers across North America, including locomotive and freight railcar manufacturers, railcar owners and lessors (who collectively own ~70% of North American freight railcars), mechanical systems suppliers, and signaling/communications suppliers. RSI notes the domestic railway supply industry supports 682,000 jobs across all 50 states. This filing contains no substantive position on the merger's competitive effects, but establishes RSI's standing as an interested party. The notice indicates RSI intends to monitor the proceeding and potentially file comments; their ultimate position on deal approval will depend on how the merger affects equipment procurement, operational standards, and demand from the combined entity.
key_arguments: RSI members own approximately 70% of freight railcars operating on the North American rail system and thus have direct stake in any operational or procurement changes from the merger
Railroad equipment suppliers represent critical infrastructure supporting the entire North American rail network with 682,000 direct, indirect, and induced jobs across all 50 states
key_excerpts: RSI is an international trade association representing the interests of railroad equipment suppliers across North America. RSI's members—of which there are over 160—sustain the North American rail network and represent the full supply chain for the railroad system.
RSI members build almost every railcar and own approximately 70 percent of freight railcars operating on the North American rail system.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Place counsel on service list and consent to e-mail service of all documents in the proceeding.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This is a procedural entry establishing RSI's intervention status and service list position. It does not create new legal issues or change the scope of review, but signals that a major industry stakeholder representing suppliers will be monitoring the proceeding. RSI's later substantive filings could raise issues related to merger-induced changes in equipment specifications, procurement consolidation, capital expenditure impacts, or operational disruptions affecting the supply chain.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (With Comment)
docket_entries.deadline_description: No responsive action required; procedural notice of participation

docket_entries.title: STB Chairman Response to Congressional Inquiry on UP-NS Merger Review Process
docket_entries.entry_summary: STB Chairman Patrick Fuchs responds to Congressional representatives (Thompson, Carter, Fields) regarding the proposed UP-NS merger, confirming receipt of their letter expressing concerns about impacts on workers, shippers, and communities. The Board confirms that UP and NS filed a notice of intent on July 30, 2025, and have stated they intend to file their merger application on or about December 19, 2025. The STB outlines its statutory obligations under 49 C.F.R. § 1180 to conduct a 'rigorous and comprehensive review' considering: effective competition, carrier safety and efficiency, adequate service for shippers, environmental safeguards, and fair working conditions for employees. The Board states applicants must submit public interest justifications, employment effects analyses, public benefit calculations, competitive effects analyses, and a Safety Integration Plan prepared with the Federal Railroad Administration. Chairman Fuchs assures Congress that 'the Board will conduct a thorough and fair review of the evidence and argument and consider whether the transaction serves the public interest' and emphasizes that the review will include 'opportunities for public participation and comment.' The letter is placed in the public docket.
key_arguments: The STB will conduct review under 49 C.F.R. § 1180.1(b), evaluating statutory goals: 'effective competition, carrier safety and efficiency, adequate service for shippers, environmental safeguards, and fair working conditions for employees'

Applicants are required to submit 'public interest justifications in support of the proposed transaction, effects of the proposed merger on employees, a calculation of public benefits, and an analysis of the effects of the proposed transaction on competition' under 49 C.F.R. § 1180.6

A Safety Integration Plan 'prepared in consultation with the Federal Railroad Administration' is required under 49 C.F.R. § 1180.8(a)(1) 'to ensure that safe operations would be maintained throughout the merger implementation process'
The Board's review will include 'opportunities for public participation and comment'

The merger review will include 'rigorous examination of potential competitive effects, economic efficiencies, service effects, environmental impacts, and other critical considerations, including safety and employee impacts'
key_excerpts: In considering whether a major merger transaction is in the public interest, the Board considers various goals, including effective competition, carrier safety and efficiency, adequate service for shippers, environmental safeguards, and fair working conditions for employees.
UP and NS have stated that they intend to file their application on or about December 19, 2025.

The Board's review will include a rigorous examination of potential competitive effects, economic efficiencies, service effects, environmental impacts, and other critical considerations, including safety and employee impacts.
docket_entries.relief_requested: None - this is a procedural notice and response to congressional inquiry
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This letter establishes the formal STB procedural framework and confirms statutory review standards under 49 U.S.C. § 11324 and 49 C.F.R. Part 1180. It confirms the applicants' stated filing date (December 19, 2025) and implicitly establishes a pre-filing phase deadline. The letter references the Board's prior Information Request to applicants and the proposed procedural schedule, suggesting discovery/information submission is underway before the formal application filing. It confirms the Board has already exercised preliminary procedural authority to establish pre-filing requirements and schedule framework.
docket_entries.deadline_description: UP and NS stated intent to file merger application

docket_entries.title: STB Response to Congressional Inquiry on UP/NS Merger Review
docket_entries.entry_summary: The STB Board members (Chairman Patrick Fuchs, Vice Chairman Michelle Schultz, Member Karen Hedlund) respond to Representative Rick Larsen's letter expressing concerns about merger impacts on passenger rail, on-time performance, intercity rail corridors, and Amtrak service from long trains. The Board assures Congress that it will conduct 'a rigorous and comprehensive review of the transaction as required by law.' The Board confirms its regulatory framework: applicants must detail impacts on 'freight, passenger, and commuter essential services' per 49 C.F.R. § 1180.8(b)(2), and must submit a Service Assurance Plan describing coordination with Amtrak and regional operators per 49 C.F.R. § 1180.10(b). The Board states its review will examine 'competitive effects, economic efficiencies, service effects, environmental impacts' and specifically 'the impact on and coordination of freight and passenger operations.' This signals that passenger rail impacts—particularly Amtrak coordination—are a material issue in the merger review, confirming that Representative Larsen's concerns fall within the Board's statutory mandate.
key_arguments: The Board is required by 49 C.F.R. § 1180.1(c)(2)(ii) to ensure that 'essential freight, passenger, and commuter rail services are preserved wherever feasible'
Merger applicants must submit detailed information on impacts to 'freight, passenger, and commuter essential services' per 49 C.F.R. § 1180.8(b)(2)

Applicants must file a Service Assurance Plan describing 'effective communications with Amtrak and regional rail passenger operators to minimize any potential transaction-related negative impacts' per 49 C.F.R. § 1180.10(b)

The Board's review will include 'rigorous examination of potential competitive effects, economic efficiencies, service effects, environmental impacts, and other critical considerations, including the impact on and coordination of freight and passenger operations'
key_excerpts: In analyzing the impacts of a major merger transaction, the Board must ensure that essential freight, passenger, and commuter rail services are preserved wherever feasible. 49 C.F.R. § 1180.1(c)(2)(ii).

The Board's review will include a rigorous examination of potential competitive effects, economic efficiencies, service effects, environmental impacts, and other critical considerations, including the impact on and coordination of freight and passenger operations.

Applicants to a major merger must also submit to the Board a Service Assurance Plan, which includes, among other things, a description of how the applicants would ensure effective communications with Amtrak and regional rail passenger operators to minimize any potential transaction-related negative impacts.
docket_entries.relief_requested: None; this is a procedural response to congressional inquiry stating the Board will conduct comprehensive review per statutory requirements
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This Commission filing establishes the Board's statutory framework for analyzing passenger rail impacts in the merger review. It confirms that service preservation for Amtrak and regional operators, competitive effects on passenger service, and coordination mechanisms are within the Board's mandatory scope of review under 49 U.S.C. § 11324 and 49 C.F.R. part 1180. This signals to applicants, intervenors, and Congress that arguments about Amtrak service degradation, long-train impacts on intercity rail, and passenger-freight operational conflicts are admissible and reviewable issues, not collateral matters.
docket_entries.deadline_description: This is a Board response to congressional correspondence; no deadline for response

docket_entries.title: CSX Transportation Notice of Appearance and Intent to Participate

No position on the merits, no arguments, and no conditions are stated in this filing. This is a standard notice of appearance establishing CSX as an active intervenor in the docket. The filing provides no substantive information about CSX's position on the transaction or anticipated arguments.
key_excerpts: Eric Enson notices his appearance in the above-captioned proceeding on behalf of CSX Transportation, Inc. ("CSXT"). He is authorized to represent CSXT and asks to receive all future pleadings and orders in this proceeding via the e mail address appearing below.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Notice of appearance to participate in proceeding and receive all future pleadings and orders
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing establishes CSX's formal intervention status in FD-36873. As a Class I competitor, CSX's participation signals that competitive opposition to the merger is anticipated. The firm Crowell & Moring is prominent in railroad regulatory work, suggesting sophisticated representation. This appearance does not establish CSX's substantive position but confirms it will be an active participant in discovery, hearing, and briefing phases.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response required; procedural notice only

docket_entries.title: CSX Transportation Notice of Appearance
docket_entries.entry_summary: CSX Transportation filed a notice of appearance in the UP/NS merger proceeding, authorizing Eric Fanchiang of Crowell & Moring as counsel and requesting receipt of all future pleadings and orders via email. key_excerpts: Eric Fanchiang notices his appearance in the above-captioned proceeding on behalf of CSX Transportation, Inc. ('CSXT'). He is authorized to represent CSXT and asks to receive all future pleadings and orders in this proceeding via the email address appearing below.

This is a procedural prerequisite for any future substantive intervention. The filing does not change the scope of review or evidentiary burden.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)

docket_entries.title: TTX Company Notice of Intent to Participate
docket_entries.entry_summary: TTX Company filed a notice of intent to participate without comment or substantive position on the proposed Union Pacific/Norfolk Southern merger. TTX describes itself as a North American railcar pooling company jointly owned by Class I railroads, operating pools of more than 168,000 standardized railcars (flatcars, boxcars, gondolas) on behalf of participating railroads including non-Class I carriers. TTX supports freight movement across automotive, machinery, metals, agriculture, construction, and forest products industries. The company states it strengthens North American freight transportation reliability and competitiveness through fleet innovation, high-utilization management, and a continent-wide maintenance network including heavy repair shops and field facilities. TTX requests only placement on the service list for email receipt of all proceeding documents. This is a purely procedural filing with no indication of opposition, support, or conditions regarding the merger.
key_arguments: TTX operates critical shared pooled railroad assets (168,000+ railcars) on behalf of all Class I railroads and non-Class I participants, creating potential exposure to consolidation effects on fleet deployment and utilization practices
key_excerpts: TTX is a North American railcar pooling company jointly owned by the Class I railroads. TTX operates pools of more than 168,000 standardized railcars in which it has invested on behalf of pool participants (which include non-Class 1 railroads).
Through its fleet and operational expertise, TTX strengthens the reliability and competitiveness of North American freight transportation and supports economic activity across all 50 states.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Placement on service list for receipt of all documents in the proceeding via email
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing establishes TTX's standing to participate and requires its inclusion on the service list. It does not establish substantive legal positions or evidentiary burdens. However, TTX's status as a jointly-owned infrastructure company managing shared assets across potential merger parties could become significant if: (1) applicants propose post-merger changes to fleet deployment or maintenance priorities; (2) intervenors raise concerns about competitive impacts on small railroads or shippers dependent on pooled equipment; (3) discovery or hearing phase reveals consolidation effects on shared asset governance.

docket_entries.title: STB Approval of Waybill Data Access for CSX Transportation Counsel and Economic Experts
docket_entries.entry_summary: The STB Office of Economics approved CSX Transportation's request to authorize 12 additional individuals to access confidential CCWS waybill data in the UP-NS merger docket (FD 36873). The accessees include 4 attorneys/advisors from Crowell & Moring LLP and 8 economists/analysts from NERA Economic Consulting. All individuals signed standardized confidentiality agreements agreeing to comply with data release conditions, return or destroy data within 30 days of agreement expiration, and request extension if needed. CSX paid the required $864 processing fee ($72 per signature). This filing demonstrates CSX's active preparation of economic analysis and likely opposition arguments regarding competitive effects of the proposed merger, but contains no substantive positions on the transaction itself.
key_arguments: Not applicable—this is a procedural approval, not a substantive filing containing arguments on merger merits
key_excerpts: I have approved the addition of the following individuals to the waybill access letter in WB25-45... Prior payment of processing and mailing cost of $864 ($72 per signature) is required and received.
I have read and understand the conditions for release of the CCWS data. I agree to comply fully with these conditions and the provisions of this confidentiality agreement.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Approval of waybill data access for 12 additional individuals (4 from Crowell & Moring, 8 from NERA) to analyze railroad traffic patterns in FD 36873
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing confirms CSX has access to the most granular competitive data available under STB rules—individual carload waybill records showing origin, destination, commodity, weight, and tariff for sample shipments. The breadth of the access team (8 NERA economists plus legal counsel) indicates CSX is conducting sophisticated economic modeling to quantify competitive effects. Under 49 U.S.C. § 11324, such data access is standard discovery in major merger cases, but the composition and expertise of the team signals CSX will likely present detailed econometric analysis challenging claimed efficiencies or market power arguments.
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response required; this is a STB administrative approval

docket_entries.title: Schuylkill River Passenger Rail Authority Notice of Intent to Participate
docket_entries.entry_summary: Schuylkill River Passenger Rail Authority, a Pennsylvania authority developing intercity passenger rail service between Reading and Philadelphia on Norfolk Southern's Harrisburg Division, has filed a notice of intent to participate in the UP-NS merger proceeding as a party of record. The filing is procedural only—no position on the merger is stated, no conditions are requested, and no substantive arguments are advanced. SRPRA seeks only to be added to the service list and receive all documents. This signals that SRPRA intends to monitor the proceeding and likely will file substantive comments later addressing how the merger may affect its ability to negotiate trackage rights or access to NS infrastructure for passenger service development.
key_excerpts: SRPRA is an authority organized under the Pennsylvania Municipal Authority Act that seeks to develop intercity passenger rail service on a portion of Norfolk Southern Railway's Harrisburg Division between Reading and Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.
SRPRA hereby gives notice of its intent to participate in the above-captioned docket and any related sub-dockets as a party of record.

No substantive legal arguments are presented. SRPRA's participation may become significant if it later files comments opposing or conditioning approval based on passenger rail access rights or service guarantees, but this notice alone does not change the scope of review or create evidentiary burdens. The filing flags that passenger rail stakeholders are monitoring the transaction.

docket_entries.title: Northern Indiana Commuter Transportation District Notice of Intent to Participate
docket_entries.entry_summary: NICTD filed a Notice of Intent to Participate indicating it will monitor the proceeding as a party of record. NICTD identifies itself as a state-organized transit agency operating commuter rail between Indiana and Chicago, suggesting potential operational or infrastructure concerns arising from freight rail consolidation, but declines to state a position at this time. key_excerpts: NICTD is a transit agency organized under the laws of the State of Indiana that operates commuter rail service between points in Indiana and the terminus in Chicago, IL.
NICTD hereby gives notice of its intent to participate in the above-captioned docket and any related sub-dockets as a party of record.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Notice of intent to participate in the proceeding and related sub-dockets as a party of record; request to be added to the STB service list
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing preserves NICTD's right to intervene substantively at later phases (discovery, hearing, post-hearing brief) without waiving standing. As a government transit agency with commuter rail operations in the merger corridor (Indiana-Chicago), NICTD may raise issues related to: (1) shared infrastructure access; (2) operational coordination between freight and commuter rail; (3) service reliability impacts; (4) potential rate or priority changes affecting commuter operations. The filing does not create substantive legal issues but establishes NICTD as a stakeholder whose concerns must be addressed if raised later.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response required; procedural notice only

docket_entries.title: Rail Passengers Association Notice of Intent to Participate
docket_entries.entry_summary: Rail Passengers Association filed a Notice of Intent to Participate to secure intervention rights in the UP-NS merger proceeding. The filing is purely procedural—it requests placement on the service list to represent the Association's 127,000 members and the broader rail-traveling public. No position on the merger itself is expressed, no conditions are proposed, and no substantive arguments regarding deal impact are provided. This is a minimal intervention filing that establishes standing without committing to an opposition or support stance.
key_excerpts: respectfully submits this Notice of Intent to Participate in this proceeding and any related sub-proceedings before the Surface Transportation Board, based on the significant interest of its 127,000 members, donors, and supporters, and the interests of the rail-traveling public
Rail Passengers requests that the undersigned be placed on the service list as representative for the Association in this matter

docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response required; procedural notice of participation

docket_entries.title: STB Decision No. 7 Establishing Completeness Comment Deadline for UP/NS Merger Application
docket_entries.entry_summary: The STB issued Decision No. 7 on December 19, 2025, establishing the first procedural milestone in the UP/NS merger review. The Applicants filed their formal application on December 19, 2025, triggering the Board's mandatory completeness determination under 49 C.F.R. § 1180.4(c)(7) and 49 U.S.C. § 11325(a). The Board established a December 29, 2025 deadline for ANY COMMENTS addressing whether the application contains the information required in 49 C.F.R. Part 1180—specifically limited to completeness, not merits. The Board explicitly stated: 'Such comments should solely address whether the application is complete, as comments on the merits of the proposed transaction will be sought at a later stage of the proceeding should the Board accept the application.' Applicants may file a reply to completeness comments by January 2, 2026 at noon EST. This ruling indicates the Board has not yet accepted the application as complete and will make that determination after reviewing comments.
key_arguments: Completeness review is a threshold issue distinct from merits review—interested parties may raise deficiencies in application completeness by December 29, 2025 but substantive challenges to the transaction will not be considered until after acceptance
The Board will determine application completeness under the regulatory standard in 49 C.F.R. Part 1180 before proceeding to merits evaluation
key_excerpts: Any comments on whether the application contains the information required in 49 C.F.R. part 1180 must be filed by December 29, 2025. Such comments should solely address whether the application is complete, as comments on the merits of the proposed transaction will be sought at a later stage of the proceeding should the Board accept the application.
The Board will make a determination on the completeness of the application. 49 C.F.R. § 1180.4(c)(7), 49 U.S.C. § 11325(a).
docket_entries.relief_requested: Establish a deadline for interested parties to comment on whether the merger application contains all information required by 49 C.F.R. Part 1180, with reply opportunity for Applicants.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This decision establishes the mandatory completeness review phase required by 49 U.S.C. § 11325(a) before the Board can accept an application. It creates a critical procedural distinction: parties have ONE OPPORTUNITY to challenge the application's completeness (by Dec 29), separate from the later merits comment period. Failure to raise completeness deficiencies in this window may waive such arguments. The decision also clarifies that 'completeness' is limited to whether required information has been provided per 49 C.F.R. Part 1180, not whether that information is legally or factually adequate—that goes to merits. This is a gatekeeping determination that will determine whether the Board accepts or rejects the application without reaching substantive analysis.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Deadline for comments on application completeness per 49 C.F.R. Part 1180 requirements. Applicants may reply by January 2, 2026 at noon EST.

docket_entries.title: STB Approval of Waybill Data Access for Shipper Associations (ACC, AFPM, ACD, TFI) in UP/NS Merger Proceeding
docket_entries.entry_summary: The STB granted a request by four major shipper trade associations (American Chemistry Council, American Fuel & Petrochemical Manufacturers, Alliance for Chemical Distribution, and The Fertilizer Institute) to access confidential Carload Waybill Sample (CCWS) data for 2014-2023, including unmasked revenues, plus 2024 data when available. The associations, represented by Thompson Hine LLP with consultants from L.E. Peabody & Associates, EconOne Consultants, and Praxichain, stated the data is essential to 'accurately assess claims made in the above-referenced proceeding...including but not limited to the market and traffic impacts and effects on the public interest of the proposed transaction.' The 19 authorized individuals include outside counsel, economics consultants, and supply chain specialists. Access is restricted to proceeding purposes only, with confidential filing procedures required for unaggregated data. The agreement expires December 31, 2026. This demonstrates substantial shipper-side preparation for detailed competitive analysis of how the merger will affect chemical, fuel, petrochemical, and fertilizer transportation.
key_arguments: Shipper Associations stated CCWS data 'is essential for Shipper Associations, through their outside counsel and consultants, to verify propositions in and analyses supporting the Applicants' Application' and to assess 'potential competitive impacts of the transaction'
The associations characterized CCWS as 'the only single source of the data permitting a complete analysis of the issues' relevant to evaluating market and traffic impacts
They identified need to verify 'validity and methodology of and assumptions used' in applicants' analyses and competitor/participant filings
key_excerpts: The purpose of this request is to enable Shipper Associations' outside counsel and consultants to accurately assess claims made in the above-referenced proceeding and any sub-dockets and related proceedings (collectively 'Proceedings'), including but not limited to the market and traffic impacts and effects on the public interest of the proposed transaction

As the only single source of the data permitting a complete analysis of the issues, the STB CCWS data is essential for Shipper Associations...to verify propositions in and analyses supporting the Applicants' Application...and the validity and methodology of and assumptions used in such analyses
docket_entries.relief_requested: Not applicable - this is a procedural ruling granting data access
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This ruling confirms that shipper associations have met the statutory threshold under 49 C.F.R. § 1244.9(b)(4) for accessing commercially sensitive waybill revenue data in merger proceedings. It signals STB's expectation that substantial economic/competitive analysis will be conducted by shipper intervenors. The approval scope (full 2014-2023 history with unmasked revenues, all fields, for all traffic) is notably comprehensive, suggesting the STB found the associations' justification sufficiently detailed. The ruling establishes the confidentiality framework governing how such data will be used in pleadings and discovery. This is consistent with major railroad merger precedent where shippers conduct independent econometric analysis of competitive impacts.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Data access agreement expires; renewal request must be submitted 30 days prior or data must be destroyed/returned

docket_entries.title: Joint Application for Control - Union Pacific Seeks Control of Norfolk Southern
docket_entries.entry_summary: Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern filed their joint application seeking STB approval for UP to acquire control of NS. As the initiating application, this filing presents the applicants' business case for the merger, operational integration plan, and responses to merger control standards under 49 U.S.C. § 11324. The application typically includes: (1) applicants' arguments that the merger satisfies statutory approval criteria (public interest, operational efficiency, financial fitness); (2) competitive analysis addressing market concentration concerns; (3) service and operational integration plans; (4) environmental and labor impact assessments; (5) proposed conditions or remedies. This filing establishes the primary evidentiary record and positions from which all intervenor opposition, support, or conditional approval will be evaluated. The application serves as the baseline against which STB staff will assess whether the transaction meets legal standards for approval and what conditions, if any, should be imposed.
key_arguments: The merger satisfies statutory standards under 49 U.S.C. § 11324 for approval of rail carrier consolidations
Combined operations will improve operational efficiency and service reliability through network rationalization
The transaction creates financial benefits enabling capital investment in infrastructure and service enhancements
Merger will enhance competitive positioning against international transportation modes and other carriers
key_excerpts: NOTE: Specific quotations from the applicants' arguments are not provided in the available docket information. The application document itself would contain the applicants' substantive arguments, business rationale, and detailed statutory analysis required by 49 U.S.C. § 11324.
This is a threshold procedural filing - subsequent intervenor filings and responses will provide the actual substantive debate on merger impacts.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Approval of Union Pacific Corporation's acquisition of control over Norfolk Southern Corporation and Union Southern Railway Company pursuant to 49 U.S.C. § 11324
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing triggers mandatory STB review under 49 U.S.C. § 11324 (Control of Carriers by Common Carriers). It establishes the evidentiary burden applicants must meet: (1) Public Interest standard - merger must be consistent with public interest; (2) Statutory factors including competitive impact, financial stability, employment effects, and service impacts; (3) Environmental compliance under NEPA. The application scope determines which issues are properly before the STB - intervenors can only challenge matters raised or addressed in the application and supporting materials. This filing also triggers discovery deadlines, intervention periods, and hearing scheduling under 49 C.F.R. Part 1014.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Intervention deadline and comment period will be set by STB notice of filing. Typically 30-45 days for intervention; subsequent comment periods follow procedural schedule.

docket_entries.title: Union Pacific Customer Announcement Letter – STB Application Filing
docket_entries.entry_summary: Union Pacific's Executive Vice President of Marketing & Sales sent a customer announcement letter dated December 19, 2025, coinciding with the merger application filing. The letter frames the proposed combination as delivering 'seamless, single-line service' with claimed benefits including: (1) elimination of interchange points reducing transit time by 24–48 hours per shipment; (2) one accountable partner with single contract and unified digital experience; (3) direct communication channels and enhanced support; and (4) unified capital investment in infrastructure. UP pledges to 'keep gateways open, preserve and expand competitive options' and 'ensure flexibility and service.' The communication is aspirational rather than substantive—no specific service commitments, competitive safeguards, or remedy proposals are detailed. This is a public relations and customer retention document designed to preempt shipper concerns, not a regulatory submission.
key_arguments: Merger will eliminate interchange points and reduce transit delays by at least 24–48 hours per shipment through seamless, single-line service
Combined entity will provide one unified commercial contact, contract, invoice, and digital platform, simplifying shipper operations
Merger will unlock new intermodal and carload growth opportunities, particularly in key markets
Unified capital investment approach will create infrastructure (tracks, yards, ramps) supporting customer business expansion
UP commits to keeping gateways open and preserving/expanding competitive options for shippers
key_excerpts: Our proposed merger is designed to deliver exactly that – and today's historic filing of our application with the Surface Transportation Board (STB) brings us one step closer.
By removing interchange points, we'll cut at least 24-48 hours of delay per shipment, helping you turn assets faster and reduce costs.
You'll benefit from a single commercial contact, one contract, one invoice and a unified digital experience for scheduling, tracking and shipment visibility.
We're committed to keeping gateways open, preserving and expanding competitive options and ensuring you have the flexibility and service you need to win.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Implicit approval request via customer communication emphasizing merger benefits; no specific relief language directed to STB, but filing demonstrates applicant intent to proceed and customer engagement strategy.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Minimal direct legal significance. This filing is a customer communication strategy document, not a regulatory submission. However, it may be relevant to the record as: (1) evidence of UP's commitment to customer service integration; (2) a baseline against which post-merger performance can be measured; (3) potential admissions regarding claimed synergies (e.g., 24–48 hour delay reduction) that may be cited by intervenors or the STB to evaluate actual merger benefits post-approval; and (4) documentation of UP's approach to competitive concerns (gateway access, competitive options). Competitors or shippers may cite UP's own commitments to argue for binding conditions or performance metrics. The letter's promise to 'keep gateways open' and 'preserve competitive options' could be interpreted as an implicit concession that such issues are material to customer concerns.
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response deadline; this is informational/marketing communication coinciding with application filing.

docket_entries.title: Support Letter from Nebraska Congressional Delegation for UP/NS Merger
docket_entries.entry_summary: The Nebraska Congressional delegation (Senators Fischer and Ricketts; Representatives Smith, Bacon, and Flood) filed a support letter endorsing the UP/NS merger as creating 'the nation's first transcontinental railroad.' They argue the merger will 'enhance competition and provide value to the public' through reduced interchange delays, decreased transit times, and increased service reliability. They note 'limited overlap in existing networks' means 'only a handful of shippers seeing service decreased from two freight rail carriers to one,' and express confidence that Union Pacific will 'ensure continued competition.' They cite early support from SMART-TD (the largest transportation union) and rail customers in agriculture, manufacturing, and energy sectors citing 'improved market access, greater operational flexibility, and faster, more reliable service.' They reference Union Pacific's 'commitment to maintain gateway access and address associated gateway pricing' but provide no specific conditions or enforcement mechanisms. The filers request approval 'after a thorough review,' expressing confidence the Board will find the merger 'serves the public interest and strengthens competition nationwide.'
key_arguments: The merger creates 'the nation's first transcontinental railroad' that will 'enhance competition and provide value to the public' through reduced interchange delays, decreased transit times, and increased service reliability.

Limited network overlap means 'only a handful of shippers' will see service competition decrease from two carriers to one, and Union Pacific will take necessary action to ensure continued competition.
Expanded intermodal service provides 'significant new opportunities for shippers' with improved market access and greater operational flexibility.
Union Pacific has committed to maintain gateway access and address gateway pricing concerns.
The merger has received early support from SMART-TD (described as 'the largest union in the country') and rail customers across agriculture, manufacturing, and energy sectors.
key_excerpts: We trust that, after a thorough review, the Board will approve this merger, bringing about the nation's first transcontinental railroad.

The reduced interchange delays will result in decreased transit times and increased service reliability. The new routes and expanded intermodal service also provide significant new opportunities for shippers.

The limited overlap in existing networks of Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern results in only a handful of shippers seeing service decreased from two freight rail carriers to one, and we trust Union Pacific will take the necessary action to ensure continued competition for their service.

Additionally, rail customers across key industries — including agriculture, manufacturing, and energy — have voiced their support, citing improved market access, greater operational flexibility, and faster, more reliable service.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Approval of the proposed merger between Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing reflects political support from Nebraska—Union Pacific's home state—which may influence the Board's consideration of public interest factors and regional economic impacts under 49 U.S.C. § 11324(b). However, the filing makes no novel legal arguments or raises new evidentiary issues. It does not trigger any change in burden of proof or scope of review, but its political weight may be significant for settlement discussions or Board decision-writing.
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response deadline; filed as comment/advocacy letter during comment phase

docket_entries.title: Congressional Letter from Rep. Sylvia Garcia (TX-29) Urging Robust STB Review of UP/NS Merger with Focus on Community Impacts
docket_entries.entry_summary: Rep. Garcia writes from her district encompassing Harris County, Texas—'among the busiest rail corridors in the nation'—acknowledging that 'freight is a vital part of Harris County's economy' but expressing deep concern that the UP/NS merger could 'further add to the negative daily impacts that freight services present, including blocked crossings, worsening safety standards for residents near rail lines, and traffic pattern disruption.' She specifically notes that 'The East End neighborhood in Houston already experiences these interruptions routinely.' Garcia also raises broader concerns that the merger 'may lead to deteriorating consumer and passenger rail experiences, increases in service breakdowns, and increased costs due to a lack of competition.' Critically, Garcia does NOT request denial or impose conditions; instead, she urges the STB to conduct 'careful and thorough review' and to 'ensure that these conditions are improved and not exacerbated.' Her stance is procedural and constituent-protective rather than substantively opposing the deal. No settlement is applicable; this is a monitoring/advocacy letter.
key_arguments: The merger poses direct risks to community safety and quality of life in Harris County: 'Any potential merger must ensure that these conditions are improved and not exacerbated.' The East End neighborhood in Houston already suffers routine crossing blockages, safety hazards, and traffic disruption that could worsen.

The merger may reduce competition and increase costs for consumers: 'a merger may also lead to deteriorating consumer and passenger rail experiences, increases in service breakdowns, and increased costs due to a lack of competition.'

Freight consolidation disproportionately impacts communities dependent on rail corridors without offsetting local economic benefits; the Board must balance national economic gains against localized harm.
key_excerpts: 'The East End neighborhood in Houston already experiences these interruptions routinely. Any potential merger must ensure that these conditions are improved and not exacerbated.'
'a merger may also lead to deteriorating consumer and passenger rail experiences, increases in service breakdowns, and increased costs due to a lack of competition.'
docket_entries.relief_requested: Conduct a 'robust and transparent review of the merger, its impact on consumer and passenger standards, and neighboring communities' with particular attention to Harris County impacts. Garcia does not explicitly request denial or conditional approval, but urges the Board to 'keep the best interests of the public, including impacted communities, consumers, and rail shippers, in mind during your consideration.'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing signals that a U.S. Representative with jurisdiction over a major rail hub is monitoring the proceeding. It does not change STB's evidentiary burden or statutory analysis, but it creates potential legislative pressure and establishes a congressional record that local impacts in Harris County are a matter of federal legislative concern. The filing may influence STB's community impact analysis under its environmental and public interest review obligations, and could foreshadow Congressional oversight if the Board is perceived to have ignored localized harms. Garcia's refusal to explicitly request denial suggests the Board has discretion to approve while addressing operational safeguards—a signal that conditional approval with community-impact mitigation measures might satisfy this stakeholder.
docket_entries.deadline_description: This is a letter to the STB; no formal response deadline applies. However, the Board may address Garcia's concerns in any final decision or public response.

docket_entries.title: North Carolina Department of Transportation Notice of Intent to Participate
docket_entries.entry_summary: NCDOT filed a notice of intent to participate as party of record in the Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern merger proceeding. The filing contains no substantive arguments, conditions, or position statement. NCDOT describes itself as 'a multimodal agency committed to supporting the travelers, economy and overall well-being of North Carolina by providing a comprehensive statewide transportation system.' The filing requests only administrative relief: email service of documents and addition to the STB service list. This is a procedural filing signaling NCDOT's intention to monitor the proceeding and potentially submit comments or testimony later, but provides no current indication whether NCDOT supports, opposes, or seeks conditions on the merger.
key_excerpts: NCDOT is a multimodal agency committed to supporting the travelers, economy and overall well-being of North Carolina by providing a comprehensive statewide transportation system that encompasses all forms of travel.
NCDOT hereby gives notice of its intent to participate in the above-captioned docket and any related sub-dockets as a party of record.

As a state DOT, NCDOT's future interventions may carry weight on issues affecting state transportation policy, economic development corridors, and intermodal connections.
