docket_entries.title: CPKC Reply to Applicants' Motion to Strike CPKC-14 Supporting BNSF's Appeal of Discovery Scheduling Decision
docket_entries.entry_summary: CPKC opposes Applicants' motion to strike its February 23 supporting brief (CPKC-14) that backs BNSF's appeal of the ALJ's decision deferring discovery until after application acceptance. CPKC argues it has an explicit right to be heard on issues that 'would fundamentally affect the conduct of this proceeding and CPKC's practical ability to seek discovery from Applicants.' CPKC characterizes the Applicants' strike motion as revealing 'the intensity of their desire to avoid having to address the points raised in CPKC's submission, to which they have absolutely zero response on the merits.' The filing signals CPKC's strategic alignment with BNSF's procedural objections and CPKC's intent to aggressively pursue discovery on competitive impacts. CPKC is not requesting deal denial but is asserting procedural rights to participate in discovery timing—a conditional opposition stance focused on ensuring robust factual development.
key_arguments: CPKC has an explicit right to be heard on the Board's disposition of BNSF's appeal because it 'would fundamentally affect the conduct of this proceeding and CPKC's practical ability to seek discovery from Applicants'
Applicants' motion to strike CPKC-14 points to no legal authority and reveals Applicants' desire to avoid merits-based response to CPKC's substantive arguments on discovery timing
Deferring discovery until after application acceptance impairs CPKC's ability to develop a competitive record and participate meaningfully in the proceeding
key_excerpts: CPKC is entitled to reply to Applicants' motion, and we do so by pointing out that (a) Applicants point to no reason to strike CPKC's submission, and no authority for doing so, which is not surprising in light of CPKC's right to be heard on the Board's disposition of BNSF's appeal, which would fundamentally affect the conduct of this proceeding and CPKC's practical ability to seek discovery from Applicants
Applicants' motion reveals the intensity of their desire to avoid having to address the points raised in CPKC's submission, to which they have absolutely zero response on the merits
docket_entries.relief_requested: CPKC requests that the Board: (1) REJECT Applicants' motion to strike CPKC's February 23 submission (CPKC-14), and (2) CONSIDER CPKC's February 23 submission as the Board addresses BNSF's appeal of the ALJ's February 11 discovery scheduling decision.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing establishes that CPKC—a competitor intervenor—has explicit procedural rights to be heard on discovery scheduling orders even when not directly named as a party to the motion. More importantly, CPKC's position on discovery timing may shift the burden-of-proof framework: if the Board agrees that discovery should precede application acceptance (as BNSF's appeal requests), Applicants will face earlier and more extensive competitive scrutiny. This could strengthen the factual record on competitive harms and give intervenors more leverage in subsequent merits phases. The filing also demonstrates coordinated procedural strategy between BNSF and CPKC—two major competitors working in parallel to preserve discovery rights.
docket_entries.deadline_description: This is a reply filing; no further response deadline established by this filing alone

docket_entries.title: DOJ Supplemental Protective Order—Federal Records Act and Law Enforcement Carve-Out
docket_entries.entry_summary: The DOJ Antitrust Division filed a motion for a Supplemental Protective Order to modify the Board's existing confidentiality protections, citing three incompatibilities between the original Protective Order and federal law. First, Paragraph 12 of the original order requires destruction of all Designated Material upon proceeding completion, which conflicts with DOJ's obligations under the Federal Records Act to retain certain materials. As DOJ states: 'Destruction of Designated Material as required by the Protective Order may run afoul of the Department's obligations to retain materials that are subject to the Federal Records Act.' Second, Paragraph 11 prohibits use of Designated Material for any purpose beyond the Board proceeding, but DOJ argues: 'Given the Department's law enforcement function, the Department routinely retains the ability to use information it obtains in any proceedings or investigation for any law enforcement purpose and a blanket requirement for the Department to destroy all Designated Material would unnecessarily hamper the Department's ability to carry out its law enforcement function.' Third, Paragraphs 7 and 8 require individual employee undertakings, which DOJ asserts are 'unnecessary given the Department's confidentiality policies' codified in Justice Manual § 1-7.100. The proposed Supplemental Order would permit DOJ to retain materials when legally required and use them for law enforcement purposes, while maintaining confidentiality through other mechanisms: no public disclosure without redaction, no use in non-sealed pleadings, sealed presentation protocols, and reliance on DOJ's institutional confidentiality regime rather than individual signatures. DOJ represents that this accommodation 'protects against such disclosure while accommodating the Department's legal obligations and law enforcement function.' The Board GRANTED the motion on March 4, 2026.
key_arguments: The original Protective Order's mandatory destruction requirement conflicts with DOJ's statutory obligations under the Federal Records Act (44 U.S.C. § 3101 et seq.) to retain certain materials; DOJ cannot be required to destroy records it is legally obligated to preserve.

DOJ's law enforcement function requires the ability to use information obtained in regulatory proceedings for antitrust enforcement investigations and prosecutions; a blanket prohibition on law enforcement use would 'unnecessarily hamper the Department's ability to carry out its law enforcement function.'

Individual employee undertakings are redundant and burdensome given DOJ's existing institutional confidentiality obligations under Justice Manual § 1-7.100, which imposes criminal and administrative penalties for unauthorized disclosure of sensitive information.

The proposed Supplemental Order maintains competitive protection through alternative mechanisms (sealed filings, redaction requirements, hearing attendance restrictions) while accommodating federal legal requirements.
key_excerpts: Destruction of Designated Material as required by the Protective Order may run afoul of the Department's obligations to retain materials that are subject to the Federal Records Act.

Given the Department's law enforcement function, the Department routinely retains the ability to use information it obtains in any proceedings or investigation for any law enforcement purpose and a blanket requirement for the Department to destroy all Designated Material would unnecessarily hamper the Department's ability to carry out its law enforcement function.
Such a requirement is unnecessary given the Department's confidentiality policies. See Justice Manual 1-7.100.
Issuance of the proposed Supplemental Protective Order protects against such disclosure while accommodating the Department's legal obligations and law enforcement function.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Grant a Supplemental Protective Order modifying the Board's existing Protective Order (Decision No. 1, August 5, 2025) to: (1) Permit DOJ to retain Designated Material when required by the Federal Records Act (44 U.S.C. § 3101 et seq.), rather than destroying it upon proceeding completion; (2) Allow DOJ to use Designated Material for law enforcement purposes outside this proceeding; (3) Exempt DOJ employees from signing individual undertakings (Exhibits A and B), relying instead on DOJ's internal confidentiality policies under Justice Manual § 1-7.100.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This order clarifies that federal agency intervention rights under 49 U.S.C. § 11325(b)(1) carry an implicit exemption from standard protective order destruction and use restrictions when those restrictions conflict with other federal statutory obligations (Federal Records Act) or the intervening agency's core statutory function (law enforcement). The Board's grant of the Supplemental Order establishes precedent that agencies like DOJ cannot be bound by confidentiality regimes that prevent them from fulfilling federal legal duties or law enforcement missions. This has significant implications for future merger proceedings involving federal agency participation: standard protective orders will be modified to accommodate government actors' unique legal positions. The decision also signals that DOJ views this merger as raising material antitrust concerns warranting full information access for investigation purposes—the fact that DOJ explicitly retained the ability to use materials for 'law enforcement purposes' suggests active consideration of potential enforcement theories.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Motion GRANTED by Chief Counsel on March 4, 2026. No response deadline; decision is final.

docket_entries.title: Union Pacific & Norfolk Southern Reply to DOJ Letter on Discovery Disputes
docket_entries.entry_summary: Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern filed a reply to a March 3, 2026 DOJ letter regarding discovery disputes, defending their production record and rejecting competitor allegations of obstruction. Applicants claim they have voluntarily produced 56,000+ pages and hundreds of gigabytes of data, and have 'agreed to conduct reasonable searches for certain responsive documents' and 'consistently expressed their willingness to confer with the other parties regarding specific requests.' They characterize disputes as arising because 'BNSF (and other parties) have attempted to circumvent the conferral process and the Board's rules in order to pursue sprawling and untimely discovery.' Critically, applicants argue that the DOJ's merger review discovery standards—which impose broad document production and criminal penalties for disclosure to competitors—are inapplicable to STB proceedings, which use a 'distinctive and deliberately application-centric merger review framework' and deliberately require applicants to produce sensitive data to competitors for their own analyses. Applicants assert: 'determinations regarding the scope of or approach to discovery in this proceeding must be grounded in the governing statutes and the Board's own rules, rather than by the practices of other regulatory bodies.' The filing reveals that DOJ involvement is based on information from 'Applicants' railroad competitors' rather than DOJ's own investigation, and that BNSF is driving aggressive discovery tactics. This is a defensive posture suggesting discovery will remain contested throughout the proceeding.
key_arguments: Applicants have not refused production of 'ordinary course' documents; they have voluntarily produced 56,000+ pages and hundreds of gigabytes of data and have agreed to conduct reasonable searches for responsive documents including those cited by DOJ.

BNSF and other competitors, not applicants, are driving discovery disputes by attempting to 'circumvent the conferral process and the Board's rules in order to pursue sprawling and untimely discovery.'

The DOJ's broad merger review discovery standards are inapplicable to STB proceedings because the STB's 'distinctive and deliberately application-centric' framework is fundamentally different: it requires submission of a comprehensive control application addressing statutory topics, not blanket document production, and deliberately requires applicants to disclose sensitive data to competitors—a practice incompatible with DOJ's criminal confidentiality protections.
Discovery determinations must be grounded in STB statutes and rules, not DOJ practices, which 'overlooks fundamental statutory and procedural differences' between the agencies.
DOJ's position is based on 'mischaracterizations offered by Applicants' railroad competitors' rather than DOJ's independent investigation.
key_excerpts: Applicants are not refusing to produce such documents. Applicants have agreed to conduct reasonable searches for certain responsive documents, including documents responsive to the very requests cited by the DOJ, and have consistently expressed their willingness to confer with the other parties regarding specific requests with the goal of identifying workable solutions using targeted collections.

To date, Applicants have voluntarily produced more than 56,000 pages and hundreds of gigabytes of requested data sets, agreements, and other materials. Disputes have arisen not because Applicants have refused to produce 'ordinary course' documents, but because BNSF (and other parties) have attempted to circumvent the conferral process and the Board's rules in order to pursue sprawling and untimely discovery.

the Board's industry-specific process requires parties to submit a comprehensive control application, supported by detailed workpapers, addressing topics specifically identified in the governing statute and the Board's regulations. The Board's process also requires merging parties to produce to their competitors a substantial amount of highly sensitive internal data so those competitors can perform their own analyses of the proposed transaction.

determinations regarding the scope of or approach to discovery in this proceeding must be grounded in the governing statutes and the Board's own rules, rather than by the practices of other regulatory bodies.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Applicants request that the STB ground discovery determinations 'in the governing statutes and the Board's own rules, rather than by the practices of other regulatory bodies' (i.e., reject DOJ's discovery standards as inapplicable to STB merger review). They seek dismissal or limitation of broad discovery requests they characterize as 'sprawling and untimely,' particularly from BNSF.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing establishes a critical procedural framework argument that may limit intervenor discovery rights. Applicants argue that STB merger review is categorically different from DOJ antitrust review and should not adopt DOJ discovery standards. If ALJ or Board accepts this argument, it could narrow discovery to matters 'specifically identified in the governing statute and the Board's regulations' (49 U.S.C. § 11324), potentially limiting competitor access to internal strategic documents. Conversely, if DOJ and intervenors succeed in importing HSR-style discovery, applicants' position becomes untenable and broader document production will be mandatory. The filing also signals potential conflicts between STB and DOJ over merger review scope—DOJ letter on March 3, 2026 suggests DOJ is monitoring the merger, possibly indicating antitrust review concerns running parallel to STB review. This could create leverage for intervenors if DOJ ultimately takes a public position on competition concerns.
docket_entries.deadline_description: This is a reply filing; no specific deadline indicated for further response, though ALJ or Board may schedule hearing on discovery disputes.

docket_entries.title: PBF Holding Company LLC Notice of Intent to Participate
docket_entries.entry_summary: PBF Energy filed a notice of intent to participate without substantive comment on the merger itself. The filing is purely procedural—requesting placement on the service list to monitor the proceeding. As a major petroleum refiner and shipper, PBF has significant commercial interest in the outcome: rail rates for refined products and crude feedstock logistics could change materially post-merger, and competitive service options between UP and NS may narrow. This notice signals PBF intends to evaluate the merger and may file substantive comments later during the comment period.
key_excerpts: PBF Holding Company LLC hereby submits its Notice of Intent to Participate in this proceeding as a party of record.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Placement on service list to participate and monitor proceedings
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Procedural filing only—establishes PBF Energy's status as intervenor and entitles them to service of all subsequent filings and hearing notices. Does not create substantive issues or change scope of review. Signals that a major industrial shipper is monitoring the merger; substantive opposition or conditions may follow during comment period.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)

docket_entries.title: South Heidelberg Township Notice of Intent to Participate (No Position on Merits)
docket_entries.entry_summary: South Heidelberg Township filed a notice of intent to participate without taking a position on the proposed Union Pacific/Norfolk Southern merger. The township states: 'This Notice of Intent to Participate is intended solely to ensure that South Heidelberg Township's transportation, safety, and community interests may be appropriately considered in the Board decision, and South Heidelberg Township reserves the right to comment.' The township requests placement on the service list and explicitly reserves the right to file comments as the proceeding develops. This is a placeholder intervention to preserve standing on local transportation, safety, and community issues without committing to support or opposition at this early stage.
key_excerpts: South Heidelberg Township currently takes no position regarding the merits of the proposed transaction.

This Notice of Intent to Participate is intended solely to ensure that South Heidelberg Township's transportation, safety, and community interests may be appropriately considered in the Board decision, and South Heidelberg Township reserves the right to comment.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Inclusion on service list; right to comment on transportation, safety, and community impacts as the proceeding develops
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Filing preserves South Heidelberg Township's right to intervene and comment in later phases of the proceeding without waiving future participation rights. No substantive issues raised at this stage. Township is signaling that it may file comments addressing local transportation, safety, or community impacts during the comment period.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.deadline_description: This is a notice of intent; no response required. Township may file substantive comments during comment period.

docket_entries.title: Union Pacific/Norfolk Southern Motion to Strike BNSF and CPKC Reply Letters as Procedurally Improper
docket_entries.entry_summary: Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern filed a motion to strike two letters from BNSF and CPKC filed on March 3, 2026. The applicants argue that BNSF's March 3 letter is an improper reply to the applicants' reply on timeliness grounds, and that CPKC's March 3 reply is an improper reply to a reply making further arguments in support of BNSF's appeal. Both filings, the applicants contend, violate 49 C.F.R. § 1104.13(c) and should be struck from the record. The applicants emphasize that they did not themselves 'raise' the timeliness issue—BNSF argued its appeal was timely and the applicants' reply merely refuted that argument—making BNSF's responsive letter an unauthorized further reply. This motion is part of ongoing litigation regarding Judge Soulikias's ruling in Decision No. 10 and BNSF's interlocutory appeal challenging that decision.
key_arguments: BNSF's March 3 letter constitutes an improper reply to a reply, as BNSF is responding to applicants' rebuttal of timeliness rather than raising a new issue applicants initiated
CPKC's March 3 reply is an improper reply to a reply, as it makes further arguments in support of BNSF's substantive appeal rather than responding to an issue CPKC itself raised
Both filings violate the procedural rules at 49 C.F.R. § 1104.13(c) limiting reply practice and should be excluded from the record
key_excerpts: BNSF's letter is an improper reply to a reply, and it should be struck from the record pursuant to 49 C.F.R. § 1104.13(c).
CPKC's reply is also an improper reply to a reply that should be struck from the record pursuant to 49 C.F.R. § 1104.13(c).
docket_entries.relief_requested: Strike BNSF's March 3, 2026 letter and CPKC's March 3, 2026 reply letter from the record pursuant to 49 C.F.R. § 1104.13(c) as improper replies to replies.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This motion invokes STB's reply practice rules and seeks to limit the procedural opportunities available to competitors to address the applicants' substantive arguments. If granted, it would prevent BNSF and CPKC from further briefing a substantive interlocutory appeal (Decision No. 10) that appears to involve significant competitive concerns. This impacts the scope of the record ALJ Soulikias and the Board will consider on a material interim ruling. The motion also establishes a procedural dispute about reply rights that could have broader implications for how subsequent briefing is handled in the proceeding.
docket_entries.deadline_description: No explicit response deadline stated; BNSF and CPKC may have opportunity to reply to this motion before ALJ rules, or ALJ may rule summarily.

docket_entries.title: Harris County Commissioner Ellis Disavows Trees for Houston Letter; Reaffirms Environmental Justice Opposition
docket_entries.entry_summary: Harris County Commissioner Rodney Ellis issues a public clarification that he did NOT authorize Trees for Houston's October 21, 2025 letter supporting the UP-NS merger, and explicitly disavows any implication that his name on Trees for Houston's Board of Advisors constitutes his endorsement of the transaction. Ellis reaffirms his "clear position": he "stand[s] with the residents of Settegast and Greater Fifth Ward in demanding environmental justice, including meaningful reductions in emissions and particulate matter that harm families, and real accountability from Union Pacific and other polluters." Ellis states that "[a]ny proposed action that risks increasing heavy traffic, air pollution, or cumulative health burdens in these neighborhoods is a matter of serious concern," and that he will "continue to evaluate it through that lens of community health, equity, and environmental protection for frontline neighborhoods." The letter serves as both a procedural correction and a substantive statement of opposition grounded in environmental justice for low-income, communities-of-color neighborhoods in Houston that already bear disproportionate pollution burdens.
key_arguments: The merger poses environmental justice risks to frontline Houston neighborhoods (Settegast and Greater Fifth Ward) through increased heavy traffic, air pollution, and cumulative health burdens that would fall disproportionately on residents who already suffer from pollution from Union Pacific and other carriers.

Any merger approval must be conditioned on 'meaningful reductions in emissions and particulate matter' and 'real accountability' from Union Pacific—not merely approval of the transaction that would increase operational activity in these communities.

Local government opposition on environmental justice grounds is not adequately represented by environmental advocacy groups and requires direct articulation by elected officials accountable to affected residents.
key_excerpts: My position has been and remains clear: I stand with the residents of Settegast and Greater Fifth Ward in demanding environmental justice, including meaningful reductions in emissions and particulate matter that harm families, and real accountability from Union Pacific and other polluters operating in and around these communities.

Any proposed action that risks increasing heavy traffic, air pollution, or cumulative health burdens in these neighborhoods is a matter of serious concern, and I will continue to evaluate it through that lens of community health, equity, and environmental protection for frontline neighborhoods.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Implicit denial based on environmental justice grounds; no affirmative approval conditions proposed. Commissioner demands that any merger approval be conditioned on elimination or mitigation of increased emissions and health burdens in frontline communities, or that the Board reject the transaction to protect environmental justice in Settegast and Greater Fifth Ward.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing establishes that Harris County government (represented by an elected commissioner) is formally on the record opposing the merger on environmental justice grounds. While not a Petition to Deny, it creates a government record that may influence STB environmental review under 49 U.S.C. § 11324(c) (which requires consideration of effects on rail communities) and could be cited in hearing testimony. The disavowal of Trees for Houston's support letter removes one piece of community support from the merger's record, strengthening the perception that local opposition to environmental impacts is genuine and politically significant. If environmental conditions are not binding and enforceable, Ellis's opposition signals that local political pressure and potential third-party litigation risks (under Clean Air Act or environmental justice statutes) will persist post-approval.
docket_entries.deadline_description: This is a clarification statement; no response deadline applies. However, it is a matter of public record that may be cited by other intervenors and could trigger requests for environmental impact analysis.

docket_entries.title: AISI Opposes UP-NS Merger as Anticompetitive; Urges Rejection and DOJ Review
docket_entries.entry_summary: AISI, representing U.S. steelmakers and steel processors, lodges an outright opposition to the UP-NS merger. The organization argues the transaction is fundamentally anticompetitive and incompatible with U.S. manufacturing competitiveness. AISI contends that 'one company would control nearly half of all rail traffic in the United States,' creating 'a railway with monopoly-like power and a nation full of captive shippers.' The organization specifically criticizes the incomplete January 2026 STB rejection, noting UP-NS failed to provide the required 'full system analysis' demonstrating competitive impacts. AISI frames the merger as directly harming American steelmakers' ability to compete globally: 'This proposed merger could result in foreign-made goods arriving at our shores having more, better shipping options than do American steel makers.' The steel industry argument is that reduced rail competition will force price increases and service degradation ('Americans manufacturers, farmers and ranchers, and consumers will pay more for less – less options and less reliable service'), undermining the Trump administration's manufacturing revival agenda. Notably, AISI does not request specific remedial conditions—it seeks outright rejection, signaling this opposition is based on structural/competitive objections that cannot be remedied through behavioral remedies or service commitments.
key_arguments: Merged entity would control 'nearly half of all rail traffic in the United States,' conferring monopoly-like power on a single carrier and leaving most steel shippers as captive users with no competitive alternatives.

The merged railroad would reduce market competition and eliminate incentives for safe and efficient service, directly undermining American steelmakers' ability to compete with foreign manufacturers who have superior shipping options.

Rapid consolidation in freight rail (four railroads now account for 90% of traffic) combined with this merger creates a system where steel companies lack viable competitive alternatives, contrary to STB's statutory competitive mandate.

Foreign-made goods will have access to more and better shipping options than American-produced steel, inverting comparative advantage and contradicting the Trump administration's manufacturing revival policies.

The applicants' failure to provide 'full system analysis' demonstrating competitive impacts (as required and cited by STB's January 2026 rejection) is telling evidence the merger cannot withstand competitive scrutiny.
key_excerpts: In the case of this merger, one company would control nearly half of all rail traffic in the United States. The result is a railway with monopoly-like power and a nation full of captive shippers.
This proposed merger could result in foreign-made goods arriving at our shores having more, better shipping options than do American steel makers.
Actions that reduce competition and market incentives for safe and efficient delivery of goods undermine the American steel industry's ability to compete with foreign competitors.
If past is prologue, rail consolidation means that American manufacturers, farmers and ranchers, and consumers will pay more for less – less options and less reliable service.
docket_entries.relief_requested: STB should 'reject any refiled merger application.' AISI urges DOJ Antitrust Division to 'carefully review this merger under the Department's merger guidelines.'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: AISI's intervention reinforces the STB's January 16, 2026 rejection on completeness grounds and explicitly invokes the 'full system analysis' requirement under STB regulations—establishing that competitive impact documentation is a threshold filing requirement, not a collateral issue. The citation to the Board's finding that UP-NS failed to demonstrate competitive impacts strengthens the evidentiary framework for the next filing. Additionally, AISI's explicit request for DOJ Antitrust Division review signals coordination between regulatory agencies and may indicate DOJ's antitrust concerns mirror STB competitive findings.
docket_entries.deadline_description: AISI's comment is on the record for all future filings. No specific response deadline, but material becomes part of the evidentiary record and likely addressed in any refiled application or DOJ antitrust analysis.

docket_entries.title: State Representative Zachary Gramlich (AR) - Support for UP/NS Merger Based on Regional Economic Stability
docket_entries.entry_summary: Arkansas State Representative Zachary Gramlich, representing Fort Smith and the River Valley region, supports the Union Pacific/Norfolk Southern merger. He argues that Union Pacific's historical track record of reliable service and operational strength has made the region competitive in manufacturing, distribution, and logistics. He contends the merger will extend that dependability across a broader network, enhance route stability, improve service continuity, and reduce supply chain disruptions. He frames the merger as beneficial for regional employers who rely on infrastructure consistency for production planning and payroll stability. No specific conditions are requested; he endorses approval subject to 'appropriate regulatory review.'
key_arguments: Union Pacific's historical performance as a 'reliable and consistent presence' in the Fort Smith regional economy supports confidence that the merged entity will maintain service dependability
A unified rail system will 'enhance route stability, improve service continuity, and reduce disruptions that strain supply chains'

For companies competing in national and global markets, reliability in rail service is 'often the deciding factor between expansion and hesitation,' making this merger beneficial for regional economic growth
key_excerpts: For decades, Union Pacific has been a reliable and consistent presence in our regional economy, which is why I support the merger between them and Norfolk Southern.

The proposed merger with Norfolk Southern presents an opportunity to extend that same level of dependability across a broader network. A more unified rail system can enhance route stability, improve service continuity, and reduce disruptions that strain supply chains.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Approval of the merger between Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern, subject to 'appropriate regulatory review'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Minimal. This is a local political endorsement with no analysis of competitive effects, market concentration, service standards, or regulatory conditions. It adds political support from an affected regional community but does not raise new legal issues or evidentiary requirements under the STB merger approval framework. It does not propose enforceable conditions or identify specific harms that would require remedial conditions.

docket_entries.title: Arkansas State Representative Chad Puryear Support for UP/NS Merger - Regional Economic Development Perspective
docket_entries.entry_summary: Arkansas State Representative Chad Puryear supports approval of the UP/NS merger based on regional economic development needs. He argues that Northwest Arkansas is positioned as a critical freight corridor due to I-49 development and anticipated I-69 expansion, making reliable rail service essential for local manufacturers, agricultural producers, and small businesses. Puryear contends that 'a stronger, more integrated rail network could increase capacity, enhance coordination across regions, and provide the operational stability our employers depend on.' He frames rail reliability as critical infrastructure: 'When rail service is dependable, businesses operate smoothly; but when it is unreliable, delays can disrupt the entire supply chain.' He supports the merger specifically because it would improve service, increase long-term investment, and create a rail system that evolves alongside regional highway infrastructure development. The filing contains no opposition, no specific conditions, and no detailed competitive analysis—it is a straightforward advocacy statement from a state legislator whose district would benefit from improved rail capacity.
key_arguments: Northwest Arkansas is positioned at crossroads of major logistics routes with I-49 development complete and I-69 expansion anticipated, requiring increased freight capacity that highways alone cannot handle
A merged UP/NS network would increase rail capacity and enhance coordination, providing 'operational stability' needed by regional manufacturers and agricultural producers
Reliable rail service is essential infrastructure for small businesses and agriculture: unreliable service causes supply chain disruption; dependable service enables smooth operations
The merger would lead to improved service, long-term investment, and a rail system that evolves alongside regional highway development
key_excerpts: A stronger, more integrated rail network could increase capacity, enhance coordination across regions, and provide the operational stability our employers depend on.
When rail service is dependable, businesses operate smoothly; but when it is unreliable, delays can disrupt the entire supply chain.
For a district focused on logistics, manufacturing, agriculture, rail is not just a secondary form of infrastructure—it is essential.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Approval of the proposed merger between Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Low. This filing provides legislative support for the merger from a state representative in a logistics-dependent region, which may have political weight in STB deliberations regarding regional economic impact. However, it contains no novel legal arguments, no new factual evidence about competitive effects, and no substantive regulatory analysis. It does not change the scope of review or create evidentiary burdens. Its primary significance is political/advocacy rather than regulatory.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Not applicable; this is a comment filing with no response deadline

docket_entries.title: Houston Super Neighborhoods 64 & 88 Notice of Intent to Participate - Community Opposition to UP/NS Merger
docket_entries.entry_summary: Houston Super Neighborhoods 64 & 88 files notice of intent to participate in the UP/NS merger proceeding on behalf of approximately 23,000 residents in Houston's East End (Greater Eastwood, Lawndale, Wayside) whose communities are directly traversed by Union Pacific rail lines on multiple subdivisions. The organization opposes the merger but conditionally - they reserve the right to submit location-specific data and testimony documenting 'conditions Union Pacific has created in our communities' and request that the Board impose 'reasonable and enforceable mitigation measures with completion deadlines' as a condition of any approval. This framing suggests the organization has documented existing operational harms (likely noise, air quality, traffic impacts, safety issues) related to current UP operations and seeks to leverage the merger review to compel remediation. The filing is strategically positioned to preserve record evidence while remaining open to settlement through targeted mitigation conditions rather than outright denial.
key_arguments: Union Pacific's existing operations have created documented community harms in Houston's East End neighborhoods that must be addressed in the merger review process
Merger approval should be conditioned on reasonable and enforceable mitigation measures with specific completion deadlines
The Board's merger record must accurately reflect location-specific conditions and impacts on directly-affected residential communities
key_excerpts: Super Neighborhood 64 and 88 is a community governance organization representing approximately 23,000 residents in Houston's East End, directly traversed by Union Pacific rail lines on multiple subdivisions.
We file this Notice to preserve our right to submit comments, data, testimony to ensure the record before the Board accurately reflects the conditions Union Pacific has created in our communities.
We reserve the right to request reasonable and enforceable mitigation measures with completion deadlines.
docket_entries.relief_requested: The filing reserves the right to: (1) submit comments, data, and testimony documenting Union Pacific's existing community harms in neighborhoods; (2) request reasonable and enforceable mitigation measures with completion deadlines. Implicitly seeks denial unless conditions addressing documented harms are imposed.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing establishes standing for a significant residential constituency (23,000 residents) to submit testimony and documentary evidence regarding operational harms in the merger record. The conditional framing ('reasonable and enforceable mitigation measures') signals willingness to negotiate specific remedies rather than pursue outright denial. This creates potential settlement leverage: applicants may face pressure to negotiate neighborhood-specific conditions (noise abatement, crossing safety improvements, etc.) to avoid prolonged opposition and hearing testimony. The reference to 'location-specific data' suggests the organization has baseline documentation of current impacts that could be used to establish pre-merger conditions and post-merger monitoring standards.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (With Comment)
docket_entries.deadline_description: Notice of Intent preserves right to submit comments in subsequent comment periods; no specific response deadline for applicants at this stage.

docket_entries.title: Eastwood Civic Association Notice of Intent to Participate - Houston Neighborhood Rail Blockages
docket_entries.entry_summary: The Eastwood Civic Association, representing residents of Houston's Eastwood neighborhood on the East End, filed a Notice of Intent to Participate to preserve the right to submit comments and testimony in the UP-NS merger proceeding. The association emphasizes that the Eastwood neighborhood is 'directly traversed by Union Pacific rail lines on multiple subdivisions' and sits at the center of the 'East End Triangle'—a geographic configuration where simultaneous blockages on the West Belt, Galveston Subdivision, and East Belt subdivisions 'encircle the neighborhood, leaving residents, emergency vehicles, and first responders with only one passable route in or out.' The filing documents that the Eastwood Civic Association 'has spent years engaging directly with Union Pacific to seek relief from chronic, multi-hour rail blockages — and conditions have not improved to a livable situation.' The association's implicit argument is that current Union Pacific operations already impose unacceptable burdens on the community, and the merger potentially threatens to worsen blockage conditions if operational consolidation increases traffic without corresponding infrastructure improvements. The filing does not explicitly address merger-specific harms but rather establishes that UP's baseline operational practices are problematic and should factor into the Board's review. The notice signals intent to provide community testimony about the adequacy of rail operations and their impact on neighborhood livability.
key_arguments: Union Pacific's current operations create chronic, multi-hour rail blockages that have persisted despite years of direct community engagement with the railroad, making the Eastwood neighborhood functionally cut off with only one passable route for residents and emergency vehicles.

The 'East End Triangle' configuration—where simultaneous blockages on the West Belt, Galveston Subdivision, and East Belt subdivisions encircle the neighborhood—creates a public safety and livability crisis for residents that Union Pacific has failed to remedy.

The merger proceeding provides an opportunity for the Board to condition approval on remedying the chronic operational failures that have already been documented and persistent in the Eastwood neighborhood.
key_excerpts: Eastwood neighborhood in Houston's East End, directly traversed by Union Pacific rail lines on multiple subdivisions and situated at the center of what residents and local officials have documented as the 'East End Triangle' — a configuration in which simultaneous blockages on the West Belt, Galveston Subdivision, and East Belt encircle the neighborhood, leaving residents, emergency vehicles, and first responders with only one passable route in or out.

The Eastwood Civic Association files this notice of intent to participate because our neighborhood has spent years engaging directly with Union Pacific to seek relief from chronic, multi-hour rail blockages — and conditions have not improved to a livable situation.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Not explicitly stated in this Notice of Intent. The filing preserves the right to submit comments, data, and testimony to ensure the record reflects conditions Union Pacific has created. Implied relief: remedy chronic, multi-hour rail blockages that have persisted despite years of direct engagement with Union Pacific.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing establishes a factual record in the merger proceeding about alleged chronic operational failures by Union Pacific affecting a residential community. While the filing does not explicitly address merger-specific competitive or service impacts, it creates a basis for the Board to condition merger approval on operational improvements to rail traffic management and grade crossing blockages. It also signals that community-level operational impacts are within the scope of merger review considerations and could support conditions requiring coordination with local governments on blockage mitigation, emergency vehicle access, and operational transparency. The filing may influence the Board's decision on whether merger conditions should address operational practices beyond classic competition remedies.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (With Comment)
docket_entries.deadline_description: This is a Notice of Intent to Participate. The Eastwood Civic Association will submit substantive comments at a later phase.

docket_entries.title: Notice of Intent to Participate with Comment — Lindsay Williams, Eastwood Houston Resident
docket_entries.entry_summary: Lindsay Williams, a Houston resident in the Eastwood neighborhood directly traversed by multiple Union Pacific rail subdivisions, files Notice of Intent to Participate as an individual to preserve her right to submit comments, data, and testimony regarding rail impacts. She emphasizes she is "not a newcomer to this issue" and has served as Chair of the Trains Committee of the Eastwood Civic Association, where rail impacts have been "a central focus of community organizing for years." Williams details that her community "has pursued every available avenue for relief — meetings with railroad representatives, data collection, coordination with elected officials, and participation in city and county planning processes." She states: "Union Pacific has engaged. Representatives have attended meetings, heard our concerns, and taken notes. And yet the blockages continue. We cannot take any more trains." She files individually "because what I have witnessed as a resident cannot be fully captured by any organizational filing." This is a threshold procedural filing to preserve intervention rights; substantive opposition arguments will presumably follow in comment phase.
key_arguments: Union Pacific rail operations in East End Houston cause chronic neighborhood impacts ('blockages') despite community engagement efforts and railroad responsiveness to meetings
Community has exhausted available relief mechanisms (direct railroad negotiations, elected official coordination, city/county planning participation) without achieving adequate relief
Individual resident perspective on rail impacts cannot be fully captured by organizational filings and requires separate testimony
key_excerpts: "I am a resident of the Eastwood neighborhood in Houston's East End, a community directly traversed by Union Pacific rail lines on multiple subdivisions."

"Through the Trains Committee and the East End Rail Safety Task Force, our community has pursued every available avenue for relief — meetings with railroad representatives, data collection, coordination with elected officials, and participation in city and county planning processes. Union Pacific has engaged. Representatives have attended meetings, heard our concerns, and taken notes. And yet the blockages continue. We cannot take any more trains."
"I file this Notice on my own behalf because what I have witnessed as a resident cannot be fully captured by any organizational filing."
docket_entries.relief_requested: Add filer to service list for proceeding; preserve right to submit comments, data, and testimony regarding Union Pacific rail operations impacts on Eastwood neighborhood
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This is a threshold procedural filing that establishes intervenor status under STB Rules of Practice. While substantively focused on existing Union Pacific operations rather than merger-specific arguments, it creates a record of organized community opposition to railroad consolidation in a major transportation hub (Houston). The filing signals that if the merger is approved, community intervention regarding rail congestion and operational impacts in affected residential neighborhoods may intensify. The filer's emphasis on individual testimony separate from organizational input suggests coordination between Eastwood Civic Association and individual community members — potential indicium of broader grassroots mobilization.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (With Comment)
docket_entries.deadline_description: Notice of Intent; no response deadline. Williams will file substantive comments in subsequent comment period.

docket_entries.title: STB Decision No. 12: Procedural Order on Certificate of Service Requirements for Unserved Materials
docket_entries.entry_summary: The STB Board issued a procedural decision addressing deficiencies in filing practices within the UP/NS merger docket. The Board noted that it has received multiple submissions lacking required certificates of service and therefore has not added them to the docket record. The Board ordered that persons wishing to have previously submitted but unserved materials accepted must: (1) serve copies on all Parties of Record as reflected on the official service list, and (2) file with the Board within 10 days a certificate of service documenting that service and attaching the served materials. The Board emphasized that going forward, every filing must include its own certificate of service as required by 49 C.F.R. § 1104.12. This decision is particularly significant because it establishes enforcement of the Board's regulations and may result in the exclusion of substantive intervenor filings from the record if procedural requirements are not met. The decision reflects that the Board is actively managing the docket and has received enough non-compliant submissions to warrant a formal ruling.
key_arguments: The Board has authority to exclude filings that lack proper certificates of service under 49 C.F.R. § 1104.12(a), which requires every document filed with the Board to include a certificate showing service upon all parties to the proceeding.

Unserved materials previously submitted will not be considered part of the docket record unless the submitter cures the deficiency by serving copies and filing a certificate of service within 10 days.
Going forward, all submissions must comply with the Board's filing regulations or face exclusion from the Board's consideration.
key_excerpts: To date, the Board has received a number of submissions without the necessary certificate of service. See 49 C.F.R. § 1104.12(a) (requiring every document filed with the Board to include a certificate showing service upon all parties to the proceeding). Those submissions have not been added to the docket as filings.

Those wishing to have such submissions accepted as filings for consideration by the Board will be required to (1) serve upon all Parties of Record (as reflected on the service list) a copy of any such previously submitted but unserved materials, and (2) file with the Board, within 10 days of the service date of this decision, a certificate of service indicating that service has been accomplished and attaching copies of the served materials.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Persons submitting previously unfiled materials must: (1) serve copies on all Parties of Record within the service list, and (2) file a certificate of service with the Board within 10 days of this decision's service date (by March 27, 2026), attaching copies of the served materials. All future filings must include their own certificate of service per 49 C.F.R. § 1104.12.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This decision clarifies and enforces the Board's mandatory filing requirements under 49 C.F.R. § 1104.12. It establishes that failure to include a certificate of service results in non-acceptance of the filing—the material is excluded from the docket record and not considered by the Board. The 10-day cure period (ending March 27, 2026) creates a procedural deadline for any intervenor whose prior submissions were incomplete. This has direct consequences for substantive intervenor comments: parties must ensure compliance or risk their arguments being excluded entirely from the record. The decision also establishes that Parties of Record who cure deficiencies will receive all future Board filings and decisions.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Parties with previously submitted but unserved materials must serve all Parties of Record and file a certificate of service with the Board within 10 days of March 17, 2026 service date.

docket_entries.title: STB Decision Denying BNSF Appeal of ALJ Discovery Order and Directing Applicants to Submit Transaction Documents
docket_entries.entry_summary: The STB denied BNSF Railway Company's untimely interlocutory appeal of an ALJ order denying BNSF's motion to compel discovery in the Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern merger proceeding. The Board found BNSF's appeal was filed five days late under 49 C.F.R. § 1115.9(b) and declined to waive the deadline. Sua sponte, the Board directed Applicants to submit 'ordinary course' transaction documents by April 7, 2026, modeled on HSR Act requirements, to facilitate review of the proposed transcontinental railroad merger.
key_arguments: BNSF's appeal was untimely, filed on February 23, 2026, five days after the seven-day deadline from the February 11, 2026 ALJ order
The Board has clear precedent that ALJ rulings on discovery are subject to the seven-day interlocutory appeal deadline under 49 C.F.R. § 1115.9(b)
BNSF's subsequent arguments attempting to re-litigate timeliness constituted an impermissible reply to a reply
The Board declined to waive the appeal deadline as BNSF did not establish good cause and failed to address its regulatory non-compliance
Applicants correctly distinguished between the Board's control transaction process and DOJ's HSR Act process
The proposed transaction's significance and size, combined with it being the first assessed under the 2001 merger rules, warranted ordering 'ordinary course' documents
'Ordinary course' documents are more probative than advocacy and self-serving statements in evaluating merger competitive effects
key_excerpts: BNSF filed its appeal five days late, incorrectly asserting that its appeal was timely under 49 C.F.R. § 1115.1(c).
As BNSF failed to file an appeal within the applicable seven-day deadline for interlocutory rulings by an ALJ, BNSF's appeal of the ALJ discovery order is untimely.

the Board sua sponte will direct that Applicants file with the Board certain transaction-related documents...the Board will direct that Applicants submit the 'ordinary course' documents that DOJ and FTC request from parties as a matter of course when reviewing proposed mergers under the HSR Act.

these 'ordinary course' documents are likely to provide valuable insight into the proposed transaction's effects because they 'reflect real-time business decisions and forecasts concerning the merging parties' operations, and views of past, present, and future market conditions.'
In this proceeding where Applicants seek approval to 'create America's first transcontinental railroad,' the highly probative nature of these documents is clear.

docket_entries.title: Montana Legislative Transportation Interim Committee - Opposition to UP-NS Merger Based on Competition and Western Rail Market Consolidation
docket_entries.entry_summary: The Montana Legislature's Transportation Interim Committee opposes the UP-NS merger on the grounds that it represents unprecedented consolidation that will eliminate competition and harm Montana's freight rail-dependent economy. The committee argues: 'Consolidation reduces competition' and 'Competition drives down prices.' Currently, BNSF serves over 90% of Montana's freight, while UP and BNSF compete roughly equally on track mileage west of the Mississippi and for access to eastern corridors. The merger would create 'the largest railroad in the country with over 50,000 miles of track in 43 states' and leave 'BNSF as the only remaining Class 1 railroad whose service area is west of the Mississippi.' Montana is characterized as a 'captive shipper' state where agriculture (time-sensitive harvest shipments), energy, and natural resources rely on 'consistent and timely freight service'—any service interruptions or price increases 'will be immediately felt by Montana's freight rail-dependent customers.' The committee emphasizes that this is 'the first merger proposal to come before the STB under the revised Major Rail Consolidation Procedures' and therefore 'will establish precedent for future merger decisions and affect freight rail transportation for years to come.' The committee requests rigorous review but does not propose specific conditions that would render the merger acceptable—opposition is framed as categorical based on consolidation harms.
key_arguments: The proposed merger would reduce the number of Class 1 railroads competing in the western United States from two (UP and BNSF) to one (BNSF), eliminating meaningful competitive options for Montana's freight-dependent industries.

Montana is a 'captive shipper' state with landlocked geography and economy-critical dependence on agriculture, energy, and natural resources that require 'time-sensitive shipments during harvest seasons,' making it uniquely vulnerable to service interruptions or price increases from rail consolidation.

BNSF currently serves over 90% of Montana's freight needs; the merger would leave BNSF as 'the only remaining Class 1 railroad whose service area is west of the Mississippi,' eliminating competitive pressure on pricing and service levels.

The U.S. domestic freight rail system is already 'highly consolidated' with access to only six Class 1 railroads (two Canada-based), making this merger a further step toward monopolistic control in an already concentrated market.

The merger precedent is critical: As 'the first merger proposal to come before the STB under the revised Major Rail Consolidation Procedures,' the UP-NS decision 'will establish precedent for future merger decisions and affect freight rail transportation for years to come.'

Competition is the only mechanism preventing price increases: 'Competition drives down prices. Consolidation reduces competition.' Any merger-driven cost increases will be 'immediately felt by Montana's freight rail-dependent customers.'
key_excerpts: The proposed UP-NS merger would be an unprecedented consolidation and would create the largest railroad in the country with over 50,000 miles of track in 43 states.

Montana is landlocked, and top industries like agriculture, energy, and natural resources rely heavily on consistent and timely freight service. Agriculture in particular requires time-sensitive shipments during harvest seasons, and any service interruptions can cause product spoilage and losses in global as well as domestic markets.

As things stand today, both UP and BNSF operate west of the Mississippi River and on roughly the same amount of track mileage. Both companies must compete for access to railroads and their markets east of the Mississippi. The proposed merger would remove competition for UP while leaving BNSF to continue fighting for access to these rail corridors.
Any negative effects, such as price increases or interruption of services, will be immediately felt by Montana's freight rail-dependent customers.
This would leave BNSF as the only remaining Class 1 railroad whose service area is west of the Mississippi. This would be a dramatic shift in the landscape of freight rail in the western states.
Competition drives down prices. Consolidation reduces competition.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Deny the proposed UP-NS merger. The committee urges the STB to 'conduct a methodical, rigorous, and comprehensive review of submitted materials throughout this merger process and to carefully consider the impacts on Montana's many freight rail transportation customers.'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing invokes the 2001 Major Rail Consolidation Procedures as the controlling standard and argues that the UP-NS merger is the first test of the revised procedures. The committee emphasizes that the STB's decision will establish precedent for future rail consolidation review. The filing does not raise technical antitrust arguments but frames the merger as violating the fundamental competitive-preservation purpose of the STB's consolidation review framework. The precedential framing may influence the STB's articulation of competitive standards in its order.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Comment filing; no response deadline

docket_entries.title: CN Expert Analysis Challenging UP-NS Merger Diversion Study Methodology
docket_entries.filer_name: Grand Trunk Corporation (CN) and U.S. Rail Operating Subsidiaries
docket_entries.entry_summary: CN filed a verified statement by economist Dr. Henry Kahwaty arguing that the applicants' rail-to-rail diversion analysis is fundamentally flawed and unreliable due to methodological errors in predicting market shares on routes where UP and NS have no current traffic. The analysis claims the diversion estimates systematically understate diversions by approximately 50% (215,000 carloads), which compromises the reliability of the operating plan, environmental analysis, and competitive impact assessment.
key_arguments: The Diversion Analysis uses a statistical model that assigns significant pre-merger market shares to over 15,000 UP/NS Zero Traffic Routes where actual 2023 traffic data shows zero percent market share
These inaccurate pre-merger predictions artificially cap diversion estimates by treating predicted post-merger growth as pre-merger traffic, resulting in systematic understatement of diversions
95% of bulk diversions, 62% of merchandise diversions, and 61% of automotive diversions stem from Zero Traffic Routes where the model's predictions are most erroneous
The methodology generates 'phantom carloads' and negative market shares that are economically meaningless and impossible in the real world

The statistical model fails to accurately predict actual 2023 market shares in both calibration and execution phases, with scatterplot analysis showing poor correlation between predicted and actual shares
The Diversion Analysis creates inconsistencies with the Operating Plan, which uses different post-merger market share calculations, preventing reliable assessment of competitive impacts
Understated diversions in the Operating Plan leave substantial volumes of traffic unmodeled, creating risk of inadequate capacity planning and service disruptions
Environmental analysis relies on accurate diversion estimates for segment-level impact assessment, and understated diversions may fail to identify segments triggering environmental thresholds
The analysis is not well-suited to model the proposed merger's primary efficiency claim: creation of new single-line service on routes with no current UP/NS presence
key_excerpts: Correcting this—by treating the traffic as diverted—would increase projected diversions from other Class I railroads by almost 50%, or roughly 215,000 carloads.

The Diversion Analysis estimates merger-related diversions based on this formula... For the Zero Traffic Routes specifically, because the predicted pre-merger market shares are estimated to be greater than zero, and frequently 50% or greater, the Diversion Analysis improperly counts what should be Applicants' post-merger growth as pre-merger traffic.
The statistical model's results are unrealistic when compared to actual market shares on Zero Traffic Routes, and they in all instances overestimate Applicants' pre-merger shares for these routes.

Diversions are substantially understated by the statistical model's predictions. Indeed, the result is to significantly understate merger-related rail-to-rail diversions on over 15,000 Zero Traffic Routes, in many cases by 50% or more.
Once corrected to account for the full growth projections, the diversion estimate nearly doubles. These results significantly distort the operating plan and infrastructure impacts.

The Operating Plan models only 46% post-merger market share in automotive traffic, even though the Diversion Analysis estimates 61% market share. For bulk, the operating plan uses 42% post-merger market share versus 60% as predicted by the Diversion Analysis.

Because the Diversion Analysis undercounts merger-related growth, this understatement necessarily affects the traffic levels reported for countless network segments across the combined carrier's system.
In this example, after adjusting the calculations for the omission of growth traffic, diverted traffic is nearly four times greater than the estimate from the Diversion Analysis.

docket_entries.title: Union Pacific Reply to Grand Trunk (CN) Criticisms of Diversion Study Methodology
docket_entries.entry_summary: Union Pacific responds to Grand Trunk Corporation's (CN's) March 23, 2026 letter criticizing the diversion study submitted in UP's amended application. UP defends the study by asserting that the same expert conducted diversion analyses for CN in the CN-Iowa Northern and CPKC merger proceedings using identical methodology—estimating diversions based on pre- and post-acquisition market share differences. UP argues that CN's current methodological criticisms are inconsistent with CN's prior acceptance of the same approach when CN was the applicant. UP concludes: "Applicants are confident the diversion study submitted in their amended application will provide a reasonable projection of merger-related diversions." UP proposes deferring substantive methodological disputes to the merits phase, suggesting that tactical criticism from a competitor does not warrant pre-hearing adjudication.
key_arguments: CN's own expert used the identical market-share-difference methodology in CN-Iowa Northern and CPKC proceedings, undercutting CN's current criticism of the same approach
The diversion study employed the same expert and methodology that CN previously endorsed in other STB merger proceedings
Methodological disagreements over diversion estimation are appropriately resolved in the merits phase, not through preliminary correspondence

Applicants are confident the diversion study submitted in their amended application will provide a reasonable projection of merger-related diversions. Any methodological disagreements are more appropriately addressed in the merits phase of this proceeding.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Implicit approval of merger application; procedurally, deferral of methodological disputes to merits phase of proceeding

docket_entries.title: Joint East End Super Neighborhood Alliance - Procedural Comment and Conditional Opposition with Community Benefit Demands
docket_entries.filer_name: Joint East End Super Neighborhood Alliance
docket_entries.entry_summary: The Joint East End Super Neighborhood Alliance opposes the UP-NS merger absent comprehensive community protection measures, characterizing their Houston East End neighborhoods as bearing disproportionate operational burden from rail consolidation. The Alliance represents 35,000+ residents in five Super Neighborhoods bisected by multiple freight corridors, where residents experience crossing blockages lasting 30 minutes to many hours, disrupted emergency services, air quality degradation near schools, and traffic impacts. They allege that the prior CP-KCS merger review failed to conduct adequate localized impact analysis and excluded Houston from meaningful public engagement. The Alliance explicitly frames this as conditional opposition: 'We are not opposed to freight rail—we understand its economic importance—but we cannot accept another merger that increases operational intensity without meaningful mitigation.' They request five categories of mandatory conditions: (1) procedural (Houston public hearing, neighborhood-specific forecasts, full system study, robust comment period); (2) environmental (air monitors, right-of-way maintenance); (3) safety/accessibility ($5M underpass, grade separations, Quiet Zones); (4) operational (train yard restrictions, dedicated police liaison); and (5) community investment (parks, land abandonment for community space). Their argument explicitly invokes equity: 'If Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern stand to benefit from this merger, then the communities that make their operations possible deserve meaningful investment and protection in return.' This is sophisticated conditional opposition with specific, measurable, and technically achievable remedies—signaling potential for settlement if applicants engage on mitigation framework.
key_arguments: Houston is not a peripheral player in this merger but a central operational hub as the nation's 4th-largest city and critical freight link. East End residents living adjacent to these corridors experience crossing blockages of 30 minutes to many hours—a direct operational impact that warrants localized analysis and community voice.

The prior CP-KCS merger review's narrow scope examining only merger-related lines failed to capture real-world operational dynamics. In Houston, secondary lines must wait at at-grade interchanges for priority routes to clear, creating cascade blockage effects—this full system impact must be studied in the UP-NS review.

The STB should require detailed neighborhood-specific impact forecasts, not generalized regional assessments, showing projected freight volume increases, train frequency/length changes, at-grade crossing wait times, emergency response impacts, and air quality effects on schools.

If the merger increases operational intensity, the communities bearing the burden deserve meaningful mitigation: the bare minimum includes $5M for Preston Road underpass, 25% funding for grade separations, Quiet Zone implementation on four corridors, dedicated UP police liaison, and land abandonment for community space development.

Houston residents were inadequately served in prior merger proceedings held on weekdays in distant locations (Beaumont). The STB must hold at least one evening/weekend Houston public hearing to enable working residents to testify directly about merger impacts on their neighborhoods.

East End communities experience disproportionate rail impacts—children attending schools within feet of active freight corridors, wealthier areas receiving prompt right-of-way maintenance while East End neighborhoods wait months for cleanup. Merger approval must be conditioned on equitable operational and community investment.

The proposed system impact study must examine secondary line interactions, cumulative Houston rail network impacts, at-grade crossing blockage patterns/durations, and effects on parallel roadways—not just primary merger corridors.
key_excerpts: Our residents routinely experience crossing blockages that last from 30 minutes to many hours. We are not opposed to freight rail—we understand its economic importance—but we cannot accept another merger that increases operational intensity without meaningful mitigation for the communities that bear the brunt of the burden.

Early analysis suggests that the STB may place less emphasis on post-merger freight volume impacts to expedite the merger decision process. Industry projections indicate that 'the densest lanes are projected to emerge post-merger,' yet Houston has not received clear, localized predictions about what this means for our communities.

In cities like Houston, where interchanges are at-grade, trains on secondary lines must wait for priority routes to clear before they can proceed. This cascade effect is one of the primary causes of prolonged blockages in neighborhoods like the East End, Second Ward, and Fifth Ward.
The previous merger review's narrow scope failed to capture the real-world operational dynamics that affect East End residents on a daily basis. This merger review must not repeat that mistake.
If Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern stand to benefit from this merger, then the communities that make their operations possible deserve meaningful investment and protection in return.

Our requests are not unreasonable. They represent the bare minimum of what our communities need to ensure that increased rail operations do not further degrade our quality of life, our children's health, and the safety of our neighborhoods.
docket_entries.relief_requested: If merger is approved, Union Pacific must implement five categories of mandatory community benefit measures: (1) Environmental Protection including air quality monitoring and right-of-way maintenance; (2) Safety & Accessibility including $5M for Preston Road underpass, 25% funding for ten grade separations, and Quiet Zone implementation on four specified corridors; (3) Operational Improvements including train yard restrictions and dedicated UP police liaison; (4) Community Investment including park development and land abandonment for community space; (5) Procedural requirements including Houston public hearing, neighborhood-specific impact forecasts, full system impact study, and meaningful public comment period.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing raises three significant regulatory issues: (1) PROCEDURAL SCOPE—It challenges the STB's prior practice of limiting merger analysis to direct merger-affected corridors, demanding instead a full system-wide impact study examining secondary line cascade effects and cumulative network impacts. This could expand the analytical scope required in railroad merger reviews. (2) COMMUNITY STANDING AND HEARING PROCEDURES—The demand for a Houston public hearing in accessible evening/weekend hours contests prior merger review practices (CP-KCS held hearing only in Beaumont on weekday) and signals potential Board procedure criticism. (3) MITIGATION STANDARD—The detailed, quantified mitigation requests (25% grade separation funding, $5M underpass, dedicated police liaison, Quiet Zone implementation) establish a potential baseline for 'meaningful community benefit' in future merger orders affecting residential areas. If the STB accepts these conditions, it would establish precedent for community-negotiated operational/investment conditions in railroad mergers.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Comment filed during Comment period; no specific response deadline noted, but filing dated March 27, 2026 with reference to 'Proposed Procedural Schedule' suggests comment filed early in procedural calendar

docket_entries.title: Community Opposition to UP-NS Merger with Mitigation Demands
docket_entries.filer_name: Houston Super Neighborhood 64 & 88 (Greater Eastwood, Lawndale, & Wayside)
docket_entries.entry_summary: Super Neighborhoods 64 & 88 representing 23,000 Houston residents directly oppose the UP-NS merger, citing catastrophic impacts from blocked rail crossings that already create 11-12 minute emergency response times versus 5-6 minute city average. The filing documents procedural irregularities in merger support solicitation and demands binding mitigation measures including grade separations, crossing time limits, and community oversight authority.
key_arguments: Procedural irregularities: Union Pacific hired Griffin Communications to solicit approximately 2,000 form-letter support statements from elected officials using identical template language before merger application was filed and during period when STB requested only procedural comments

Current crisis: Houston experiences most freight rail congestion in US; eight of ten most blocked crossings nationally are in East End; 26% of trains on Galveston Subdivision stop, making north-south corridor inaccessible for hours daily

Life-threatening impacts: Emergency response times in East End are 11-12 minutes versus 5-6 minute city average; documented deaths (2023 baby death, 2024 student death) attributable to blocked crossings preventing emergency access

Merger will exacerbate: Applicants' own filings show 36% increase in daily train traffic on Lafayette Subdivision within 5 years; Norfolk Southern announced Houston as major intermodal hub with 1.4 million additional annual loads

Truck traffic contradiction: Despite merger narrative of reducing truck traffic, applicants disclosed Settegast Yard will experience 209.8% increase in daily truck traffic (246 to 762 trucks daily) - fifth-highest projected increase nationwide
Infrastructure inadequacy: No alternative routing analysis; no consideration of distributing traffic away from Houston Complex; malfunctioning grade-crossing equipment remains chronic problem
Withdrawn commitments: Applicants removed $750 million previously announced concessions; 'For Our Communities' section removed from merger promotional website entirely
Chicago precedent: Union Pacific plans to double train traffic on two-mile stretch of Chicago's West Side with same vague assurance of 'localized impacts offset by merger benefits'
key_excerpts: These are not isolated incidents. They represent routine, documented reality for our residents.

The national average first responder response time is 5-6 minutes. In the East End, it takes 11-12 minutes because first responders must navigate around trains, which is more than double the citywide average.
2023: A baby died because first responders could not reach the scene in time. 2024: Police could not access a potential school shooting situation due to blocked crossings.
The applicants' own STB filings reveal the merger will increase daily train traffic on the Lafayette Subdivision-becoming the Terminal Subdivision inside Loop 610-by 36 percent within 5 years.

When asked to identify facilities experiencing transaction-related truck traffic increases exceeding 10 percent or 50 vehicles daily, the applicants disclosed that Houston's Settegast Yard would experience a 209.8 percent increase in daily truck traffic by year five-from 246 trucks daily to 762 trucks daily.

Our residents deserve more than perfunctory consultation through pre-written endorsements drafted by political consultants. We deserve concrete solutions to a crisis that threatens our children's safety, impedes emergency response, and diminishes quality of life.

During the company's third-quarter earnings call, UP CEO Jim Vena himself criticized premature opposition, asking, 'Why would you come out so strong when you haven't even read what the merger document is?' Yet Union Pacific simultaneously recruited premature support through form letters before anyone could review the actual proposal.

key_excerpts: Applicants have become aware that confidentiality designations were inadvertently omitted from the workpapers listed in the 'Reference File' tabs of the index titled 'Op. Plan Workpaper Reference File Index.'
