docket_entries.title: CN Motion to Adjust Filing Date and Comment Deadlines Due to Applicants' Inaccessible Encrypted Workpaper Databases
docket_entries.entry_summary: CN alleges that Union Pacific failed to comply with STB Decision No. 3's clear directive that 'no files contained within the filing should be restricted or password protected. All files and data should be fully accessible and modifiable by anyone authorized to view the evidence of the case.' CN states that critical Highly Confidential and Confidential SQL databases from the Hunt Verified Statement remained encrypted and inaccessible from April 30 through May 3, 2026—preventing CN's consultants from running 'most of the Hunt and Gehringer/Orr code and none of Hunt's code relating to diversion modeling or market shares.' The databases contain 762 objects including 'input data tables required for running code and code procedures.' CN argues the Application was not complete until May 4, when Union Pacific finally provided unencrypted files. CN requests the Board adopt the precedent from Bessemer & Lake Erie Railroad (FD 36347), where the Board deemed the filing date to be the date applicant corrected a material deficiency (a blank signature page), and similarly treat May 4 as the effective filing date here, recalculating all dependent comment deadlines. CN emphasizes that the missing database components here are 'far more consequential than a missing signature.'
key_arguments: Union Pacific's individually encrypted files violate STB Decision No. 3's explicit requirement that 'all files and data should be fully accessible and modifiable by anyone authorized to view the evidence of the case,' making the April 30 submission non-compliant with Board directives.

The encrypted databases prevented CN's consultants from executing critical analytical code, specifically Hunt's diversion modeling and market share code, and prevented access to 762 database objects including input data tables required for reproducing and verifying the Applicants' analysis.

Following Bessemer & Lake Erie precedent (FD 36347), where the Board reset the filing date when applicants omitted a signature page, the Board should recognize May 4, 2026 as the effective filing date here, since the missing workpaper databases are substantively far more material than a procedural signature defect.

All parties, including CN, the Board, and other intervenors, have been prejudiced in their ability to assess Application completeness and conduct adequate technical review during a limited comment window due to the delayed availability of the complete evidentiary record.
key_excerpts: CN first realized on April 30 that certain Highly Confidential and Confidential SQL databases from the Hunt Verified Statement were encrypted and thus inaccessible. [and] Prior to gaining access, CN's consultants were unable to run most of the Hunt and Gehringer/Orr code and none of Hunt's code relating to diversion modeling or market shares.

Applicants' encryption runs afoul of the Board's directive in Decision No. 3, that '[s]ubmissions may include a password protected filing (e.g., a protected ZIP archive transmitted via Secure File Transfer Protocol), but no files contained within the filing should be restricted or password protected. All files and data should be fully accessible and modifiable by anyone authorized to view the evidence of the case.'
The databases contain 762 objects, including, but not limited to, input data tables required for running code and code procedures.

Consistent with that decision, and considering that the missing components of the Application here are far more consequential than a missing signature, CN requests the Board consider today, May 4, 2026, to be the filing date of the Application and to adjust the deadlines set forth in Decision No. 17.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Adjust the filing date of Applicants' Amended Application from April 30, 2026 to May 4, 2026, and recalculate all subsequent comment deadlines and procedural dates set forth in Decision No. 17 and all other decisions to account for the delayed access to required workpaper files.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This motion raises a critical issue about the completeness and accessibility of the Application record during the comment phase. If granted, it would reset all procedural deadlines calculated from April 30, extending the comment period and all derivative deadlines. The motion invokes STB precedent (Bessemer & Lake Erie, FD 36347) establishing that when applicants fail to provide a complete, accessible filing in compliance with Board directives, the filing date is reset to when compliance is achieved. This affects the schedule for CN's and all other intervenors' substantive analysis, discovery, and comment deadlines. The merits argument also directly implicates whether the Application satisfied STB Decision No. 3's specific technical requirements for workpaper accessibility—a compliance issue that could affect the record's adequacy and the Board's ability to review the case fully.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Motion filed May 4, 2026 requesting immediate Board consideration for adjustment of all filing-date-dependent deadlines in Decision No. 17 and subsequent decisions. CN's counsel contacted UP counsel on April 30 regarding the encrypted databases; the issue persisted until May 3 when access was finally provided.

docket_entries.title: Union Pacific & Norfolk Southern Motion to Enter Proposed Discovery Guidelines
docket_entries.entry_summary: Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern jointly petition the STB to adopt their proposed Discovery Guidelines to govern discovery procedures. The applicants state they 'conferred with non-applicant Class I railroads regarding potential discovery guidelines for this proceeding and exchanged drafts, but the parties did not reach agreement on a stipulated proposal.' The proposed guidelines impose strict limits on written discovery (maximum 50 requests per party per applicant), limit depositions to witnesses who have submitted verified statements with one day (7 hours) per witness maximum, require virtual deposition participation capability, impose 21-day document production timelines, and establish a tiered letter-brief process for dispute resolution before ALJ Soulikias. The applicants cite past STB practice in major railroad mergers (CSX-Conrail 1997, CN-Illinois Central 1998, UP-Southern Pacific 1995) as precedent. Notably, applicants acknowledge disagreement with competing Class I railroads (likely BNSF, CSX, CN, CPKC) over discovery scope, but moved forward unilaterally rather than with stipulated agreement. This suggests potential resistance from intervenor railroads who may view the limits as constraining their ability to challenge the merger on competitive grounds.
key_arguments: Entry of discovery guidelines will 'ensure that discovery proceeds smoothly and disputes are resolved efficiently, and is consistent with the past practice of the Board in other proceedings involving proposed railroad combinations'
Applicants proposed guidelines unilaterally after failing to reach stipulated agreement with non-applicant Class I railroads, indicating they determined applicant-favorable terms were necessary

Strict numerical and temporal limits (50 discovery requests per party, 21-day production, 7-hour depositions, one deposition per witness) are justified as necessary to keep discovery 'consistent with the procedural schedule adopted in the proceeding'
Virtual deposition participation and electronic repositories with undertaking-based access will accommodate confidential business information while enabling broad participation
key_excerpts: Applicants conferred with non-applicant Class I railroads regarding potential discovery guidelines for this proceeding and exchanged drafts, but the parties did not reach agreement on a stipulated proposal. Applicants have subsequently prepared the attached Discovery Guidelines for the Board's consideration.

Entry of Discovery Guidelines in this proceeding will ensure that discovery proceeds smoothly and disputes are resolved efficiently, and is consistent with the past practice of the Board in other proceedings involving proposed railroad combinations.
Each party of record may not propound more than 50 written discovery requests (including requests for production and interrogatories) on each Applicant.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Board entry of proposed Discovery Guidelines (Appendix A) to govern discovery procedures in the proceeding, ensuring discovery 'proceeds smoothly and disputes are resolved efficiently'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing establishes the procedural framework governing all discovery exchanges in the proceeding. The guidelines modify standard 49 C.F.R. pt. 1114 discovery rules by imposing quantitative and temporal limits that significantly constrain intervenor discovery rights. The 50-request cap per party per applicant is restrictive for large intervenor coalitions challenging the merger on multiple competitive, service, and rate issues. The one-day deposition limit and requirement to depose only verified-statement witnesses limits cross-examination opportunities. Critically, applicants' unilateral proposal (rather than stipulated agreement with competitors) signals the applicants anticipated intervenor objections. Any intervenor motion to modify these guidelines could delay discovery openings and trigger disputes over scope. The guidelines also establish email service and ALJ Soulikias as the dispute arbiter, creating procedural dependency on ALJ rulings during active discovery.
docket_entries.deadline_description: No explicit response deadline stated, but Board typically rules on such procedural motions within 2-3 weeks absent opposition. Intervenors may file objections or counter-proposals.

docket_entries.title: STB Decision No. 19: Procedural Ruling on Revised Application Filing Date and Workpaper Access; Comment Deadline Adjustment
docket_entries.entry_summary: On May 5, 2026, the STB issued Decision No. 19 addressing a technical issue raised by Canadian National (CN) regarding access to workpaper databases supporting the Revised Application filed on April 30, 2026. CN argued that encryption issues prevented access to witness workpapers until May 3, 2026 (Sunday), and requested the Board treat the filing as occurring on the next business day, May 4. Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern replied that they promptly resolved the access issue upon CN's notification and that modifying filing dates based on changes to supporting documents in complex proceedings would be inconsistent with normal Board practice. The Board agreed, finding that Applicants had rectified the workpaper access issue promptly upon notification and declined to reset the application filing date. However, the Board did adjust the comment deadline from May 8 at noon to May 8 at 11:59 p.m. EDT to provide additional time for parties to review the Revised Application and comment on whether it contains all information required under 49 C.F.R. Part 1180. Applicants were given until May 12, 2026 at 5 p.m. EDT to file a reply. This ruling establishes that the Revised Application is deemed filed as of April 30, 2026, and all other schedule dates remain unchanged, but parties have marginally extended time to assess completeness of regulatory submissions.
key_arguments: Applicants' argument: Modifying filing dates based on changes to supporting documents in complex proceedings involving voluminous workpaper submissions is 'irreconcilable with normal practice before the Board'—suggesting that technical issues with data access should not reset procedural timelines once promptly remedied.

Board finding: Applicants promptly rectified the workpaper access issue upon notification from CN, satisfying the regulatory requirement that applicants make supporting data available and supply such data on request per 49 C.F.R. § 1180.7(b)(7).

Board reasoning: While the encryption issue warranted some schedule accommodation, it did not justify resetting the filing date itself; instead, the Board extended the comment deadline by approximately 12 hours to provide additional review time consistent with the Board's determination timeframe.
key_excerpts: Applicants promptly rectified the workpaper access issue upon notification from CN in this instance... Accordingly, the application filing date will not be reset.

Applicants argue, among other things, that modifying filing dates based on changes to supporting documents in complex proceedings involving voluminous workpaper submissions is irreconcilable with normal practice before the Board.

Nevertheless, the deadline for comments on whether the Revised Application contains the information required in 49 C.F.R. part 1180 will be adjusted to provide some additional time, consistent with the timeframe for the Board's determination.
docket_entries.relief_requested: The Board granted the parties' request for schedule adjustment: Comments on whether the Revised Application contains required regulatory information due by May 8, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. EDT; Applicants' reply due by May 12, 2026, at 5 p.m. EDT. The Board declined CN's request to reset the filing date.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This decision establishes a precedent that technical issues with workpaper access will not result in resetting application filing dates if promptly remedied, protecting the applicants' procedural position and timeline. It confirms the Board's authority to adjust procedural deadlines (but not filing dates) to accommodate legitimate access issues. The decision also clarifies the Board's expectations regarding 49 C.F.R. § 1180.7(b)(7)—the requirement that applicants provide supporting data in accessible form—and demonstrates the Board's view that compliance occurs when applicants promptly cure access issues upon notification. The ruling does not change the scope of review or evidentiary burden but does affect the practical timeline for intervenor review and comment.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Comments limited to whether the Revised Application contains information required in 49 C.F.R. Part 1180 due by May 8, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. EDT; Applicants' reply due by May 12, 2026, at 5 p.m. EDT.

docket_entries.title: Union Pacific Reply Opposition to Canadian National's Request to Retroactively Change Amended Application Filing Date
docket_entries.entry_summary: Union Pacific opposes Canadian National's request to retroactively change the filing date of the Amended Application, arguing that CN has failed to demonstrate any prejudice to its ability to evaluate completeness. UP emphasizes that CN has had full access to the 7,000-page Amended Application text and sixteen verified statements, and that CN's actual concerns relate to the merits (sufficiency of support for assertions), not completeness. UP argues it responded promptly to the workpaper access issue, resolving the technical problem by 9 AM ET on Sunday, May 3, 2026—only one business day after being notified. UP further contends that granting CN's request would set a dangerous precedent incompatible with STB precedent (Decision No. 8) and normal Board practice, noting that 'some technical issues are bound to arise despite everyone's best efforts' in filings of this scale and complexity, and that workpaper replacement is common practice. UP portrays CN's challenge as an attempt to weaponize a good-faith technical glitch.
key_arguments: CN has not identified any prejudice from workpaper access delay: 'CN has not identified any way in which its inability to access the limited set of workpapers at issue for the limited period of time at issue prejudiced its ability to determine whether the Amended Application contains the information required to be considered complete.'

CN's actual objections concern merits, not completeness: 'CN's concerns relate to the merits of the Amended Application—whether Applicants sufficiently supported assertions in the Amended Application—not the completeness of the Amended Application.'

UP resolved the issue promptly and in good faith: 'Applicants worked through the weekend to determine the source of the issue and provided replacement files shortly after 9 AM ET on Sunday, May 3, 2026—allowing only one business day to pass between being notified of the issue and resolving it.'

Workpaper replacements are routine and the Board has created a process for them: 'The Board's docket is full of matters where party filings are supported by voluminous and complex workpapers... and it is common practice in Board proceedings for parties to have to replace workpapers when other parties identify issues. Indeed, in this very proceeding the Board recognized that workpaper replacements may be necessary, and it created a process to document such changes.'

Granting CN's request would create an unworkable precedent: 'The notion that any workpaper issue—and particularly one that was resolved quickly and in good faith—is sufficient to somehow nullify a filing until the workpaper issue has been addressed is irreconcilable with Decision No. 8 and with normal practice before the Board.'
key_excerpts: CN has had full access to the text of the 7,000-page Amended Application, including the sixteen supporting verified statements, as well as hundreds of gigabytes of supporting workpapers.
CN's concerns relate to the merits of the Amended Application—whether Applicants sufficiently supported assertions in the Amended Application—not the completeness of the Amended Application.

Applicants worked through the weekend to determine the source of the issue and provided replacement files shortly after 9 AM ET on Sunday, May 3, 2026—allowing only one business day to pass between being notified of the issue and resolving it.

In filings of this scale and complexity, some technical issues are bound to arise despite everyone's best efforts, and it is common practice in Board proceedings for parties to have to replace workpapers when other parties identify issues.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Applicants request that the Board deny CN's request to retroactively change the filing date of the Amended Application.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing clarifies the STB's procedural rules regarding workpaper access and filing completeness (referencing Decision No. 8). It establishes UP's argument that technical workpaper glitches do not invalidate filings if (1) no prejudice to substantive review is demonstrated, (2) replacement occurs promptly, and (3) the underlying document is complete in substance. This procedural framing may influence how the STB handles similar challenges throughout the proceeding and could set precedent for managing large, complex merger applications.
docket_entries.deadline_description: CN's original motion was May 4, 2026; this reply was filed May 5, 2026. STB ruling on CN's retroactive filing date request is pending.

docket_entries.title: Air Alliance Houston Notice of Intent to Participate
docket_entries.entry_summary: Air Alliance Houston filed a notice of intent to participate as a Party of Record in the UP/NS merger proceeding. No substantive position on the merger, conditions, or specific arguments are stated in this filing. This is purely a procedural notice establishing intervention status to enable future participation.
key_excerpts: Air Alliance Houston hereby gives notice of its intent to participate in this proceeding as a Party of Record.
docket_entries.relief_requested: To participate as a Party of Record in the proceeding
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing establishes Air Alliance Houston as a Party of Record entitled to receive service of future filings and participate in discovery, hearing, and briefing phases. As an environmental/air quality organization, their full participation may later introduce environmental review requirements, Clean Air Act compliance arguments, or regional emissions impact analysis into the record—potentially expanding the STB's scope of review beyond traditional rail competition metrics.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)

docket_entries.title: Certificate of Service and Notice of Amended Railroad Control Application Filed
docket_entries.entry_summary: Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern filed a Certificate of Service on May 5, 2026, certifying that they have served an Amended Railroad Control Application on all parties of record pursuant to STB Decision No. 18 (issued May 1, 2026). The filing notifies interested parties that the applicants are seeking authority under 49 U.S.C. §§ 11323-25 for Union Pacific's acquisition of control of Norfolk Southern. The Amended Application is available on the STB website (www.stb.gov) or by request from Covington & Burling. This certificate establishes proper service and marks the formal commencement of the public comment period on the amended application. The filing itself contains no substantive arguments regarding the merger's effects, conditions, or defenses—it is purely procedural notice.
key_excerpts: Union Pacific Corporation and Union Pacific Railway Company ('Union Pacific') and Norfolk Southern Corporation and Norfolk Southern Railway Company ('Norfolk Southern') are hereby notifying you that their Amended Railroad Control Application, which seeks authority under 49 U.S.C. §§ 11323-25 for the acquisition of control by Union Pacific of Norfolk Southern, has been filed with the Board.

The Amended Application is available on the Board's website, www.stb.gov, and can be accessed by searching for filings on the FD 36873 docket or via the 'UP-NS Merger Resources' link on the home page.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Approval of railroad control application seeking authority under 49 U.S.C. §§ 11323-25 for Union Pacific's acquisition of control of Norfolk Southern.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing establishes proper statutory notice under 49 C.F.R. § 1180.4(c)(5)(i)-(iv) and compliance with STB Decision No. 18, which likely imposed service requirements on the applicants. The certificate triggers the formal comment period for interested parties and creates a paper trail establishing that all parties of record, the Secretary of Transportation, the Attorney General, and the ALJ received actual notice of the Amended Application. This is legally significant for defending against any later procedural challenges based on inadequate notice. The reference to an 'Amended' Application (rather than the original) suggests material changes to the application filed earlier in the proceeding.
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response deadline imposed by this filing. The certificate simply establishes compliance with prior procedural orders. Intervenors will have their own comment deadlines established by STB scheduling orders.

docket_entries.title: CPKC Letter Opposing Applicants' Proposed Discovery Guidelines; Coordinating Joint Response on Behalf of Competing Railroads
docket_entries.entry_summary: CPKC files a letter on behalf of itself, BNSF, CSX, and Grand Trunk Corporation coordinating a joint response to Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern's proposed Discovery Guidelines (filed as UP-45/NS-43). CPKC explicitly states that the Applicants' proposed protocols 'solely reflect Applicants' positions and do not reflect any agreement on the part of the Parties Seeking Discovery of Applicants.' The competing railroads announce they will file a joint response by May 12, 2026 (5:00 pm EDT) to challenge the proposed discovery framework. This filing demonstrates active coordination among major railroad competitors—who collectively operate extensive competing networks—and signals they view the discovery process as critical to establishing competitive harm arguments. The May 12 response date falls by the same deadline for applicants' responses to completeness comments, suggesting competitors are timing their discovery objections to coincide with broader substantive challenges to the application.
key_arguments: Applicants' proposed Discovery Guidelines do not reflect agreement or consensus among competing railroads actively seeking discovery, and therefore should not be adopted unmodified
The coordinated competitors (CPKC, BNSF, CSX, Grand Trunk) have distinct discovery interests and are preparing a unified alternative framework
key_excerpts: the Protocols proposed by Applicants (set forth in their Appendix A) solely reflect Applicants' positions and do not reflect any agreement on the part of the Parties Seeking Discovery of Applicants
the Parties Seeking Discovery of Applicants anticipate responding promptly to Applicants' Motion, and will endeavor to do so jointly and no later than 5:00 pm EDT on Tuesday, May 12
docket_entries.relief_requested: CPKC requests that the STB reject or modify Applicants' proposed Discovery Guidelines (UP-45/NS-43), which CPKC contends 'solely reflect Applicants' positions and do not reflect any agreement on the part of the Parties Seeking Discovery of Applicants.' CPKC and the coordinated group of competing railroads (BNSF, CSX, Grand Trunk) will file a joint response by May 12, 2026, 5:00 pm EDT opposing the proposed protocols.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing signals that competing railroads have coordinated discovery strategy and will present a unified challenge to the Applicants' proposed discovery protocols. Under STB merger rules, discovery scope and protocols are critical to establishing competitive harm, and Applicants typically propose narrow discovery to limit exposure. Competitor coordination here suggests they intend to demand broader discovery into competitive impacts, network overlap, pricing data, and service quality comparisons. The joint response will likely propose alternative discovery protocols (broader document requests, depositions, interrogatories on competitive effects). Judge Soulikias will need to balance Applicants' interest in narrow discovery against competitors' need for evidence to support merger opposition.
docket_entries.deadline_description: CPKC and coordinating parties (BNSF, CSX, Grand Trunk) will file joint response to Applicants' Motion to Enter Proposed Discovery Guidelines by 5:00 pm EDT, May 12, 2026

docket_entries.title: Comprehensive Intervenor Comments Opposing UP-NS Merger Based on Labor Violations, Safety Negligence, and Procedural Fraud
docket_entries.entry_summary: Ruth Tines, a 33-year veteran railroad employee with February 7, 1965 labor protections, files comprehensive comments opposing the UP-NS merger based on documented evidence of systematic labor displacement targeting legacy employees, safety violations related to equipment negligence causing her federally-approved occupational disability, procedural fraud including perjured testimony and expunged records misuse, and a pattern of retaliation against whistleblowers. Tines argues Union Pacific lacks operational fitness to expand given its designation as a 'Serial Violator' and demonstrates a corporate culture prioritizing shareholder value over worker safety and federal labor compliance.
key_arguments: Union Pacific systematically purged CNW Legacy employees with February 7, 1965 protections through pretextual testing (70-lb lifts, clerical exams unrelated to warehouse work) and Rule 1.6 catch-all charges, particularly targeting women with 25-30+ years of service

Carrier forced claimant to operate defective forklift equipment (bald tires, solid rubber without air cushioning) while medicated, causing documented spinal injuries (L4-L5 protrusion and L5-S1 disc bulge) later approved for occupational disability by Railroad Retirement Board in record 6-month timeframe

Systematic procedural fraud including: perjured testimony from witness located in Houston, TX claiming to witness May 21, 2025 incident while on medical leave; use of expunged 2020 disciplinary record in October 2025 appeal despite arbitrator John Parker's 2022 award requiring complete expungement; biased hearing officer who was also labor relations manager

Termination occurred July 15, 2025, exactly 14 days before July 29, 2025 merger announcement, strategically timed to remove $626,326.54 liability and eliminate 'High Five' railroad retirement pension calculations before contractual raises took effect

Pattern of retaliation against protected whistleblower activity, including May 8, 2025 safety report on hazardous equipment conditions dismissed as 'paranoia' and June 5, 2025 Rule 1.6 charges filed less than 24 hours after reporting Sr. Director Delarrio Perkins to senior leadership

Union Pacific is documented 'Serial Violator' with 25-year non-compliance record: 200+ whistleblower complaints, $193M+ in penalties (2015-2025), August 2025 official 'Serial Violator' designation, March 6, 2026 OSHA $315,000 penalty for retaliatory termination of another employee

Incomplete amended application fails to disclose labor purges, financial liabilities from pension manipulation, operational integrity breakdown through record tampering, and contradicts February 7 Agreement protections promised by ICC in 1995 Finance Docket No. 32133

Management misconduct includes falsified FMLA records via unauthorized Excel sheets, fabricated witness testimony, EEOC false statements claiming claimant 'refused to participate' when documented accommodation was entered in hearing record, and expunged records misuse violating binding arbitrator award
key_excerpts: Union Pacific pressured me to work unprotected despite knowing I was battling a mental health crisis and taking high-risk medication. My position required me to operate a forklift with bald tires in a raggedy railyard... I worked the third shift alone with no backup... a 'kill zone' created by a company that prioritized the budget over human life and American safety.
The fact that my L4-5 protrusion shrank by over 50% specifically after I was pulled from service proves that the equipment-not aging-was the source of the trauma.

I was dismissed on July 15 at 7:00 AM; by July 16 at 7:00 AM, my union legacy-protected position was already posted for bid and filled by a lower-grade, non-legacy employee. This is a fraudulent labor-displacement scheme allegedly to manufacture 'merger synergies.'

Director Perkins confronted me with the following threatening statements: He asked me repeatedly: 'Do you believe in karma? Have you ever heard of karma?' He stated: 'I believe in karma.' He further warned me: 'I am not Jesus; I only have two cheeks to turn.'

Senior Manager D'uane Merchant testified as a live witness, claiming she personally observed me being 'disruptive' on May 21, 2025. However, Merchant's own testimony admits she was out of work on medical leave for 30 days and did not return until June 3, 2025.

By establishing aggressive 'Operating Ratio' targets, Vena and Hamann incentivized lower-level managers to utilize fraudulent geolocation data and 'moving bar' testing to eliminate the final C&NW Legacy employees from the payroll.

How can the STB trust a 'serial violator' with one of the largest mergers in American history? A company that manipulates federal records, forces medicated workers into 'kill zones,' and mocks employees in the midst of a health crisis lacks the operational fitness to expand.

docket_entries.title: STB Approval of Waybill Data Access for Berkley Research Group Consultant in UP-NS Merger Docket
docket_entries.entry_summary: The STB Office of Economics approved CN's request to add Calvin Morley from Berkley Research Group to the confidential waybill data access authorization in the UP-NS merger docket. The approval was granted on May 6, 2026, following payment of the $72 processing fee. This indicates CN is engaged in detailed economic analysis of the proposed merger, likely to support competitive impact testimony or expert reports. The waybill data (Carload Commodity Waybill Sample) is highly detailed railroad operational and pricing information subject to strict confidentiality restrictions. The approval itself is routine administrative processing but the underlying request reflects CN's active preparation for substantive intervention in the docket.
key_arguments: CN requires access to confidential waybill data to support expert economic analysis of the UP-NS merger's competitive effects
key_excerpts: Grand Trunk Corporation and its U.S. rail operating subsidiaries (collectively, 'CN') request additional authorization for the below consultant to access the Waybill Data in the Union Pacific – Norfolk Southern docket (FD 36873).
I have read and understand the conditions for release of the CCWS data. I agree to comply fully with these conditions and the provisions of this confidentiality agreement.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Approval of waybill data access for Calvin Morley (Berkley Research Group) under Waybill Agreement WB25-55, contingent on confidentiality compliance and $72 processing fee payment.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This approval grants CN access to highly sensitive competitive data under strict confidentiality protocols (49 U.S.C. § 11146 and STB waybill access procedures). The data is essential for preparing detailed competitive impact analyses and supporting expert testimony. The approval does not change the scope of review but indicates discovery is underway and CN is preparing substantive filings. Approval of consultant access signals the STB's expectation of detailed economic testimony in this proceeding.
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response deadline; this is STB administrative action

docket_entries.title: City of Detroit Notice of Intent to Participate
docket_entries.entry_summary: City of Detroit filed a notice of intent to participate in the UP/NS merger proceeding on May 6, 2026. The filing contains no substantive arguments, no position on the merger itself, and no specific conditions or relief beyond seeking placement on the service list. This is a standard procedural intervention notice by a municipal government entity preserving its right to monitor and potentially comment on the merger's impact on Detroit.
key_excerpts: The City of Detroit respectfully submits its Notice of Intent to Participate in this proceeding and any related sub-proceedings before the Surface Transportation Board, as its interests may appear.
docket_entries.relief_requested: City of Detroit requests to be placed on the service list as representative for the City of Detroit and to participate in this proceeding and any related sub-proceedings.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: No immediate significance. This is a ministerial filing establishing City of Detroit as an intervenor on the service list. No change to scope of review, evidentiary burden, or substantive issues. The city may file substantive comments or opposition later in the proceeding.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)

docket_entries.title: Letter of Comment on UP-NS Merger Application - Substantive Deficiencies Analysis
docket_entries.entry_summary: Retired BNSF executive and IEDC Fellow submits detailed technical critique of UP-NS merger application, identifying six substantive deficiencies in the applicants' burden to demonstrate competitive enhancement under the 2001 Major Merger Rules. Argues procedural compliance masks substantive evasion on volume projections, operational constraints, captive shipper protections, labor opposition, and historical precedent from UP-SP merger failure.
key_arguments: Volume growth projection of 12% within three years lacks credible explanation against documented decade-long 13% decline in combined volumes
Meridian Speedway train-length limits impose mandatory re-blocking that negates claimed elimination of 2,550 daily handlings; constraint not disclosed in application
American Chemistry Council's 240% rate increase for single-railroad-served facilities versus 24% with competitive options demonstrates captive shipper risk
Committed Gateway Pricing framework covers only 1-20% of eligible customers (excludes intermodal, automobiles, hazmat) and expires after merger oversight period
Schedule 5.8 walk-away rights suggest deal profitability depends on market dominance rather than efficiency gains
BLET and BMWED representing 53% of combined workforce oppose merger based on job protection loopholes, branch-line spinoff risks, and safety culture incompatibility
UP-SP merger (1996) produced $100M/month shipper losses and $1B+ UP losses before regulatory intervention; application fails to address comparable risks at greater scale
Pattern of procedural compliance coupled with substantive evasion suggests legally-sophisticated risk management rather than genuine confidence in benefit claims
key_excerpts: The burden is on the applicants to demonstrate affirmative competitive enhancement. Vol. 1 does not carry that burden.

The block-swapping silence is the hardest to explain innocently. The applicants own and operate the Meridian Speedway. Its train-length limits are not obscure. Their absence from the discussion of transit time savings is a substantive omission, not an oversight.

Shippers are being asked to accept permanent structural consolidation in exchange for temporary pricing protections. The temporal asymmetry between permanent consolidation and time-limited rate protection is acknowledged in the application but not resolved.

If the merger genuinely produced the public benefits UP claims, 2.1 million truckloads diverted and $3.5 billion in annual shipper savings, UP would be prepared to accept competitive guardrails as a condition of approval.
The 2001 rules were a direct regulatory response to the last time a railroad of this size made promises it did not keep.

docket_entries.title: Bartlett and Company Notice of Intent to Participate
docket_entries.entry_summary: Bartlett and Company, LLC filed a notice of intent to participate in the UP/NS merger proceeding without providing any substantive comments, arguments, or position on the transaction. key_excerpts: Bartlett and Company, LLC hereby provides notice of its intent to participate in this proceeding as its interests may appear, and requests to be placed on the service list for this proceeding.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Request for placement on service list to receive all filings and documents. Consent to email service.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Minimal. This filing establishes Bartlett's standing to participate in the proceeding and creates an obligation for the applicants and other parties to serve documents upon the filer. It does not change the scope of review, create evidentiary issues, or introduce new substantive claims. The filing simply perfects procedural participation rights under STB rules.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response required. Filing is notice-only for service list placement.

docket_entries.title: STB Response to Representative Paul D. Tonko Letter on UP/NS Merger Review Status
docket_entries.entry_summary: The STB, responding to Congressional inquiry from Rep. Tonko about merger safety and community impacts, confirms its rigorous review process. The Board rejected the applicants' initial application filed December 19, 2025 as incomplete on January 16, 2026, requiring deficiency remediation. UP and NS filed a revised application on April 30, 2026, and the Board is conducting a 30-day completeness review with public comment deadline extended to May 8, 2026. The Board explicitly states it will examine: (1) competitive effects, (2) carrier safety and efficiency, (3) adequate shipper service, (4) environmental safeguards, (5) fair employee working conditions, and (6) impacts on local communities. The Board confirms applicants must submit a Safety Integration Plan (prepared with FRA) and address blocked crossing impacts per 49 C.F.R. § 1180.8(a). The Board commits to 'rigorous examination of potential competitive effects, economic efficiencies, service effects, environmental impacts, and other critical considerations, including the impact on local communities.' Notably, the Board states: 'Comments on the merits of the proposed transaction will be sought at a later stage of the proceeding, should the Board accept the revised application,' indicating the proceeding is still in the gatekeeping phase.
key_arguments: The STB rejected the initial application as incomplete and has required remediation before proceeding to substantive review, confirming the merger applicants did not satisfy regulatory filing requirements on first attempt

The Board's statutory review mandate requires examination of six distinct categories: effective competition, carrier safety and efficiency, adequate shipper service, environmental safeguards, fair employee working conditions, and local community impacts
The Board requires applicants to submit specific Safety Integration Plan prepared with FRA and analysis of blocked crossing impacts as part of the completeness determination
Substantive merits comments will only be sought if the Board accepts the revised application, meaning the proceeding could terminate at the completeness stage if deficiencies are not cured
key_excerpts: On January 16, 2026, the Board issued a unanimous decision finding that that application was incomplete because it did not contain certain information required by the Board's regulations at 49 C.F.R. part 1180.

In considering whether a major merger transaction is in the public interest, the Board considers various goals, including effective competition, carrier safety and efficiency, adequate service for shippers, environmental safeguards, and fair working conditions for employees.

Applicants are also required to submit—as part of the environmental review process—a Safety Integration Plan, prepared in consultation with the Federal Railroad Administration, to ensure that safe operations would be maintained throughout the merger implementation process, and information on what measures the Applicants plan to take to address potentially blocked crossings.

The Board's review will include a rigorous examination of potential competitive effects, economic efficiencies, service effects, environmental impacts, and other critical considerations, including the impact on local communities.
Comments on the merits of the proposed transaction will be sought at a later stage of the proceeding, should the Board accept the revised application.
docket_entries.relief_requested: None - this is a procedural status letter. The Board states it will conduct rigorous review consistent with statutory mandate and regulations.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing establishes: (1) The applicants' initial submission was materially deficient under 49 C.F.R. Part 1180 and 49 U.S.C. § 11325(a), requiring complete re-filing; (2) The STB is applying the statutory six-factor public interest test (49 U.S.C. § 11324) encompassing competition, safety, efficiency, service, environment, and labor; (3) Applicants bear burden of proving public benefits and analyzing competitive effects under 49 C.F.R. § 1180.6; (4) FRA-coordinated Safety Integration Plan is a mandatory filing requirement; (5) The proceeding remains in the completeness review phase and may not advance to substantive hearing stage if revised application is found inadequate. This frames the evidentiary burden and defines the scope of permissible relief (the Board can deny on grounds of incomplete application, accept for further review, or accept conditionally).
docket_entries.deadline_description: Public comments on completeness due May 8, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. EDT; Applicants' reply comments due May 12, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. EDT; STB to issue completeness determination within 30 days of April 30, 2026 filing (by approximately May 30, 2026)

docket_entries.title: M4 Railcar Group opposes merger, citing infrastructure and labor capacity constraints
docket_entries.entry_summary: M4 Railcar Group opposes the merger on grounds that: (1) The applicants' projected intermodal benefits (2.1 million truckloads converted to rail) are unachievable and reflect inflated merger synergy claims—the railroads have failed to capture this traffic for years, and single-line service will not change that; (2) The projected conversion of 2.1 million truckloads would require approximately 10,500 additional double-stacked trains, which the existing infrastructure cannot support; (3) The railroads currently cannot reliably handle the filer's modest request for 5 boxcars per month, demonstrating severe capacity limitations; (4) Expansion at intermodal terminals, ports, and inland terminals is constrained by land availability and would require substantial capital investment in locomotives, facilities, and equipment over many years; (5) The merger will exacerbate an existing conductor crew shortage and labor crisis—'the RR's treat the crews horribly'—making the promised capacity increases impossible to staff; (6) Competing traffic demands (lumber, paper, autos, steel mill shipments) will compete for limited capacity, creating service bottlenecks. The filer argues these constraints are insurmountable even under divestiture scenarios ('sell off lines and make trunks'). The filer provided a Facebook video link as evidence of conductor crew shortages.
key_arguments: The applicants claim 2.1 million truckloads can be converted to rail through single-line service, but railroads have failed to capture this traffic for years—merger-related single-line service will not overcome fundamental market barriers.

Converting 2.1 million truckloads to rail would require ~10,500 additional double-stacked trains, but existing rail infrastructure is already inadequate: M4 cannot reliably obtain 5 boxcars per month, demonstrating the current system is at or beyond capacity.

The merger will coincide with acute conductor crew shortages and poor labor treatment by railroads, making it impossible to staff the additional crews needed to operate 10,500 new trains and expanded intermodal terminals.

Expansion of intermodal and inland container terminals is constrained by land availability at ports and rail yards; without detailed timelines and capital plans, the 2.1 million truckload projection is speculative.
Competing traffic demands (lumber, paper, autos, steel mill production from new mills) will saturate network capacity, creating service conflicts that merger will worsen rather than resolve.
Capital requirements for new locomotives, well cars, terminal facilities, and crew hiring are massive and undefined; the merger applicants have not demonstrated feasibility.
key_excerpts: 'With regards to intermodal, 2.1M truckloads!!! My questions is, why do they have to merge to make this happen?? Juust start marketing lanes now to grab the traffic. And "HELLO" they've, the RR's have been trying to grab this traffic all these years. And haven't.'

'doing the math, 2.1 million truck loads is 10,500 more trains, double stacked at a (100) wells each.. The RR's cry when I want (5) boxcars a month moved!! The existing infrastructure will never handle this 2.1M trucks converted to the rails.'
'This is another reason why this merger should never happen. They RR's treat the crews horribly .. check out the conductor crew shortage video I added below.'

'There needs to be expansion at each facility and is land available? or at the ports? Domestic too. Again, this is just intermodal. what about other traffic, lumber, paper, auto's, with the current administrations steel mills additions and added jobs there. Where does that traffic go and get pulled? Where does the staffing come to fill the jobs?'
docket_entries.relief_requested: M4 Railcar Group requests outright denial of the merger. In their words: 'M4 is not for Merger.'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: The filing raises infrastructure capacity, labor availability, and service adequacy concerns that fall within STB's merger review mandate under 49 U.S.C. § 11324(c) (effects on rail transportation efficiency and safety). However, the filing lacks the evidentiary detail, economic analysis, and formal intervention standing necessary to trigger heightened scrutiny. The infrastructure saturation argument—if developed with data—could support an argument that merger does not produce claimed efficiencies or that public benefits are overstated. The labor shortage argument may interest STB if developed to show operational risk. The argument that existing service is already constrained (inability to provide 5 boxcars/month) suggests a demand-driven market where merger may not increase capacity meaningfully.
docket_entries.deadline_description: No specific deadline mentioned; this is a substantive comment submitted during the comment period.

docket_entries.title: Applicants' Motion to Enter Amended Proposed Discovery Guidelines - Deposition Modification
docket_entries.entry_summary: Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern jointly request STB entry of amended discovery guidelines for FD 36873, specifically modifying the deposition provision (Section C.2.a.). The amendment provides that witnesses who have submitted written testimony in the proceeding 'shall be made available for deposition,' while witnesses who have NOT submitted written testimony may be deposed 'on notice in accordance with 49 C.F.R. § 1114.22, which notice shall identify the cause or reason why such deposition will be taken.' This represents a refinement of the applicants' original May 4, 2026 proposed guidelines, made 'after discussion with other interested parties.' The applicants are not requesting substantive relief on the merger itself but rather procedural framework for discovery. The guidelines also establish: (1) a 50-request limit per intervenor per applicant; (2) one-day, seven-hour maximum deposition limits; (3) virtual participation in depositions; (4) letter brief procedures for discovery disputes before ALJ Soulikias; (5) 21-day document production timeframe; and (6) expedited procedures for resolving discovery disputes through meet-and-confer and ALJ conference. This appears to be a negotiated outcome incorporating intervenor feedback.
key_arguments: Witnesses who have submitted written testimony shall be made available for deposition as of right, while witnesses without written testimony may be deposed only on notice showing cause or reason for the deposition
Deposition limits: each witness deposed no more than once, extended to a second deposition only if witness submits additional verified statement; maximum one day/seven hours per deposition
Discovery requests capped at 50 per intervenor per applicant to manage volume and expedite proceedings
Depositions to be conducted where witness is located or in Washington, DC (at witness preference) with virtual participation options
Discovery disputes resolved through letter briefs (3 pages opening, 1 page supporting, 3 pages opposition) with ALJ conference option within 3 business days
All documents to be produced within 21 days, with Bates numbering and confidentiality designations per Protective Order
key_excerpts: "A person who has submitted written testimony in this proceeding shall be made available for deposition. A person who has not submitted written testimony in this proceeding may be deposed on notice in accordance with 49 C.F.R. § 1114.22, which notice shall identify the cause or reason why such deposition will be taken."
"After discussion with other interested parties, Applicants propose amending Section C.2.a. in the previously submitted Discovery Guidelines" (indicates negotiated outcome)
"No deposition shall be longer than one day of seven (7) hours. Parties shall use their best efforts to complete depositions as promptly as practicable."
"Each party of record may not propound more than 50 written discovery requests (including requests for production and interrogatories) on each Applicant."
docket_entries.relief_requested: Board entry of Amended Discovery Guidelines, specifically modifying Section C.2.a. to provide that 'A person who has submitted written testimony in this proceeding shall be made available for deposition. A person who has not submitted written testimony in this proceeding may be deposed on notice in accordance with 49 C.F.R. § 1114.22, which notice shall identify the cause or reason why such deposition will be taken.'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: These discovery guidelines establish the procedural framework governing evidence-gathering in a major railroad merger proceeding under 49 U.S.C. § 11324. The amendment to Section C.2.a. distinguishes between witnesses with and without written testimony, creating a two-tiered deposition regime: automatic availability for direct participants (those submitting written testimony) vs. notice-and-cause requirement for others. This allocation may affect intervenor ability to depose applicant personnel who do not formally submit written testimony but have relevant knowledge. The 50-request cap, one-deposition limit, and seven-hour maximum per witness establish expedition constraints that compress discovery scope compared to typical antitrust proceedings. The guidelines indicate Board delegation to ALJ Soulikias for discovery dispute resolution via expedited letter brief procedures. The fact that these are 'amended' guidelines incorporating 'discussion with other interested parties' suggests prior intervenor objections may have prompted modifications, though the specific negotiation history is not disclosed in this filing.
docket_entries.deadline_description: No deadline for responses to this procedural motion. STB will rule by Board decision on guideline entry.

docket_entries.title: Reply and Motion for Modern Public Interest Protections - Colin Finney Party of Record
docket_entries.entry_summary: Colin Finney, as a Party of Record, filed a comprehensive reply opposing the Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern merger without substantial federal protections for regional passenger transit. The filing argues that approval of a 40% freight volume increase on the Lehigh Line requires either dual-track expansion, capacity caps, or permanent public access mandates to serve the public interest of over 7 million Pennsylvanians and prevent environmental, safety, and infrastructure hazards.
key_arguments: Federal merger review annuls historical private conduit claims and imposes modern public interest obligations
Single-track mainline at 24 daily trains constitutes saturation that blocks regional transit planning capacity
40% freight surge creates unacceptable derailment, HAZMAT, and environmental justice risks in high-density residential zones
Applicants have failed to provide granular data on infrastructure capacity, structural health, or post-Conrail maintenance standards
Localized PM2.5 and NOx concentration from ultra-long diesel consists outweighs macro-level truck reduction claims
Lehigh Valley corridor represents critical redundancy for Northeast Corridor climate adaptation and national security
Three-mile freight consists create emergency response paralysis and public safety barriers
Proposed merger offers zero local economic return while imposing full infrastructure and environmental burden on region
Lehigh Valley's historical interurban rail infrastructure and nodes remain embedded in regional topography
Unified transit authority network (NEPTA, SRPRA, SEPTA, PRT) serves 54% of Pennsylvania's population
key_excerpts: While historically managed as a private, freight only network, the Applicants' voluntary submission for federal review under 49 U.S.C. § 11324 effectively annuls those claims of private exclusivity.
The Applicants can no longer hide behind 1900s era logic that treats the railroad as a private backyard.
24 trains per day on a single lane mainline constitutes practically full saturation, meaning this surge does not represent increased efficiency but rather perpetual ownership of the corridor.

This operational model guarantees localized emission pooling, where the concentrated discharge of Nitrogen Oxides (NOx) and fine Diesel Particulate Matter (PM2.5) in dense suburban corridors far outweighs the theoretical macrolevel carbon savings cited in their filing.
Approving this merger without federal capacity protections for NEPTA and SRPRA is not just an infrastructure oversight, it is a disenfranchisement of the majority.
To grant a merger of this magnitude without a verified, independent audit of the post Conrail infrastructure is to accept a blind risk.
The Lehigh Valley will no longer be a private conduit for overhead profit; it must be a modernized corridor for the people who live and work there.

docket_entries.title: NYS Comment on Completeness of UP-NS Amended Application
docket_entries.filer_name: New York State Department of Transportation
docket_entries.entry_summary: New York State Department of Transportation filed a completeness challenge to the Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern merger amended application, arguing that it omits one of two NS routes between New York and Massachusetts (the Southern Route via CSXT to Worcester, MA) from network maps and appendices, and fails to analyze merger impacts on commuter rail service on the Port Jervis Line in southern New York operated by Metro-North Railroad. The state requests the Board reject the application as incomplete until these omissions are addressed.
key_arguments: The Amended Application violates Board merger regulations 49 C.F.R. § 1180.6(a)(6) by omitting the Southern Route (Voorheesville, NY to Worcester, MA) from required network maps
Operating Plan and Electronic Appendices violate 49 C.F.R. § 1180.8(b)(1) and (b)(5) by omitting traffic density data for the Southern Route despite acknowledging two NS routes to Massachusetts
Applicants fail to comply with 49 C.F.R. § 1180.8(b)(2) and § 1180.10(b) by omitting impact analysis on Port Jervis Line commuter passenger rail service operated by Metro-North Railroad
Board previously rejected original application for omitting passenger and commuter rail service data in Decision No. 9; Amended Application repeats this deficiency

The omission is significant because pro forma density charts show 50,000 additional annual cars and 5 million additional gross tons of traffic between Binghamton and Albany area under growth scenario, with approximately half continuing to Massachusetts routes
key_excerpts: The Amended Application is incomplete because it omits: (1) one of the two NS routes between New York and Massachusetts from Applicants' network map and the Electronic Appendices supporting the Amended Application; and (2) discussion or analysis of the merger's impacts on commuter passenger rail service on an NS-operated rail line in southern New York.
NS's New England access 'funnels through an intermodal terminal in Ayer, Massachusetts, via PAS [Pan Am Southern] or alternatively via trackage rights on CSXT to Worcester, Massachusetts'

Although Applicants' Operating Plan, consistent with the regulatory history, acknowledges two NS routes between New York and Massachusetts—the Northern Route and the Southern Route—Applicants' network map and Electronic Appendices appear to only reflect NS's trackage rights over one line, the Northern Route.
The Board has already admonished Applicants to detail any impacts anticipated on all passenger services operated on UP or NS lines.

Because the Applicants have the burden of demonstrating that the merger is in the public interest...it is imperative that the Amended Application consider and discuss the impacts of the merger on all passenger and commuter rail services within the Applicants' network.

docket_entries.title: Norfolk Southern's Reply to BNSF Railway Company's Motion to Enforce Decision No. 13
docket_entries.entry_summary: Norfolk Southern filed a reply opposing BNSF Railway Company's motion to enforce Decision No. 13 regarding document production related to Hart-Scott-Rodino Act requirements. Norfolk Southern argues it fully complied with the Board's order by conducting a comprehensive search and producing all responsive non-privileged documents consistent with HSR Act standards and FTC/DOJ guidance.
key_arguments: Norfolk Southern conducted a comprehensive custodial search of 51 potentially relevant individuals and identified 29 'Relevant Custodians' from whom documents were sought
HSR document requests are intentionally narrowly tailored and targeted by design, not intended to produce exhaustive compilations of all documents
The production of 82 responsive documents (38 non-privileged) is consistent with HSR filing practices and there is no statutory requirement for a specific number of documents
BNSF's and CPKC's speculation that more documents 'must exist' is unsupported and based on mischaracterization of HSR Act requirements
HSR guidance explicitly excludes common deal-related documents such as press releases, investor presentations, ordinary course documents, and materials created after the decision to proceed
The speed of transaction formation and late timing of discussions (primarily May 2025) explains the limited number of responsive documents
All key executives including Board Chair Richard Anderson, CEO Mark George, and Supervisory Deal Team Lead Michael McClellan were included in relevant custodians
key_excerpts: Norfolk Southern fully complied with the letter and spirit of the Board's Decision No. 13.

The HSR document requests are targeted by design. They are specifically intended to identify the critical competitive analyses undertaken as parties are evaluating whether to enter into a proposed transaction.
The only relevant question is whether Norfolk Southern complied with Decision No. 13. It did.

Norfolk Southern identified the appropriate custodians, collected and reviewed their documents (including email and electronic documents), and produced non-privileged documents responsive to the HSR document categories that the Board ordered produced.
BNSF's and CPKC's unsupported speculation to the contrary should be rejected, and the BNSF Motion should be denied.

docket_entries.title: Supply Chain Acumen LLC Comments on Application Completeness - Missing Sensitivity Analysis for Fixed Charge Obligations
docket_entries.entry_summary: Supply Chain Acumen challenges the financial completeness of the Revised Application, arguing that applicants have failed to provide sensitivity analysis addressing what happens if projected traffic growth does not materialize. The filing identifies a critical gap: while the application projects efficiency gains and revenue enhancements, it lacks analysis of how the combined entity will service approximately $1.4 billion in annual fixed charges (debt-related) if growth projections fail. The filer argues this omission prevents meaningful Board evaluation under the statutory standard requiring analysis of the merged carrier's ability to service fixed charges (49 U.S.C. § 11324(b)(3)). Supply Chain Acumen provides illustrative equivalencies showing the scale of fixed-charge pressure: the $1.4B could translate to either 10,000 job losses at $140,000 per employee, elimination of 56,000 local switching operations, or 6-14% systemwide rate increases depending on where the burden falls. The filing notes that the rail industry experienced substantial volatility over the past decade (economic contraction, supply-chain disruption, geopolitical instability, public-health emergencies), making stress-scenario analysis not theoretical but necessary. Without sensitivity analysis and stated mitigation plans, the Board and interested parties cannot evaluate whether public benefits remain achievable without adverse consequences on service levels, network resiliency, infrastructure investment, and rail-dependent shippers.
key_arguments: The Revised Application is incomplete because it lacks sensitivity analysis showing how the combined entity will service $1.4B in annual fixed charges if projected traffic growth does not materialize: 'If the growth projected in the UPNS merger application does not materialize, the fixed-charge of $1.4B (as stated in forward looking financials Appendix E, Exhibit 16) must be serviced against a static or potentially declining revenue base.'

Forward-looking financial projections are substantially dependent upon traffic growth projections, creating unanalyzed risk if those projections fail to materialize: 'The forward-looking financial projections appear substantially dependent upon projected traffic growth contained within the Revised Application and supporting studies.'

Forecast sensitivity analysis is critical to the Board's statutory obligation under 49 U.S.C. § 11324(b)(3) to evaluate fixed-charge implications: 'A forecast sensitivity analysis is critical to meeting the Board's statutory obligation to evaluate the fixed-charge implications of the transaction under 49 U.S.C. § 11324(b)(3).'

Without sensitivity analysis, the Board cannot meaningfully evaluate public benefits or adverse consequences to service, resiliency, and infrastructure: 'Without sensitivity analysis demonstrating resiliency, the Board and interested parties cannot meaningfully evaluate whether the public benefits remain achievable without creating adverse consequences upon service levels, network resiliency, infrastructure investment, and rail-dependent shippers.'

Applicants must disclose specific mitigation plans (pricing, cost reduction, workforce reduction, deferred investment) to address the $1.4B fixed-charge obligation under stressed conditions: 'The forecast risk requires stated plans for mitigation through operational and financial measures. Such measures could include increased pricing, operating-ratio-driven cost reductions, train-start reductions, workforce reductions, deferred capital investment, or other actions undertaken to satisfy the transaction's substantial fixed financial obligations.'

Historical rail industry volatility (economic contraction, supply-chain disruption, geopolitical instability, public-health emergencies) demonstrates that stress-scenario analysis is not theoretical but necessary: 'during the past decade the rail industry experienced substantial volatility arising from economic contraction, supply-chain disruption, geopolitical instability, and public-health emergencies. These events underscore the importance of evaluating whether the proposed transaction would remain financially and operationally resilient under stressed conditions.'
key_excerpts: If the growth projected in the UPNS merger application does not materialize, the fixed-charge of $1.4B (as stated in forward looking financials Appendix E, Exhibit 16) must be serviced against a static or potentially declining revenue base. A forecast sensitivity analysis is critical to meeting the Board's statutory obligation to evaluate the fixed-charge implications of the transaction under 49 U.S.C. § 11324(b)(3).

Without sensitivity analysis demonstrating resiliency, the Board and interested parties cannot meaningfully evaluate whether the public benefits remain achievable without creating adverse consequences upon service levels, network resiliency, infrastructure investment, and rail-dependent shippers.

The forecast risk requires stated plans for mitigation through operational and financial measures. Such measures could include increased pricing, operating-ratio-driven cost reductions, train-start reductions, workforce reductions, deferred capital investment, or other actions undertaken to satisfy the transaction's substantial fixed financial obligations.

The absence of such analysis materially limits the ability of the Board and interested parties to evaluate the fixed-charge implications of the proposed transaction under both 49 U.S.C. § 11324(b)(3) and 49 C.F.R. Part 1180.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Require applicants to provide sensitivity analysis evaluating lower-growth and no-growth scenarios demonstrating financial resiliency and mitigation plans if projected traffic growth does not materialize. The Board must receive this information to meaningfully evaluate fixed-charge implications under 49 U.S.C. § 11324(b)(3) and 49 C.F.R. Part 1180.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing raises a statutory completeness issue under 49 C.F.R. § 1180.7(b)(7) (requiring supporting data for analyses) and invokes the Board's substantive review standard under 49 U.S.C. § 11324(b)(3) (fixed-charge analysis). If accepted as valid, it establishes an evidentiary burden requiring applicants to demonstrate financial resiliency under adverse scenarios, not just base-case projections. The filing effectively reopens the question of what constitutes 'sufficient information' for Board evaluation, potentially extending the comment period or requiring supplemental disclosures before the Board can proceed to substantive review. This is a procedural gate-keeping issue that challenges the foundation of the financial case.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Procedural comment on application completeness; applicants likely required to respond in their reply comments or face Board completeness determination.

docket_entries.title: NJ TRANSIT Comment on Amended Application Completeness - Missing Analysis of Freight/Passenger Coordination on Shared Rights of Way
docket_entries.entry_summary: NJ TRANSIT files a targeted completeness challenge on behalf of the nation's third-largest transit provider, identifying three categories of missing analysis in the Amended Application. First, NJ TRANSIT states: 'While the Amended Application projects traffic increases to occur on the CSAO's Lehigh Line as a result of the proposed transaction, the Amended Application includes no analysis of any impacts to passenger trains operating in CSAO territory, including impacts to NJ TRANSIT's operations.' Second, NJ TRANSIT notes that 'the Applicants have not provided any data on the transaction's impacts on NJ TRANSIT's commuter operations,' despite the fact that 'NS holds operating rights over most of NJ TRANSIT's lines, including its Pascack Valley Line, Bergen Line, Main Line, Montclair-Boonton Line, Morristown Line, Gladstone Branch, and Raritan Valley Line,' and that 'Increased frequency of freight operations on these lines could materially and negatively impact NJ TRANSIT's commuter operations.' Third, while the Service Assurance Plan acknowledges NS trackage rights on NJ TRANSIT lines, 'NJ TRANSIT did not find any details of those impacts in the Amended Application' and is 'concerned about the lack of information on how Applicants will ensure that NJ TRANSIT can continue to facilitate current levels of commuter services.' Critically, NJ TRANSIT explicitly reserves its position: 'Through the submission of this letter, NJ TRANSIT is not advancing a position on the acceptance or rejection of the Amended Application and is reserving its right to provide comments later in the proceedings.' This procedural stance signals NJ TRANSIT views the gaps as potentially curable through supplementation rather than fatal, but has preserved the right to shift to active opposition if Applicants' responses are inadequate. The filing implicitly threatens future formal opposition unless operational coordination impacts are fully disclosed.
key_arguments: Amended Application's system impact analysis projecting traffic increases on CSAO Lehigh Line contains zero analysis of impacts to passenger trains already operating in CSAO territory, specifically NJ TRANSIT's Raritan Valley Line operations

Operating Plan fails to provide data on transaction impacts to NJ TRANSIT commuter operations despite NS holding operating rights on 7 of NJ TRANSIT's 12 commuter rail lines (Pascack Valley, Bergen, Main, Montclair-Boonton, Morristown, Gladstone Branch, Raritan Valley)
Increased freight frequency on lines where NS has operating rights 'could materially and negatively impact NJ TRANSIT's commuter operations' but Applicants provide no mitigation analysis
Service Assurance Plan acknowledges trackage rights coordination but contains no details of operational impacts or Applicants' plans to ensure NJ TRANSIT maintains current commuter service levels
Lehigh Line segment between Manville and Newark lacks any analysis of how projected freight traffic increases will be accommodated alongside existing passenger operations
key_excerpts: While the Amended Application projects traffic increases to occur on the CSAO's Lehigh Line as a result of the proposed transaction, the Amended Application includes no analysis of any impacts to passenger trains operating in CSAO territory, including impacts to NJ TRANSIT's operations.
Increased frequency of freight operations on these lines could materially and negatively impact NJ TRANSIT's commuter operations.

NJ TRANSIT is concerned about the lack of information on how Applicants will ensure that NJ TRANSIT can continue to facilitate current levels of commuter services on their lines should the Board approve the transaction.

Through the submission of this letter, NJ TRANSIT is not advancing a position on the acceptance or rejection of the Amended Application and is reserving its right to provide comments later in the proceedings.
docket_entries.relief_requested: NJ TRANSIT requests: (1) Board review of NJ TRANSIT's completeness comments; (2) If procedural schedule is set, Board provide 'ample time for the Applicants' preparation and production of the outstanding information'; and (3) 'Ample time for NJ TRANSIT and other interested parties to review and comment on this additional information.'
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing directly invokes STB's statutory duty to examine competitive and operational impacts under 49 U.S.C. § 11324. NJ TRANSIT's completeness challenge establishes factual record gaps on a statutory-mandated topic: impacts on non-applicant rail operators sharing infrastructure. By framing gaps as incompleteness rather than substantive opposition, NJ TRANSIT places affirmative burden on Applicants to supplement record in discovery/comment phases. The filing creates evidentiary foundation for later conditional opposition if supplementation is inadequate. Additionally, NJ TRANSIT's invocation of 'materially and negatively impact' language creates leverage for negotiating operational safeguards in modified Service Assurance Plan or supplemental agreement.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Board should address in completeness determination and subsequent procedural schedule. NJ TRANSIT requests 'ample time' for applicant supplementation and intervenor review.
