key_arguments: Amended Application provides complete projected market shares, revenues, and traffic volumes as required by 49 C.F.R. § 1180.7(b), incorporating both Day One combination effects and traffic diversion estimates
Applicants made unambiguous commitment not to obtain control of TRRA and offered to condition merger approval on this commitment, eliminating need for separate TRRA control application
Dr. Bailey's market impact analysis properly incorporates projected diversion data and represents forward-looking competitive assessment appropriate for merger review
Projected traffic diversions represent procompetitive benefits of merger, not competitive harms, and should not be mechanically incorporated into competitive harm analyses
Board rules do not require applicants to identify every 2-to-1 and 3-to-2 shipper facility or provide detailed solutions before application acceptance
Questions regarding downstream effects of future mergers, adequacy of competitive enhancements, vertical competition issues, and fixed charges involve merits determinations, not completeness
Minor omissions regarding Southern Route trackage rights and Port Jervis line do not render Application incomplete; corrections will be filed
Discovery disputes and temporary workpaper access issues have no bearing on completeness; applicants have diligently resolved such matters
Applicants' compliance with Decision No. 13 is separate from completeness determination
key_excerpts: The Amended Application is comprehensive and complete, and provides all the information that the Board identified in Decision No. 9 as necessary to complete the application.

Every single 'projection' contained in the original CRA report has been updated in Mr. Hunt's statement to reflect not just the combination of UP and NS, but also the anticipated traffic diversions in the Amended Application.

Unlike in the original Application, Applicants' commitment in the Amended Application is not contingent on the willingness of TRRA's other owners to purchase NS's shares for fair market value. Applicants also explicitly 'offer to condition the Transaction on this divestiture.'

Such diversions are a benefit of the proposed merger, and she addresses them as such in her report. It would not be appropriate as a matter of economic analysis to consider the diverted traffic and any associated increases in the post-merger firm's market shares as a potential competitive harm.

In accordance with the Board's order that 'comments should solely address whether the [Amended] Application is complete,' Applicants are not responding to comments addressing the merits of the Amended Application.

docket_entries.title: Union Pacific Motion for Conference on Discovery Guidelines Disputes
docket_entries.entry_summary: Union Pacific files a motion requesting that ALJ Soulikias convene a conference to resolve discovery guideline disputes. UP notes that while parties agree on 'many key aspects of case management,' 'material disputes remain regarding certain provisions.' The applicants argue that a conference will help 'clarify respective positions, narrowing disputes, and, where possible, reaching agreement on a framework that will promote efficient and orderly discovery.' This filing reveals that competing Class I railroads (BNSF, CPKC, CSXT, CN) have submitted proposed revisions to UP's discovery guidelines (referenced as BNSF-25/CPKC-20/CSXT-8/CN-16), indicating that competitors are actively contesting the scope and pace of discovery in the proceeding. UP frames the motion as collaborative problem-solving but the reference to 'material disputes' and the need for ALJ intervention suggests substantive disagreement on discovery scope—potentially a delaying tactic or defensive posture by competitors seeking broader discovery rights.
key_arguments: Parties agree on many key aspects of case management, but material disputes remain regarding certain discovery provisions that require ALJ clarification
A pre-discovery conference will assist parties in narrowing disputes and, where possible, reaching agreement on an efficient discovery framework
UP is prepared to appear before ALJ at any time suitable to the judge
key_excerpts: The parties' recent submissions agree on many key aspects of case management, but material disputes remain regarding certain provisions.

Applicants submit that a conference before the Administrative Law Judge will assist the parties in clarifying their respective positions, narrowing disputes, and, where possible, reaching agreement on a framework that will promote efficient and orderly discovery.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Request that Administrative Law Judge Jenifer Soulikias convene a conference at her earliest convenience to address discovery guidelines disputes and proposed revisions by competing Class I railroads (BNSF, CPKC, CSXT, CN).
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This motion reveals that discovery framework is contested among multiple Class I competitors, which may indicate: (1) competitors are seeking broad discovery rights to obtain sensitive UP/NS operational data; (2) UP is seeking to limit discovery scope to accelerate proceedings; (3) discovery disputes may delay the proceeding if not resolved quickly; (4) ALJ intervention is already necessary to manage party positions on procedural matters, suggesting deeper substantive disputes lie ahead.
docket_entries.deadline_description: ALJ will determine conference timing at her discretion

docket_entries.title: North Carolina Railroad Company Notice of Intent to Participate
docket_entries.entry_summary: North Carolina Railroad Company, a state-owned entity, filed a notice of intent to participate in the UP/NS merger proceeding. NCRR owns a 317-mile rail corridor that Norfolk Southern Railway operates under lease. The filing contains no substantive arguments for or against the merger, but signals NCRR's intent to monitor the proceeding as its interests may appear—likely regarding lease stability, operational continuity under new merged ownership, or potential service changes on its corridor. This is a pure intervention notice with procedural request for service list placement.
key_excerpts: North Carolina Railroad Company ("NCRR"), a private corporation whose stock is wholly owned by the State of North Carolina, and the owner of a 317-mile rail corridor leased to and operated by Norfolk Southern Railway Company, hereby gives notice of its intent to participate in the above-referenced docket and any related sub-dockets as its interests may appear.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Update the Surface Transportation Board's service list to reflect NCRR as a participant in FD 36873 and any related sub-dockets.
docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: This filing establishes NCRR's formal intervention status, making it a party of record entitled to service of all pleadings and orders. It signals potential concerns about lease arrangements and operational impacts, which could emerge later in substantive filings. NCRR's state ownership (North Carolina state asset) may give it standing to raise public interest or state-level concerns beyond typical commercial landlord/tenant issues.
docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (With Comment)
docket_entries.deadline_description: No response deadline; notice of intent is self-effectuating upon filing.

docket_entries.title: TGS Cedar Port Railroad LLC Notice of Intent to Participate
docket_entries.entry_summary: TGS Cedar Port Railroad LLC filed a notice of intent to participate in the UP/NS merger docket. Wimbish, Fletcher & Sippel LLC) and requests service list inclusion. No substantive arguments, harms, or remedies are articulated. This is typical placeholder filings common early in major merger proceedings; future substantive filings would indicate whether TGSC opposes the merger or has competitive/operational concerns.
key_excerpts: TGS Cedar Port Railroad LLC ('TGSC') hereby gives notice of its intent to participate in the above-referenced docket and any related sub-dockets as its interests may appear.
docket_entries.relief_requested: Service list update to reflect counsel representation (Robert A. Wimbish, Fletcher & Sippel LLC) for purposes of participation in docket FD 36873 and related sub-dockets.

This notice establishes intervenor status for TGSC and ensures it receives service of all future Board orders, notices, and pleadings. docket_entries.document_type: Notice Of Intent To Participate (Without Comment)

docket_entries.title: Union Pacific Errata: Corrected Exhibit 1 Map Showing NS Trackage Rights Over CSX Southern Route
docket_entries.entry_summary: Union Pacific filed a corrected version of Exhibit 1 (the network map at Volume 1, page 118 of the Application) to clarify that Norfolk Southern holds trackage rights over CSX on the 'Southern Route,' which extends between Voorheesville, New York, and Ayer, Massachusetts. The correction was referenced in UP's earlier Reply to Comments on Completeness (UP-51/NS-49) and is being submitted both electronically (JPG) and in 20 printed unbound copies. This is a factual/technical correction to the network diagram showing rail routes and trackage rights arrangements relevant to competitive analysis of the merged entity's network configuration.
key_arguments: The corrected map clarifies existing trackage right arrangements that will remain in place post-merger, affecting NS/UP competitive positioning on the Northeast corridor
The Southern Route trackage right over CSX between Voorheesville, NY and Ayer, MA is material to understanding network configuration and competitive alternatives available to merged entity
key_excerpts: The corrected map shows NS trackage rights over CSX on the 'Southern Route,' which extends between Voorheesville, New York, and Ayer, Massachusetts.

docket_entries.legal_regulatory_significance: Minor but not inconsequential: corrects the factual foundation of the competitive analysis presented to the Board and intervenors. Intervenors and ALJ rely on accurate network maps to assess competitive impacts. The trackage right clarification may affect intervenors' assessment of whether the merged entity will have competitive constraints on the Northeast corridor. No change to substantive legal burdens, but ensures evidentiary record is accurate.
docket_entries.deadline_description: Administrative correction; no response deadline indicated

docket_entries.title: Gateway Cities Coalition Comments on Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern Transaction - Environmental Justice and Rail Corridor Reuse Conditions
docket_entries.filer_name: Gateway Cities of Southeast Los Angeles (City of South Gate on behalf of coalition)
docket_entries.entry_summary: A coalition of 14 Southeast Los Angeles County cities opposes the proposed Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern transaction unless specific conditions are imposed to address inactive rail corridors and environmental justice concerns. The filers request Board-imposed conditions requiring inventory disclosure, good faith negotiations for public use and rail banking, facilitation of greenway projects, and maintenance measures for neglected rail infrastructure in densely populated, predominantly Latino communities.
key_arguments: Board authority under 49 U.S.C. § 11324(c) and § 10101 to impose conditions protecting public interest, environmental protection, and community coordination

Inactive rail corridors in Southeast LA communities create disproportionate impacts including illegal dumping, fire hazards, encampments, and visual blight in already overburdened environmental justice communities
Transaction presents opportunity to advance equitable community investment by transforming neglected infrastructure into public assets
Communities hosting freight transportation burdens should share in benefits of infrastructure modernization and reinvestment
Rail corridor conversion to greenways and active transportation supports regional climate, public health, and sustainability goals
key_excerpts: On behalf of a coalition of Gateway and Southeast Los Angeles County cities...we oppose the proposed transaction unless and until the concerns raised herein are addressed and effective enforcement mechanism is established.

These impacts disproportionately burden densely populated working-class communities that are predominantly Latino and already experience some of the highest cumulative environmental burdens in California
Communities that have long hosted the burdens associated with freight transportation should also share in the benefits of reinvestment and infrastructure modernization.

Absent such conditions, the proposed transaction risks perpetuating longstanding harms while further consolidating control over critical transportation infrastructure without corresponding community accountability.
